**Create `internal/ecalc/tablefuncs.go`** with exactly this content:

```go
package ecalc

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"strings"
)

// The table functions of the expression language read the tables of the catalog:
//
//	lookup(T, C, key)       the value of column C in the row whose key column equals key
//	lookup_ge(T, C, x, OUT) the value of column OUT in the first row whose column C is at least x
//	interp(T, X, Y, x)      the linear interpolation of column Y over column X
//
// T, C, X, Y and OUT are names, not values: a table id, a column id of that table, or an alias that a choice option
// defines in its refs (every option of the choice defines the same aliases, so the choice selects the table or the
// column). They are no variables: Deps leaves them out, and the loader resolves every call for every combination of
// the options of the choices whose aliases it uses.

// tableAlias is how the loader names a choice ref in the table of names an expression may use: an alias is no value.
const tableAlias = "choice alias"

// tableFunc describes a table function: the positions of the arguments that name a table or a column (the table first)
// and the position of the one argument that is an ordinary expression.
type tableFunc struct {
	refs  []int
	value int
}

var tableFuncs = map[string]tableFunc{
	"lookup":    {refs: []int{0, 1}, value: 2},
	"lookup_ge": {refs: []int{0, 1, 3}, value: 2},
	"interp":    {refs: []int{0, 1, 2}, value: 3},
}

func isTableFunc(name string) bool {
	_, ok := tableFuncs[name]
	return ok
}

// valueArgs returns the arguments of a call that are expressions: all of them, except for a table function, whose
// names of tables and columns are left out.
func valueArgs(n *Node) []*Node {
	if n.T == "call" {
		if tf, ok := tableFuncs[n.Name]; ok {
			return []*Node{n.Args[tf.value]}
		}
	}
	return n.Args
}

// walkCalls calls f for every call node of the tree.
func walkCalls(n *Node, f func(*Node)) {
	if n == nil {
		return
	}
	if n.T == "call" {
		f(n)
	}
	walkCalls(n.A, f)
	walkCalls(n.L, f)
	walkCalls(n.R, f)
	for _, a := range n.Args {
		walkCalls(a, f)
	}
	for _, a := range n.Parts {
		walkCalls(a, f)
	}
}

// hasTableCall reports whether the tree calls a table function.
func hasTableCall(n *Node) bool {
	found := false
	walkCalls(n, func(call *Node) { found = found || isTableFunc(call.Name) })
	return found
}

// resolveTableCall finds the table and the columns (in the order of the ref positions after the table) that a call names
// when the aliases in refs apply. The tables must exist, the columns must exist and be numeric, and lookup needs a
// numeric key column.
func resolveTableCall(call *Node, refs map[string]string, tables map[string]*Table) (*Table, []int, error) {
	if tables == nil {
		return nil, nil, errNoTable
	}
	pos := tableFuncs[call.Name].refs
	name := func(i int) string {
		n := call.Args[i].Name
		if r, ok := refs[n]; ok {
			return r
		}
		return n
	}
	t := tables[name(pos[0])]
	if t == nil {
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown table %q", name(pos[0]))
	}
	cols := make([]int, 0, len(pos)-1)
	for _, p := range pos[1:] {
		id := name(p)
		switch ci := t.ColumnIndex(id); {
		case ci < 0:
			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("table %q has no column %q", t.ID, id)
		case !t.Columns[ci].Numeric():
			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("column %q of table %q is text, %s needs numeric columns", id, t.ID, call.Name)
		default:
			cols = append(cols, ci)
		}
	}
	if call.Name == "lookup" && !t.Columns[t.keyIdx].Numeric() {
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("table %q has the text key column %q, lookup needs a numeric key", t.ID, t.Columns[t.keyIdx].ID)
	}
	return t, cols, nil
}

var errNoTable = errors.New("no tables are available to the table functions")

// evalTableCall evaluates lookup, lookup_ge and interp.
func evalTableCall(n *Node, env Env) (float64, error) {
	t, cols, err := resolveTableCall(n, env.Refs, env.Tables)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	x, err := Eval(n.Args[tableFuncs[n.Name].value], env)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	switch n.Name {
	case "lookup":
		return t.lookup(cols[0], x), nil
	case "lookup_ge":
		return t.lookupGE(cols[0], x, cols[1]), nil
	}
	return t.interp(cols[0], cols[1], x), nil
}

// ---- use of tables by a calculator -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// choice returns the choice with the given id, or nil.
func (c *Calculator) choice(id string) *Choice {
	for i := range c.Choices {
		if c.Choices[i].ID == id {
			return &c.Choices[i]
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// selectedRefs returns the aliases of the selected option of every choice (a missing or unknown selection is the
// default of the choice).
func (c *Calculator) selectedRefs(choices map[string]string) map[string]string {
	refs := map[string]string{}
	for i := range c.Choices {
		ch := &c.Choices[i]
		for k, v := range ch.option(choices[ch.ID]).Refs {
			refs[k] = v
		}
	}
	return refs
}

// EvalEnv returns the environment in which the expressions of the calculator are evaluated for the given selection of
// choices: the constants of the selected options as values, their table aliases and the tables of the catalog. The
// caller adds the variables.
func (c *Calculator) EvalEnv(choices map[string]string) Env {
	env := Env{Vals: map[string]float64{}, Lists: map[string][]float64{}, Refs: c.selectedRefs(choices), Tables: c.tables}
	for i := range c.Choices {
		ch := &c.Choices[i]
		for k, v := range ch.option(choices[ch.ID]).Consts {
			env.Vals[k] = v
		}
	}
	return env
}

// tableCall is one call of a table function in an expression of a calculator: where it sits, the expression text and
// the call node.
type tableCall struct {
	what string
	src  string
	node *Node
}

// tableCalls lists the table-function calls of every expression of the calculator.
func (c *Calculator) tableCalls() []tableCall {
	var out []tableCall
	add := func(what, src string, n *Node) {
		walkCalls(n, func(call *Node) {
			if isTableFunc(call.Name) {
				out = append(out, tableCall{what: what, src: src, node: call})
			}
		})
	}
	for _, r := range c.Rules {
		for _, a := range r.Alts {
			add("rule "+r.Target, a.Src, a.Node)
		}
	}
	for _, d := range c.Derived {
		for _, a := range d.Alts {
			add("derived "+d.ID, a.Src, a.Node)
		}
	}
	for i, ch := range c.Checks {
		add(fmt.Sprintf("check %d", i+1), ch.When.Src, ch.When.Node)
	}
	if c.Chart != nil {
		add("chart to", c.Chart.To.Src, c.Chart.To.Node)
	}
	for i, n := range c.FormulaAST {
		add("formula", c.Formula[i], n)
	}
	return out
}

// involved lists the indexes of the choices whose aliases a call names, ascending.
func (c *Calculator) involved(call *Node) []int {
	seen := map[int]bool{}
	for _, p := range tableFuncs[call.Name].refs {
		if ci, ok := c.aliasChoice[call.Args[p].Name]; ok {
			seen[ci] = true
		}
	}
	out := make([]int, 0, len(seen))
	for ci := range seen {
		out = append(out, ci)
	}
	sort.Ints(out)
	return out
}

// eachSelection calls f with every combination of the options of the given choices (indexes), as choice id -> option id.
// With no choice f is called once with an empty selection.
func (c *Calculator) eachSelection(choices []int, f func(sel map[string]string)) {
	idx := make([]int, len(choices))
	for {
		sel := map[string]string{}
		for k, ci := range choices {
			sel[c.Choices[ci].ID] = c.Choices[ci].Options[idx[k]].ID
		}
		f(sel)
		k := len(idx) - 1
		for ; k >= 0; k-- {
			if idx[k]++; idx[k] < len(c.Choices[choices[k]].Options) {
				break
			}
			idx[k] = 0
		}
		if k < 0 {
			return
		}
	}
}

// referencesTable reports whether some table-function call names the table when the choices in fixed (choice id ->
// option id) are selected, for at least one selection of the other choices the call depends on.
func (c *Calculator) referencesTable(tableID string, fixed map[string]string) bool {
	for _, call := range c.tableCalls() {
		found := false
		c.eachSelection(c.involved(call.node), func(sel map[string]string) {
			merged := map[string]string{}
			for k, v := range sel {
				merged[k] = v
			}
			for k, v := range fixed {
				if o, ok := merged[k]; ok && o != v {
					return
				}
				merged[k] = v
			}
			refs := c.selectedRefs(merged)
			name := call.node.Args[tableFuncs[call.node.Name].refs[0]].Name
			if r, ok := refs[name]; ok {
				name = r
			}
			found = found || name == tableID
		})
		if found {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// checkTableUse gives every calculator the tables of the catalog and resolves every table-function call for every
// combination of the options of the choices whose aliases it uses: the table and the columns must exist, be numeric,
// and interp needs a strictly monotonic x column. An alias that no call uses is an error.
func (l *loader) checkTableUse(cat *Catalog) {
	for _, c := range cat.Calculators {
		c.tables = cat.tableByID
		file := l.ids[c.ID]
		seen := map[string]bool{}
		fail := func(format string, args ...any) {
			msg := fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s: %s", file, c.ID, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...))
			if !seen[msg] {
				seen[msg] = true
				l.errs = append(l.errs, errors.New(msg))
			}
		}
		usedAlias := map[string]bool{}
		for _, call := range c.tableCalls() {
			for _, p := range tableFuncs[call.node.Name].refs {
				usedAlias[call.node.Args[p].Name] = true
			}
			c.eachSelection(c.involved(call.node), func(sel map[string]string) {
				t, cols, err := resolveTableCall(call.node, c.selectedRefs(sel), cat.tableByID)
				if err == nil && call.node.Name == "interp" {
					err = t.checkInterp(cols[0], cols[1])
				}
				if err != nil {
					fail("%s: %v in %q%s", call.what, err, call.src, c.selectionText(sel))
				}
			})
		}
		aliases := make([]string, 0, len(c.aliasChoice))
		for a := range c.aliasChoice {
			aliases = append(aliases, a)
		}
		sort.Strings(aliases)
		for _, a := range aliases {
			if !usedAlias[a] {
				fail("table alias %q is never used by a table function", a)
			}
		}
	}
}

// checkFinders validates the finders of the tables once all calculators are known: the calculator and its variable
// exist and have the dimension of the column, the fixed choices are real options, and the calculator's table functions
// name this table when those options are selected.
func (l *loader) checkFinders(cat *Catalog) {
	for _, t := range cat.Tables {
		f := t.Finder
		if f == nil {
			continue
		}
		fail := func(format string, args ...any) {
			l.errs = append(l.errs, fmt.Errorf("%s: %s: finder: %s", l.ids[t.ID], t.ID, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)))
		}
		c := cat.byID[f.Calc]
		if c == nil {
			fail("%q is not a calculator", f.Calc)
			continue
		}
		dim := ""
		if v := c.Var(f.Var); v != nil {
			dim = v.Dim
		}
		for _, d := range c.Derived {
			if d.ID == f.Var {
				dim = d.Dim
			}
		}
		switch col := &t.Columns[t.ColumnIndex(f.Column)]; {
		case dim == "":
			fail("%q is neither a variable nor a derived quantity of %s", f.Var, c.ID)
		case dim != col.Dim:
			fail("%s has the dimension %s, column %s has %s", f.Var, dim, col.ID, col.Dim)
		}
		keys := make([]string, 0, len(f.Choices))
		for k := range f.Choices {
			keys = append(keys, k)
		}
		sort.Strings(keys)
		for _, k := range keys {
			ch := c.choice(k)
			switch {
			case ch == nil:
				fail("%q is not a choice of %s", k, c.ID)
			case !hasOption(*ch, f.Choices[k]):
				fail("%q is not an option of choice %s", f.Choices[k], k)
			}
		}
		if !c.referencesTable(t.ID, f.Choices) {
			fail("the table functions of %s do not name table %s when the choices are %s", c.ID, t.ID, choiceList(keys, f.Choices))
		}
	}
}

func choiceList(keys []string, choices map[string]string) string {
	if len(keys) == 0 {
		return "unset"
	}
	parts := make([]string, len(keys))
	for i, k := range keys {
		parts[i] = k + "=" + choices[k]
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
}

// selectionText describes a selection of options for an error message.
func (c *Calculator) selectionText(sel map[string]string) string {
	var parts []string
	for _, ch := range c.Choices {
		if o, ok := sel[ch.ID]; ok {
			parts = append(parts, ch.ID+"="+o)
		}
	}
	if len(parts) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	return " (with " + strings.Join(parts, ", ") + ")"
}
```

**Create `ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc-tables.js`** with exactly this content:

```js
/* ECalc tables: the table items of the catalog JSON (kind "table") indexed for the table functions of the expression
   language (lookup, lookup_ge, interp) and for the table page. A DOM-free classic script that publishes
   window.ECalcCore.tables, a mirror of the lookups in internal/ecalc/tables.go that scripts/test-ecalc-core.mjs runs
   against the shared vectors.

   A table item is {id, key, columns[{id, dim, unit, ...}], rows[[cell]]}: a cell of a numeric column is a number in SI
   units or null (empty), a cell of a text column (dim "text") is a string or null. The shell calls register(items) once
   the catalog has loaded (every item that is not a table is skipped; a table registered again replaces the old one).
   Table and column arguments name a table id and a column id; an unknown table, an unknown column and a text column
   throw an error with code 'eval', which the solver turns into NaN for the quantity. */
(function () {
    'use strict';

    const core = (window.ECalcCore = window.ECalcCore || {});
    const REL = 1e-9;
    const registry = new Map();

    function fail(message) {
        const error = new Error(message);
        error.code = 'eval';
        return error;
    }

    // Equal within 1e-9 of the larger magnitude; exact equality counts, NaN and infinities never match unless identical.
    function closeEnough(a, b) {
        if (a === b) return true;
        if (!Number.isFinite(a) || !Number.isFinite(b)) return false;
        return Math.abs(a - b) <= REL * Math.max(Math.abs(a), Math.abs(b));
    }

    function build(item) {
        const index = new Map(item.columns.map((column, i) => [column.id, i]));
        return { id: item.id, item, columns: item.columns, rows: item.rows, index, keyIndex: index.has(item.key) ? index.get(item.key) : 0 };
    }

    function register(items) {
        let count = 0;
        for (const item of items || []) {
            if (item && item.kind === 'table') { registry.set(item.id, build(item)); count += 1; }
        }
        return count;
    }

    const reset = () => registry.clear();
    const get = id => registry.get(id) || null;

    function table(id) {
        const found = registry.get(id);
        if (!found) throw fail('unknown table ' + id);
        return found;
    }

    // The index of a numeric column of a table.
    function numericColumn(t, id) {
        if (!t.index.has(id)) throw fail('table ' + t.id + ' has no column ' + id);
        const i = t.index.get(id);
        if (t.columns[i].dim === 'text') throw fail('column ' + id + ' of table ' + t.id + ' is text');
        return i;
    }

    const cellValue = (t, row, column) => (t.rows[row][column] === null ? NaN : t.rows[row][column]);

    // The first row (table order) whose numeric column equals x within 1e-9 relative, or -1.
    function rowOf(t, column, x) {
        for (let r = 0; r < t.rows.length; r += 1) {
            const value = t.rows[r][column];
            if (value !== null && closeEnough(value, x)) return r;
        }
        return -1;
    }

    // findRow(tableId, columnId, value): the row index for the finder highlight and the table page, or -1.
    function findRow(id, columnId, value) {
        const t = table(id);
        return rowOf(t, numericColumn(t, columnId), value);
    }

    // lookup(T, C, key): the value of column C in the row whose key column equals key; NaN when no row matches or the cell is empty.
    function lookup(id, columnId, key) {
        const t = table(id), c = numericColumn(t, columnId);
        if (t.columns[t.keyIndex].dim === 'text') throw fail('table ' + t.id + ' has a text key column, lookup needs a numeric key');
        const row = rowOf(t, t.keyIndex, key);
        return row < 0 ? NaN : cellValue(t, row, c);
    }

    // lookup_ge(T, C, x, OUT): column OUT of the first row whose column C is filled and at least x; NaN when there is none.
    function lookupGe(id, columnId, x, outId) {
        const t = table(id), c = numericColumn(t, columnId), o = numericColumn(t, outId);
        if (Number.isNaN(x)) return NaN;
        for (let r = 0; r < t.rows.length; r += 1) {
            const value = t.rows[r][c];
            if (value !== null && value >= x) return cellValue(t, r, o);
        }
        return NaN;
    }

    // interp(T, X, Y, x): the linear interpolation of Y over X through the rows where both are filled; exact at the nodes,
    // NaN outside the range of X.
    function interp(id, xId, yId, x) {
        const t = table(id), xc = numericColumn(t, xId), yc = numericColumn(t, yId);
        const xs = [], ys = [];
        for (const row of t.rows) {
            if (row[xc] !== null && row[yc] !== null) { xs.push(row[xc]); ys.push(row[yc]); }
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < xs.length; i += 1) if (xs[i] === x) return ys[i];
        for (let i = 0; i + 1 < xs.length; i += 1) {
            const x0 = xs[i], x1 = xs[i + 1];
            if ((x > x0 && x < x1) || (x < x0 && x > x1)) return ys[i] + (ys[i + 1] - ys[i]) * ((x - x0) / (x1 - x0));
        }
        return NaN;
    }

    core.tables = { register, reset, get, findRow, lookup, lookupGe, interp, closeEnough };
})();
```

### Task A3: Generated tables (AWG, IPC-2221, E-series), the table vector format and the unit `mm`

**Goal:** four tables that the engine derives from formulas and from its own IEC 60063 tables, shipped in `catalog/tables/generated.yaml`: `awg` (44 rows, ASTM B258 diameters, cross-sections and the DC resistance of 1 km of annealed copper at 20 °C), `ipc2221` (12 currents, six widths from the IPC-2221 equation), `eseries_e24` (24 rows, membership in E3/E6/E12/E24) and `eseries_e192` (192 rows, membership in E48/E96/E192). Their cells are checked against published values by `testdata/vectors/tables/<id>.json`, and the format and its two enforcing tests (Go `TestTableVectors`, `TestTableVectorFilesNameATable`; Node the same) are what part C fills.

**Files:**

- Replace: `internal/ecalc/tablegen.go` (the stub of task A1)
- Create: `internal/ecalc/catalog/tables/generated.yaml`, `internal/ecalc/tablevectors_test.go`, `internal/ecalc/tablegen_test.go`, `internal/ecalc/testdata/vectors/tables/{awg,ipc2221,eseries_e24,eseries_e192}.json`
- Modify: `internal/ecalc/catalog/units.yaml`, `internal/ecalc/units_test.go`, `internal/ecalc/testdata/vectors/core.json` (unit vectors for `mm`), `internal/ecalc/testdata/catalog.en.json` (regenerated), `scripts/test-ecalc-core.mjs`

**The vector format** (`testdata/vectors/tables/<table id>.json`, the file name is the table id; a file without a table fails): `{"table": id, "cells": [{"key", "column", "want", "tol", "ref"}], "lookups": [{"expr", "env", "refs", "want", "tol", "ref"}]}`. `key` is a number in the unit of the key column or the English text of a text key; `column` a column id; `want` a number in the unit of that column, the English text of a text cell, or `null` for an empty cell; `tol` is the relative tolerance (default 1e-9); a lookup `want` is an SI number or `"nan"`. Every entry names its source in `ref`. Transcribed tables (part C) need at least three cells; a generated table at least five checked against published values.

**Where the generated values come from.** AWG: diameter `0.127 mm x 92^((36 - n)/39)` (ASTM B258; 4/0 is n = -3, 1/0 is n = 0), area `pi/4 d^2`, resistance `(1/58 ohm mm2/m) x 1000 m / area`; the vectors pin the two defining sizes (4/0 = 0.4600 in, AWG 36 = 0.0050 in) exactly and the widely tabulated sizes (1/0 8.251 mm, 2/0 9.266 mm, AWG 10 2.588 mm / 5.261 mm2 / 3.277 ohm/km, AWG 20, 24, 30, 40) at the four-digit precision of the tables. IPC-2221: `I = k dT^0.44 A^0.725` with A in mil2, k 0.048 outer and 0.024 inner, 1 oz = 35 µm; the vectors were worked out independently with 50-digit decimals (not by the Go code). E-series: membership comes from the engine's IEC 60063 tables; the vectors check the published lists (E3 1.0 2.2 4.7, E6 adds 1.5 3.3 6.8, E12 adds 1.2 1.8 2.7 3.9 5.6 8.2, E24 adds the odd values, E96 every second and E48 every fourth E192 value, 9.20 as the exception).

```go
package ecalc

import (
	"fmt"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// tableCellVector and tableLookupVector are the entries of testdata/vectors/tables/<table id>.json.
//
// A cell vector names a row by key (a number in the unit of the key column, or the English text of a text key), a column,
// and the value want that the cell must hold: a number in the unit of that column (matching at the relative error tol,
// 1e-9 when unset), the English text of a text cell, or null for an empty cell. A lookup vector evaluates expr (with env
// and refs) against the tables of the catalog and wants an SI number, or "nan", at the relative error tol. Every entry
// names its source in ref. A transcribed table has at least three cells, a generated one at least five, which the
// vectors check against published values.
type tableCellVector struct {
	Key    any     `json:"key"`
	Column string  `json:"column"`
	Want   any     `json:"want"`
	Tol    float64 `json:"tol"`
	Ref    string  `json:"ref"`
}

type tableLookupVector struct {
	Expr string             `json:"expr"`
	Env  map[string]float64 `json:"env"`
	Refs map[string]string  `json:"refs"`
	Want any                `json:"want"`
	Tol  float64            `json:"tol"`
	Ref  string             `json:"ref"`
}

type tableVectors struct {
	Table   string              `json:"table"`
	Cells   []tableCellVector   `json:"cells"`
	Lookups []tableLookupVector `json:"lookups"`
}

const tableVectorDir = "testdata/vectors/tables"

// checkTableCell checks one cell vector against the table; it returns a description of the problem or "".
func checkTableCell(t *Table, v tableCellVector) string {
	ci := t.ColumnIndex(v.Column)
	if ci < 0 {
		return fmt.Sprintf("table %s has no column %q", t.ID, v.Column)
	}
	key := &t.Columns[t.KeyColumn()]
	row := -1
	switch k := v.Key.(type) {
	case float64:
		if !key.Numeric() {
			return fmt.Sprintf("key %v is a number but the key column %s is text", k, key.ID)
		}
		row = t.FindRow(t.KeyColumn(), key.ToSI(k))
	case string:
		if key.Numeric() {
			return fmt.Sprintf("key %q is a string but the key column %s is numeric", k, key.ID)
		}
		for r := range t.Rows {
			if t.CellText(r, t.KeyColumn(), "en") == k {
				row = r
				break
			}
		}
	default:
		return fmt.Sprintf("key %v must be a number or a string", v.Key)
	}
	if row < 0 {
		return fmt.Sprintf("no row has the key %v in column %s", v.Key, key.ID)
	}
	cell, col := t.Rows[row][ci], &t.Columns[ci]
	switch want := v.Want.(type) {
	case nil:
		if !cell.Null {
			return fmt.Sprintf("row %v, column %s is not empty", v.Key, v.Column)
		}
	case string:
		if col.Numeric() {
			return fmt.Sprintf("row %v, column %s is numeric but want is the text %q", v.Key, v.Column, want)
		}
		if got := t.CellText(row, ci, "en"); cell.Null || got != want {
			return fmt.Sprintf("row %v, column %s = %q, want %q", v.Key, v.Column, got, want)
		}
	case float64:
		if !col.Numeric() {
			return fmt.Sprintf("row %v, column %s is text but want is the number %v", v.Key, v.Column, want)
		}
		if cell.Null {
			return fmt.Sprintf("row %v, column %s is empty, want %v", v.Key, v.Column, want)
		}
		got := col.FromSI(cell.Num)
		tol := v.Tol
		if tol == 0 {
			tol = 1e-9
		}
		if !near(got, want, tol) {
			return fmt.Sprintf("row %v, column %s = %v, want %v (tolerance %g)", v.Key, v.Column, got, want, tol)
		}
	default:
		return fmt.Sprintf("want %v must be a number, a string or null", v.Want)
	}
	return ""
}

func TestTableVectors(t *testing.T) {
	cat, err := Default()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(cat.Tables) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("the catalog has no tables")
	}
	for _, tbl := range cat.Tables {
		t.Run(tbl.ID, func(t *testing.T) {
			var v tableVectors
			readJSON(t, tableVectorDir+"/"+tbl.ID+".json", &v)
			if v.Table != tbl.ID {
				t.Fatalf("%s.json declares table %q", tbl.ID, v.Table)
			}
			need := 3
			if tbl.Generate != "" {
				need = 5
			}
			if len(v.Cells) < need {
				t.Errorf("%d cells, a table of this kind needs at least %d spot-checked cells", len(v.Cells), need)
			}
			for i, c := range v.Cells {
				if c.Ref == "" {
					t.Errorf("cell %d (%v, %s) has no ref", i, c.Key, c.Column)
				}
				if msg := checkTableCell(tbl, c); msg != "" {
					t.Errorf("cell %d (%s): %s", i, c.Ref, msg)
				}
			}
			for i, l := range v.Lookups {
				if l.Ref == "" {
					t.Errorf("lookup %d (%s) has no ref", i, l.Expr)
				}
				n, err := ParseExpr(l.Expr)
				if err != nil {
					t.Errorf("lookup %d %s: %v", i, l.Expr, err)
					continue
				}
				got, err := Eval(n, Env{Vals: l.Env, Refs: l.Refs, Tables: cat.tableByID})
				if err != nil {
					t.Errorf("lookup %d %s: %v", i, l.Expr, err)
					continue
				}
				tol := l.Tol
				if tol == 0 {
					tol = 1e-9
				}
				if want := vecNum(t, l.Want); !near(got, want, tol) {
					t.Errorf("lookup %d %s = %v, want %v (%s)", i, l.Expr, got, want, l.Ref)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestTableVectorFilesNameATable keeps the vector directory strict, like the calculator one: every file is <table>.json
// and names a table of the catalog, so vectors written before their table go red.
func TestTableVectorFilesNameATable(t *testing.T) {
	cat, err := Default()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	files, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.FromSlash(tableVectorDir + "/*"))
	if err != nil || len(files) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("no table vector files found (%v)", err)
	}
	for _, file := range files {
		name := filepath.Base(file)
		if !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".json") {
			t.Errorf("%s: only <table>.json files belong in %s", name, tableVectorDir)
			continue
		}
		var v tableVectors
		readJSON(t, tableVectorDir+"/"+name, &v)
		switch {
		case v.Table == "":
			t.Errorf("%s declares no table", name)
		case name != v.Table+".json":
			t.Errorf("%s declares table %q, so the file must be called %s.json", name, v.Table, v.Table)
		case cat.Table(v.Table) == nil:
			t.Errorf("%s names the table %q, which the catalog does not have", name, v.Table)
		}
	}
}

// The checker itself: it must see a wrong value, a wrong text, a missing row, a wrong key type and an empty cell.
func TestTableCellVectorCheckerSeesMistakes(t *testing.T) {
	tbl := loadTable(t, baseTable)
	ok := []tableCellVector{
		{Key: 1.5, Column: "amps", Want: 15.5},
		{Key: 2.5, Column: "section", Want: 2.5},
		{Key: 1.5, Column: "temp", Want: 70.0},
		{Key: 2.5, Column: "note", Want: "see note"},
		{Key: 4.0, Column: "amps", Want: nil},
		{Key: 1.5, Column: "amps", Want: 15.51, Tol: 1e-3},
	}
	for _, c := range ok {
		if msg := checkTableCell(tbl, c); msg != "" {
			t.Errorf("%+v: %s", c, msg)
		}
	}
	bad := map[string]tableCellVector{
		"a wrong number":      {Key: 1.5, Column: "amps", Want: 15.6},
		"a wrong text":        {Key: 2.5, Column: "note", Want: "other"},
		"a missing row":       {Key: 3.0, Column: "amps", Want: 1.0},
		"an unknown column":   {Key: 1.5, Column: "nope", Want: 1.0},
		"a string key":        {Key: "1.5", Column: "amps", Want: 15.5},
		"a text for a number": {Key: 1.5, Column: "amps", Want: "15.5"},
		"a number for a text": {Key: 1.5, Column: "note", Want: 5.0},
		"an empty cell":       {Key: 4.0, Column: "amps", Want: 1.0},
		"a filled cell":       {Key: 1.5, Column: "amps", Want: nil},
	}
	for name, c := range bad {
		if msg := checkTableCell(tbl, c); msg == "" {
			t.Errorf("%s: the checker accepted %+v", name, c)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
		t.Error("ipc2221 is a design guide: guide values")
	}
	if got := generatorIDs(); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []string{"awg", "eseries_e192", "eseries_e24", "ipc2221"}) {
		t.Errorf("generatorIDs = %v", got)
	}
}

func TestGeneratedAWGTable(t *testing.T) {
	cat, tbl := defaultTable(t, "awg")
	if tbl.Key != "size" || len(tbl.Rows) != 44 {
		t.Fatalf("key %s, %d rows, want key size and the 44 sizes 4/0 ... 40", tbl.Key, len(tbl.Rows))
	}
	col := func(id string) *Column { return &tbl.Columns[tbl.ColumnIndex(id)] }
	if c := col("size"); c.Numeric() {
		t.Error("size is text")
	}
	if c := col("awg"); c.Dim != "number" || c.Unit != "" {
		t.Errorf("awg column = %+v", c)
	}
	if c := col("diameter"); c.Dim != "length" || c.Unit != "" || !reflect.DeepEqual(c.Units, []string{"", "in", "mil"}) {
		t.Errorf("diameter column = %+v", c)
	}
	if c := col("area"); c.Dim != "area" || c.Unit != "mm2" || !reflect.DeepEqual(c.Units, []string{"mm2", "kcmil"}) {
		t.Errorf("area column = %+v", c)
	}
	if c := col("r_km"); c.Dim != "resistance" || c.Unit != "" {
		t.Errorf("r_km column = %+v", c)
	}
	sizes := []string{"4/0", "3/0", "2/0", "1/0", "1", "2", "3"}
	for i, want := range sizes {
		if got := tbl.CellText(i, 0, "en"); got != want {
			t.Errorf("row %d size = %q, want %q", i, got, want)
		}
	}
	if tbl.CellText(43, 0, "en") != "40" || tbl.Rows[0][1].Num != -3 || tbl.Rows[3][1].Num != 0 || tbl.Rows[43][1].Num != 40 {
		t.Error("the sizes run from 4/0 (-3) through 1/0 (0) to 40")
	}

	// The rows agree with the AWG units of units.yaml (the same ASTM B258 formula, written there as expressions), and the
	// resistance is that of 1 km of annealed copper, 1/58 ohm*mm2/m.
	length, area := cat.Units.Dim("length").Unit("AWG"), cat.Units.Dim("area").Unit("AWG")
	di, ai, ri, ni := tbl.ColumnIndex("diameter"), tbl.ColumnIndex("area"), tbl.ColumnIndex("r_km"), tbl.ColumnIndex("awg")
	for r, row := range tbl.Rows {
		n := row[ni].Num
		if !near(row[di].Num, length.ToBase(n), 1e-12) || !near(row[ai].Num, area.ToBase(n), 1e-12) {
			t.Errorf("AWG %v: diameter %v / area %v differ from the AWG units %v / %v", n, row[di].Num, row[ai].Num, length.ToBase(n), area.ToBase(n))
		}
		if want := 1000 * (1e-6 / 58) / row[ai].Num; !near(row[ri].Num, want, 1e-12) {
			t.Errorf("AWG %v: r_km = %v, want %v", n, row[ri].Num, want)
		}
		if r > 0 {
			prev := tbl.Rows[r-1]
			if !(row[di].Num < prev[di].Num && row[ai].Num < prev[ai].Num && row[ri].Num > prev[ri].Num) {
				t.Errorf("AWG %v: a higher number is a thinner wire with more resistance", n)
			}
			if !near(row[di].Num/prev[di].Num, math.Pow(92, -1.0/39), 1e-12) {
				t.Errorf("AWG %v: the diameter ratio of neighbouring gauges is 92^(-1/39), got %v", n, row[di].Num/prev[di].Num)
			}
		}
	}
	// Defining sizes: AWG 36 is 0.005 in and 4/0 is 0.460 in.
	if !near(tbl.Rows[0][di].Num, 0.46*0.0254, 1e-12) || !near(tbl.Rows[39][di].Num, 0.005*0.0254, 1e-12) {
		t.Errorf("4/0 = %v m, AWG 36 = %v m", tbl.Rows[0][di].Num, tbl.Rows[39][di].Num)
	}
}

func TestGeneratedIPC2221Table(t *testing.T) {
	_, tbl := defaultTable(t, "ipc2221")
	if tbl.Key != "current" || len(tbl.Rows) != 12 || len(tbl.Columns) != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("key %s, %d rows, %d columns, want key current, 12 currents and 7 columns", tbl.Key, len(tbl.Rows), len(tbl.Columns))
	}
	amps := []float64{0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10}
	for r, want := range amps {
		if tbl.Rows[r][0].Num != want {
			t.Errorf("row %d current = %v, want %v", r, tbl.Rows[r][0].Num, want)
		}
	}
	for _, id := range []string{"ext_1oz_10", "ext_1oz_20", "ext_2oz_10", "int_1oz_10", "int_1oz_20", "int_2oz_10"} {
		c := tbl.Columns[tbl.ColumnIndex(id)]
		if c.Dim != "length" || c.Unit != "mm" || !reflect.DeepEqual(c.Units, []string{"mm", "mil"}) {
			t.Errorf("column %s = %+v, want length in mm, shown in mm or mil", id, c)
		}
	}
	// Every width solves the IPC-2221 equation back to its current: I = k * dT^0.44 * A^0.725, A in square mils.
	const mil, ounce = 25.4e-6, 35e-6
	type variant struct {
		id        string
		k, dT, oz float64
	}
	for _, v := range []variant{{"ext_1oz_10", 0.048, 10, 1}, {"ext_1oz_20", 0.048, 20, 1}, {"ext_2oz_10", 0.048, 10, 2}, {"int_1oz_10", 0.024, 10, 1}, {"int_1oz_20", 0.024, 20, 1}, {"int_2oz_10", 0.024, 10, 2}} {
		ci := tbl.ColumnIndex(v.id)
		for r, row := range tbl.Rows {
			areaMil2 := row[ci].Num * v.oz * ounce / (mil * mil)
			if got := v.k * math.Pow(v.dT, 0.44) * math.Pow(areaMil2, 0.725); !near(got, row[0].Num, 1e-9) {
				t.Errorf("%s at %v A: the width carries %v A", v.id, row[0].Num, got)
			}
			if r > 0 && row[ci].Num <= tbl.Rows[r-1][ci].Num {
				t.Errorf("%s: a larger current needs a wider trace", v.id)
			}
		}
	}
	// 2 oz halves the width, an inner layer needs 2^(1/0.725) times the outer width, a larger rise allows a narrower trace.
	e1, e2, i1, e20 := tbl.ColumnIndex("ext_1oz_10"), tbl.ColumnIndex("ext_2oz_10"), tbl.ColumnIndex("int_1oz_10"), tbl.ColumnIndex("ext_1oz_20")
	for _, row := range tbl.Rows {
		if !near(row[e2].Num, row[e1].Num/2, 1e-12) || !near(row[i1].Num/row[e1].Num, math.Pow(2, 1/0.725), 1e-12) || !(row[e20].Num < row[e1].Num) {
			t.Errorf("%v A: widths %v %v %v %v break the IPC-2221 relations", row[0].Num, row[e1].Num, row[e2].Num, row[i1].Num, row[e20].Num)
		}
	}
}

func TestGeneratedESeriesTables(t *testing.T) {
	_, e24 := defaultTable(t, "eseries_e24")
	_, e192 := defaultTable(t, "eseries_e192")
	if e24.Key != "value" || e192.Key != "value" || len(e24.Rows) != 24 || len(e192.Rows) != 192 {
		t.Fatalf("keys %s %s, rows %d %d, want key value and 24 and 192 rows", e24.Key, e192.Key, len(e24.Rows), len(e192.Rows))
	}
	check := func(tbl *Table, series ...string) {
		finest := series[len(series)-1]
		for r, row := range tbl.Rows {
			if row[0].Num != eseriesTables[finest][r] {
				t.Errorf("%s row %d = %v, want the %s value %v", tbl.ID, r, row[0].Num, finest, eseriesTables[finest][r])
			}
		}
		for _, s := range series {
			ci := tbl.ColumnIndex(strings.ToLower(s))
			if ci < 0 || tbl.Columns[ci].Numeric() || tbl.Columns[ci].Name["en"] != s {
				t.Fatalf("%s lacks the text column %s", tbl.ID, s)
			}
			marked := 0
			for r, row := range tbl.Rows {
				mark := tbl.CellText(r, ci, "en")
				if mark != "" && mark != "●" {
					t.Errorf("%s %s row %d = %q, want a dot or nothing", tbl.ID, s, r, mark)
				}
				if (mark == "●") != slices.Contains(eseriesTables[s], row[0].Num) {
					t.Errorf("%s: %v is marked %q in %s", tbl.ID, row[0].Num, mark, s)
				}
				if mark == "●" {
					marked++
				}
			}
			if marked != len(eseriesTables[s]) {
				t.Errorf("%s marks %d values in %s, want %d", tbl.ID, marked, s, len(eseriesTables[s]))
			}
		}
	}
	check(e24, "E3", "E6", "E12", "E24")
	check(e192, "E48", "E96", "E192")
	// The engine's tables nest: E3 in E6 in E12 in E24, and E48 in E96 in E192.
	for _, pair := range [][2]string{{"E3", "E6"}, {"E6", "E12"}, {"E12", "E24"}, {"E48", "E96"}, {"E96", "E192"}} {
		for _, v := range eseriesTables[pair[0]] {
			if !slices.Contains(eseriesTables[pair[1]], v) {
				t.Errorf("%v of %s is not in %s", v, pair[0], pair[1])
			}
		}
	}
}

// A generated table takes everything but the descriptive fields from the engine.
func TestLoadRejectsBrokenGeneratedTables(t *testing.T) {
	const awg = `- id: g_awg
  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: conductors
  name: NAME16
  tags: [test]
  source: "Textbook"
  generate: awg
`
	src := strings.ReplaceAll(awg, "NAME16", flow16("T"))
	cat, err := Load(treeFS(t, map[string]string{"tables/g.yaml": src}))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a generated table: %v", err)
	}
	if g := cat.Table("g_awg"); g == nil || len(g.Rows) != 44 || g.Key != "size" {
		t.Fatalf("generated table = %+v", g)
	}

	// The key can be another column of the generated table.
	cat, err = Load(treeFS(t, map[string]string{"tables/g.yaml": src + "  key: awg\n"}))
	if err != nil || cat.Table("g_awg").Key != "awg" || cat.Table("g_awg").KeyColumn() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("key awg: %v", err)
	}

	cases := map[string]struct{ extra, want string }{
		"columns": {"  columns:\n    - {id: x, name: {en: X, de: X}, dim: ratio}\n", "a generated table must not list columns or rows"},
		"rows":    {"  rows:\n    - [1]\n", "a generated table must not list columns or rows"},
		"key":     {"  key: nope\n", `key "nope" is not a column of the table`},
	}
	for name, c := range cases {
		if _, err := Load(treeFS(t, map[string]string{"tables/g.yaml": src + c.extra})); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), c.want) {
			t.Errorf("%s: error = %v, want it to contain %q", name, err, c.want)
		}
	}
	unknown := strings.Replace(src, "generate: awg", "generate: awg2", 1)
	if _, err := Load(treeFS(t, map[string]string{"tables/g.yaml": unknown})); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), `generate "awg2" is not one of awg, eseries_e192, eseries_e24, ipc2221`) {
		t.Errorf("unknown generator: error = %v", err)
	}
}

// The generated tables are served like any other table: SI numbers, localized names, all columns.
func TestGeneratedTablesInTheCatalogJSON(t *testing.T) {
	en, _, _ := fetch(t, "en")
	byID := map[string]int{}
	for i, it := range en.Items {
		byID[it.ID] = i
	}
	for _, id := range []string{"awg", "ipc2221", "eseries_e24", "eseries_e192"} {
		if _, ok := byID[id]; !ok {
			t.Errorf("the catalog JSON lacks the generated table %s", id)
		}
	}
	if en.Items[byID["awg"]].Name != "AWG wire gauges" {
		t.Errorf("name = %q", en.Items[byID["awg"]].Name)
	}
	de, _, _ := fetch(t, "de")
	if de.Items[byID["awg"]].Name != "AWG-Leitergrößen" || de.Items[byID["awg"]].NameEN != "AWG wire gauges" {
		t.Errorf("de name %q / %q", de.Items[byID["awg"]].Name, de.Items[byID["awg"]].NameEN)
	}
}
```

Replace

```js
// ---- calculators/*.json: consistent solutions and single solves -----------------------------------------------------
```

with

```js
count += 5;

// ---- tables/*.json: the cells and lookups of every table of the catalog (the Go twin: TestTableVectors) -----------------
// A cell vector names a row by key (a number in the unit of the key column, or the English text of a text key), a column and
// the value that cell holds in the unit of that column (a string for a text cell, null for an empty one); a lookup vector
// evaluates a table function against the registered tables.
const tableItems = catalog.items.filter(item => item.kind === 'table');
for (const id of ['awg', 'ipc2221', 'eseries_e24', 'eseries_e192']) assert.ok(core.tables.get(id), `the generated table ${id} is in the catalog`);
const tableVectorDir = path.join(root, 'internal/ecalc/testdata/vectors/tables');
const columnUnit = column => (column.unit ? units.dim(column.dim).unitById.get(column.unit) : null);
for (const file of fs.readdirSync(tableVectorDir)) {
    assert.ok(file.endsWith('.json') && tableItems.some(item => item.id + '.json' === file), `${file} in testdata/vectors/tables names no table of the catalog`);
    count += 1;
}
for (const item of tableItems) {
    const set = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(tableVectorDir, item.id + '.json'), 'utf8'));
    assert.equal(set.table, item.id);
    assert.ok(set.cells.length >= 3, `${item.id} needs at least three spot-checked cells`);
    const keyIndex = item.columns.findIndex(column => column.id === item.key), keyColumn = item.columns[keyIndex];
    set.cells.forEach((cell, index) => {
        const label = `${item.id} cell ${index} (${cell.ref})`;
        assert.ok(cell.ref, `${label}: no ref`);
        const columnIndex = item.columns.findIndex(column => column.id === cell.column);
        assert.ok(columnIndex >= 0, `${label}: unknown column ${cell.column}`);
        const column = item.columns[columnIndex];
        let row;
        if (keyColumn.dim === 'text') row = item.rows.findIndex(entry => entry[keyIndex] === cell.key);
        else row = core.tables.findRow(item.id, keyColumn.id, columnUnit(keyColumn) ? columnUnit(keyColumn).toBase(cell.key) : cell.key);
        assert.ok(row >= 0, `${label}: no row has the key ${cell.key}`);
        const value = item.rows[row][columnIndex];
        if (cell.want === null) assert.equal(value, null, label);
        else if (typeof cell.want === 'string') assert.equal(value, cell.want, label);
        else same(columnUnit(column) ? columnUnit(column).fromBase(value) : value, cell.want, label, cell.tol || 1e-9);
        count += 1;
    });
    for (const lookup of set.lookups || []) {
        assert.ok(lookup.ref, `${item.id} lookup ${lookup.expr} has no ref`);
        same(expr.evaluate(expr.parse(lookup.expr), environment(lookup), lookup.refs), lookup.want, `${item.id} lookup ${lookup.expr}`, lookup.tol || 1e-9);
        count += 1;
    }
}

// ---- calculators/*.json: consistent solutions and single solves -----------------------------------------------------
```

**Replace the whole content of `internal/ecalc/tablegen.go`** (the stub of task A1) with exactly this content:

```go
package ecalc

import (
	"fmt"
	"math"
	"slices"
	"sort"
	"strings"
)

// Generated tables (generate: in tables/*.yaml): the columns and rows come from formulas and from the engine's own
// data, so they cannot disagree with them. The item in the YAML carries every other field (name, doc, notes, source,
// group, tags). The columns written here are validated like the columns of a transcribed table, and the rows are
// already in SI units.

// genResult is the output of a generator: the columns as the YAML would list them, the default key column and the rows.
type genResult struct {
	cols []rawColumn
	key  string
	rows [][]Cell
}

var tableGenerators = map[string]func() genResult{
	"awg":          genAWG,
	"ipc2221":      genIPC2221,
	"eseries_e24":  func() genResult { return genESeries([]string{"E3", "E6", "E12", "E24"}) },
	"eseries_e192": func() genResult { return genESeries([]string{"E48", "E96", "E192"}) },
}

func generatorIDs() []string {
	ids := make([]string, 0, len(tableGenerators))
	for id := range tableGenerators {
		ids = append(ids, id)
	}
	sort.Strings(ids)
	return ids
}

func en2(en, de string) Text { return Text{"en": en, "de": de} }

func numCell(x float64) Cell { return Cell{Num: x} }

func textCell(s string) Cell { return Cell{Num: math.NaN(), Text: Text{"en": s}} }

// Constants of the formulas. The values are SI.
const (
	awgBaseDiameter     = 0.000127  // m, AWG 36 = 0.005 in
	copperResistivity20 = 1e-6 / 58 // Ohm*m, annealed copper at 20 degC: 1/58 Ohm*mm2/m (IEC 60028)
	milMetres           = 25.4e-6   // m, one mil
	copperOunce         = 35e-6     // m, the thickness of 1 oz/ft2 copper (the unit oz)
)

// awgDiameter is the ASTM B258 diameter of gauge n: 0.127 mm * 92^((36 - n) / 39); 4/0 is n = -3, 3/0 is -2, 2/0 is -1
// and 1/0 is 0.
func awgDiameter(n int) float64 { return awgBaseDiameter * math.Pow(92, float64(36-n)/39) }

// awgSize is the name of gauge n: "4/0" for -3 ... "1/0" for 0, then "1" ... "40".
func awgSize(n int) string {
	if n < 1 {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%d/0", 1-n)
	}
	return fmt.Sprint(n)
}

// genAWG is the AWG wire table, AWG 4/0 to 40: diameter, cross-section and the DC resistance of 1 km of annealed
// copper at 20 degC.
func genAWG() genResult {
	g := genResult{key: "size", cols: []rawColumn{
		{ID: "size", Name: en2("AWG size", "AWG-Größe"), Dim: textDim},
		{ID: "awg", Name: en2("Gauge number (4/0 = -3, 1/0 = 0)", "Nummer (4/0 = -3, 1/0 = 0)"), Dim: "number"},
		{ID: "diameter", Name: en2("Diameter", "Durchmesser"), Dim: "length", Units: []string{"", "in", "mil"}, Label: "d"},
		{ID: "area", Name: en2("Cross-section", "Querschnitt"), Dim: "area", Unit: "mm2", Units: []string{"mm2", "kcmil"}, Label: "A"},
		{ID: "r_km", Name: en2("DC resistance per km (copper, 20 °C)", "Gleichstromwiderstand je km (Kupfer, 20 °C)"), Dim: "resistance", Label: "R"},
	}}
	for n := -3; n <= 40; n++ {
		d := awgDiameter(n)
		area := math.Pi / 4 * d * d
		g.rows = append(g.rows, []Cell{textCell(awgSize(n)), numCell(float64(n)), numCell(d), numCell(area), numCell(copperResistivity20 * 1000 / area)})
	}
	return g
}

// ipcWidth is the trace width in metres that carries current amps at a temperature rise dT (kelvin) in a layer of the
// given weight (ounces of copper): IPC-2221 gives I = k * dT^0.44 * A^0.725 with A the cross-section in square mils,
// k = 0.048 for an outer and 0.024 for an inner layer.
func ipcWidth(amps, k, dT, ounces float64) float64 {
	areaMil2 := math.Pow(amps/(k*math.Pow(dT, 0.44)), 1/0.725)
	return areaMil2 * milMetres * milMetres / (ounces * copperOunce)
}

// genIPC2221 is the trace width grid of IPC-2221: for currents of 0.25 A to 10 A the width of an external and an
// internal trace in 1 oz copper at a rise of 10 K and 20 K and in 2 oz copper at 10 K.
func genIPC2221() genResult {
	type variant struct {
		id, en, de string
		k, dT, oz  float64
	}
	variants := []variant{
		{"ext_1oz_10", "External, 1 oz, rise 10 °C", "Außenlage, 1 oz, Erwärmung 10 °C", 0.048, 10, 1},
		{"ext_1oz_20", "External, 1 oz, rise 20 °C", "Außenlage, 1 oz, Erwärmung 20 °C", 0.048, 20, 1},
		{"ext_2oz_10", "External, 2 oz, rise 10 °C", "Außenlage, 2 oz, Erwärmung 10 °C", 0.048, 10, 2},
		{"int_1oz_10", "Internal, 1 oz, rise 10 °C", "Innenlage, 1 oz, Erwärmung 10 °C", 0.024, 10, 1},
		{"int_1oz_20", "Internal, 1 oz, rise 20 °C", "Innenlage, 1 oz, Erwärmung 20 °C", 0.024, 20, 1},
		{"int_2oz_10", "Internal, 2 oz, rise 10 °C", "Innenlage, 2 oz, Erwärmung 10 °C", 0.024, 10, 2},
	}
	g := genResult{key: "current", cols: []rawColumn{{ID: "current", Name: en2("Current", "Strom"), Dim: "current", Label: "I"}}}
	for _, v := range variants {
		g.cols = append(g.cols, rawColumn{ID: v.id, Name: en2(v.en, v.de), Dim: "length", Unit: "mm", Units: []string{"mm", "mil"}, Label: "w"})
	}
	for _, amps := range []float64{0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10} {
		row := []Cell{numCell(amps)}
		for _, v := range variants {
			row = append(row, numCell(ipcWidth(amps, v.k, v.dT, v.oz)))
		}
		g.rows = append(g.rows, row)
	}
	return g
}

// genESeries is a table of the IEC 60063 mantissas of the finest listed series with one text column per listed series
// that marks (with a dot) the values that belong to it.
func genESeries(series []string) genResult {
	finest := series[len(series)-1]
	mantissas := eseriesTables[finest]
	g := genResult{key: "value", cols: []rawColumn{{ID: "value", Name: en2("Value (one decade, 1 to 10)", "Wert (eine Dekade, 1 bis 10)"), Dim: "number"}}}
	for _, s := range series {
		g.cols = append(g.cols, rawColumn{ID: strings.ToLower(s), Name: en2(s, s), Dim: textDim})
	}
	for _, m := range mantissas {
		row := []Cell{numCell(m)}
		for _, s := range series {
			mark := ""
			if slices.Contains(eseriesTables[s], m) {
				mark = "●"
			}
			row = append(row, textCell(mark))
		}
		g.rows = append(g.rows, row)
	}
	return g
}
```

### What the other parts get from this part

- **UT (table page).** Catalog JSON: `items` keeps one array, calculators first, then tables, then codes. A table item has exactly `kind id category group name name_en doc notes tags source guide mains key columns rows finder`; `columns[]` is `{id, name, dim, unit, units, label}` (`dim` is a dimension of `units.dims` or `"text"`; `unit` the unit of the cells and the default display unit, `""` = automatic prefix; `units` the offered display units, `[]` = all, `""` inside it = automatic prefix); `rows[][]` hold SI numbers, `null` (empty) or localized strings; `finder` is `null` or `{calc, column, var, choices}` (`choices` is `{}` when nothing is fixed). `key` is the id of the key column. A choice option now carries `refs` (`{}` when unset). The JavaScript side: after the catalog loads call `ECalcCore.tables.register(catalog.items)` (other kinds are skipped; registering again replaces); `ECalcCore.tables.findRow(tableId, columnId, siValue)` is the finder highlight (row index or -1, within 1e-9 relative; it throws `{code: 'eval'}` for an unknown table or a text column); `ECalcCore.tables.get(id)` returns `{id, item, columns, rows, index (column id -> position), keyIndex}`; `lookup`, `lookupGe` and `interp` take table and column ids. Cells convert with `units.dim(col.dim).unitById.get(col.unit).fromBase(v)` (or `units.format(v, dim, unitId, sig)`); the length dimension now has an explicit `mm`. A solve of a finder calculator needs the tables registered first (it reads them through `ECalcCore.tables`). The directory then holds 22 scripts (see the verification note above); load `ecalc-tables.js` anywhere after `ecalc-expr.js` (it is only read at call time), best right after `ecalc-solve.js`. The typesetter prints table and column names of a formula as plain identifiers, so finders should keep table functions out of `formula`.
- **K (codes).** In `codes.go` `init()` call `RegisterCodeKind(id, CodeKind{Load, JSON})`; `Load(raw *yaml.Node, fail)` validates the `data` of a code item (use `fail` for every problem, it prefixes file and item id; `decodeNode(raw, &v)` is the strict decoder) and returns the typed value that is stored in `Code.Data`; `JSON(data, lang)` returns what the catalog JSON carries under `data` (never nil: a nil result is written as `{}`). `Code{ID, Category, CodeKind, Name, Doc, Tags, Source, Data}`, `Catalog.Codes`, `Catalog.Code(id)`, `Catalog.Item(id)`, `CodeKindIDs()` (sorted; use it for an enum). An unknown `code:` fails loading with the list of registered kinds, so register before the default catalog loads (an `init` does). The test kind `test_words` is registered by `codeitems_test.go`; do not register that id.
- **B (tool).** `Catalog.Tables`, `Catalog.Table(id)`, `Catalog.Codes`, `Catalog.Item(id) (kind, ok)`; `Table{ID, Group, Name, Doc, Notes, Tags, Source, Guide, Mains, Key, Generate, Columns, Rows, Finder}`; `Column{ID, Name, Dim, Unit, Units, Label}` with `Numeric()`, `ToSI(x)` and `FromSI(v)` (convert between the column's own unit and SI); `Cell{Num (SI, NaN when empty), Text, Null}`; `Table.CellText(row, col, lang)`, `ColumnIndex(id)`, `KeyColumn()`, `FindRow(col, siValue)`, and the three table functions as `Lookup(column, key)`, `LookupGE(column, x, out)` and `Interp(xcol, ycol, x)` (SI in, SI out, NaN when there is no result). Format values with `Units.Format(v, col.Dim, col.Unit, sig)`. `Text.in(lang)` is the English-fallback accessor. Do not rename `(*Catalog).lookup` of `query.go`; nothing here uses that name. `Calculator.EvalEnv(choices)` is the environment for evaluating a calculator's expressions.
- **C (table content).** Schema: see the contract section 1.1 plus these precisions: a numeric cell is written in the column's `unit` (`""` = SI, otherwise an explicit unit id such as `mm2`, `kcmil`, `degC`, `ppmK`, `mm`, `mil`; the loader converts), `null` is an empty cell, a text cell must be a string (quote numbers such as `"1"`) or `{en, de}`; the key column (first unless `key:`) must be filled with unique values; `rows` and `columns` must not appear with `generate:`. A finder is `finder: {calc, column, var, choices}`; `column` must be numeric with the dimension of `var`; the calculator must name the table in a table function under those choices. Table functions in calculators: write the table and column ids directly (`lookup_ge(cable_ampacity_cu_pvc, a1_2, i, section)`) or define aliases with `refs: {tbl: cable_ampacity_cu_pvc, col: a1_2}` on every option of a choice and use `tbl`/`col`; every alias must be used and every option must define the same aliases; the columns used must be numeric and, for `interp`, the x column strictly monotonic; `lookup` needs a numeric key column. Vectors: `testdata/vectors/tables/<table id>.json` (format in task A3); `TestTableVectors` and the Node script fail for a table without a file, with fewer than 3 cells, or with a cell without `ref`. Finder calculators need `calculators_test.go`'s `EvalEnv` (included here) for their `sets` vectors. Rows of an `interp` column must be listed in monotonic order; rows of a `lookup_ge` column in ascending order of that column (the function returns the first row that qualifies).

## Part UT — Table page and routing by kind (tasks UT1–UT5)


**Goal of this part:** teach the ECalc app its second item kind. A **table page** (title, favorite and "Copy table", the guide-values and mains banners, an optional finder header, a filter box, sortable columns, a unit dropdown per column, a sticky header inside a scroll area, notes, explanation and source under the table), a **shell** that routes every item to the page creator of its kind (calculator, table, code) with one options object, the Tables list **sectioned by group**, the **registration of the catalog tables** with `ECalcCore.tables` (Part A) so that the table functions can read them, the **finder header mode** of the calculator page, and the 17 strings of all this in 16 languages. The table page also hides the columns that have no value in any row (with a line under the table that says how many), and its unit dropdown follows the phase 2 rules for a `units` list that has only explicit units. The code pages are Part UK's: this part defines the options object they receive and shows a message while no `ECalcCodePage` exists.

**Prerequisite (Part A, same wave):** `ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc-tables.js` publishes `window.ECalcCore.tables = { register(items), reset, get(id), findRow, lookup, lookupGe, interp, closeEnough }` (`get(id)` returns `{id, item, columns, rows, index, keyIndex}`), `ecalc-solve.js` reads the table aliases of the selected choice options (`choiceRefs`), and the served catalog JSON has the table items of contract §1.3 (`kind id category group name name_en doc notes tags source guide mains key columns rows finder`, rows in SI, strings localized). Part UT calls `register` from the shell (guarded: skipped when the API is missing, a throwing registry does not take the app down) and reads the table JSON directly; it needs nothing else from Part A.

**Order:** UT1 → UT2 → UT3 → UT4 → UT5. UT2 writes the browser test first; it stays red (and is skipped unless `AURAGO_RUN_BROWSER_SMOKE=1`) until UT5 wires the shell, so every commit keeps `go test ./ui` green.

### How this part was made and verified

The part was built for real in a scratch worktree at base commit `4b3b14ec0` (ECalc phases 1 and 2 landed) and verified there; every code block below was **generated** from the verified files by a script that also checks that the edits of all tasks, applied in task order to the base files, reproduce the verified files byte for byte. The plan was then replayed task by task on a clean base (red and green runs of every task are recorded in Verification).

**Verified against Part A's real engine.** The worktree received Part A's final files (the Go engine, the generated tables `awg`, `ipc2221`, `eseries_e24`, `eseries_e192`, `ecalc-tables.js`, the table-function solver) once the first drafts of this part were done, and the whole part was re-run on them: the fixture finder `fx_finder` solves `smin = lookup_ge(tbl, col, ieq, out)` through the real JavaScript solver (the material option defines the aliases `tbl`/`col`/`out` with `refs`; the table page pins the material and the highlight follows the solved cross-section), and the browser test opens every table of the real catalog (the four generated ones) next to its fixtures. **Verified against Part C's real content too.** After the integration run failed on the real VDE ampacity table, the content of Part C (44 real tables in the catalog, six of them with a finder bound to `cable_cross_section_finder` or `trace_spacing_finder`, the aluminium tables with up to ten columns without data, the ASCII table with radix units) was copied into the worktree and the part was fixed and re-run on it (deviation 17). The real-catalog loop of the browser test now checks every real table: rows equal to the registry's, the shown columns equal the columns that have data, no sideways scroll of the page or of the list, the scroll area inside the window, no placeholder text such as NaN in a cell, a units list that never offers an unlisted unit, and for a table with a finder the header, and either exactly one highlighted row, a check warning or the no-match hint; the ASCII table's radix column is switched to hex.

### Contract deviations

Where this list and the contract disagree, this list wins.

1. **One options object, a richer page object (contract §4: "return `{dispose()}`").** The shell needs the DOM element of a page and wants to tell it about layout and settings, so a page creator returns `{el, dispose}` (both required) plus the optional `layout()`, `refresh()` and `focusFilter()`; the shell guards every optional call. The options object is the one in "Page creator contract" below; `item` is the canonical name, the calculator page still reads the older `calc`.
2. **The finder header is a mode of `ECalcCalcPage` (`options.header = {choices, onResult}`), and a header is not a page:** it carries `data-finder="<calc id>"` instead of `data-calc`, so the tests and the shell, which find pages by `data-calc`, never mistake it for one. The header has no title row of its own (a small title and the reset button), no schematic, formula, chart, combiner, E-series block or explanation; the choices the table fixes are pinned in every state (stored, default, reset) and their controls are not drawn. Every solve is reported through `header.onResult(result)`.
3. **The finder header keeps its own stored state per table**, under the store key `<calculator id>@<table id>` (a scoped store handed to the header). Reason: several tables share one finder with different fixed choices, and the fixed choices must never leak into the calculator's own page or into another table. Unit choices of the header's fields are scoped the same way.
4. **`ecalc.js` is unchanged.** The registration happens in the shell, which already receives the whole catalog.
5. **Browser test in its own file.** Contract §9 says "browser test extended"; the table scenarios need a fresh browser state (remembered page, window, stored units), so they are a new test, `TestDesktopECalcTablesBrowser`, in `ui/desktop_ecalc_tables_browser_test.go`, on top of a **reusable fixture helper** `ui/desktop_ecalc_fixture_test.go` (`newECalcBrowserFixture(t, patch)`: the desktop shell of the bundle, the German desktop words, the catalog of the server route with a JavaScript patch applied, `Wait`, `Shot`, `OpenApp`, `CloseWindows`). Part UK's code-page test should use it.
6. **The page budget of `TestDesktopECalcBrowser` goes from 90 to 170 seconds** (the new fixture helper uses 170 too). The old test needed 87 of its 90 seconds at the base commit and failed with `context deadline exceeded` on a slower run; it grows with every phase, and on a machine that is busy with other work (CPU at 99 % during the drafting) it needed more than 150. The launcher context of `newSmokeBrowserWith` (`ui/destructive_flow_browser_test.go`, not touched here) stops the browser after 180 s, which bounds this; if the old test grows past that it has to be split, or that context raised.
7. **`ecalcScripts` in `ui/desktop_ecalc_test.go` no longer pins "exactly 21 scripts"** (done in UT1: Part A's `ecalc-tables.js` is already the 22nd script and turns seven ECalc tests of `./ui` red). Four parts add scripts in phase 3 (tables, table page, codes, code pages); the count check becomes "at least 21", the loader test (`TestECalcIsWiredIntoTheDesktopCore`) pins the exact list and order. This part's loader order: `…eseries, solve, tables, typeset…` (Part A: "anywhere after `ecalc-expr.js`", everything reads `ECalcCore.tables` lazily) and `…calc-page, table-page, shell, ecalc.js`; Part K adds `ecalc-codes.js` and Part UK its two files after `ecalc-table-page.js`.
8. **Table cells follow the significant-digits setting** (contract §4 asks for it): a table with more digits than the setting shows them rounded, in the page and in the copied text. The unit of a column is written once in its header (a dropdown, or static text when the `units` list offers one choice or the column has a fixed `unit` and no list), the cells show the bare number; with the automatic prefix the cells carry prefix and symbol. A cell the unit cannot show (dBV for a negative value) falls back to the automatic prefix.
9. **The `/` shortcut lives in the shell** (root keydown: not with a modifier, not typed into a field, only when the page has `focusFilter`), and the page host has `tabindex="-1"` so that a click into the page leaves the focus inside the app. Escape in the filter box clears it (and stops propagation like the search box does).
10. **Strings: 17 new keys** instead of the two the contract names: `ecalc_guide_values`, `ecalc_mains_note`, `ecalc_page_unavailable`, `ecalc_group_{conductors,components,materials,general}`, `ecalc_table_{columns_hidden,copy,filter,no_match,no_rows,notes,rows,rows_filtered,sort,unit}`. `ecalc_table_rows` / `_rows_filtered` / `_unit` / `_columns_hidden` carry the placeholders `{total}`, `{shown}`, `{name}`, `{count}` (pinned in all 16 languages). The row counts are written "Rows: N" (a colon, no plural forms). Part UK delivers its own keys.
11. **The highlight keeps its own `findRow`** (`ecalc-table-page.js`, same rule as `ECalcCore.tables.findRow` of Part A: equal within 1e-9 relative of the larger magnitude, empty cells never match) instead of calling the registry: the page reads the item JSON directly and still works when the registry refused the tables. **The sticky header takes `--vd-theme-panel-bg-strong`**, which is 94 to 100 % opaque in the 15 desktop skins (measured: standard 0.98, orbit 0.94, cyberpunk 0.95, the rest 0.96 to 1); the browser test accepts 0.9 and up, so a skin with a glass token fails it.
12. **Two shell glyphs (`info`, `bolt`) and two exports of the calculator page (`unitChoices`, `copyText`)** are new: the banners use the glyphs; the table page reuses the unit whitelist logic and the clipboard fallback of the calculator page (`copyText` moved out of `create` to module level, unchanged). `TestECalcLaunchHookIsWired` pins the new export line.
13. **Table matching tolerance:** the finder row is the first row whose `finder.column` cell equals the solved `finder.var` within 1e-9 relative (the contract's rule); an empty cell never matches. A solved value without a row shows the hint `desktop.ecalc_table_no_match` next to the row count.
14. **Columns without any value are hidden** (requirement of the content drafters: the aluminium ampacity tables keep columns without verified data because the finder aliases need them to exist). A column whose cells are all `null` is not drawn and is skipped by the filter, by sorting and by the copied text; a line under the table (`desktop.ecalc_table_columns_hidden`, "Columns without verified data are hidden: N", `<p class="ec-table-hidden">`, also `data-hidden-columns` on the page) says how many. A table without rows, or with no column that has a cell, shows everything. A finder whose `column` is hidden highlights nothing.
15. **A `units` list without `""`** (for example the ASCII table's `dec` column with `[dec, hex, bin, oct]`, the radix units of the `integer` dimension) has the semantics of a phase 2 variable: `""` admits the automatic prefix and the fixed prefixes, every other entry admits exactly that explicit unit. The dropdown offers only the listed units, the first one applies when the column's `unit` is not offered, the cells are written by `ECalcCore.units.format` (`0x41`, `0b1000001`, `0o101`), sorting uses the value, the filter reads the text shown and the copied header names the system (`Code [hex]`).
16. **A finder without a value shows the warning of its check.** The header is the calculator page, so a check whose condition holds is listed in it (`.ec-warnings`); the finder field shows the "no finite result" message and no row is highlighted (and no no-match hint: there is no solved value). The solver skips a check whose condition depends on a quantity that is not finite, so a finder check must be written on the inputs or on a derived quantity that stays finite (`current / factor > limit`), not on the finder's own output.

17. **Wide content never widens the page or the list** (found by the integration run: the real VDE ampacity table, the 15-column `cable_ampacity_cu_pvc`, made the page scroll sideways; the cause was the finder header's installation-method choice, a segmented control with ten long options, whose minimum width became the width of the grid column of the page, 2200 px). The stylesheet fixes the class of problems, not the one table: `.ec-page` has `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)` (an item cannot widen the track), `.ec-seg` wraps (`flex-wrap: wrap`, the separators are shadows so that a wrapped row has no stray left border), `.ec-items` and `.ec-item-text` have the same zero-minimum track (a long word in a table name no longer gives the list a horizontal scrollbar). A table wider than the page scrolls inside `.ec-table-scroll`, with the sticky header. The browser test pins it with fixtures (`fx_wide`: 16 columns and a very long name; `fx_finder`: a third choice with twelve long options) and for every real table.

### Page creator contract (Part UK relies on this)

The shell (`ecalc-shell.js`, `pageOptions(item)`) creates the page of the selected item with `window.ECalcCalcPage.create(options)` for `kind` calculator, `window.ECalcTablePage.create(options)` for table and `window.ECalcCodePage.create(options)` for code (a missing creator shows `desktop.ecalc_page_unavailable`). The **options object has exactly these keys** (the browser test pins them):

| key | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `item` | the catalog item of the page (the JSON of `internal/ecalc/localize.go`; for a code item `{kind, id, category, code, name, name_en, doc, tags, source, data}`) |
| `units` | `ECalcCore.units.create(catalog.units)` (`parse`, `format(value, dim, unit, sig)`, `options(dim)`, `dim(id)`, …) |
| `store` | the window's `ECalcStore`: `prefs()` (`sig`, `eseries`, `symbols`, …), `isFavorite(id)`, `toggleFavorite(id)`, `unitOf(id, key)` / `setUnit(id, key, unit)`, `calcState`/`saveCalc`, `flush()` |
| `t` | `t('desktop.ecalc_…', {name: value})`, fills `{name}` placeholders |
| `icon` | `icon(name)` returns the svg markup of the shell glyph (`search settings back star clock copy reset lock warning info bolt`) |
| `schematics` | `window.ECalcSchematics` (calculators only) |
| `uid` | an element-id prefix unique per window and item (`ec-<window>-<item id>`); derive ids from it |
| `decimalComma` | `true` in the languages that write the decimal comma (the core always uses the point; replace `(\d)\.(\d)` by `$1,$2` for display) |
| `getItem` | `id => catalog item or null` |
| `onFavorite` | call it after the page changed its item's favorite flag; the shell repaints rail and list |

The **page object** a creator returns: `el` (the `<article class="ec-page …">` the shell puts into `.ec-page-host`, required), `dispose()` (required; clear timers, `store.flush()`), and optional `layout()` (the host changed its size; also called once after the page is attached; the element has no size before that), `refresh()` (digits, E series or symbol standard changed: draw everything again) and `focusFilter()` (the `/` shortcut). Pages are found by attribute: calculators `data-calc="<id>"`, tables `data-table="<id>"`; Part UK should use `data-code="<id>"` (the fixture test of this part uses `data-code-stub`). Use the favorite markup of the table page (`[data-action="favorite"]`, `aria-pressed`, glyph `star`) so the buttons look alike; the stylesheet already has `.ec-page-head`, `.ec-title`, `.ec-actions`, `.ec-btn`, `.ec-banner`, `.ec-source`, `.ec-doc`. Part UK appends its own `/* code pages */` section at the end of `ui/css/desktop-app-ecalc.css`; this part's table section sits in front of the "One stack below 720 px" section.

### Environment

- Windows box. Go: set `GOTMPDIR` to a short backslash path (`$env:GOTMPDIR = 'C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p3-ut'`, create the folder once). If D: (the Go cache) is full use a per-run `GOCACHE`.
- Browser tests need `AURAGO_RUN_BROWSER_SMOKE=1` and Chrome started from a test binary: run them from PowerShell with the sandbox disabled. `AURAGO_BROWSER_ARTIFACT_DIR` keeps screenshots (the tables test saves `table-ampacity`, `table-long`, `table-awg`, `table-long-<skin>` and the compact ones).
- The working copies of `ui/js/**` and `ui/css/**` may be CRLF on a Windows checkout (git stores LF): use an edit tool that matches across line endings or normalise the file to LF first. Every "Replace … with …" block must match exactly once.
- Tools that decode backslash-u escapes (the Write/Edit tools): none of the code below contains one; write µ, Ω, ², · and the em dash as characters.
- GitNexus: before modifying an existing function run `node .gitnexus/run.cjs impact "<symbol>" --direction upstream --repo .`; before every commit run `detect_changes` (the index is behind the working tree: re-run `analyze` first, or read `partial`/`behind` as "unseen", not "clean").
- Commit messages end with the trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- Core bundle: `module-loader.js` is loaded by `desktop.html` and is **not** part of `main.bundle.js`; nothing in this part changes a bundled file, `node scripts/build-ui-bundles.js --check` stays clean (it is run in UT5).

```js
const prefix = 'desktop.ecalc_';
for (const [lang, texts] of Object.entries(words)) {
    if (texts.length !== keys.length) throw new Error(lang + ': ' + texts.length + ' texts for ' + keys.length + ' keys');
    const file = path.join(root, 'ui', 'lang', 'desktop', lang + '.json');
    const raw = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
    const data = JSON.parse(raw);
    const entries = Object.entries(data);
    const first = entries.findIndex(([key]) => key.startsWith(prefix));
    let last = -1;
    entries.forEach(([key], index) => { if (key.startsWith(prefix)) last = index; });
    const block = entries.slice(first, last + 1);
    if (!block.every(([key]) => key.startsWith(prefix))) throw new Error(lang + ': the ecalc keys are not one run');
    const sortedBefore = block.map(([key]) => key).every((key, index, list) => index === 0 || list[index - 1] < key);
    if (!sortedBefore) throw new Error(lang + ': the ecalc run is not sorted');
    keys.forEach((key, index) => {
        if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(data, prefix + key)) throw new Error(lang + ': ' + prefix + key + ' exists already');
        block.push([prefix + key, texts[index]]);
    });
    block.sort((a, b) => (a[0] < b[0] ? -1 : a[0] > b[0] ? 1 : 0));
    const merged = Object.fromEntries(entries.slice(0, first).concat(block, entries.slice(last + 1)));
    fs.writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify(merged, null, 2) + '\n');
}
console.log('inserted ' + keys.length + ' keys into ' + Object.keys(words).length + ' languages');
```

- Modify: `ui/desktop_ecalc_browser_test.go` (page budget 90 → 150 s)

The test injects **fixture content into the served catalog** (a JavaScript patch in the exact JSON shape of contract §1.3): six tables in the groups conductors, general and an unknown one (`fx_ampacity` and `fx_ampacity_al` with both banners, notes, doc, null cells, unit lists and the finder `fx_finder`, which solves `smin = lookup_ge(tbl, col, ieq, out)` through the real solver with the material fixed to `cu` / `al` (the option's `refs` name the table) and a free `method` choice; `fx_awg` with a text key column and the columns of the generated AWG table; `fx_long` with 60 rows and the finder `fx_pick`; `fx_plain`; `fx_misc` with a fixed unit and no units list; `fx_ascii` with an integer column whose `units` list holds only radix units; `fx_wide` with 16 columns and a very long name), two finder calculators in the category wiring, and one `code` item. `fx_ampacity_al` carries two columns without any value (hidden, counted under the table, absent from the copied text and the filter); the check of `fx_finder` fires for a current beyond the tables (no value, the warning in the header, no highlight), and `fx_finder` has a third choice with twelve long options (the page must not scroll sideways because of it). Real catalog tables are taken out of the served JSON until the last phase of the test, which opens every one of them. It checks, in German: the rail (Tables and Codes shown, Pinouts hidden), the sectioned list, the banners, the finder header (fixed choice hidden, free choice shown, highlight, no-match hint, per-table stored state, the finder calculator's own page untouched), the highlight scrolled into view in both directions, the sticky header, the filter box and `/`, sorting with empty cells last, the unit dropdowns and the copied text, settings, favorites, the search, the identical options object of the three page creators (the code creator is a stub the test installs), the message for a kind without a creator, the opaque header in every desktop skin, the pre-fill bridge opening a table, every real catalog table, and the phone-sized layout.

```go
package ui

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/desktop"
	"aurago/internal/ecalc"

	"github.com/go-rod/rod"
)

// ecalcBrowserFixture is the fixture desktop of the ECalc browser tests of phase 3 (tables, code pages): the real desktop
// shell of the bundle with the fixture API of testdata/aurora-fixture.js, the German words of the desktop, and the
// catalog of the server route (ecalc.Default, localized to the requested language) with a patch applied to the JSON
// before the app sees it. The patch is the source of a JavaScript function `catalogJSON => catalogJSON` that adds the
// content later parts write (fixture tables, a finder calculator, a code item) in exactly the shape of the served
// catalog. The shell runs in German; set AURAGO_BROWSER_ARTIFACT_DIR to keep the screenshots.
type ecalcBrowserFixture struct {
	T       *testing.T
	Page    *rod.Page
	Words   map[string]string // the merged German desktop words
	Catalog *ecalc.Catalog
}

func newECalcBrowserFixture(t *testing.T, patch string) *ecalcBrowserFixture {
	t.Helper()
	requirePrecisionBrowserSmoke(t)
	catalog, err := ecalc.Default()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	html := regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)<script\b[^>]*>.*?</script>`).ReplaceAllString(readDesktopAssetText(t, "desktop.html"), "")
	html = regexp.MustCompile(`\{\{[^}]*\}\}`).ReplaceAllString(html, "")
	html = strings.Replace(html, "</body>", `<script src="/js/shared/lazy-assets.js"></script><script src="/js/desktop/core/module-loader.js"></script><script src="/ecalc-fixture-shell.js"></script><script src="/testdata/aurora-fixture.js"></script></body>`, 1)
	shell := readDesktopAssetText(t, "js/desktop/bundles/main.bundle.js")
	cut := strings.LastIndex(shell, "    ensureDesktopRadialMenuAnchor();")
	if cut < 0 {
		t.Fatal("desktop startup seam missing")
	}
	shell = shell[:cut] + `window.aurora={state,loadIconManifest,applyDesktopSettings,renderIcons,renderStartApps,renderStartButtonIcon,wireShellChromeControls,bindViewportMetrics,handleDesktopKeydown,closeContextMenu,openApp,closeWindow};})();`

	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.Handle("/", http.FileServer(http.FS(Content)))
	mux.HandleFunc("/fixture", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { fmt.Fprint(w, html) })
	mux.HandleFunc("/ecalc-fixture-shell.js", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/javascript")
		fmt.Fprint(w, shell)
	})
	mux.HandleFunc("/ecalc-catalog.json", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		body, _, err := catalog.LocalizedJSON(r.URL.Query().Get("lang"))
		if err != nil {
			http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusInternalServerError)
			return
		}
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		_, _ = w.Write(body)
	})
	mux.HandleFunc("/fixture-words", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		fmt.Fprint(w, readDesktopAssetText(t, "lang/desktop/de.json"))
	})
	mux.HandleFunc("/fixture-apps", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(desktop.BuiltinApps()) })
	server := httptest.NewServer(mux)
	t.Cleanup(server.Close)
	// The page budget is 170 seconds (a loaded machine needs far more than the 90 the first drafts had); the browser itself is
	// stopped after 180 (newSmokeBrowserWith).
	page := newSmokeBrowser(t).MustPage(server.URL + "/fixture").Timeout(170 * time.Second)
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = page.Close() })
	page.MustWaitLoad()
	page.MustSetViewport(1366, 900, 1, false)
	// The fixture answers every /api/ request with an empty object; the catalog route gets the real catalog of the
	// requested language with the patch applied.
	page.MustEval(`async()=>{
		await fixtureReady;
		window.ecalcPatchCatalog=` + patch + `;
		const base=window.fetch;
		window.fetch=(url,options)=>{
			const text=String(url);
			if(!text.startsWith('/api/ecalc/catalog'))return base(url,options);
			return base('/ecalc-catalog.json'+text.slice('/api/ecalc/catalog'.length)).then(r=>r.json()).then(j=>{
				window.ecalcPatchCatalog(j);
				return new Response(JSON.stringify(j),{headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}});
			});
		};
		fixtureTheme('standard');
	}`)
	return &ecalcBrowserFixture{T: t, Page: page, Words: readMergedLangMap(t, "de"), Catalog: catalog}
}

// Wait polls a JavaScript predicate (a function source) for up to five seconds; a timeout reports the errors the page
// logged meanwhile.
func (f *ecalcBrowserFixture) Wait(expr string) {
	f.T.Helper()
	begin := time.Now()
	deadline := begin.Add(5 * time.Second)
	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
		if f.Page.MustEval(expr).Bool() {
			if took := time.Since(begin); took > time.Second {
				f.T.Logf("slow wait (%v): %s", took.Round(time.Millisecond), expr)
			}
			return
		}
		time.Sleep(25 * time.Millisecond)
	}
	f.T.Fatalf("condition did not become true: %s\npage errors: %s", expr, f.Page.MustEval(`()=>JSON.stringify(fixtureErrors)`).Str())
}

// Shot saves a screenshot when AURAGO_BROWSER_ARTIFACT_DIR is set.
func (f *ecalcBrowserFixture) Shot(name string) {
	f.T.Helper()
	dir := os.Getenv("AURAGO_BROWSER_ARTIFACT_DIR")
	if dir == "" {
		return
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
		f.T.Fatal(err)
	}
	f.Page.MustScreenshot(filepath.Join(dir, name+".png"))
}

// OpenApp opens the ECalc window and waits until `ready` (a selector) exists.
func (f *ecalcBrowserFixture) OpenApp(ready string) {
	f.T.Helper()
	f.Page.MustEval(`async()=>{await fixtureOpen('ecalc');}`)
	f.Wait(`()=>!!document.querySelector('` + ready + `')`)
}

// CloseWindows closes every desktop window (and with it every ECalc instance).
func (f *ecalcBrowserFixture) CloseWindows() {
	f.Page.MustEval(`()=>[...aurora.state.windows.keys()].forEach(id=>aurora.closeWindow(id))`)
}
```

```go
package ui

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
```
