## Part K — Component codes in Go and JavaScript (tasks K1–K2)


**Goal of this part:** read and write the markings of passive components in Go and in the DOM-free JavaScript mirror, held together by shared vectors: the five code items of the catalog (`resistor_color_code`, `inductor_color_code`, `smd_resistor_code`, `capacitor_code`, `ceramic_temp_code`) with their tables as data, the engine functions `(*Catalog).Decode(kind, code)` and `(*Catalog).Encode(kind, EncodeRequest)` that Part B wraps in the tool actions `decode` and `encode`, and `window.ECalcCore.codes = {decode(item, code, units), encode(item, req, units)}` that Part UK builds the code pages on.

**Architecture:** unchanged from phases 1 and 2 (declarative embedded catalog, validated at load, served localized, evaluated twice and held together by vectors). Part A built the plumbing: a code item names a registered code kind whose `Load` validates the item's `data` and whose `JSON` renders it for a language. This part registers the five kinds in `init` (`codes.go`) and gives each a typed data struct that also carries the codec (`decode`/`encode`): the colours, digits, exponents of the multipliers, tolerances and temperature coefficients, the EIA-96 table, the tolerance letters, the voltage codes and the class tables live in `catalog/codes/*.yaml`, not in Go. The JavaScript twin reads the same tables from the catalog JSON (`item.data`). Both run `internal/ecalc/testdata/vectors/codes.json`.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.27 (`gopkg.in/yaml.v3`), vanilla JavaScript classic script, Node for `scripts/test-ecalc-codes.mjs`.

**Spec and contract:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-01-ecalc-design.md` ("Component codes", "Code page", "Content correctness"); the phase 3 contract sections 1.2, 6 and 9; research `P3\research\codes\` (SUMMARY.md and one file per kind). Base commit of this part: `4b3b14ec0` with Part A applied.

**How this part was made and verified:** every file below was built and tested in a scratch worktree (base `4b3b14ec0` + Part A, uncommitted); the code blocks are the exact text of those files. The five YAML files were written by a program from the research tables (so no value was typed by hand) and the expected values of the vectors were written by hand from the standards and data sheets named in each `ref`, never from the engine. Two tasks, K1 (Go: data, engine, vectors) and K2 (JavaScript mirror and parity script). Both tasks were replayed on a copy of the worktree without the K files, with the blocks of this document extracted mechanically: the red runs failed as recorded in the verification section, the green runs passed, the regenerated snapshot and every file equal the drafting worktree byte for byte (line endings aside). Beyond the vectors, a differential run fed 58,336 decode and encode requests (all three- and four-digit SMD codes, all 3-character ceramic codes, 4,000 random band lists per colour kind, a grid of values, tolerances and band counts for every kind) through both languages: every result (code, bands, value, dimension, fields, warnings) and every error code was identical; only the wording of some error messages differs (the parse errors of the units parser of Part A, and the list of kinds in the error for an unknown kind, which in the Go test binary also names the test kind).

### Contract deviations (where this list and the contract disagree, this list wins)

1. **Files.** The contract names `codes.go` (+ `codes_test.go`). The engine is split by family: `codes.go` (result types, errors, `Decode`/`Encode`, the number, tolerance and nearest-standard-value helpers, the `init` that registers the five kinds), `codes_bands.go` (resistor and inductor colour bands), `codes_smd.go`, `codes_capacitor.go`, `codes_ceramic.go`; one test file `codes_test.go`. Item ids (stable): `resistor_color_code`, `inductor_color_code`, `smd_resistor_code`, `capacitor_code`, `ceramic_temp_code`; the kind ids that `decode`/`encode` take as `kind` (the registered code kinds, `CodeKindIDs()`): `resistor_bands`, `inductor_bands`, `smd_resistor`, `capacitor`, `ceramic_temp`. `Decode`/`Encode` use the first code item of a kind.
2. **Three error codes, not two.** Contract: `invalid_code:` and `unsupported:`. A bad field of an encode request is not an invalid code, so there is a third: `invalid_value:` (an unreadable or contradicting request field, for example `tolerance: cannot read "abc" as a percentage`, a band count that does not fit). Meaning of the three: `invalid_code` the text to decode is malformed; `invalid_value` a field of an encode request cannot be read or the fields contradict each other; `unsupported` the input is well formed but is not decodable (a letter that is not cross-checked or is ambiguous between makers, an unknown kind) or not codable (outside the range of the scheme, no colour or letter exists for it). Go: `*CodeError{Code, Message}` whose `Error()` is `code + ": " + message`, `AsCodeError(err)`, the constants `CodeInvalidCode`, `CodeInvalidValue`, `CodeUnsupported`. JavaScript throws an `Error` with `code` and a `message` **without** the prefix. The vectors check the code and a fragment of the message.
3. **`EncodeRequest` is generic; the fields mean this per kind** (every field a kind does not use is ignored; texts are quantities as typed in a field, a bare number is in the base unit named here):
   - `resistor_bands`: `Value` ohm, `Bands` 0 (choose) | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6, `Tolerance` percent (`5%`, `0.25`), `TempCo` ppm/K (`50ppm`; implies 6 bands).
   - `inductor_bands`: `Value` henry (`6.8u`), `Bands` 0 or 4 (EIA) | 5 (military), `Tolerance` 5 or 10 percent.
   - `smd_resistor`: `Value` ohm, `Tolerance` percent (chooses the family and the series). The result lists every marking that can express the value.
   - `capacitor`: `Value` farad (`100n`), `Tolerance` as a letter (`K`), a percentage (`10%`), a value in pF (`0.25pF`) or an asymmetric tolerance (`-20/+80`), `Voltage` volts (`50V`); at least one of the three.
   - `ceramic_temp`: `Class` `"1"` | `"2"` (inferred when empty). Class 1: `TempCo` (or `Value`) is the temperature coefficient in ppm/K (`-750ppm`), `Tolerance` its tolerance in ppm/K (`120ppm`). Class 2: `Value` is the category range in degrees Celsius (`-55..125`, `-55 to 85`, `-55 … +125 °C`), `Tolerance` the capacitance change (`15%`, `+22/-82`).
4. **Encode picks the standard value as the contract says, with three clarifications.** (a) For tolerances below 5 % the standard values are the implied series **and E24**: 47 kΩ ±1 % is the example of the TT note and of IEC 60062 clause 3.3.2, but 4.7 is no E96 value. (b) A request without a tolerance gets one from the value (5 % for an E24 value, 1 % for E96, 0.5 % for E192, otherwise 5 % and then the nearest E24 value) and says so in the warning `no tolerance given; ±5 % assumed`; a capacitor request without a tolerance letter is not snapped at all (it must fit two digits). (c) A resistor request with `Bands` 3 and no tolerance means ±20 %; `Bands` 3 with another tolerance, `Bands` 6 without `TempCo`, `TempCo` with 4 or 5 bands and ±20 % with 4 to 6 bands are errors, never a silently different code. The warning for a changed value reads `4.99 kΩ is not a standard value for ±5 % (E24); encoded the nearest, 5.1 kΩ (+2.2 %)`.
5. **Resistor colours follow IEC 60062:2016 (+COR1:2016, +AMD1:2019), as decided.** Grey ±0.01 %, orange ±0.05 %, yellow ±0.02 %, pink ×10⁻³. Decoding such a tolerance band adds the warning with the older maker reading (`grey tolerance band: ±0.01 % in IEC 60062:2016; older charts and some makers read ±0.05 %`; orange and yellow: `older charts give orange no tolerance`), encoding does the same; there is no extra field. Two more warnings: a single black band is a zero-ohm jumper, and a decoded value that is neither an E24 nor an E192 value says `check the reading direction`. The input also accepts the IEC 60757 letter codes (`BU-GY-RD`), `gray`, and the separators blank, comma, semicolon, underscore, hyphen, en dash and em dash.
6. **EIA-96 letters.** Decoded: `Y X A B C D E F` (four makers agree). `S` and `H` give `unsupported: the EIA-96 letter S is ambiguous between makers`, as decided. **Decision for the controller:** `R` after two digits (`10R`) is a valid RKM code and by far the most common reading (10 Ω), so it is decoded as RKM with the warning `R after two digits is read as the RKM decimal point (10R = 10 Ω); some makers use R as an EIA-96 multiplier letter, which is not decoded`; R is never decoded as an EIA-96 letter. `Z` (×0.001, two sources, rare) is decoded with a warning; `G` (Venkel only) is not an EIA-96 letter, so `10G` reads as RKM giga.
7. **UNVERIFIED and single-source cells are not in the data** (controller decision), and the decoder answers `unsupported: ... is not cross-checked (found in one source only)`. The data holds only their symbols, in `not_cross_checked` lists (no value): capacitor tolerance letters `E H N P S Y` and multiplier digit `7`; ceramic class 1 letters `B L A V` and multiplier digits `4 9`, class 2 upper-temperature digits `2 9` and change letters `A B C D E F L`; inductor MIL tolerance colours brown, red, orange and every EIA tolerance other than gold and silver (decoded as `unsupported`, no list needed); resistor tolerance letters W, P, L are not decoded at all (the resistor code is band-only); the nine single-source voltage codes `0L 1D 2Q 2B 2Z 2P 2F 2L 2X` are not in the table (`1D` answers `unsupported: the voltage code 1D is not a standard code ...`), and Murata's `YA` answers `unsupported: ... maker-specific voltage code`. What stays in is listed in the research files (22 voltage codes, 13 tolerance rows, 7 class-1 significant letters).
8. **Capacitor scope.** The value code is the picofarad code (3 digits `104`, R notation `4R7`/`R50`, RKM `4p7`/`2n2`/`4µ7`/`100n`). The microfarad reading of aluminium electrolytic part numbers (`101` = 100 µF) is not offered: it cannot be told from the pF code by its shape and the decode call has no family argument; the item note says so. The third digits 8 and 9 (×0.01, ×0.1) are the KEMET ordering convention and decode with a warning. A trailing `F` behind an RKM prefix letter (`100nF`) is the unit farad, not the tolerance letter F. A marking may have up to three parts in any order (`104K 1H`, `104 K 1H`). Tolerance letters follow the capacitance: `W B C D` mean pF below 10 pF, `D F G J K M Q T Z` percent as the maker tables list them; a letter that the sources list only for the other capacitance range answers `unsupported ... not cross-checked for a capacitance below 10 pF`. The voltage codes are a maker convention, not IEC 60062: every decoded voltage code adds that warning (and the 3F note of Murata and TDK).
9. **Values and dimensions of a result.** `Value` is SI: ohm (`resistance`), henry (`inductance`), farad (`capacitance`); a lone voltage code gives volts (`voltage`); the ceramic class 1 code gives the temperature coefficient in 1/K (`tempco`, C0G = 0); class 2 and a lone tolerance letter give NaN/`null` and an empty `dim`. Field values: tolerances as fractions (`ratio`, 5 % = 0.05; pF tolerances in farad), temperature coefficients in 1/K (`tempco`), category temperatures in kelvin (`temperature`). An asymmetric tolerance has `value` null in the field `tolerance` (text `−20 % / +80 %`) and the two deviations as extra fields `*_minus`/`*_plus`.
10. **Colour names and colours.** Names in 16 locales come from the research file (own translations); **the Hindi names (`काला`, `स्लेटी` for grey, `रुपहला` for silver ...) need a review by a native speaker.** The hex colours are the research file's display choice (IEC 60062 says its example colours are not normative); `none` has `transparent`.
11. **Catalog JSON `data`** is the YAML data with the names and notes resolved for the language, plus `note_en` on the voltage codes (the warnings are English in every language). The shapes are listed in "What the other parts get".
12. **Snapshot:** `internal/ecalc/testdata/catalog.en.json` grows from 81 to 86 items (+1354 lines, all additions after the tables).
13. **No existing function is modified** (new files, one `package.json` script, the regenerated snapshot), so no GitNexus impact analysis applies; `detect-changes` runs before each commit. Every unexported package-level identifier of the Go files of this part (functions, types, variables, constants and the test helpers) carries the prefix `code` (`codeDecimal`, `codeCompact`, `codeCloseTo`, `codeListed`, `codeBandColor`, `codeCapacitorData`, `codeSMD3Digit`, ...), so nothing can clash with the files of the other parts in package `ecalc`; the tests are named `TestCodes...`. `ecalc-codes.js` keeps everything inside one function scope and exports only `ECalcCore.codes`.
14. **`ui` pin.** `go test ./ui -run TestECalc` fails in this worktree with `js/desktop/apps/ecalc holds 23 scripts, want the 21 of the plan` (`ecalc-tables.js` of Part A and `ecalc-codes.js`); with that pin raised to 23 in a throwaway edit all ECalc UI tests pass, so the new script satisfies the source scans (no `eval`, no `Function`, no translation keys). Part UT owns the pin; the controller adds `ecalc-codes.js` to the `ecalc` entry of `module-loader.js` anywhere after `ecalc-eseries.js` (it needs `ecalc-units.js` and `ecalc-eseries.js` at call time, which in turn need `ecalc-expr.js`), best right after `ecalc-solve.js`/`ecalc-tables.js`.

### Environment and edit conventions

- Windows box. Set `GOTMPDIR` to a short backslash path and create it once (`$env:GOTMPDIR = 'C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p3-k'`). Run every command from the repository root.
- `internal/ecalc/**` and the YAML/JSON files are LF in a Windows working copy; `ui/js/**` and `scripts/*.mjs` are CRLF (git stores LF): create those files with LF or convert them to CRLF after writing, and do not mix line endings in one file.
- Every "Replace ... with ..." block is the exact text of an edit: the replaced text occurs exactly once in the file at that point of the task and is replaced line for line.
- Use the micro sign U+00B5 and the Greek capital omega U+03A9 in YAML, Go, JavaScript and JSON (never U+03BC or U+2126 for units; the Greek locale names contain the Greek letter mu as part of a word); tools that decode backslash-u escapes (Write/Edit) must be given the characters themselves.
- Commit messages end with the trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Run `detect-changes` before each commit (CLAUDE.md); it must not be `partial` or `truncated`.

### Task K1: The five code items and the engine in Go

**Goal:** `Default()` loads five code items whose `data` holds the tables of IEC 60062 (resistor colours), the military and EIA inductor colours, the EIA-96 table and letters, the capacitor multipliers, RKM prefixes, tolerance letters and voltage codes, and the EIA-198 class tables; `(*Catalog).Decode(kind, code)` and `(*Catalog).Encode(kind, EncodeRequest)` read and write the markings of the five kinds; the shared vectors `testdata/vectors/codes.json` (128 decode, 64 encode and 125 error cases, each with a `ref`) pass.

**Files:**

- Create: `internal/ecalc/codes_test.go`, `internal/ecalc/testdata/vectors/codes.json`
- Create: `internal/ecalc/catalog/codes/resistor_bands.yaml`, `inductor_bands.yaml`, `smd_resistor.yaml`, `capacitor.yaml`, `ceramic_temp.yaml`
- Create: `internal/ecalc/codes.go`, `internal/ecalc/codes_bands.go`, `internal/ecalc/codes_smd.go`, `internal/ecalc/codes_capacitor.go`, `internal/ecalc/codes_ceramic.go`
- Modify (regenerated): `internal/ecalc/testdata/catalog.en.json`

**Behaviour fixed by this task** (all of it is covered by the tests and vectors below; the exact error texts and field ids are in the code):

- *Resistor bands.* Input: 1 to 6 colour names (English ids, IEC 60757 letters, `gray`), case-insensitive, separated by blanks, commas, semicolons, underscores, hyphens or dashes. 3 bands = two digits and a multiplier (±20 %), 4 = + tolerance, 5 = three digits, multiplier, tolerance, 6 = + temperature coefficient; one black band is 0 Ω. Gold, silver and pink never stand first (the message suggests reading from the other end). Result fields: `tolerance`, `tcr`. Encode: `Bands` 0 picks 3 (±20 %), 4 (value fits two digits), 5, or 6 (with `TempCo`).
- *Inductor bands.* 4 bands (EIA: digit, digit, multiplier incl. gold ×0.1 and silver ×0.01, tolerance gold ±5 % or silver ±10 %) or 5 bands (MIL-PRF-15305: wide silver first, then three value bands where gold in band 2 or 3 is the decimal point, or two digits and a multiplier black to orange, then the tolerance). Value in henry. Result fields: `layout`, `tolerance`.
- *SMD resistor.* Normalised (blanks, `_`, `|` removed, upper case); the family is detected: zero (`0`, `00`, `000`, `0000`, `0R0`), EIA-96 (two digits 01..96 and `Z Y X A B C D E F`), RKM / R notation (`4R7`, `R47`, `1L5`, `4K7`, `47K`; at most four digits), 3 digits (two digits + exponent), 4 digits (three digits + exponent). Encode lists `code_3digit`, `code_4digit`, `code_eia96` (those that exist) and puts the 3-digit code first for tolerances of 2 % and more, the 4-digit code first for 1 % and finer.
- *Capacitor.* Parts recognised by their shape: `104`, `R50`, `4p7`, `2n2`, `4µ7`, `100n` (value), `K` (tolerance letter, behind a value or alone), `1H` (voltage code). Encode writes `104K 1H`, with `value_code`, `rkm`, the tolerance fields and `voltage`.
- *Ceramic temperature.* 3 characters; `X Y Z` first means class 2 (lower temperature letter, upper temperature digit, change letter), everything else class 1 (significant-figure letter, multiplier digit, tolerance letter, TC = figure × multiplier ppm/K); aliases `NP0`, `NPO`, `N750`, `N1500`, `COG`. Encode builds the code and decodes it, so encode and decode cannot disagree.
- *Load* validates every table (unique symbols, ranges, 16 locales for the colour names, English and German notes, hex colours, the EIA-96 table against the E96 values of IEC 60063, at least two makers for a voltage code, symmetric pF tolerances) and reports every problem with the item id.

- [ ] **Step 1: write the failing tests and the shared vectors**


**Create `internal/ecalc/codes_test.go`** with exactly this content:

```go
package ecalc

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"math"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// The vectors of testdata/vectors/codes.json are shared with scripts/test-ecalc-codes.mjs. A decode vector gives the code
// and the whole result that is wanted, an encode vector the request and the result, an error vector the operation, the
// input and the error code with a fragment of its message. Every vector names its source in ref. The expected values were
// written by hand from the standards and data sheets, never taken from the engine.
type codeWant struct {
	Code     string   `json:"code"`
	Bands    []string `json:"bands"`
	Value    *float64 `json:"value"`
	Dim      string   `json:"dim"`
	Fields   [][]any  `json:"fields"` // [id, name, text, value or null, dim]
	Warnings []string `json:"warnings"`
}

type codeVectors struct {
	Decode []struct {
		Kind string   `json:"kind"`
		Code string   `json:"code"`
		Want codeWant `json:"want"`
		Ref  string   `json:"ref"`
	} `json:"decode"`
	Encode []struct {
		Kind string        `json:"kind"`
		Req  EncodeRequest `json:"req"`
		Want codeWant      `json:"want"`
		Ref  string        `json:"ref"`
	} `json:"encode"`
	Errors []struct {
		Op       string        `json:"op"`
		Kind     string        `json:"kind"`
		Code     string        `json:"code"`
		Req      EncodeRequest `json:"req"`
		Error    string        `json:"error"`
		Contains string        `json:"contains"`
		Ref      string        `json:"ref"`
	} `json:"errors"`
}

const codeVectorFile = "testdata/vectors/codes.json"

func codeTestCatalog(t *testing.T) *Catalog {
	t.Helper()
	cat, err := Default()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Default: %v", err)
	}
	return cat
}

// codeCheckResult compares a result with a vector; it returns a description of the first difference or "".
func codeCheckResult(got CodeResult, want codeWant, kind string) string {
	switch {
	case got.Kind != kind:
		return fmt.Sprintf("kind = %q, want %q", got.Kind, kind)
	case got.Code != want.Code:
		return fmt.Sprintf("code = %q, want %q", got.Code, want.Code)
	case !reflect.DeepEqual(orEmpty(got.Bands), orEmpty(want.Bands)):
		return fmt.Sprintf("bands = %v, want %v", got.Bands, want.Bands)
	case got.Dim != want.Dim:
		return fmt.Sprintf("dim = %q, want %q", got.Dim, want.Dim)
	case !reflect.DeepEqual(orEmpty(got.Warnings), orEmpty(want.Warnings)):
		return fmt.Sprintf("warnings = %q, want %q", got.Warnings, want.Warnings)
	case len(got.Fields) != len(want.Fields):
		return fmt.Sprintf("%d fields %v, want %d", len(got.Fields), got.Fields, len(want.Fields))
	}
	wantValue := math.NaN()
	if want.Value != nil {
		wantValue = *want.Value
	}
	if !near(got.Value, wantValue, 1e-12) {
		return fmt.Sprintf("value = %v, want %v", got.Value, wantValue)
	}
	for i, f := range got.Fields {
		w := want.Fields[i]
		if len(w) != 5 {
			return fmt.Sprintf("field %d of the vector has %d entries, want 5", i, len(w))
		}
		fv := math.NaN()
		if w[3] != nil {
			fv = w[3].(float64)
		}
		if f.ID != w[0] || f.Name != w[1] || f.Text != w[2] || f.Dim != w[4] || !near(f.Value, fv, 1e-12) {
			return fmt.Sprintf("field %d = %+v, want %v", i, f, w)
		}
	}
	return ""
}

func TestCodesVectors(t *testing.T) {
	cat := codeTestCatalog(t)
	var v codeVectors
	readJSON(t, codeVectorFile, &v)
	perKind := map[string]int{}
	for _, c := range v.Decode {
		if c.Ref == "" {
			t.Errorf("decode %s %q has no ref", c.Kind, c.Code)
		}
		perKind["decode "+c.Kind]++
		got, err := cat.Decode(c.Kind, c.Code)
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("decode %s %q: %v", c.Kind, c.Code, err)
			continue
		}
		if diff := codeCheckResult(got, c.Want, c.Kind); diff != "" {
			t.Errorf("decode %s %q: %s", c.Kind, c.Code, diff)
		}
	}
	for _, c := range v.Encode {
		if c.Ref == "" {
			t.Errorf("encode %s %+v has no ref", c.Kind, c.Req)
		}
		perKind["encode "+c.Kind]++
		got, err := cat.Encode(c.Kind, c.Req)
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("encode %s %+v: %v", c.Kind, c.Req, err)
			continue
		}
		if diff := codeCheckResult(got, c.Want, c.Kind); diff != "" {
			t.Errorf("encode %s %+v: %s", c.Kind, c.Req, diff)
		}
	}
	for _, c := range v.Errors {
		if c.Ref == "" {
			t.Errorf("error vector %s %s has no ref", c.Op, c.Kind)
		}
		perKind["error "+c.Kind]++
		var err error
		if c.Op == "decode" {
			_, err = cat.Decode(c.Kind, c.Code)
		} else {
			_, err = cat.Encode(c.Kind, c.Req)
		}
		ce := AsCodeError(err)
		switch {
		case err == nil:
			t.Errorf("%s %s %q %+v: no error, want %s", c.Op, c.Kind, c.Code, c.Req, c.Error)
		case ce == nil:
			t.Errorf("%s %s %q %+v: error %v is no CodeError", c.Op, c.Kind, c.Code, c.Req, err)
		case ce.Code != c.Error || !strings.Contains(ce.Message, c.Contains) || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), c.Error+": "):
			t.Errorf("%s %s %q %+v: error %q, want %s containing %q", c.Op, c.Kind, c.Code, c.Req, err, c.Error, c.Contains)
		}
	}
	for _, kind := range []string{"resistor_bands", "inductor_bands", "smd_resistor", "capacitor", "ceramic_temp"} {
		for _, what := range []string{"decode", "encode", "error"} {
			if n := perKind[what+" "+kind]; n < 8 {
				t.Errorf("%s %s has %d vectors, want at least 8", what, kind, n)
			}
		}
	}
}

func TestCodesKindsAndItemsInTheDefaultCatalog(t *testing.T) {
	cat := codeTestCatalog(t)
	want := map[string]string{
		"resistor_color_code": "resistor_bands", "inductor_color_code": "inductor_bands", "smd_resistor_code": "smd_resistor",
		"capacitor_code": "capacitor", "ceramic_temp_code": "ceramic_temp",
	}
	for id, kind := range want {
		c := cat.Code(id)
		if c == nil || c.CodeKind != kind || c.Category != "codes" {
			t.Errorf("code item %s = %+v, want kind %s in the category codes", id, c, kind)
			continue
		}
		if k, ok := cat.Item(id); !ok || k != "code" {
			t.Errorf("Item(%s) = %q, %v", id, k, ok)
		}
		if !contains(CodeKindIDs(), kind) {
			t.Errorf("CodeKindIDs() lacks %s", kind)
		}
		for _, l := range Locales {
			if strings.TrimSpace(c.Name[l]) == "" {
				t.Errorf("%s: no name in %s", id, l)
			}
		}
		if c.Doc["en"] == "" || c.Doc["de"] == "" || c.Source == "" || len(c.Tags) == 0 {
			t.Errorf("%s: doc, source and tags are required", id)
		}
	}
	if len(cat.Codes) != len(want) {
		t.Errorf("the catalog has %d code items, want %d", len(cat.Codes), len(want))
	}
	// A kind that has no code item in the catalog (a registered kind of a test, or a typo) is unsupported and names the real ones.
	for _, kind := range []string{"nope", "test_words", ""} {
		_, err := cat.Decode(kind, "x")
		if ce := AsCodeError(err); ce == nil || ce.Code != CodeUnsupported || !strings.Contains(ce.Message, "kinds: ") || !strings.Contains(ce.Message, "resistor_bands") {
			t.Errorf("Decode of the kind %q: %v", kind, err)
		}
	}
}

// The JSON of a code item is what the JavaScript twin reads: the tables of the kind, with the names and notes in the
// language of the request.
func TestCodesItemJSONCarriesTheTables(t *testing.T) {
	cat := codeTestCatalog(t)
	body, _, err := cat.LocalizedJSON("de")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var doc struct {
		Items []map[string]any `json:"items"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &doc); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	data := map[string]map[string]any{}
	for _, it := range doc.Items {
		if it["kind"] == "code" {
			data[it["code"].(string)] = it["data"].(map[string]any)
		}
	}
	keys := map[string][]string{
		"resistor_bands": {"colors", "layouts", "notes"},
		"inductor_bands": {"colors", "notes"},
		"smd_resistor":   {"eia96", "letters", "rkm", "ambiguous", "notes"},
		"capacitor":      {"multipliers", "rkm", "tolerances", "voltages", "not_cross_checked", "notes"},
		"ceramic_temp":   {"class1", "class2", "aliases", "industry", "not_cross_checked", "common", "notes"},
	}
	for kind, want := range keys {
		d := data[kind]
		if len(d) != len(want) {
			t.Errorf("%s: data has %d keys, want %d: %v", kind, len(d), len(want), d)
		}
		for _, k := range want {
			if _, ok := d[k]; !ok {
				t.Errorf("%s: data lacks %s", kind, k)
			}
		}
	}
	colors := data["resistor_bands"]["colors"].([]any)
	if len(colors) != 14 {
		t.Fatalf("resistor colours = %d, want 14", len(colors))
	}
	first := colors[0].(map[string]any)
	if first["id"] != "black" || first["name"] != "schwarz" || first["hex"] != "#000000" || first["digit"] != 0.0 || first["exp"] != 0.0 || first["tcr"] != 250.0 || first["tol"] != nil {
		t.Errorf("first resistor colour = %v", first)
	}
	if notes := data["resistor_bands"]["notes"].([]any); len(notes) < 5 || !strings.Contains(notes[0].(string), "Lesen") {
		t.Errorf("resistor notes are not German: %v", notes)
	}
	voltages := data["capacitor"]["voltages"].([]any)
	if len(voltages) != 22 {
		t.Errorf("voltage codes = %d, want 22", len(voltages))
	}
	last := voltages[len(voltages)-1].(map[string]any)
	if last["code"] != "3F" || !strings.Contains(last["note"].(string), "Murata führt") || !strings.Contains(last["note_en"].(string), "Murata lists") {
		t.Errorf("3F = %v", last)
	}
	if d := data["smd_resistor"]["eia96"].([]any); len(d) != 96 || d[0] != 100.0 || d[95] != 976.0 {
		t.Errorf("eia96 = %v", d)
	}
}

func TestCodesResultJSON(t *testing.T) {
	res := codeNewResult("capacitor")
	res.field("tolerance", "Tolerance", "±20 % / +80 %", math.NaN(), "ratio")
	body, err := json.Marshal(res)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	const want = `{"kind":"capacitor","code":"","bands":[],"value":null,"dim":"","fields":[{"id":"tolerance","name":"Tolerance","text":"±20 % / +80 %","value":null,"dim":"ratio"}],"warnings":[]}`
	if string(body) != want {
		t.Errorf("JSON = %s\nwant   %s", body, want)
	}
	var zero CodeResult
	if body, _ := json.Marshal(zero); !strings.Contains(string(body), `"bands":[]`) || !strings.Contains(string(body), `"fields":[]`) || !strings.Contains(string(body), `"warnings":[]`) {
		t.Errorf("the zero result writes null lists: %s", body)
	}
}

func TestCodesErrorsCarryTheirCode(t *testing.T) {
	cat := codeTestCatalog(t)
	_, err := cat.Decode("resistor_bands", "gold")
	ce := AsCodeError(err)
	if ce == nil || ce.Code != CodeInvalidCode || err.Error() != CodeInvalidCode+": "+ce.Message {
		t.Errorf("error = %#v", err)
	}
	if AsCodeError(nil) != nil || AsCodeError(fmt.Errorf("x")) != nil {
		t.Error("AsCodeError must return nil for other errors")
	}
	if _, err := cat.Decode("resistor_bands", strings.Repeat("x", 65)); AsCodeError(err) == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "longer than 64") {
		t.Errorf("a long code: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := cat.Encode("capacitor", EncodeRequest{Value: strings.Repeat("1", 65)}); AsCodeError(err) == nil || AsCodeError(err).Code != CodeInvalidValue {
		t.Errorf("a long request field: %v", err)
	}
}

// The IEC 60062 colour table, pinned independently of the vectors: tolerance and temperature coefficient per colour.
func TestCodesResistorColourTableIsIEC60062(t *testing.T) {
	cat := codeTestCatalog(t)
	d := cat.Code("resistor_color_code").Data.(*codeResistorData)
	type row struct {
		digit, exp int
		tol, tcr   float64
	}
	// colour: digit, exponent of the multiplier (-1 = no digit/multiplier), tolerance %, TCR ppm/K (0 = none)
	want := map[string]row{
		"black": {0, 0, 0, 250}, "brown": {1, 1, 1, 100}, "red": {2, 2, 2, 50}, "orange": {3, 3, 0.05, 15}, "yellow": {4, 4, 0.02, 25},
		"green": {5, 5, 0.5, 20}, "blue": {6, 6, 0.25, 10}, "violet": {7, 7, 0.1, 5}, "grey": {8, 8, 0.01, 1}, "white": {9, 9, 0, 0},
	}
	for id, w := range want {
		c := d.byID[id]
		if c == nil || c.Digit == nil || *c.Digit != w.digit || c.Exp == nil || *c.Exp != w.exp {
			t.Errorf("%s: digit/exp = %+v", id, c)
			continue
		}
		if (w.tol == 0) != (c.Tol == nil) || (c.Tol != nil && *c.Tol != w.tol) || (w.tcr == 0) != (c.TCR == nil) || (c.TCR != nil && *c.TCR != w.tcr) {
			t.Errorf("%s: tol/tcr = %v/%v, want %v/%v", id, c.Tol, c.TCR, w.tol, w.tcr)
		}
	}
	for id, w := range map[string]struct {
		exp int
		tol float64
	}{"gold": {-1, 5}, "silver": {-2, 10}, "pink": {-3, 0}, "none": {0, 20}} {
		c := d.byID[id]
		if c == nil || c.Digit != nil || c.TCR != nil || (w.tol == 0) != (c.Tol == nil) || (c.Tol != nil && *c.Tol != w.tol) || (id != "none" && (c.Exp == nil || *c.Exp != w.exp)) {
			t.Errorf("%s: %+v", id, c)
		}
	}
	// the older chart readings of the three colours IEC 60062:2016 assigned later
	if g := d.byID["grey"]; g.LegacyTol == nil || *g.LegacyTol != 0.05 || !d.byID["orange"].LegacyNone || !d.byID["yellow"].LegacyNone || d.byID["red"].LegacyNone || d.byID["red"].LegacyTol != nil {
		t.Error("the older tolerance readings of grey, orange and yellow are wrong")
	}
	for _, id := range []string{"black", "brown", "red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "violet", "grey", "white", "gold", "silver", "pink", "none"} {
		if d.byID[id] == nil {
			t.Errorf("colour %s is missing", id)
		}
	}
}

// Every EIA-96 code decodes to the E96 value of IEC 60063 times the multiplier of its letter.
func TestCodesSMDEveryEIA96Code(t *testing.T) {
	cat := codeTestCatalog(t)
	letters := map[string]int{"Y": -2, "X": -1, "A": 0, "B": 1, "C": 2, "D": 3, "E": 4, "F": 5}
	for i := 0; i < 96; i++ {
		for letter, exp := range letters {
			code := fmt.Sprintf("%02d%s", i+1, letter)
			res, err := cat.Decode("smd_resistor", code)
			if err != nil {
				t.Errorf("%s: %v", code, err)
				continue
			}
			want := codeDecimal(int(math.Round(e96[i]*100)), exp)
			if !near(res.Value, want, 1e-12) {
				t.Errorf("%s = %v, want %v", code, res.Value, want)
			}
		}
	}
}

// What Encode writes, Decode reads back to the same value (and the same bands).
func TestCodesEncodeThenDecodeAgrees(t *testing.T) {
	cat := codeTestCatalog(t)
	tolerances := []struct {
		text   string
		series string
	}{{"20%", "E6"}, {"10%", "E12"}, {"5%", "E24"}, {"2%", "E48"}, {"1%", "E96"}, {"0.5%", "E192"}, {"0.25%", "E192"}, {"0.1%", "E192"}, {"0.05%", "E192"}, {"0.02%", "E192"}, {"0.01%", "E192"}}
	checked := 0
	for _, tol := range tolerances {
		mant, _ := ESeriesValues(tol.series)
		for _, decade := range []float64{1, 1e3, 1e5, 1e-1} {
			for i := 0; i < len(mant); i += 7 {
				v := roundSig(mant[i]*decade, 6)
				req := EncodeRequest{Value: fmt.Sprintf("%g", v), Tolerance: tol.text}
				enc, err := cat.Encode("resistor_bands", req)
				if err != nil {
					t.Errorf("encode %+v: %v", req, err)
					continue
				}
				dec, err := cat.Decode("resistor_bands", enc.Code)
				if err != nil || !near(dec.Value, v, 1e-12) || !reflect.DeepEqual(dec.Bands, enc.Bands) || !near(dec.Value, enc.Value, 1e-12) {
					t.Errorf("%+v -> %q -> %+v, %v", req, enc.Code, dec, err)
				}
				checked++
			}
		}
	}
	for _, kind := range []string{"smd_resistor", "capacitor", "inductor_bands"} {
		dim := map[string]string{"smd_resistor": "", "capacitor": "p", "inductor_bands": "u"}[kind]
		mant, _ := ESeriesValues("E12")
		for _, decade := range []float64{1, 10, 100, 1000, 1e4, 1e5} {
			for _, m := range mant {
				req := EncodeRequest{Value: fmt.Sprintf("%g%s", roundSig(m*decade, 6), dim), Tolerance: "10%"}
				enc, err := cat.Encode(kind, req)
				if err != nil {
					continue // out of the range of the kind
				}
				if kind == "capacitor" {
					enc.Code = strings.Fields(enc.Code)[0]
					enc.Code = strings.TrimRight(enc.Code, "K")
				}
				dec, err := cat.Decode(kind, enc.Code)
				if err != nil || !near(dec.Value, enc.Value, 1e-12) {
					t.Errorf("%s %+v -> %q -> %+v, %v", kind, req, enc.Code, dec, err)
				}
				if kind == "smd_resistor" {
					for _, f := range enc.Fields {
						if strings.HasPrefix(f.ID, "code_") {
							other, err := cat.Decode(kind, f.Text)
							if err != nil || !near(other.Value, enc.Value, 1e-12) {
								t.Errorf("%s %s %q decodes to %+v, %v, want %v", kind, f.ID, f.Text, other, err, enc.Value)
							}
						}
					}
				}
				checked++
			}
		}
	}
	// the military inductor style
	for _, v := range []string{"0.1u", "0.47u", "1u", "6.8u", "10u", "82u", "100u", "1000u", "10m", "82m"} {
		enc, err := cat.Encode("inductor_bands", EncodeRequest{Value: v, Tolerance: "10%", Bands: 5})
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("MIL %s: %v", v, err)
			continue
		}
		dec, err := cat.Decode("inductor_bands", enc.Code)
		if err != nil || !near(dec.Value, enc.Value, 1e-12) || len(dec.Bands) != 5 {
			t.Errorf("MIL %s -> %q -> %+v, %v", v, enc.Code, dec, err)
		}
		checked++
	}
	// every ceramic code of the tables
	d := cat.Code("ceramic_temp_code").Data.(*codeCeramicData)
	for _, lo := range d.Class2.Low {
		for _, hi := range d.Class2.High {
			for _, ch := range d.Class2.Change {
				code := lo.Letter + hi.Digit + ch.Letter
				tolText := fmt.Sprintf("%g%%", ch.Plus)
				if ch.Plus != ch.Minus {
					tolText = fmt.Sprintf("+%g/-%g", ch.Plus, ch.Minus)
				}
				enc, err := cat.Encode("ceramic_temp", EncodeRequest{Class: "2", Value: fmt.Sprintf("%g..%g", lo.C, hi.C), Tolerance: tolText})
				if err != nil || enc.Code != code {
					t.Errorf("class 2 %s: %q, %v", code, enc.Code, err)
				}
				checked++
			}
		}
	}
	for _, s := range d.Class1.Sig {
		for _, m := range d.Class1.Mult {
			for _, tl := range d.Class1.Tol {
				code := s.Letter + m.Digit + tl.Letter
				dec, err := cat.Decode("ceramic_temp", code)
				if err != nil {
					t.Errorf("class 1 %s: %v", code, err)
					continue
				}
				enc, err := cat.Encode("ceramic_temp", EncodeRequest{Class: "1", TempCo: fmt.Sprintf("%gppm", dec.Value/1e-6), Tolerance: fmt.Sprintf("%gppm", tl.PPM)})
				if err != nil || enc.Code[2:] != code[2:] || !near(enc.Value, dec.Value, 1e-9) {
					t.Errorf("class 1 %s: %q, %v", code, enc.Code, err)
				}
				checked++
			}
		}
	}
	if checked < 700 {
		t.Errorf("only %d round trips ran", checked)
	}
}

// Decode never panics and rejects what is no code: single characters, odd separators and long runs of every kind.
func TestCodesDecodeSurvivesGarbage(t *testing.T) {
	cat := codeTestCatalog(t)
	inputs := []string{"", " ", "-", ",", "µ", "0", "00", "R", "L", "p", "100000", "ÄÖÜ", "☃", "1 2 3 4", "red,", ",red", "--red", "X7R7", "\t\n", "1H1H", "٣٣٣"}
	for _, ch := range "0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz.|_" {
		inputs = append(inputs, string(ch), string(ch)+string(ch), "1"+string(ch), string(ch)+"1", "10"+string(ch), "1"+string(ch)+"1")
	}
	for _, kind := range []string{"resistor_bands", "inductor_bands", "smd_resistor", "capacitor", "ceramic_temp"} {
		for _, in := range inputs {
			res, err := cat.Decode(kind, in)
			if err != nil && AsCodeError(err) == nil {
				t.Errorf("%s %q: error %v is no CodeError", kind, in, err)
			}
			if err == nil && res.Code == "" {
				t.Errorf("%s %q: a result without a code", kind, in)
			}
		}
	}
}

// Load checks the data of a code item.
func TestCodesLoadRejectsBrokenData(t *testing.T) {
	read := func(name string) string {
		data, err := catalogFS.ReadFile("catalog/codes/" + name + ".yaml")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return string(data)
	}
	cases := []struct{ file, old, new, want string }{
		{"resistor_bands", `zh: "黑色"`, `zh: ""`, `colour black name: missing "zh" text`},
		{"resistor_bands", `digit: 1, exp: 1`, `digit: 0, exp: 1`, "digit must be 0 to 9 and used once"},
		{"resistor_bands", `"#8B4513"`, `"brown"`, "hex must be #rrggbb or transparent"},
		{"resistor_bands", `roles: ["digit", "digit", "multiplier"]`, `roles: ["digit", "nope", "multiplier"]`, `unknown role "nope"`},
		{"resistor_bands", `roles: ["digit", "digit", "multiplier"]`, `roles: ["digit", "digit", "digit"]`, "exactly one multiplier band"},
		{"resistor_bands", "    layouts:\n", "    extra: 1\n    layouts:\n", "extra"},
		{"resistor_bands", `tol: 20`, `tol: 21`, "colour none with the tolerance 20 is required"},
		{"resistor_bands", `de: "Lesen ab dem Ende`, `dd: "Lesen ab dem Ende`, `notes[0]: missing "de" text`},
		{"inductor_bands", `digit: 9`, `digit: 8`, "digit must be 0 to 9 and used once"},
		{"inductor_bands", `mil_role: "point"`, `mil_role: "dot"`, "mil_role must be point or identifier"},
		{"smd_resistor", `eia96: [100, 102,`, `eia96: [100, 103,`, "eia96[1] = 103, the E96 value is 102"},
		{"smd_resistor", `{letter: "S"}`, `{letter: "Y"}`, "ambiguous[0]"},
		{"smd_resistor", `{letter: "K", exp: 3}`, `{letter: "k", exp: 3}`, "the letters are L, R, K, M and G"},
		{"capacitor", `makers: ["tdk", "nichicon", "panasonic"]}`, `makers: ["tdk"]}`, "at least two makers are required"},
		{"capacitor", `unit: "pf", when: "lt10pf"`, `unit: "pf", when: "any"`, "a pF tolerance is symmetric and applies below 10 pF"},
		{"capacitor", `{code: "0E",`, `{code: "0e",`, "a unique code of a digit and a capital letter"},
		{"capacitor", `{letters: ["m"], exp: -3}`, `{letters: ["m"], exp: 0}`, "with an exponent other than 0"},
		{"ceramic_temp", `{letter: "M", value: 1}`, `{letter: "C", value: 1}`, "class1.sig[1]: a unique letter"},
		{"ceramic_temp", `{digit: "5", value: 1}`, `{digit: "5", value: 0}`, "a unique digit and a multiplier other than 0"},
		{"ceramic_temp", `{letter: "G", ppm: 30}`, `{letter: "G", ppm: -30}`, "a unique letter and a positive tolerance"},
		{"ceramic_temp", `{name: "NP0", code: "C0G"}`, `{name: "", code: "C0G"}`, "aliases: a name and a 3-character code"},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		src := read(c.file)
		if !strings.Contains(src, c.old) {
			t.Errorf("%s: the shipped file does not contain %q", c.file, c.old)
			continue
		}
		_, err := Load(treeFS(t, map[string]string{"codes/k.yaml": strings.Replace(src, c.old, c.new, 1)}))
		if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), c.want) {
			t.Errorf("%s: %q -> %q: error = %v, want it to contain %q", c.file, c.old, c.new, err, c.want)
		}
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: create the five code items**

The tables are the research tables of `P3\research\codes\` (IEC 60062:2016 Table 1, Bourns and MIL-PRF-15305F, Yageo/Bourns/Venkel/TT EIA-96 tables, the maker tables for capacitors, Vishay 23140 and Murata for the EIA-198 codes) minus the cells marked UNVERIFIED or found in a single source (contract deviation 7). Multipliers are exponents of ten (`exp`), tolerances percent, temperature coefficients ppm/K.

```yaml
      - {bands: 4, roles: ["digit", "digit", "multiplier", "tolerance"]}
      - {bands: 5, roles: ["digit", "digit", "digit", "multiplier", "tolerance"]}
      - {bands: 6, roles: ["digit", "digit", "digit", "multiplier", "tolerance", "tcr"]}
    notes:
      - {en: "Read from the end where the bands start; the tolerance band is at least 1.5 times as wide as the others (IEC 60062, corrigendum 2016). Gold, silver and pink never stand first.", de: "Lesen ab dem Ende, an dem die Ringe beginnen; der Toleranzring ist mindestens 1,5-mal so breit wie die anderen (IEC 60062, Berichtigung 2016). Gold, Silber und Rosa stehen nie an erster Stelle."}
      - {en: "Older charts use grey = ±0.05 % and give orange and yellow no tolerance; IEC 60062:2016 uses grey ±0.01 %, orange ±0.05 % and yellow ±0.02 %. Check the datasheet of precision resistors.", de: "Ältere Tabellen verwenden Grau = ±0,05 % und geben Orange und Gelb keine Toleranz; IEC 60062:2016 verwendet Grau ±0,01 %, Orange ±0,05 % und Gelb ±0,02 %. Bei Präzisionswiderständen das Datenblatt prüfen."}
      - {en: "Pink (×0.001) is new in IEC 60062:2016 for very low resistances.", de: "Rosa (×0,001) ist seit IEC 60062:2016 neu, für sehr kleine Widerstandswerte."}
      - {en: "A single black band marks a zero-ohm jumper.", de: "Ein einzelner schwarzer Ring kennzeichnet eine Null-Ohm-Brücke."}
      - {en: "The temperature coefficient band only exists together with three significant figures (six bands).", de: "Den Temperaturkoeffizient-Ring gibt es nur zusammen mit drei signifikanten Stellen (sechs Ringe)."}
      - {en: "Displayed colours are illustrations only.", de: "Die angezeigten Farben sind nur Illustrationen."}
```

```yaml
      - {name: "NP0", code: "C0G"}
      - {name: "NPO", code: "C0G"}
      - {name: "N750", code: "U2J"}
      - {name: "N1500", code: "P3K"}
    industry:
      - {code: "C0G", name: "NP0"}
      - {code: "U2J", name: "N750"}
      - {code: "P3K", name: "N1500"}
    not_cross_checked: {c1_sig: ["B", "L", "A", "V"], c1_mult: ["4", "9"], c2_high: ["2", "9"], c2_change: ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "L"]}
    common: ["C0G", "U2J", "P3K", "X5R", "X6S", "X7R", "X7S", "X7T", "X7U", "X8R", "Y5V", "Z5U"]
    notes:
      - {en: "C0G (NP0) is the most stable class 1 dielectric: 0 ± 30 ppm/K.", de: "C0G (NP0) ist das stabilste Klasse-1-Dielektrikum: 0 ± 30 ppm/K."}
      - {en: "Class 2 codes describe only the temperature range and the change over temperature; DC bias and ageing reduce the capacitance further.", de: "Klasse-2-Codes beschreiben nur Temperaturbereich und Änderung über die Temperatur; Gleichspannung und Alterung verringern die Kapazität zusätzlich."}
      - {en: "X7R: −55 to +125 °C, ±15 %; Y5V: −30 to +85 °C, +22/−82 %.", de: "X7R: −55 bis +125 °C, ±15 %; Y5V: −30 bis +85 °C, +22/−82 %."}
      - {en: "Y5V and Z5U are class 2 here; some manufacturers call them class 3.", de: "Y5V und Z5U zählen hier zu Klasse 2; manche Hersteller nennen sie Klasse 3."}
      - {en: "Letters and digits that only one source lists are not decoded; the decoder says so.", de: "Buchstaben und Ziffern, die nur eine Quelle nennt, werden nicht gelesen; der Decoder weist darauf hin."}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: create the engine**

`codes.go` holds the shared part: the result and request types (the contract shapes), `CodeError`, `Decode`/`Encode`, the helpers (`codeDecimal` and `codeScaleDec` build numbers from digits so that Go and JavaScript agree to the last bit; `codeSigDigits` writes a value with n significant digits and says whether that is exact; `codeSnapToSeries`, `codeAssumeTolerance`, `codeParsePercent`, `codeParseAsym`) and the `init` that registers the five kinds. The other files hold, per family, the typed data with its `Load` (validation) and `JSON` (rendering for a language) functions and the codec.


**Create `internal/ecalc/codes.go`** with exactly this content:

```go
package ecalc

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"math"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// Component codes: reading and writing the markings of resistors, inductors and capacitors. The five code kinds
// (resistor_bands, inductor_bands, smd_resistor, capacitor, ceramic_temp) are registered here and in codes_*.go; their
// tables (colours, letters, voltage codes ...) are the data of the code items in catalog/codes/*.yaml. This file holds what
// the kinds share: the result types, the errors, Decode and Encode, and the helpers for digits, tolerances and the
// nearest standard value. The JavaScript twin is ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc-codes.js; both run the vectors of
// testdata/vectors/codes.json.

// Error codes of CodeError (the prefix of its message).
const (
	CodeInvalidCode  = "invalid_code"  // the code to decode is malformed
	CodeInvalidValue = "invalid_value" // a field of an encode request cannot be read, or the fields contradict each other
	CodeUnsupported  = "unsupported"   // well formed, but not decodable (not cross-checked, ambiguous) or not codable (outside the scheme)
)

// CodeError is a problem with a decode or encode request; its message starts with the code ("invalid_code: ...").
type CodeError struct {
	Code    string
	Message string
}

func (e *CodeError) Error() string { return e.Code + ": " + e.Message }

func codeErr(code, format string, args ...any) error {
	return &CodeError{Code: code, Message: fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)}
}

// AsCodeError returns err as a *CodeError, or nil when it is none.
func AsCodeError(err error) *CodeError {
	var ce *CodeError
	if errors.As(err, &ce) {
		return ce
	}
	return nil
}

// CodeResult is what Decode and Encode return. Bands holds colour ids for the band kinds, Value is in SI units (Ω, H, F, V,
// 1/K) or NaN when the kind has none, and Fields carry the further decoded parts. Warnings are English.
type CodeResult struct {
	Kind     string      `json:"kind"`
	Code     string      `json:"code"`
	Bands    []string    `json:"bands"`
	Value    float64     `json:"value"`
	Dim      string      `json:"dim"`
	Fields   []CodeField `json:"fields"`
	Warnings []string    `json:"warnings"`
}

// CodeField is one decoded part of a code (tolerance, temperature coefficient, voltage ...). Name is English; the ids are
// stable and are what the pages translate. Text is language neutral ("±5 %", "-55 °C"). Value is in SI units or NaN.
type CodeField struct {
	ID    string  `json:"id"`
	Name  string  `json:"name"`
	Text  string  `json:"text"`
	Value float64 `json:"value"`
	Dim   string  `json:"dim"`
}

// MarshalJSON writes a NaN value as null.
func (f CodeField) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
	type plain struct {
		ID    string   `json:"id"`
		Name  string   `json:"name"`
		Text  string   `json:"text"`
		Value *float64 `json:"value"`
		Dim   string   `json:"dim"`
	}
	p := plain{ID: f.ID, Name: f.Name, Text: f.Text, Dim: f.Dim}
	if !math.IsNaN(f.Value) {
		v := f.Value
		p.Value = &v
	}
	return json.Marshal(p)
}

// MarshalJSON writes a NaN value as null and the lists as arrays, never null.
func (r CodeResult) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
	type plain struct {
		Kind     string      `json:"kind"`
		Code     string      `json:"code"`
		Bands    []string    `json:"bands"`
		Value    *float64    `json:"value"`
		Dim      string      `json:"dim"`
		Fields   []CodeField `json:"fields"`
		Warnings []string    `json:"warnings"`
	}
	p := plain{Kind: r.Kind, Code: r.Code, Bands: orEmpty(r.Bands), Dim: r.Dim, Fields: r.Fields, Warnings: orEmpty(r.Warnings)}
	if p.Fields == nil {
		p.Fields = []CodeField{}
	}
	if !math.IsNaN(r.Value) {
		v := r.Value
		p.Value = &v
	}
	return json.Marshal(p)
}

// EncodeRequest asks for the code of a value. Value is a quantity as typed in a field ("4.7k", "100n"); Bands is 0 (choose),
// 3, 4, 5 or 6 for the resistor and 4 (EIA) or 5 (MIL) for the inductor; Tolerance is a percentage ("5%"), for some kinds a
// letter or a quantity; TempCo a temperature coefficient ("50ppm"); Voltage a rated voltage ("50V"); Class the ceramic
// class ("1" or "2"). Fields a kind does not use are ignored.
type EncodeRequest struct {
	Value     string `json:"value"`
	Bands     int    `json:"bands"`
	Tolerance string `json:"tolerance"`
	TempCo    string `json:"tempco"`
	Voltage   string `json:"voltage"`
	Class     string `json:"class"`
}

// codeCodec is what the typed data of a code kind provides.
type codeCodec interface {
	decode(u *Units, code string) (CodeResult, error)
	encode(u *Units, req EncodeRequest) (CodeResult, error)
}

// codeMaxText is the longest code or request field Decode and Encode accept (UTF-16 code units, like Parse).
const codeMaxText = 64

func init() {
	RegisterCodeKind("resistor_bands", CodeKind{Load: codeLoadResistorBands, JSON: codeResistorBandsJSON})
	RegisterCodeKind("inductor_bands", CodeKind{Load: codeLoadInductorBands, JSON: codeInductorBandsJSON})
	RegisterCodeKind("smd_resistor", CodeKind{Load: codeLoadSMDResistor, JSON: codeSMDResistorJSON})
	RegisterCodeKind("capacitor", CodeKind{Load: codeLoadCapacitor, JSON: codeCapacitorJSON})
	RegisterCodeKind("ceramic_temp", CodeKind{Load: codeLoadCeramicTemp, JSON: codeCeramicTempJSON})
}

// codec finds the first code item of a kind and its codec.
func (c *Catalog) codec(kind string) (codeCodec, error) {
	for _, it := range c.Codes {
		if it.CodeKind != kind {
			continue
		}
		if cc, ok := it.Data.(codeCodec); ok {
			return cc, nil
		}
		break
	}
	return nil, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "unknown code kind %q (kinds: %s)", kind, strings.Join(CodeKindIDs(), ", "))
}

// Decode reads a code of one of the registered kinds: band colours as English ids ("brown black red gold"), SMD and
// capacitor markings as printed ("472", "4R7", "01C", "104K 1H", "4p7"), ceramic codes ("X7R", "C0G"). Errors are
// *CodeError with the codes invalid_code and unsupported.
func (c *Catalog) Decode(kind, code string) (CodeResult, error) {
	cc, err := c.codec(kind)
	if err != nil {
		return CodeResult{}, err
	}
	if textLength(code) > codeMaxText {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "the code is longer than %d characters", codeMaxText)
	}
	return cc.decode(c.Units, code)
}

// Encode writes the code of a value. The value is replaced by the nearest standard value of the series that the tolerance
// implies (20 % E6, 10 % E12, 5 % E24, 2 % E48, 1 % E96, 0.5 % and finer E192; E24 values also count as standard from
// 5 % down) and a warning says so; without a tolerance one is assumed from the value. Errors are *CodeError with the
// codes invalid_value and unsupported.
func (c *Catalog) Encode(kind string, req EncodeRequest) (CodeResult, error) {
	cc, err := c.codec(kind)
	if err != nil {
		return CodeResult{}, err
	}
	for _, s := range []string{req.Value, req.Tolerance, req.TempCo, req.Voltage, req.Class} {
		if textLength(s) > codeMaxText {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "a request field is longer than %d characters", codeMaxText)
		}
	}
	if req.Bands < 0 || req.Bands > 6 {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "bands must be 0 (choose), 3, 4, 5 or 6")
	}
	return cc.encode(c.Units, req)
}

// ---- result building --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

func codeNewResult(kind string) CodeResult {
	return CodeResult{Kind: kind, Bands: []string{}, Value: math.NaN(), Fields: []CodeField{}, Warnings: []string{}}
}

func (r *CodeResult) field(id, name, text string, value float64, dim string) {
	r.Fields = append(r.Fields, CodeField{ID: id, Name: name, Text: text, Value: value, Dim: dim})
}

func (r *CodeResult) warn(format string, args ...any) {
	r.Warnings = append(r.Warnings, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...))
}

// ---- numbers -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// codeDecimal returns n*10^exp as the double nearest to that decimal (the same in JavaScript: Number(n + "e" + exp)).
func codeDecimal(n, exp int) float64 {
	v, _ := strconv.ParseFloat(strconv.Itoa(n)+"e"+strconv.Itoa(exp), 64)
	return v
}

// codeDecimalText returns the number "whole.frac" times 10^exp for digit strings (whole may be empty).
func codeDecimalText(whole, frac string, exp int) float64 {
	if whole == "" {
		whole = "0"
	}
	if frac != "" {
		whole += "." + frac
	}
	v, _ := strconv.ParseFloat(whole+"e"+strconv.Itoa(exp), 64)
	return v
}

// codeScaleDec returns x*10^exp as the double nearest to that decimal (x is a short decimal such as 0.25 or 50; the same in
// JavaScript: Number(String(x) + "e" + exp)). A magnitude outside 1e-6 .. 1e21, where String(x) uses an exponent, is
// multiplied instead.
func codeScaleDec(x float64, exp int) float64 {
	if a := math.Abs(x); a == 0 || a < 1e-6 || a >= 1e21 {
		return x * math.Pow10(exp)
	}
	v, _ := strconv.ParseFloat(strconv.FormatFloat(x, 'f', -1, 64)+"e"+strconv.Itoa(exp), 64)
	return v
}

// codeSigDigits writes v (> 0) with n significant digits: the integer N of exactly n digits and the exponent e with v = N*10^e,
// and whether v equals that number to within 1e-9 relative (so that it is not a rounded value).
func codeSigDigits(v float64, n int) (N, e int, exact bool) {
	s := strconv.FormatFloat(v, 'e', n-1, 64)
	i := strings.IndexByte(s, 'e')
	N, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.Replace(s[:i], ".", "", 1))
	e, _ = strconv.Atoi(s[i+1:])
	e -= n - 1
	return N, e, math.Abs(codeDecimal(N, e)-v) <= 1e-9*v
}

// codeSeriesHas reports whether v, written with 3 significant digits, is a value of the E-series (any decade).
func codeSeriesHas(series string, v float64) bool {
	n, _, exact := codeSigDigits(v, 3)
	if !exact {
		return false
	}
	for _, m := range eseriesTables[series] {
		if int(math.Round(m*100)) == n {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// codeSeriesForTolerance is the E-series that a tolerance (percent) implies.
func codeSeriesForTolerance(tol float64) string {
	switch {
	case tol >= 20:
		return "E6"
	case tol >= 10:
		return "E12"
	case tol >= 5:
		return "E24"
	case tol >= 2:
		return "E48"
	case tol >= 1:
		return "E96"
	}
	return "E192"
}

// codeAssumeTolerance picks a tolerance for a value without one: 5 % for an E24 value, 1 % for an E96 value, 0.5 % for an
// E192 value, otherwise 5 % (the value is then replaced by an E24 value).
func codeAssumeTolerance(v float64) float64 {
	switch {
	case codeSeriesHas("E24", v):
		return 5
	case codeSeriesHas("E96", v):
		return 1
	case codeSeriesHas("E192", v):
		return 0.5
	}
	return 5
}

// codeSnapToSeries returns the standard value for tolerance tol (percent) that is nearest to v: a value of the series that tol
// implies or, for tolerances below 5 %, of E24 (47 kΩ is a normal 1 % value). A tie goes to the lower value. changed says
// that the value is not v (within 1e-9 relative).
func codeSnapToSeries(v, tol float64) (value float64, changed bool, err error) {
	best, _, err := Nearest(codeSeriesForTolerance(tol), v)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, false, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "the value is outside the range of the code")
	}
	if tol < 5 {
		if alt, _, err := Nearest("E24", v); err == nil {
			da, db := math.Abs(alt-v), math.Abs(best-v)
			if da < db || (da == db && alt < best) {
				best = alt
			}
		}
	}
	return best, math.Abs(best-v) > 1e-9*v, nil
}

// codeSnapWarning is the warning that a value was replaced by the nearest standard value.
func codeSnapWarning(u *Units, dim string, in, out, tol float64) string {
	label := codeSeriesForTolerance(tol)
	if tol < 5 {
		label += " or E24"
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s is not a standard value for ±%s %% (%s); encoded the nearest, %s (%s %%)",
		u.Format(in, dim, "", 4), fmtSig(tol, 6), label, u.Format(out, dim, "", 4), codeSignedText((out-in)/in*100, 2))
}

// codeSignedText writes x with sig significant digits and an explicit sign: "+5", "−0.5" (U+2212), "0".
func codeSignedText(x float64, sig int) string {
	switch {
	case x == 0:
		return "0"
	case x < 0:
		return "−" + fmtSig(-x, sig)
	}
	return "+" + fmtSig(x, sig)
}

// ---- reading request fields --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

var (
	codePercentRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^\+?(\d+(?:\.\d+)?|\.\d+)%?$`)
	codeAsymRe    = regexp.MustCompile(`^([+\-−])(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)/([+\-−])(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)%?$`)
)

// codeCompact removes all white space and turns a decimal comma into a point.
func codeCompact(s string) string {
	return strings.ReplaceAll(strings.Join(strings.Fields(s), ""), ",", ".")
}

// codeParsePercent reads "5", "5%", "±5 %", "0,25%" as a percentage.
func codeParsePercent(s string) (float64, bool) {
	m := codePercentRe.FindStringSubmatch(strings.TrimPrefix(codeCompact(s), "±"))
	if m == nil {
		return 0, false
	}
	p, err := strconv.ParseFloat(m[1], 64)
	return p, err == nil
}

// codeParseAsym reads an asymmetric tolerance "-20/+80", "+22/-56 %": the sizes of the upward and the downward deviation.
func codeParseAsym(s string) (plus, minus float64, ok bool) {
	m := codeAsymRe.FindStringSubmatch(codeCompact(s))
	if m == nil || (m[1] == "+") == (m[3] == "+") {
		return 0, 0, false
	}
	a, _ := strconv.ParseFloat(m[2], 64)
	b, _ := strconv.ParseFloat(m[4], 64)
	if m[1] == "+" {
		return a, b, true
	}
	return b, a, true
}

// codeRequestedTolerance is the tolerance (percent) of an encode request: the percentage given, or one assumed from the value
// (assumed is then true).
func codeRequestedTolerance(req EncodeRequest, v float64) (tol float64, assumed bool, err error) {
	if strings.TrimSpace(req.Tolerance) == "" {
		return codeAssumeTolerance(v), true, nil
	}
	p, ok := codeParsePercent(req.Tolerance)
	if !ok || p <= 0 {
		return 0, false, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "tolerance: cannot read %q as a percentage", req.Tolerance)
	}
	return p, false, nil
}

// codeCloseTo reports a == b within 1e-9 relative (exactly equal values included).
func codeCloseTo(a, b float64) bool {
	return a == b || math.Abs(a-b) <= 1e-9*math.Max(math.Abs(a), math.Abs(b))
}

// codeBandSeparators split a list of band colours: white space, comma, semicolon, underscore, hyphen, en dash, em dash.
var codeBandSeparators = regexp.MustCompile(`[\s\p{Z},;_\-–—]+`)

// codeSplitWords splits text at the band separators, lower-cased, without empty parts.
func codeSplitWords(text string) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, w := range codeBandSeparators.Split(strings.ToLower(text), -1) {
		if w != "" {
			out = append(out, w)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// codeLocalizedNotes renders the notes of a code kind for a language.
func codeLocalizedNotes(notes []Text, lang string) []string {
	out := make([]string, 0, len(notes))
	for _, n := range notes {
		out = append(out, n.in(lang))
	}
	return out
}

// codeNeedLocales reports a name that lacks one of the 16 locales.
func codeNeedLocales(fail func(string, ...any), what string, t Text) {
	for _, l := range Locales {
		if strings.TrimSpace(t[l]) == "" {
			fail("data: %s: missing %q text", what, l)
		}
	}
	for l := range t {
		if !isLocale(l) {
			fail("data: %s: unknown language %q", what, l)
		}
	}
}

// codeNeedEnDe reports a note that lacks English or German text.
func codeNeedEnDe(fail func(string, ...any), what string, t Text) {
	for _, l := range docLocales {
		if strings.TrimSpace(t[l]) == "" {
			fail("data: %s: missing %q text", what, l)
		}
	}
}

var codeHexRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^(#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}|transparent)$`)

// ---- shared pieces of the data ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// codeCheckNotes validates the notes of a code kind (English and German each).
func codeCheckNotes(fail func(string, ...any), notes []Text) {
	for i, n := range notes {
		codeNeedEnDe(fail, fmt.Sprintf("notes[%d]", i), n)
	}
}
```
