**Create `internal/ecalc/codes_bands.go`** with exactly this content:

```go
package ecalc

import (
	"fmt"
	"math"
	"sort"
	"strings"

	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

// The colour band kinds: resistor_bands (IEC 60062, 3 to 6 bands) and inductor_bands (EIA style with 4 bands, military
// style with 5 bands). The colours, their digits, multipliers (as exponents of ten), tolerances and temperature
// coefficients are the data of the code item.

const (
	codeRoleDigit      = "digit"
	codeRoleMultiplier = "multiplier"
	codeRoleTolerance  = "tolerance"
	codeRoleTCR        = "tcr"
)

var codeRoleLabel = map[string]string{codeRoleDigit: "a digit", codeRoleMultiplier: "a multiplier", codeRoleTolerance: "a tolerance", codeRoleTCR: "a temperature coefficient"}

// codeBandColor is one colour of the resistor code. Exp is the exponent of the multiplier, Tol the tolerance in percent, TCR
// the temperature coefficient in ppm/K; LegacyTol / LegacyNone give what older charts print for the same colour.
type codeBandColor struct {
	ID         string   `yaml:"id"`
	IEC        string   `yaml:"iec"`
	Hex        string   `yaml:"hex"`
	Name       Text     `yaml:"name"`
	Digit      *int     `yaml:"digit"`
	Exp        *int     `yaml:"exp"`
	Tol        *float64 `yaml:"tol"`
	TCR        *float64 `yaml:"tcr"`
	LegacyTol  *float64 `yaml:"legacy_tol"`
	LegacyNone bool     `yaml:"legacy_tol_none"`
}

type codeBandLayout struct {
	Bands int      `yaml:"bands" json:"bands"`
	Roles []string `yaml:"roles" json:"roles"`
}

type codeResistorData struct {
	Colors  []codeBandColor  `yaml:"colors"`
	Layouts []codeBandLayout `yaml:"layouts"`
	Notes   []Text           `yaml:"notes"`

	byName  map[string]*codeBandColor // ids, IEC 60757 letters (lower case) and "gray"; "none" is no band
	byID    map[string]*codeBandColor
	byDigit map[int]*codeBandColor
	byExp   map[int]*codeBandColor
	layout  map[int]*codeBandLayout
}

func codeLoadResistorBands(raw *yaml.Node, fail func(string, ...any)) any {
	var d codeResistorData
	if err := decodeNode(raw, &d); err != nil {
		fail("data: %v", err)
		return nil
	}
	d.byName, d.byID, d.byDigit, d.byExp, d.layout = map[string]*codeBandColor{}, map[string]*codeBandColor{}, map[int]*codeBandColor{}, map[int]*codeBandColor{}, map[int]*codeBandLayout{}
	for i := range d.Colors {
		c := &d.Colors[i]
		if !idRe.MatchString(c.ID) {
			fail("data: colors[%d]: id must match %s", i, idRe)
			continue
		}
		if d.byID[c.ID] != nil {
			fail("data: colour %s appears twice", c.ID)
			continue
		}
		d.byID[c.ID] = c
		codeNeedLocales(fail, "colour "+c.ID+" name", c.Name)
		if !codeHexRe.MatchString(c.Hex) {
			fail("data: colour %s: hex must be #rrggbb or transparent", c.ID)
		}
		if c.Digit != nil {
			if *c.Digit < 0 || *c.Digit > 9 || d.byDigit[*c.Digit] != nil {
				fail("data: colour %s: digit must be 0 to 9 and used once", c.ID)
			} else {
				d.byDigit[*c.Digit] = c
			}
		}
		if c.Exp != nil {
			if *c.Exp < -3 || *c.Exp > 9 || d.byExp[*c.Exp] != nil {
				fail("data: colour %s: exp must be -3 to 9 and used once", c.ID)
			} else {
				d.byExp[*c.Exp] = c
			}
		}
		for what, p := range map[string]*float64{"tol": c.Tol, "tcr": c.TCR, "legacy_tol": c.LegacyTol} {
			if p != nil && !(*p > 0) {
				fail("data: colour %s: %s must be positive", c.ID, what)
			}
		}
		if c.ID == "none" {
			continue
		}
		names := []string{c.ID}
		if c.IEC != "" {
			names = append(names, strings.ToLower(c.IEC))
		}
		if c.ID == "grey" {
			names = append(names, "gray")
		}
		for _, n := range names {
			if d.byName[n] != nil {
				fail("data: colour name %q is used twice", n)
			}
			d.byName[n] = c
		}
	}
	if b := d.byID["black"]; b == nil || b.Digit == nil || *b.Digit != 0 || b.Exp == nil || *b.Exp != 0 {
		fail("data: colour black with digit 0 and exp 0 is required")
	}
	if n := d.byID["none"]; n == nil || n.Tol == nil || *n.Tol != 20 {
		fail("data: colour none with the tolerance 20 is required (a code without a tolerance band)")
	}
	for i, l := range d.Layouts {
		if len(l.Roles) != l.Bands || l.Bands < 3 || l.Bands > 6 || d.layout[l.Bands] != nil {
			fail("data: layouts[%d]: bands must be 3 to 6, used once, with one role per band", i)
			continue
		}
		multipliers := 0
		for j, r := range l.Roles {
			if codeRoleLabel[r] == "" {
				fail("data: layouts[%d]: unknown role %q", i, r)
			}
			if (j == 0) != (r == codeRoleDigit && j == 0) {
				fail("data: layouts[%d]: the first band is a digit", i)
			}
			if r == codeRoleMultiplier {
				multipliers++
			}
		}
		if multipliers != 1 {
			fail("data: layouts[%d]: exactly one multiplier band is required", i)
		}
		d.layout[l.Bands] = &d.Layouts[i]
	}
	if len(d.Layouts) == 0 {
		fail("data: layouts must not be empty")
	}
	codeCheckNotes(fail, d.Notes)
	return &d
}

type codeBandColorJSON struct {
	ID            string   `json:"id"`
	Name          string   `json:"name"`
	IEC           string   `json:"iec"`
	Hex           string   `json:"hex"`
	Digit         *int     `json:"digit"`
	Exp           *int     `json:"exp"`
	Tol           *float64 `json:"tol"`
	TCR           *float64 `json:"tcr"`
	LegacyTol     *float64 `json:"legacy_tol"`
	LegacyTolNone bool     `json:"legacy_tol_none"`
}

type codeResistorBandsDoc struct {
	Colors  []codeBandColorJSON `json:"colors"`
	Layouts []codeBandLayout    `json:"layouts"`
	Notes   []string            `json:"notes"`
}

func codeResistorBandsJSON(data any, lang string) any {
	d := data.(*codeResistorData)
	out := codeResistorBandsDoc{Colors: make([]codeBandColorJSON, 0, len(d.Colors)), Layouts: orEmpty(d.Layouts), Notes: codeLocalizedNotes(d.Notes, lang)}
	for _, c := range d.Colors {
		out.Colors = append(out.Colors, codeBandColorJSON{ID: c.ID, Name: c.Name.in(lang), IEC: c.IEC, Hex: c.Hex, Digit: c.Digit, Exp: c.Exp, Tol: c.Tol, TCR: c.TCR, LegacyTol: c.LegacyTol, LegacyTolNone: c.LegacyNone})
	}
	return out
}

// codeBandsOf reads a list of colour names.
func codeBandsOf(byName map[string]*codeBandColor, code string) ([]*codeBandColor, error) {
	words := codeSplitWords(code)
	if len(words) == 0 {
		return nil, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "the code is empty")
	}
	out := make([]*codeBandColor, 0, len(words))
	for _, w := range words {
		c := byName[w]
		if c == nil {
			var ids []string
			for n, c := range byName {
				if n == c.ID {
					ids = append(ids, n)
				}
			}
			sort.Strings(ids)
			return nil, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "unknown colour %q (colours: %s)", w, strings.Join(ids, ", "))
		}
		out = append(out, c)
	}
	return out, nil
}

func codeBandIDs(cs []*codeBandColor) []string {
	out := make([]string, len(cs))
	for i, c := range cs {
		out[i] = c.ID
	}
	return out
}

// codeLegacyWarning says how older charts read a tolerance colour that IEC 60062:2016 assigned later ("" when they agree).
func codeLegacyWarning(c *codeBandColor) string {
	switch {
	case c.LegacyTol != nil:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s tolerance band: ±%s %% in IEC 60062:2016; older charts and some makers read ±%s %%", c.ID, fmtSig(*c.Tol, 6), fmtSig(*c.LegacyTol, 6))
	case c.LegacyNone:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s tolerance band: ±%s %% in IEC 60062:2016; older charts give %s no tolerance", c.ID, fmtSig(*c.Tol, 6), c.ID)
	}
	return ""
}

func codeToleranceField(res *CodeResult, tol float64) {
	res.field("tolerance", "Tolerance", "±"+fmtSig(tol, 6)+" %", codeScaleDec(tol, -2), "ratio")
}

func (d *codeResistorData) decode(u *Units, code string) (CodeResult, error) {
	cs, err := codeBandsOf(d.byName, code)
	if err != nil {
		return CodeResult{}, err
	}
	res := codeNewResult("resistor_bands")
	res.Dim = "resistance"
	res.Bands = codeBandIDs(cs)
	res.Code = strings.Join(res.Bands, " ")
	if len(cs) == 1 {
		if cs[0].ID != "black" {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "a single band must be black (a zero-ohm jumper)")
		}
		res.Value = 0
		res.warn("a single black band marks a zero-ohm jumper (no tolerance)")
		return res, nil
	}
	lay := d.layout[len(cs)]
	if lay == nil {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "a resistor code has 3 to 6 bands (or one black band), got %d", len(cs))
	}
	digits, exp := 0, 0
	var tol, tcr *codeBandColor
	for i, c := range cs {
		role := lay.Roles[i]
		ok := false
		switch role {
		case codeRoleDigit:
			ok = c.Digit != nil
		case codeRoleMultiplier:
			ok = c.Exp != nil
		case codeRoleTolerance:
			ok = c.Tol != nil
		case codeRoleTCR:
			ok = c.TCR != nil
		}
		if !ok {
			if i == 0 {
				return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "the first band cannot be %s (gold, silver and pink never stand first); the bands may be read from the wrong end", c.ID)
			}
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "band %d (%s) cannot be %s", i+1, c.ID, codeRoleLabel[role])
		}
		switch role {
		case codeRoleDigit:
			digits = digits*10 + *c.Digit
		case codeRoleMultiplier:
			exp = *c.Exp
		case codeRoleTolerance:
			tol = c
		case codeRoleTCR:
			tcr = c
		}
	}
	res.Value = codeDecimal(digits, exp)
	if tol == nil {
		codeToleranceField(&res, *d.byID["none"].Tol)
	} else {
		codeToleranceField(&res, *tol.Tol)
		if w := codeLegacyWarning(tol); w != "" {
			res.warn("%s", w)
		}
	}
	if tcr != nil {
		res.field("tcr", "Temperature coefficient", "±"+fmtSig(*tcr.TCR, 6)+" ppm/K", codeScaleDec(*tcr.TCR, -6), "tempco")
	}
	if res.Value > 0 && !codeSeriesHas("E24", res.Value) && !codeSeriesHas("E192", res.Value) {
		res.warn("the value is not an E24 or E192 value; check the reading direction")
	}
	return res, nil
}

// codeParseTempco reads a temperature coefficient ("50", "50ppm", "±50 ppm/K") in 1/K.
func codeParseTempco(u *Units, s string) (float64, error) {
	t := strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(s), "±")
	if strings.HasSuffix(strings.ToLower(t), "ppm") {
		t = t[:len(t)-3] + "ppm/K"
	}
	return u.Parse(t, "tempco", "ppmK")
}

// tolerances lists the tolerance values (percent) of the coloured bands, ascending, as text.
func (d *codeResistorData) toleranceList() string {
	var vals []float64
	for _, c := range d.Colors {
		if c.Tol != nil {
			vals = append(vals, *c.Tol)
		}
	}
	sort.Float64s(vals)
	parts := make([]string, len(vals))
	for i, v := range vals {
		parts[i] = fmtSig(v, 6)
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
}

func (d *codeResistorData) encode(u *Units, req EncodeRequest) (CodeResult, error) {
	v, err := u.Parse(req.Value, "resistance", "")
	if err != nil {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "value: %v", err)
	}
	if v < 0 {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "value: the resistance must not be negative")
	}
	res := codeNewResult("resistor_bands")
	res.Dim = "resistance"
	if v == 0 {
		res.Bands, res.Code, res.Value = []string{"black"}, "black", 0
		res.warn("a single black band marks a zero-ohm jumper (no tolerance)")
		return res, nil
	}
	bands := req.Bands
	if bands != 0 && d.layout[bands] == nil {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "bands must be 0 (choose), 3, 4, 5 or 6")
	}

	// tolerance
	tol, assumed := 20.0, true // the 3-band code without a tolerance band is +-20 %
	if bands != 3 || strings.TrimSpace(req.Tolerance) != "" {
		var err error
		if tol, assumed, err = codeRequestedTolerance(req, v); err != nil {
			return CodeResult{}, err
		}
	}
	var tolC *codeBandColor
	for i := range d.Colors {
		if c := &d.Colors[i]; c.Tol != nil && codeCloseTo(*c.Tol, tol) {
			tolC = c
		}
	}
	if tolC == nil {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "no band colour for a tolerance of ±%s %% (tolerances: %s)", fmtSig(tol, 6), d.toleranceList())
	}

	// temperature coefficient
	var tcrC *codeBandColor
	if strings.TrimSpace(req.TempCo) != "" {
		x, err := codeParseTempco(u, req.TempCo)
		if err != nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "tempco: %v", err)
		}
		for i := range d.Colors {
			if c := &d.Colors[i]; c.TCR != nil && codeCloseTo(codeScaleDec(*c.TCR, -6), x) {
				tcrC = c
			}
		}
		if tcrC == nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "no band colour for a temperature coefficient of %s ppm/K", fmtSig(x/1e-6, 6))
		}
		if bands != 0 && bands != 6 {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "a temperature coefficient needs the 6-band code")
		}
		bands = 6
	}
	if bands == 6 && tcrC == nil {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "the 6-band code needs a temperature coefficient (tempco)")
	}
	noTol := tolC.ID == "none"
	if bands == 3 && !noTol {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "the 3-band code has no tolerance band (±20 %%); give a tolerance of 20%% or use 4 bands")
	}
	if noTol {
		if bands > 3 {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "±20 %% has no tolerance colour; the code without a tolerance band has 3 bands")
		}
		bands = 3
	}

	// the standard value
	vs, changed, err := codeSnapToSeries(v, tol)
	if err != nil {
		return CodeResult{}, err
	}
	_, _, two := codeSigDigits(vs, 2)
	if bands == 0 {
		if two {
			bands = 4
		} else {
			bands = 5
		}
	}
	n := 3
	if bands == 3 || bands == 4 {
		n = 2
		if !two {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "%s needs 3 significant digits; a %d-band code holds 2 (use 5 or 6 bands)", u.Format(vs, "resistance", "", 4), bands)
		}
	}
	N, e, exact := codeSigDigits(vs, n)
	if !exact {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "%s needs more than %d significant digits", u.Format(vs, "resistance", "", 4), n)
	}
	mult := d.byExp[e]
	if mult == nil {
		lo, hi := codeDecimal(int(math.Pow10(n-1)), -3), codeDecimal(int(math.Pow10(n))-1, 9)
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "%s is outside the range of a %d-band code (%s to %s)", u.Format(vs, "resistance", "", 4), bands, u.Format(lo, "resistance", "", 4), u.Format(hi, "resistance", "", 4))
	}
	digitsText := fmt.Sprintf("%0*d", n, N)
	for _, ch := range digitsText {
		res.Bands = append(res.Bands, d.byDigit[int(ch-'0')].ID)
	}
	res.Bands = append(res.Bands, mult.ID)
	if !noTol {
		res.Bands = append(res.Bands, tolC.ID)
	}
	if tcrC != nil {
		res.Bands = append(res.Bands, tcrC.ID)
	}
	res.Code = strings.Join(res.Bands, " ")
	res.Value = codeDecimal(N, e)
	codeToleranceField(&res, tol)
	if tcrC != nil {
		res.field("tcr", "Temperature coefficient", "±"+fmtSig(*tcrC.TCR, 6)+" ppm/K", codeScaleDec(*tcrC.TCR, -6), "tempco")
	}
	if assumed {
		res.warn("no tolerance given; ±%s %% assumed", fmtSig(tol, 6))
	}
	if changed {
		res.warn("%s", codeSnapWarning(u, "resistance", v, vs, tol))
	}
	if !noTol {
		if w := codeLegacyWarning(tolC); w != "" {
			res.warn("%s", w)
		}
	}
	return res, nil
}

// ---- inductor_bands ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// codeInductorColor is one colour of the inductor code. EIAExp / MILExp are exponents of ten of the multiplier (value in µH);
// MILRole is "point" (gold, the decimal point of the military style) or "identifier" (silver, the wide first band).
type codeInductorColor struct {
	ID     string   `yaml:"id"`
	Hex    string   `yaml:"hex"`
	Name   Text     `yaml:"name"`
	Digit  *int     `yaml:"digit"`
	EIAExp *int     `yaml:"eia_exp"`
	EIATol *float64 `yaml:"eia_tol"`
	MILExp *int     `yaml:"mil_exp"`
	MILTol *float64 `yaml:"mil_tol"`
	Role   string   `yaml:"mil_role"`
}

type codeInductorData struct {
	Colors []codeInductorColor `yaml:"colors"`
	Notes  []Text              `yaml:"notes"`

	byName     map[string]*codeInductorColor
	byDigit    map[int]*codeInductorColor
	byEIAExp   map[int]*codeInductorColor
	byMILExp   map[int]*codeInductorColor
	identifier *codeInductorColor
	point      *codeInductorColor
}

func codeLoadInductorBands(raw *yaml.Node, fail func(string, ...any)) any {
	var d codeInductorData
	if err := decodeNode(raw, &d); err != nil {
		fail("data: %v", err)
		return nil
	}
	d.byName, d.byDigit, d.byEIAExp, d.byMILExp = map[string]*codeInductorColor{}, map[int]*codeInductorColor{}, map[int]*codeInductorColor{}, map[int]*codeInductorColor{}
	for i := range d.Colors {
		c := &d.Colors[i]
		if !idRe.MatchString(c.ID) || d.byName[c.ID] != nil {
			fail("data: colors[%d]: id %q must match %s and be unique", i, c.ID, idRe)
			continue
		}
		d.byName[c.ID] = c
		if c.ID == "grey" {
			d.byName["gray"] = c
		}
		codeNeedLocales(fail, "colour "+c.ID+" name", c.Name)
		if !codeHexRe.MatchString(c.Hex) {
			fail("data: colour %s: hex must be #rrggbb", c.ID)
		}
		if c.Digit != nil {
			if *c.Digit < 0 || *c.Digit > 9 || d.byDigit[*c.Digit] != nil {
				fail("data: colour %s: digit must be 0 to 9 and used once", c.ID)
			} else {
				d.byDigit[*c.Digit] = c
			}
		}
		if c.EIAExp != nil {
			if *c.EIAExp < -2 || *c.EIAExp > 3 || d.byEIAExp[*c.EIAExp] != nil {
				fail("data: colour %s: eia_exp must be -2 to 3 and used once", c.ID)
			} else {
				d.byEIAExp[*c.EIAExp] = c
			}
		}
		if c.MILExp != nil {
			if *c.MILExp < 0 || *c.MILExp > 3 || d.byMILExp[*c.MILExp] != nil {
				fail("data: colour %s: mil_exp must be 0 to 3 and used once", c.ID)
			} else {
				d.byMILExp[*c.MILExp] = c
			}
		}
		for what, p := range map[string]*float64{"eia_tol": c.EIATol, "mil_tol": c.MILTol} {
			if p != nil && !(*p > 0) {
				fail("data: colour %s: %s must be positive", c.ID, what)
			}
		}
		switch c.Role {
		case "":
		case "point":
			d.point = c
		case "identifier":
			d.identifier = c
		default:
			fail("data: colour %s: mil_role must be point or identifier", c.ID)
		}
	}
	for n := 0; n <= 9; n++ {
		if d.byDigit[n] == nil {
			fail("data: no colour for the digit %d", n)
		}
	}
	if d.point == nil || d.identifier == nil {
		fail("data: the military style needs a colour with mil_role point and one with mil_role identifier")
	}
	codeCheckNotes(fail, d.Notes)
	return &d
}

type codeInductorColorJSON struct {
	ID     string   `json:"id"`
	Name   string   `json:"name"`
	Hex    string   `json:"hex"`
	Digit  *int     `json:"digit"`
	EIAExp *int     `json:"eia_exp"`
	EIATol *float64 `json:"eia_tol"`
	MILExp *int     `json:"mil_exp"`
	MILTol *float64 `json:"mil_tol"`
	Role   string   `json:"mil_role"`
}

type codeInductorBandsDoc struct {
	Colors []codeInductorColorJSON `json:"colors"`
	Notes  []string                `json:"notes"`
}

func codeInductorBandsJSON(data any, lang string) any {
	d := data.(*codeInductorData)
	out := codeInductorBandsDoc{Colors: make([]codeInductorColorJSON, 0, len(d.Colors)), Notes: codeLocalizedNotes(d.Notes, lang)}
	for _, c := range d.Colors {
		out.Colors = append(out.Colors, codeInductorColorJSON{ID: c.ID, Name: c.Name.in(lang), Hex: c.Hex, Digit: c.Digit, EIAExp: c.EIAExp, EIATol: c.EIATol, MILExp: c.MILExp, MILTol: c.MILTol, Role: c.Role})
	}
	return out
}

const (
	codeLayoutEIA = "EIA (4 bands)"
	codeLayoutMIL = "MIL-PRF-15305 (5 bands, wide silver first)"
)

func codeInductorBandIDs(cs []*codeInductorColor) []string {
	out := make([]string, len(cs))
	for i, c := range cs {
		out[i] = c.ID
	}
	return out
}

func (d *codeInductorData) decode(u *Units, code string) (CodeResult, error) {
	words := codeSplitWords(code)
	if len(words) == 0 {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "the code is empty")
	}
	cs := make([]*codeInductorColor, 0, len(words))
	for _, w := range words {
		c := d.byName[w]
		if c == nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "unknown colour %q", w)
		}
		cs = append(cs, c)
	}
	res := codeNewResult("inductor_bands")
	res.Dim = "inductance"
	res.Bands = codeInductorBandIDs(cs)
	res.Code = strings.Join(res.Bands, " ")
	digit := func(i int) (int, error) {
		if cs[i].Digit == nil {
			return 0, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "band %d (%s) cannot be a digit", i+1, cs[i].ID)
		}
		return *cs[i].Digit, nil
	}
	var value float64
	var tol float64
	switch len(cs) {
	case 4: // EIA: digit, digit, multiplier, tolerance
		d1, err := digit(0)
		if err != nil {
			return CodeResult{}, err
		}
		d2, err := digit(1)
		if err != nil {
			return CodeResult{}, err
		}
		if cs[2].EIAExp == nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "band 3 (%s) cannot be a multiplier (black, brown, red, orange, gold or silver)", cs[2].ID)
		}
		if cs[3].EIATol == nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "the tolerance colour %s is not cross-checked for inductors (gold ±5 %%, silver ±10 %%)", cs[3].ID)
		}
		value = codeDecimal(d1*10+d2, *cs[2].EIAExp-6)
		tol = *cs[3].EIATol
		res.field("layout", "Layout", codeLayoutEIA, math.NaN(), "")
	case 5: // military: identifier, three value bands, tolerance
		if cs[0] != d.identifier {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "a 5-band inductor code starts with the wide %s military band", d.identifier.ID)
		}
		if cs[4].MILTol == nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "the tolerance colour %s is not cross-checked for inductors (gold ±5 %%, silver ±10 %%)", cs[4].ID)
		}
		tol = *cs[4].MILTol
		switch {
		case cs[1] == d.point && cs[2] == d.point, cs[3] == d.point:
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "%s is the decimal point: only band 2 or 3 can be %s, not both and not band 4", d.point.ID, d.point.ID)
		case cs[1] == d.point: // 0.d d
			a, err := digit(2)
			if err != nil {
				return CodeResult{}, err
			}
			b, err := digit(3)
			if err != nil {
				return CodeResult{}, err
			}
			value = codeDecimal(a*10+b, -2-6)
		case cs[2] == d.point: // d.d
			a, err := digit(1)
			if err != nil {
				return CodeResult{}, err
			}
			b, err := digit(3)
			if err != nil {
				return CodeResult{}, err
			}
			value = codeDecimal(a*10+b, -1-6)
		default: // dd x multiplier
			a, err := digit(1)
			if err != nil {
				return CodeResult{}, err
			}
			b, err := digit(2)
			if err != nil {
				return CodeResult{}, err
			}
			if cs[3].MILExp == nil {
				return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "band 4 (%s) cannot be a multiplier (black, brown, red or orange)", cs[3].ID)
			}
			value = codeDecimal(a*10+b, *cs[3].MILExp-6)
		}
		res.field("layout", "Layout", codeLayoutMIL, math.NaN(), "")
	default:
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "an inductor code has 4 bands (EIA) or 5 bands (military, wide silver first), got %d", len(cs))
	}
	if value == 0 {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "the bands give an inductance of zero")
	}
	res.Value = value
	codeToleranceField(&res, tol)
	return res, nil
}

func (d *codeInductorData) encode(u *Units, req EncodeRequest) (CodeResult, error) {
	v, err := u.Parse(req.Value, "inductance", "")
	if err != nil {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "value: %v", err)
	}
	if !(v > 0) {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "value: the inductance must be positive")
	}
	mil := false
	switch req.Bands {
	case 0, 4:
	case 5:
		mil = true
	default:
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "bands must be 4 (EIA) or 5 (military)")
	}
	res := codeNewResult("inductor_bands")
	res.Dim = "inductance"

	tol, assumed, err := codeRequestedTolerance(req, v)
	if err != nil {
		return CodeResult{}, err
	}
	var tolC *codeInductorColor
	for i := range d.Colors {
		c := &d.Colors[i]
		if c.EIATol != nil && c.MILTol != nil && codeCloseTo(*c.EIATol, tol) {
			tolC = c
		}
	}
	if tolC == nil {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "no band colour for a tolerance of ±%s %% (gold ±5 %%, silver ±10 %%)", fmtSig(tol, 6))
	}
	vs, changed, err := codeSnapToSeries(v, tol)
	if err != nil {
		return CodeResult{}, err
	}
	N, e, exact := codeSigDigits(vs, 2)
	if !exact {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "%s needs more than 2 significant digits", u.Format(vs, "inductance", "", 4))
	}
	micro := e + 6 // N * 10^micro is the value in µH
	digitColors := func(n int) []string { return []string{d.byDigit[n/10].ID, d.byDigit[n%10].ID} }
	if !mil {
		mult := d.byEIAExp[micro]
		if mult == nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "%s is outside the range of the EIA code (%s to %s)", u.Format(vs, "inductance", "", 4), u.Format(codeDecimal(10, -8), "inductance", "", 4), u.Format(codeDecimal(99, -3), "inductance", "", 4))
		}
		res.Bands = append(digitColors(N), mult.ID, tolC.ID)
		res.field("layout", "Layout", codeLayoutEIA, math.NaN(), "")
	} else {
		a, b := digitColors(N)[0], digitColors(N)[1]
		switch {
		case micro >= 0 && micro <= 3:
			res.Bands = []string{d.identifier.ID, a, b, d.byMILExp[micro].ID, tolC.ID}
		case micro == -1: // d.d
			res.Bands = []string{d.identifier.ID, a, d.point.ID, b, tolC.ID}
		case micro == -2: // 0.dd
			res.Bands = []string{d.identifier.ID, d.point.ID, a, b, tolC.ID}
		default:
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "%s is outside the range of the military code (%s to %s)", u.Format(vs, "inductance", "", 4), u.Format(codeDecimal(10, -8), "inductance", "", 4), u.Format(codeDecimal(99, -3), "inductance", "", 4))
		}
		res.field("layout", "Layout", codeLayoutMIL, math.NaN(), "")
	}
	res.Code = strings.Join(res.Bands, " ")
	res.Value = codeDecimal(N, e)
	codeToleranceField(&res, tol)
	if assumed {
		res.warn("no tolerance given; ±%s %% assumed", fmtSig(tol, 6))
	}
	if changed {
		res.warn("%s", codeSnapWarning(u, "inductance", v, vs, tol))
	}
	return res, nil
}
```

**Create `internal/ecalc/codes_smd.go`** with exactly this content:

```go
package ecalc

import (
	"fmt"
	"math"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

// The smd_resistor kind: the markings of chip resistors. Four families are read: the 3-digit code (two significant
// digits and an exponent), the 4-digit code (three digits and an exponent), the RKM / R notation (a letter is the decimal
// point and the multiplier: 4R7, R47, 1L5, 4K7) and the EIA-96 code (two digits indexing the E96 series plus a multiplier
// letter). The E96 table, the letters and the RKM letters are the data of the code item.

type codeSMDLetter struct {
	Letter string `yaml:"letter" json:"letter"`
	Exp    int    `yaml:"exp" json:"exp"`
	Rare   bool   `yaml:"rare" json:"rare"`
}

type codeSMDAmbiguous struct {
	Letter string `yaml:"letter" json:"letter"`
}

type codeSMDData struct {
	EIA96     []int              `yaml:"eia96"`
	Letters   []codeSMDLetter    `yaml:"letters"`
	RKM       []codeSMDLetter    `yaml:"rkm"`
	Ambiguous []codeSMDAmbiguous `yaml:"ambiguous"`
	Notes     []Text             `yaml:"notes"`

	letter map[string]*codeSMDLetter
	rkm    map[string]*codeSMDLetter
	amb    map[string]bool
}

func codeLoadSMDResistor(raw *yaml.Node, fail func(string, ...any)) any {
	var d codeSMDData
	if err := decodeNode(raw, &d); err != nil {
		fail("data: %v", err)
		return nil
	}
	d.letter, d.rkm, d.amb = map[string]*codeSMDLetter{}, map[string]*codeSMDLetter{}, map[string]bool{}
	if len(d.EIA96) != 96 {
		fail("data: eia96 must list the 96 values of the E96 series, got %d", len(d.EIA96))
	} else {
		for i, v := range d.EIA96 {
			if want := int(math.Round(e96[i] * 100)); v != want {
				fail("data: eia96[%d] = %d, the E96 value is %d (IEC 60063)", i, v, want)
			}
		}
	}
	for i := range d.Letters {
		l := &d.Letters[i]
		if len(l.Letter) != 1 || l.Letter < "A" || l.Letter > "Z" || d.letter[l.Letter] != nil || l.Exp < -3 || l.Exp > 6 {
			fail("data: letters[%d]: a unique capital letter and an exponent from -3 to 6 are required", i)
			continue
		}
		d.letter[l.Letter] = l
	}
	for i := range d.RKM {
		l := &d.RKM[i]
		if len(l.Letter) != 1 || !strings.Contains("LRKMG", l.Letter) || d.rkm[l.Letter] != nil {
			fail("data: rkm[%d]: the letters are L, R, K, M and G, each once", i)
			continue
		}
		d.rkm[l.Letter] = l
	}
	if len(d.rkm) != 5 {
		fail("data: rkm must list L, R, K, M and G")
	}
	for i, a := range d.Ambiguous {
		if len(a.Letter) != 1 || d.letter[a.Letter] != nil {
			fail("data: ambiguous[%d]: a letter that is not a decoded letter is required", i)
			continue
		}
		d.amb[a.Letter] = true
	}
	codeCheckNotes(fail, d.Notes)
	return &d
}

type codeSMDDoc struct {
	EIA96     []int              `json:"eia96"`
	Letters   []codeSMDLetter    `json:"letters"`
	RKM       []codeSMDLetter    `json:"rkm"`
	Ambiguous []codeSMDAmbiguous `json:"ambiguous"`
	Notes     []string           `json:"notes"`
}

func codeSMDResistorJSON(data any, lang string) any {
	d := data.(*codeSMDData)
	return codeSMDDoc{EIA96: orEmpty(d.EIA96), Letters: orEmpty(d.Letters), RKM: orEmpty(d.RKM), Ambiguous: orEmpty(d.Ambiguous), Notes: codeLocalizedNotes(d.Notes, lang)}
}

var (
	codeSMDEIA96Re = regexp.MustCompile(`^(\d\d)([A-Z])$`)
	codeSMDRKMRe   = regexp.MustCompile(`^(\d*)([LRKMG])(\d*)$`)
	codeSMDDigitRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^\d{3,4}$`)
	codeSMDZeroRe  = regexp.MustCompile(`^(0{1,4}|0R0)$`)
)

// codeNormalizeSMD removes blanks, underscores and bars (some makers underline a 1 % code) and upper-cases the code.
func codeNormalizeSMD(code string) string {
	s := strings.ToUpper(strings.Join(strings.Fields(code), ""))
	return strings.NewReplacer("_", "", "|", "").Replace(s)
}

func (d *codeSMDData) decode(u *Units, code string) (CodeResult, error) {
	s := codeNormalizeSMD(code)
	if s == "" {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "the code is empty")
	}
	res := codeNewResult("smd_resistor")
	res.Dim = "resistance"
	res.Code = s
	family := func(text string) { res.field("family", "Marking", text, math.NaN(), "") }

	if codeSMDZeroRe.MatchString(s) {
		res.Value = 0
		family("zero-ohm jumper")
		return res, nil
	}
	// two digits and a letter: an EIA-96 code, unless the letter is an RKM letter (10R, 47K, 15L read as RKM codes)
	if m := codeSMDEIA96Re.FindStringSubmatch(s); m != nil && d.rkm[m[2]] == nil {
		idx, _ := strconv.Atoi(m[1])
		if d.amb[m[2]] {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "the EIA-96 letter %s is ambiguous between makers (conflicting meanings); it is not decoded", m[2])
		}
		l := d.letter[m[2]]
		if l == nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "%s is not an EIA-96 multiplier letter", m[2])
		}
		if idx < 1 || idx > 96 {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "the EIA-96 index must be 01 to 96, got %s", m[1])
		}
		res.Value = codeDecimal(d.EIA96[idx-1], l.Exp)
		family("EIA-96")
		if l.Rare {
			res.warn("the letter %s (×%s) is only used by some makers", l.Letter, fmtNum(codeDecimal(1, l.Exp)))
		}
		return res, nil
	}
	if m := codeSMDRKMRe.FindStringSubmatch(s); m != nil && len(m[1])+len(m[3]) > 0 {
		if len(m[1])+len(m[3]) > 4 {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "an RKM code has at most 4 digits")
		}
		l := d.rkm[m[2]]
		res.Value = codeDecimalText(m[1], m[3], l.Exp)
		if l.Letter == "L" || l.Letter == "R" {
			family("R notation")
		} else {
			family("RKM notation")
		}
		if idx, _ := strconv.Atoi(m[1]); l.Letter == "R" && len(m[1]) == 2 && m[3] == "" && idx >= 1 && idx <= 96 {
			res.warn("R after two digits is read as the RKM decimal point (%s = %s); some makers use R as an EIA-96 multiplier letter, which is not decoded", s, u.Format(res.Value, "resistance", "", 4))
		}
		return res, nil
	}
	if codeSMDDigitRe.MatchString(s) {
		n := 2
		if len(s) == 4 {
			n = 3
		}
		digits, _ := strconv.Atoi(s[:n])
		exp, _ := strconv.Atoi(s[n:])
		res.Value = codeDecimal(digits, exp)
		family(fmt.Sprintf("%d-digit code", len(s)))
		return res, nil
	}
	return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "cannot read %q as an SMD resistor code (3 or 4 digits, R notation, RKM or EIA-96)", s)
}

// codeSMD3Digit writes v as a 3-character code ("472", "4R7", "R47", "R05", "1L5"); "" when it has no such code.
func codeSMD3Digit(v float64) string {
	N, e, exact := codeSigDigits(v, 2)
	if !exact {
		return ""
	}
	switch {
	case e >= 0 && e <= 9:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%d%d", N, e)
	case e == -1:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%dR%d", N/10, N%10)
	case e == -2:
		return fmt.Sprintf("R%d", N)
	case e == -3 && N%10 == 0:
		return fmt.Sprintf("R0%d", N/10)
	case e == -4:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%dL%d", N/10, N%10)
	}
	return ""
}

// codeSMD4Digit writes v as a 4-character code ("1001", "10R0", "4R99", "R499", "R020"); "" when it has no such code.
func codeSMD4Digit(v float64) string {
	N, e, exact := codeSigDigits(v, 3)
	if !exact {
		return ""
	}
	switch {
	case e >= 0 && e <= 9:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%d%d", N, e)
	case e == -1:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%dR%d", N/10, N%10)
	case e == -2:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%dR%02d", N/100, N%100)
	case e == -3:
		return fmt.Sprintf("R%03d", N)
	case e == -4 && N%10 == 0:
		return fmt.Sprintf("R%03d", N/10)
	}
	return ""
}

// code96 writes v as an EIA-96 code ("01C"); "" when v is not an E96 value from 1.00 Ω to 97.6 MΩ.
func (d *codeSMDData) code96(v float64) string {
	N, e, exact := codeSigDigits(v, 3)
	if !exact {
		return ""
	}
	for i, x := range d.EIA96 {
		if x != N {
			continue
		}
		for _, l := range d.Letters {
			if l.Exp == e && !l.Rare {
				return fmt.Sprintf("%02d%s", i+1, l.Letter)
			}
		}
	}
	return ""
}

func (d *codeSMDData) encode(u *Units, req EncodeRequest) (CodeResult, error) {
	v, err := u.Parse(req.Value, "resistance", "")
	if err != nil {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "value: %v", err)
	}
	if v < 0 {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "value: the resistance must not be negative")
	}
	res := codeNewResult("smd_resistor")
	res.Dim = "resistance"
	if v == 0 {
		res.Code, res.Value = "000", 0
		res.field("family", "Marking", "zero-ohm jumper", math.NaN(), "")
		res.field("code_4digit", "4-digit code", "0000", math.NaN(), "")
		return res, nil
	}
	tol, assumed, err := codeRequestedTolerance(req, v)
	if err != nil {
		return CodeResult{}, err
	}
	vs, changed, err := codeSnapToSeries(v, tol)
	if err != nil {
		return CodeResult{}, err
	}
	c3, c4, c96 := codeSMD3Digit(vs), codeSMD4Digit(vs), d.code96(vs)
	primary, family := c3, "3-digit code"
	if (tol <= 1 && c4 != "") || c3 == "" {
		primary, family = c4, "4-digit code"
	}
	if primary == "" {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "%s has no 3-digit or 4-digit marking", u.Format(vs, "resistance", "", 4))
	}
	N, e, _ := codeSigDigits(vs, 3)
	res.Code = primary
	res.Value = codeDecimal(N, e)
	res.field("family", "Marking", family, math.NaN(), "")
	if c3 != "" {
		res.field("code_3digit", "3-digit code", c3, math.NaN(), "")
	}
	if c4 != "" {
		res.field("code_4digit", "4-digit code", c4, math.NaN(), "")
	}
	if c96 != "" {
		res.field("code_eia96", "EIA-96 code", c96, math.NaN(), "")
	}
	codeToleranceField(&res, tol)
	if assumed {
		res.warn("no tolerance given; ±%s %% assumed", fmtSig(tol, 6))
	}
	if changed {
		res.warn("%s", codeSnapWarning(u, "resistance", v, vs, tol))
	}
	return res, nil
}
```

**Create `internal/ecalc/codes_capacitor.go`** with exactly this content:

```go
package ecalc

import (
	"fmt"
	"math"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"unicode"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

// The capacitor kind: the picofarad code of ceramic and film capacitors (104 = 100 nF, 4R7 = 4.7 pF, 4p7, 2n2), the
// tolerance letters and the two-character rated-voltage codes (1H = 50 V). One marking may carry several parts ("104K 1H");
// every part is recognised by its shape. The multipliers, the RKM prefixes, the tolerance letters and the voltage codes are
// the data of the code item.

type codeCapMultiplier struct {
	Digit string `yaml:"digit" json:"digit"`
	Exp   int    `yaml:"exp" json:"exp"`
	Maker string `yaml:"maker" json:"maker"`
}

type codeCapRKM struct {
	Letters []string `yaml:"letters" json:"letters"`
	Exp     int      `yaml:"exp" json:"exp"`
}

type codeCapTolerance struct {
	Letter string  `yaml:"letter" json:"letter"`
	Minus  float64 `yaml:"minus" json:"minus"`
	Plus   float64 `yaml:"plus" json:"plus"`
	Unit   string  `yaml:"unit" json:"unit"`
	When   string  `yaml:"when" json:"when"`
}

type codeCapVoltage struct {
	Code   string   `yaml:"code"`
	Volts  float64  `yaml:"volts"`
	Makers []string `yaml:"makers"`
	Note   Text     `yaml:"note"`
}

type codeCapNotChecked struct {
	Tolerance  []string `yaml:"tolerance" json:"tolerance"`
	Multiplier []string `yaml:"multiplier" json:"multiplier"`
}

type codeCapacitorData struct {
	Multipliers []codeCapMultiplier `yaml:"multipliers"`
	RKM         []codeCapRKM        `yaml:"rkm"`
	Tolerances  []codeCapTolerance  `yaml:"tolerances"`
	Voltages    []codeCapVoltage    `yaml:"voltages"`
	NotChecked  codeCapNotChecked   `yaml:"not_cross_checked"`
	Notes       []Text              `yaml:"notes"`

	mult    map[string]*codeCapMultiplier
	rkm     map[string]int // prefix letter -> exponent
	voltage map[string]*codeCapVoltage
}

const (
	codeWhenLess    = "lt10pf"
	codeWhenAtLeast = "ge10pf"
	codeWhenAny     = "any"
)

func codeLoadCapacitor(raw *yaml.Node, fail func(string, ...any)) any {
	var d codeCapacitorData
	if err := decodeNode(raw, &d); err != nil {
		fail("data: %v", err)
		return nil
	}
	d.mult, d.rkm, d.voltage = map[string]*codeCapMultiplier{}, map[string]int{}, map[string]*codeCapVoltage{}
	for i := range d.Multipliers {
		m := &d.Multipliers[i]
		if len(m.Digit) != 1 || m.Digit < "0" || m.Digit > "9" || d.mult[m.Digit] != nil || m.Exp < -3 || m.Exp > 9 {
			fail("data: multipliers[%d]: a unique digit and an exponent from -3 to 9 are required", i)
			continue
		}
		d.mult[m.Digit] = m
	}
	for i, r := range d.RKM {
		for _, l := range r.Letters {
			if codeUtf8Len(l) != 1 || d.rkm[l] != 0 || r.Exp == 0 {
				fail("data: rkm[%d]: letter %q must be one character, used once, with an exponent other than 0", i, l)
				continue
			}
			d.rkm[l] = r.Exp
		}
	}
	for i := range d.Tolerances {
		t := &d.Tolerances[i]
		if len(t.Letter) != 1 || t.Letter < "A" || t.Letter > "Z" || !(t.Minus > 0) || !(t.Plus > 0) {
			fail("data: tolerances[%d]: a capital letter and positive deviations are required", i)
		}
		if t.Unit != "pf" && t.Unit != "pct" {
			fail("data: tolerances[%d]: unit must be pf or pct", i)
		}
		if t.When != codeWhenLess && t.When != codeWhenAtLeast && t.When != codeWhenAny {
			fail("data: tolerances[%d]: when must be %s, %s or %s", i, codeWhenLess, codeWhenAtLeast, codeWhenAny)
		}
		if t.Unit == "pf" && (t.Minus != t.Plus || t.When != codeWhenLess) {
			fail("data: tolerances[%d]: a pF tolerance is symmetric and applies below 10 pF", i)
		}
	}
	for i := range d.Voltages {
		v := &d.Voltages[i]
		if len(v.Code) != 2 || v.Code[0] < '0' || v.Code[0] > '9' || v.Code[1] < 'A' || v.Code[1] > 'Z' || d.voltage[v.Code] != nil || !(v.Volts > 0) {
			fail("data: voltages[%d]: a unique code of a digit and a capital letter and positive volts are required", i)
			continue
		}
		if len(v.Makers) < 2 {
			fail("data: voltage code %s: at least two makers are required (a single-source code stays out)", v.Code)
		}
		if len(v.Note) > 0 {
			codeNeedEnDe(fail, "voltage code "+v.Code+" note", v.Note)
		}
		d.voltage[v.Code] = v
	}
	if len(d.mult) == 0 || len(d.rkm) == 0 || len(d.Tolerances) == 0 || len(d.Voltages) == 0 {
		fail("data: multipliers, rkm, tolerances and voltages must not be empty")
	}
	codeCheckNotes(fail, d.Notes)
	return &d
}

func codeUtf8Len(s string) int { return utf8.RuneCountInString(s) }

type codeCapVoltageJSON struct {
	Code   string   `json:"code"`
	Volts  float64  `json:"volts"`
	Makers []string `json:"makers"`
	Note   string   `json:"note"`
	NoteEN string   `json:"note_en"` // the English note, which the warnings of a decode use in every language
}

type codeCapacitorDoc struct {
	Multipliers []codeCapMultiplier  `json:"multipliers"`
	RKM         []codeCapRKM         `json:"rkm"`
	Tolerances  []codeCapTolerance   `json:"tolerances"`
	Voltages    []codeCapVoltageJSON `json:"voltages"`
	NotChecked  codeCapNotChecked    `json:"not_cross_checked"`
	Notes       []string             `json:"notes"`
}

func codeCapacitorJSON(data any, lang string) any {
	d := data.(*codeCapacitorData)
	out := codeCapacitorDoc{Multipliers: orEmpty(d.Multipliers), RKM: orEmpty(d.RKM), Tolerances: orEmpty(d.Tolerances), Voltages: make([]codeCapVoltageJSON, 0, len(d.Voltages)),
		NotChecked: codeCapNotChecked{Tolerance: orEmpty(d.NotChecked.Tolerance), Multiplier: orEmpty(d.NotChecked.Multiplier)}, Notes: codeLocalizedNotes(d.Notes, lang)}
	for _, v := range d.Voltages {
		note, noteEN := "", ""
		if len(v.Note) > 0 {
			note, noteEN = v.Note.in(lang), v.Note.in("en")
		}
		out.Voltages = append(out.Voltages, codeCapVoltageJSON{Code: v.Code, Volts: v.Volts, Makers: orEmpty(v.Makers), Note: note, NoteEN: noteEN})
	}
	return out
}

var (
	codeCapRKMRe     = regexp.MustCompile(`^(\d+)([pnuµm])(\d*)([A-Za-z]?)$`)
	codeCapRKMUpper  = regexp.MustCompile(`^(\d+)([PNU])(\d+)([A-Za-z]?)$`)
	codeCapRRe       = regexp.MustCompile(`^(\d?)R(\d{1,2})([A-Z]?)$`)
	codeCapDigitsRe  = regexp.MustCompile(`^(\d{3})([A-Z]?)$`)
	codeCapVoltageRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^\d[A-Z]$`)
	codeCapLetterRe  = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Z]$`)
	codeCapPairRe    = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Z]{2}$`)
)

// codeTenPicofarad is the boundary of the tolerance letters (below it they mean pF, from it percent).
var codeTenPicofarad = codeDecimal(10, -12)

// toleranceRows selects the tolerance rows of a letter that apply to the capacitance (when known).
func (d *codeCapacitorData) toleranceRows(letter string, capF float64, hasCap bool) ([]*codeCapTolerance, error) {
	var all, rows []*codeCapTolerance
	for i := range d.Tolerances {
		if t := &d.Tolerances[i]; t.Letter == letter {
			all = append(all, t)
		}
	}
	if len(all) == 0 {
		for _, l := range d.NotChecked.Tolerance {
			if l == letter {
				return nil, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "the tolerance letter %s is not cross-checked (found in one source only)", letter)
			}
		}
		return nil, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "unknown tolerance letter %s", letter)
	}
	for _, t := range all {
		switch {
		case !hasCap, t.When == codeWhenAny:
			rows = append(rows, t)
		case capF < codeTenPicofarad && t.When == codeWhenLess, capF >= codeTenPicofarad && t.When == codeWhenAtLeast:
			rows = append(rows, t)
		}
	}
	if len(rows) == 0 {
		if capF < codeTenPicofarad {
			return nil, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "the tolerance letter %s is not cross-checked for a capacitance below 10 pF", letter)
		}
		return nil, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "the tolerance letter %s is not cross-checked for a capacitance of 10 pF or more", letter)
	}
	return rows, nil
}

func codeToleranceRowText(t *codeCapTolerance) string {
	switch {
	case t.Unit == "pf":
		return "±" + fmtSig(t.Minus, 6) + " pF"
	case t.Minus == t.Plus:
		return "±" + fmtSig(t.Minus, 6) + " %"
	}
	return "−" + fmtSig(t.Minus, 6) + " % / +" + fmtSig(t.Plus, 6) + " %"
}

// codeAddTolerance adds the tolerance field(s) for the rows of a letter: one row gives a value, several (a letter that means
// pF below 10 pF and percent above) give the readings in the text; an asymmetric tolerance also gives the two deviations.
func codeAddTolerance(res *CodeResult, rows []*codeCapTolerance, whenKnown bool) {
	if len(rows) > 1 {
		parts := make([]string, len(rows))
		for i, t := range rows {
			parts[i] = codeToleranceRowText(t) + codeWhenSuffix(t.When)
		}
		res.field("tolerance", "Tolerance", strings.Join(parts, " or "), math.NaN(), "")
		return
	}
	t := rows[0]
	text := codeToleranceRowText(t)
	if !whenKnown {
		text += codeWhenSuffix(t.When)
	}
	switch {
	case t.Unit == "pf":
		res.field("tolerance", "Tolerance", text, codeScaleDec(t.Minus, -12), "capacitance")
	case t.Minus == t.Plus:
		res.field("tolerance", "Tolerance", text, codeScaleDec(t.Minus, -2), "ratio")
	default:
		res.field("tolerance", "Tolerance", text, math.NaN(), "ratio")
		res.field("tolerance_minus", "Lower deviation", "−"+fmtSig(t.Minus, 6)+" %", codeScaleDec(-t.Minus, -2), "ratio")
		res.field("tolerance_plus", "Upper deviation", "+"+fmtSig(t.Plus, 6)+" %", codeScaleDec(t.Plus, -2), "ratio")
	}
}

func codeWhenSuffix(when string) string {
	switch when {
	case codeWhenLess:
		return " (C < 10 pF)"
	case codeWhenAtLeast:
		return " (C ≥ 10 pF)"
	}
	return ""
}

// codeCapToken is one recognised part of a capacitor marking: a value (with an optional trailing tolerance letter), a tolerance
// letter or a voltage code.
type codeCapToken struct {
	hasValue bool
	value    float64 // farad
	family   string
	canon    string // the part as it is written canonically ("104", "4p7", "R50")
	warning  string // a warning the value part brings with it
	letter   string // a tolerance letter (alone or behind the value)
	voltage  string // a voltage code
}

// classify recognises the shape of one part of the marking.
func (d *codeCapacitorData) classify(tok string) (codeCapToken, error) {
	m := codeCapRKMRe.FindStringSubmatch(tok)
	if m == nil {
		if m = codeCapRKMUpper.FindStringSubmatch(tok); m != nil {
			m[2] = strings.ToLower(m[2])
		}
	}
	if m != nil { // RKM: 4p7, 100n, 2µ2 (the letter is the decimal point and the prefix)
		t := codeCapToken{hasValue: true, value: codeDecimalText(m[1], m[3], d.rkm[m[2]]), family: "RKM notation", canon: m[1] + m[2] + m[3]}
		if m[4] != "" && !(m[4] == "F" && m[3] == "") { // 100nF is the unit farad, not the tolerance letter F
			t.letter = strings.ToUpper(m[4])
			t.canon += t.letter
		}
		return t, nil
	}
	up := strings.ToUpper(tok)
	switch {
	case codeCapVoltageRe.MatchString(up):
		if d.voltage[up] == nil {
			return codeCapToken{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "the voltage code %s is not a standard code (codes with a single source are left out; makers differ, for example Murata writes YA for 35 V)", up)
		}
		return codeCapToken{voltage: up, canon: up}, nil
	case codeCapLetterRe.MatchString(up):
		return codeCapToken{letter: up, canon: up}, nil
	case codeCapPairRe.MatchString(up):
		return codeCapToken{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "%s looks like a maker-specific voltage code (for example Murata YA = 35 V); only the common two-character codes are decoded", up)
	}
	if m := codeCapRRe.FindStringSubmatch(up); m != nil && len(m[1])+len(m[2]) > 0 { // R notation in pF: 4R7, R50, 0R5
		return codeCapToken{hasValue: true, value: codeDecimalText(m[1], m[2], -12), family: "R notation (pF)", canon: m[1] + "R" + m[2] + m[3], letter: m[3]}, nil
	}
	if m := codeCapDigitsRe.FindStringSubmatch(up); m != nil { // 3 digits: two significant digits and the multiplier
		n, _ := strconv.Atoi(m[1][:2])
		row := d.mult[m[1][2:]]
		if row == nil {
			for _, x := range d.NotChecked.Multiplier {
				if x == m[1][2:] {
					return codeCapToken{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "the multiplier digit %s is not cross-checked", x)
				}
			}
			return codeCapToken{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "unknown multiplier digit %s", m[1][2:])
		}
		t := codeCapToken{hasValue: true, value: codeDecimal(n, row.Exp-12), family: "3-digit pF code", canon: m[1] + m[2], letter: m[2]}
		if row.Maker != "" {
			t.warning = fmt.Sprintf("the third digit %s (×%s) follows the %s ordering convention for values below 10 pF", row.Digit, fmtNum(codeDecimal(1, row.Exp)), strings.ToUpper(row.Maker))
		}
		return t, nil
	}
	return codeCapToken{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "cannot read %q as a capacitor marking (value code, tolerance letter or voltage code)", tok)
}

func (d *codeCapacitorData) decode(u *Units, code string) (CodeResult, error) {
	tokens := strings.FieldsFunc(code, func(r rune) bool { return unicode.IsSpace(r) || r == ',' || r == ';' })
	if len(tokens) == 0 {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "the code is empty")
	}
	if len(tokens) > 3 {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "a capacitor marking has at most three parts (value code, tolerance letter, voltage code)")
	}
	res := codeNewResult("capacitor")
	var whole codeCapToken
	var canon []string
	for _, tok := range tokens {
		t, err := d.classify(tok)
		if err != nil {
			return CodeResult{}, err
		}
		switch {
		case t.hasValue && whole.hasValue:
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "more than one capacitance value in the code")
		case t.letter != "" && whole.letter != "":
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "more than one tolerance letter in the code")
		case t.voltage != "" && whole.voltage != "":
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "more than one voltage code in the code")
		}
		if t.hasValue {
			if !(t.value > 0) {
				return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "the code gives a capacitance of zero")
			}
			whole.hasValue, whole.value, whole.family = true, t.value, t.family
			if t.warning != "" {
				res.warn("%s", t.warning)
			}
		}
		if t.letter != "" {
			whole.letter = t.letter
		}
		if t.voltage != "" {
			whole.voltage = t.voltage
		}
		canon = append(canon, t.canon)
	}
	res.Code = strings.Join(canon, " ")
	if whole.hasValue {
		res.Value, res.Dim = whole.value, "capacitance"
		res.field("family", "Marking", whole.family, math.NaN(), "")
	}
	if whole.letter != "" {
		rows, err := d.toleranceRows(whole.letter, whole.value, whole.hasValue)
		if err != nil {
			return CodeResult{}, err
		}
		codeAddTolerance(&res, rows, whole.hasValue)
	}
	if whole.voltage != "" {
		d.addVoltage(&res, u, d.voltage[whole.voltage], !whole.hasValue)
	}
	return res, nil
}

// addVoltage adds the voltage field and the warnings that come with a voltage code; headline makes the voltage the value.
func (d *codeCapacitorData) addVoltage(res *CodeResult, u *Units, v *codeCapVoltage, headline bool) {
	res.field("voltage", "Rated voltage", u.Format(v.Volts, "voltage", "", 4), v.Volts, "voltage")
	if headline {
		res.Value, res.Dim = v.Volts, "voltage"
	}
	res.warn("voltage codes are a maker convention, not part of IEC 60062; check the datasheet (for example Murata writes YA for 35 V)")
	if len(v.Note) > 0 {
		res.warn("%s: %s", v.Code, v.Note["en"])
	}
}

// codeCapValueCode writes C (farad, two significant digits) as the 3-digit code or the R notation in pF; "" when it has none.
func codeCapValueCode(N, e int) string {
	ep := e + 12 // N * 10^ep is the value in pF
	switch {
	case ep >= 0 && ep <= 6:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%d%d", N, ep)
	case ep == -1:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%dR%d", N/10, N%10)
	case ep == -2:
		return fmt.Sprintf("R%d", N)
	}
	return ""
}

// codeCapRKMCode writes the value N*10^e farad in RKM notation (4p7, 100n, 2µ2): the letter is the decimal point.
func codeCapRKMCode(N, e int) string {
	prefixes := []struct {
		letter string
		exp    int
	}{{"m", -3}, {"µ", -6}, {"n", -9}, {"p", -12}}
	digits := strconv.Itoa(N)
	top := e + len(digits) - 1 // exponent of the leading digit
	pick := prefixes[len(prefixes)-1]
	for _, p := range prefixes {
		if top >= p.exp {
			pick = p
			break
		}
	}
	shift := e - pick.exp // the number is digits * 10^shift in the unit of the prefix
	whole, frac := digits, ""
	switch {
	case shift >= 0:
		whole = digits + strings.Repeat("0", shift)
	case -shift >= len(digits):
		whole, frac = "0", strings.Repeat("0", -shift-len(digits))+digits
	default:
		whole, frac = digits[:len(digits)+shift], digits[len(digits)+shift:]
	}
	frac = strings.TrimRight(frac, "0")
	return whole + pick.letter + frac
}

// tolerancePick finds the tolerance letter for an encode request given as a letter, "±0.25 pF", "10 %" or "-20/+80", the
// rows of that letter and the tolerance (percent) that selects the E-series (0 = do not snap).
func (d *codeCapacitorData) tolerancePick(s string, capF float64, hasCap bool) (letter string, rows []*codeCapTolerance, pct float64, err error) {
	t := strings.TrimSpace(s)
	match := func(ok func(*codeCapTolerance) bool) (string, []*codeCapTolerance) {
		for i := range d.Tolerances {
			x := &d.Tolerances[i]
			if !ok(x) {
				continue
			}
			if r, err := d.toleranceRows(x.Letter, capF, hasCap); err == nil {
				for _, y := range r {
					if y == x {
						return x.Letter, []*codeCapTolerance{x}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		return "", nil
	}
	fail := func() (string, []*codeCapTolerance, float64, error) {
		return "", nil, 0, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "no tolerance letter for %q (letters: %s)", s, d.letterList())
	}
	switch {
	case codeCapLetterRe.MatchString(strings.ToUpper(t)):
		l := strings.ToUpper(t)
		rows, err := d.toleranceRows(l, capF, hasCap)
		if err != nil {
			return "", nil, 0, err
		}
		if r := rows[0]; len(rows) == 1 && r.Unit == "pct" {
			pct = r.Minus
			if r.Minus != r.Plus {
				pct = 20 // an asymmetric tolerance belongs to the coarse E6 values
			}
		}
		return l, rows, pct, nil
	case strings.HasSuffix(strings.ToLower(codeCompact(t)), "pf"):
		c := codeCompact(t)
		x, ok := codeParsePercent(c[:len(c)-2])
		if !ok {
			return "", nil, 0, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "tolerance: cannot read %q", s)
		}
		l, r := match(func(y *codeCapTolerance) bool { return y.Unit == "pf" && codeCloseTo(y.Minus, x) })
		if l == "" {
			return fail()
		}
		return l, r, 0, nil
	}
	if plus, minus, ok := codeParseAsym(t); ok {
		l, r := match(func(y *codeCapTolerance) bool {
			return y.Unit == "pct" && codeCloseTo(y.Plus, plus) && codeCloseTo(y.Minus, minus)
		})
		if l == "" {
			return fail()
		}
		return l, r, 20, nil
	}
	p, ok := codeParsePercent(t)
	if !ok || p <= 0 {
		return "", nil, 0, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "tolerance: cannot read %q as a letter, a percentage, a value in pF or an asymmetric tolerance such as -20/+80", s)
	}
	l, r := match(func(y *codeCapTolerance) bool { return y.Unit == "pct" && y.Minus == y.Plus && codeCloseTo(y.Minus, p) })
	if l == "" {
		return fail()
	}
	return l, r, p, nil
}

func (d *codeCapacitorData) letterList() string {
	var out []string
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, t := range d.Tolerances {
		if !seen[t.Letter] {
			seen[t.Letter] = true
			out = append(out, t.Letter)
		}
	}
	return strings.Join(out, " ")
}

func (d *codeCapacitorData) encode(u *Units, req EncodeRequest) (CodeResult, error) {
	hasValue := strings.TrimSpace(req.Value) != ""
	hasTol := strings.TrimSpace(req.Tolerance) != ""
	hasVolt := strings.TrimSpace(req.Voltage) != ""
	if !hasValue && !hasTol && !hasVolt {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "give a value, a tolerance or a voltage")
	}
	res := codeNewResult("capacitor")
	var parts []string
	var capV float64
	if hasValue {
		v, err := u.Parse(req.Value, "capacitance", "")
		if err != nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "value: %v", err)
		}
		if !(v > 0) {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "value: the capacitance must be positive")
		}
		capV = v
	}
	var letter string
	var rows []*codeCapTolerance
	pct := 0.0
	if hasTol {
		var err error
		if letter, rows, pct, err = d.tolerancePick(req.Tolerance, capV, hasValue); err != nil {
			return CodeResult{}, err
		}
	}
	if hasValue {
		vs := capV
		changed := false
		if pct > 0 {
			var err error
			if vs, changed, err = codeSnapToSeries(capV, pct); err != nil {
				return CodeResult{}, err
			}
		}
		N, e, exact := codeSigDigits(vs, 2)
		if !exact {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "%s needs more than 2 significant digits; the 3-digit capacitor code holds 2", u.Format(vs, "capacitance", "", 4))
		}
		vc := codeCapValueCode(N, e)
		if vc == "" {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "%s is outside the range of the capacitor code (%s to %s)", u.Format(vs, "capacitance", "", 4), u.Format(codeDecimal(10, -13), "capacitance", "", 4), u.Format(codeDecimal(99, -6), "capacitance", "", 4))
		}
		res.Value, res.Dim = codeDecimal(N, e), "capacitance"
		res.field("value_code", "Value code", vc, math.NaN(), "")
		res.field("rkm", "RKM notation", codeCapRKMCode(N, e), math.NaN(), "")
		parts = append(parts, vc+letter)
		if changed {
			res.warn("%s", codeSnapWarning(u, "capacitance", capV, vs, pct))
		}
	} else if letter != "" {
		parts = append(parts, letter)
	}
	if letter != "" {
		codeAddTolerance(&res, rows, hasValue)
	}
	if hasVolt {
		v, err := u.Parse(req.Voltage, "voltage", "")
		if err != nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "voltage: %v", err)
		}
		var row *codeCapVoltage
		for i := range d.Voltages {
			if codeCloseTo(d.Voltages[i].Volts, v) {
				row = &d.Voltages[i]
			}
		}
		if row == nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "no standard voltage code for %s", u.Format(v, "voltage", "", 4))
		}
		d.addVoltage(&res, u, row, !hasValue)
		parts = append(parts, row.Code)
	}
	res.Code = strings.Join(parts, " ")
	return res, nil
}
```

```go
package ecalc

import (
	"fmt"
	"math"
	"regexp"
	"strings"

	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

// The ceramic_temp kind: the EIA-198 temperature characteristics of ceramic capacitors. A class 1 code (C0G, U2J) is a
// letter for the significant figure of the temperature coefficient, a digit for the multiplier and a letter for the
// tolerance, in ppm/K; a class 2 code (X7R, Y5V) is a letter for the lower and a digit for the upper category temperature
// and a letter for the capacitance change over that range. The letters and digits that only one source lists are not in
// the data (not_cross_checked names them so that the decoder can say so).

type codeCeramicSig struct {
	Letter string  `yaml:"letter" json:"letter"`
	Value  float64 `yaml:"value" json:"value"` // the significant figure
}

type codeCeramicMult struct {
	Digit string  `yaml:"digit" json:"digit"`
	Value float64 `yaml:"value" json:"value"` // the multiplier
}

type codeCeramicTol struct {
	Letter string  `yaml:"letter" json:"letter"`
	PPM    float64 `yaml:"ppm" json:"ppm"`
}

type codeCeramicLow struct {
	Letter string  `yaml:"letter" json:"letter"`
	C      float64 `yaml:"c" json:"c"`
}

type codeCeramicHigh struct {
	Digit string  `yaml:"digit" json:"digit"`
	C     float64 `yaml:"c" json:"c"`
}

type codeCeramicChange struct {
	Letter string  `yaml:"letter" json:"letter"`
	Plus   float64 `yaml:"plus" json:"plus"`
	Minus  float64 `yaml:"minus" json:"minus"`
}

type codeCeramicClass1 struct {
	Sig  []codeCeramicSig  `yaml:"sig" json:"sig"`
	Mult []codeCeramicMult `yaml:"mult" json:"mult"`
	Tol  []codeCeramicTol  `yaml:"tol" json:"tol"`
}

type codeCeramicClass2 struct {
	Low    []codeCeramicLow    `yaml:"low" json:"low"`
	High   []codeCeramicHigh   `yaml:"high" json:"high"`
	Change []codeCeramicChange `yaml:"change" json:"change"`
}

type codeCeramicAlias struct {
	Name string `yaml:"name" json:"name"`
	Code string `yaml:"code" json:"code"`
}

type codeCeramicIndustry struct {
	Code string `yaml:"code" json:"code"`
	Name string `yaml:"name" json:"name"`
}

type codeCeramicNotChecked struct {
	C1Sig    []string `yaml:"c1_sig" json:"c1_sig"`
	C1Mult   []string `yaml:"c1_mult" json:"c1_mult"`
	C2High   []string `yaml:"c2_high" json:"c2_high"`
	C2Change []string `yaml:"c2_change" json:"c2_change"`
}

type codeCeramicData struct {
	Class1     codeCeramicClass1     `yaml:"class1"`
	Class2     codeCeramicClass2     `yaml:"class2"`
	Aliases    []codeCeramicAlias    `yaml:"aliases"`
	Industry   []codeCeramicIndustry `yaml:"industry"`
	NotChecked codeCeramicNotChecked `yaml:"not_cross_checked"`
	Common     []string              `yaml:"common"`
	Notes      []Text                `yaml:"notes"`

	sig      map[string]*codeCeramicSig
	mult     map[string]*codeCeramicMult
	tol      map[string]*codeCeramicTol
	low      map[string]*codeCeramicLow
	high     map[string]*codeCeramicHigh
	change   map[string]*codeCeramicChange
	industry map[string]string
}

func codeLoadCeramicTemp(raw *yaml.Node, fail func(string, ...any)) any {
	var d codeCeramicData
	if err := decodeNode(raw, &d); err != nil {
		fail("data: %v", err)
		return nil
	}
	d.sig, d.mult, d.tol = map[string]*codeCeramicSig{}, map[string]*codeCeramicMult{}, map[string]*codeCeramicTol{}
	d.low, d.high, d.change, d.industry = map[string]*codeCeramicLow{}, map[string]*codeCeramicHigh{}, map[string]*codeCeramicChange{}, map[string]string{}
	oneChar := func(what, s string, isLetter bool) bool {
		ok := len(s) == 1 && ((isLetter && s >= "A" && s <= "Z") || (!isLetter && s >= "0" && s <= "9"))
		if !ok {
			fail("data: %s: %q must be a single %s", what, s, map[bool]string{true: "capital letter", false: "digit"}[isLetter])
		}
		return ok
	}
	for i := range d.Class1.Sig {
		x := &d.Class1.Sig[i]
		if oneChar("class1.sig", x.Letter, true) && d.sig[x.Letter] == nil && x.Value >= 0 {
			d.sig[x.Letter] = x
		} else {
			fail("data: class1.sig[%d]: a unique letter and a figure of 0 or more are required", i)
		}
	}
	for i := range d.Class1.Mult {
		x := &d.Class1.Mult[i]
		if oneChar("class1.mult", x.Digit, false) && d.mult[x.Digit] == nil && x.Value != 0 {
			d.mult[x.Digit] = x
		} else {
			fail("data: class1.mult[%d]: a unique digit and a multiplier other than 0 are required", i)
		}
	}
	for i := range d.Class1.Tol {
		x := &d.Class1.Tol[i]
		if oneChar("class1.tol", x.Letter, true) && d.tol[x.Letter] == nil && x.PPM > 0 {
			d.tol[x.Letter] = x
		} else {
			fail("data: class1.tol[%d]: a unique letter and a positive tolerance are required", i)
		}
	}
	for i := range d.Class2.Low {
		x := &d.Class2.Low[i]
		if oneChar("class2.low", x.Letter, true) && d.low[x.Letter] == nil {
			d.low[x.Letter] = x
		} else {
			fail("data: class2.low[%d]: a unique letter is required", i)
		}
	}
	for i := range d.Class2.High {
		x := &d.Class2.High[i]
		if oneChar("class2.high", x.Digit, false) && d.high[x.Digit] == nil {
			d.high[x.Digit] = x
		} else {
			fail("data: class2.high[%d]: a unique digit is required", i)
		}
	}
	for i := range d.Class2.Change {
		x := &d.Class2.Change[i]
		if oneChar("class2.change", x.Letter, true) && d.change[x.Letter] == nil && x.Plus > 0 && x.Minus > 0 {
			d.change[x.Letter] = x
		} else {
			fail("data: class2.change[%d]: a unique letter and positive deviations are required", i)
		}
	}
	if len(d.sig) == 0 || len(d.mult) == 0 || len(d.tol) == 0 || len(d.low) == 0 || len(d.high) == 0 || len(d.change) == 0 {
		fail("data: every table of class1 and class2 must be filled")
	}
	for _, a := range d.Aliases {
		if a.Name == "" || len(a.Code) != 3 {
			fail("data: aliases: a name and a 3-character code are required")
		}
	}
	for _, x := range d.Industry {
		if len(x.Code) != 3 || x.Name == "" {
			fail("data: industry: a 3-character code and a name are required")
		}
		d.industry[x.Code] = x.Name
	}
	for _, c := range d.Common {
		if len(c) != 3 {
			fail("data: common: %q is not a 3-character code", c)
		}
	}
	codeCheckNotes(fail, d.Notes)
	return &d
}

type codeCeramicDoc struct {
	Class1     codeCeramicClass1     `json:"class1"`
	Class2     codeCeramicClass2     `json:"class2"`
	Aliases    []codeCeramicAlias    `json:"aliases"`
	Industry   []codeCeramicIndustry `json:"industry"`
	NotChecked codeCeramicNotChecked `json:"not_cross_checked"`
	Common     []string              `json:"common"`
	Notes      []string              `json:"notes"`
}

func codeCeramicTempJSON(data any, lang string) any {
	d := data.(*codeCeramicData)
	return codeCeramicDoc{
		Class1:  codeCeramicClass1{Sig: orEmpty(d.Class1.Sig), Mult: orEmpty(d.Class1.Mult), Tol: orEmpty(d.Class1.Tol)},
		Class2:  codeCeramicClass2{Low: orEmpty(d.Class2.Low), High: orEmpty(d.Class2.High), Change: orEmpty(d.Class2.Change)},
		Aliases: orEmpty(d.Aliases), Industry: orEmpty(d.Industry),
		NotChecked: codeCeramicNotChecked{C1Sig: orEmpty(d.NotChecked.C1Sig), C1Mult: orEmpty(d.NotChecked.C1Mult), C2High: orEmpty(d.NotChecked.C2High), C2Change: orEmpty(d.NotChecked.C2Change)},
		Common:     orEmpty(d.Common), Notes: codeLocalizedNotes(d.Notes, lang),
	}
}

// codeListed reports whether s is one of the symbols.
func codeListed(symbols []string, s string) bool { return contains(symbols, s) }

// codeNotCheckedErr is the error for a symbol that only one source lists.
func codeNotCheckedErr(what, symbol string) error {
	return codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "%s %s is not cross-checked (found in one source only)", what, symbol)
}

func (d *codeCeramicData) decode(u *Units, code string) (CodeResult, error) {
	s := strings.NewReplacer("-", "", "_", "").Replace(strings.ToUpper(strings.Join(strings.Fields(code), "")))
	for _, a := range d.Aliases {
		if s == a.Name {
			s = a.Code
		}
	}
	r := []rune(s)
	if len(r) == 3 && r[1] == 'O' && !strings.ContainsRune("XYZ", r[0]) {
		r[1] = '0' // COG for C0G
	}
	if len(r) != 3 {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "a ceramic temperature code has 3 characters (for example X7R or C0G)")
	}
	a, b, c := string(r[0]), string(r[1]), string(r[2])
	canon := a + b + c
	res := codeNewResult("ceramic_temp")
	res.Code = canon
	if strings.Contains("XYZ", a) {
		low, high, change := d.low[a], d.high[b], d.change[c]
		if high == nil {
			if codeListed(d.NotChecked.C2High, b) {
				return CodeResult{}, codeNotCheckedErr("the upper temperature digit", b)
			}
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "unknown upper temperature digit %s", b)
		}
		if change == nil {
			if codeListed(d.NotChecked.C2Change, c) {
				return CodeResult{}, codeNotCheckedErr("the capacitance change letter", c)
			}
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "unknown capacitance change letter %s", c)
		}
		res.field("class", "Class", "2", math.NaN(), "")
		res.field("temp_low", "Lower category temperature", codeSignedText(low.C, 6)+" °C", roundSig(low.C+273.15, 12), "temperature")
		res.field("temp_high", "Upper category temperature", codeSignedText(high.C, 6)+" °C", roundSig(high.C+273.15, 12), "temperature")
		if change.Plus == change.Minus {
			res.field("change", "Capacitance change", "±"+fmtSig(change.Plus, 6)+" %", codeScaleDec(change.Plus, -2), "ratio")
		} else {
			res.field("change", "Capacitance change", "+"+fmtSig(change.Plus, 6)+" % / −"+fmtSig(change.Minus, 6)+" %", math.NaN(), "ratio")
			res.field("change_plus", "Upper capacitance change", "+"+fmtSig(change.Plus, 6)+" %", codeScaleDec(change.Plus, -2), "ratio")
			res.field("change_minus", "Lower capacitance change", "−"+fmtSig(change.Minus, 6)+" %", codeScaleDec(-change.Minus, -2), "ratio")
		}
		return res, nil
	}
	sig, mult, tol := d.sig[a], d.mult[b], d.tol[c]
	if sig == nil {
		if codeListed(d.NotChecked.C1Sig, a) {
			return CodeResult{}, codeNotCheckedErr("the temperature coefficient letter", a)
		}
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "unknown temperature coefficient letter %s", a)
	}
	if mult == nil {
		if codeListed(d.NotChecked.C1Mult, b) {
			return CodeResult{}, codeNotCheckedErr("the multiplier digit", b)
		}
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "unknown multiplier digit %s", b)
	}
	if tol == nil {
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidCode, "unknown tolerance letter %s", c)
	}
	tc := sig.Value * mult.Value
	if tc == 0 {
		tc = 0 // no negative zero
	}
	res.Value, res.Dim = codeScaleDec(tc, -6), "tempco"
	res.field("class", "Class", "1", math.NaN(), "")
	res.field("tc", "Temperature coefficient", codeSignedText(tc, 6)+" ppm/K", codeScaleDec(tc, -6), "tempco")
	res.field("tolerance", "Tolerance", "±"+fmtSig(tol.PPM, 6)+" ppm/K", codeScaleDec(tol.PPM, -6), "tempco")
	if name := d.industry[canon]; name != "" {
		res.field("industry_code", "Industry code", name, math.NaN(), "")
	}
	return res, nil
}

var codeRangeRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^(.+?)\s*(?:\.\.|…|\bto\b)\s*(.+)$`)

// codeCelsius reads a temperature typed in °C (a bare number is in °C) and returns it in °C.
func codeCelsius(u *Units, s string) (float64, error) {
	k, err := u.Parse(strings.ReplaceAll(s, "−", "-"), "temperature", "degC")
	return k - 273.15, err
}

func (d *codeCeramicData) encode(u *Units, req EncodeRequest) (CodeResult, error) {
	class := strings.TrimSpace(req.Class)
	if class == "" {
		switch {
		case codeRangeRe.MatchString(req.Value):
			class = "2"
		case strings.TrimSpace(req.TempCo) != "" || strings.TrimSpace(req.Value) != "":
			class = "1"
		default:
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "give the class (1 or 2)")
		}
	}
	var code string
	switch class {
	case "1":
		src := req.TempCo
		if strings.TrimSpace(src) == "" {
			src = req.Value
		}
		if strings.TrimSpace(src) == "" || strings.TrimSpace(req.Tolerance) == "" {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "class 1 needs the temperature coefficient (tempco, for example -750ppm) and the tolerance (for example 120ppm)")
		}
		tcSI, err := codeParseTempco(u, src)
		if err != nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "tempco: %v", err)
		}
		tolSI, err := codeParseTempco(u, req.Tolerance)
		if err != nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "tolerance: %v", err)
		}
		tc, tolPPM := tcSI/1e-6, math.Abs(tolSI)/1e-6
		var sigL, multD, tolL string
		for _, x := range d.Class1.Sig {
			for _, m := range d.Class1.Mult {
				if p := x.Value * m.Value; sigL == "" && ((tc == 0 && p == 0) || (tc != 0 && p != 0 && codeCloseTo(p, tc))) {
					sigL, multD = x.Letter, m.Digit
				}
			}
		}
		if sigL == "" {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "no class 1 code for a temperature coefficient of %s ppm/K", fmtSig(tc, 6))
		}
		for _, x := range d.Class1.Tol {
			if tolL == "" && codeCloseTo(x.PPM, tolPPM) {
				tolL = x.Letter
			}
		}
		if tolL == "" {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "no class 1 tolerance letter for ±%s ppm/K", fmtSig(tolPPM, 6))
		}
		code = sigL + multD + tolL
	case "2":
		m := codeRangeRe.FindStringSubmatch(req.Value)
		if m == nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "class 2 needs the category temperature range in value, for example -55..125")
		}
		lo, err := codeCelsius(u, m[1])
		if err != nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "value: %v", err)
		}
		hi, err := codeCelsius(u, m[2])
		if err != nil {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "value: %v", err)
		}
		var lowL, highD, changeL string
		for _, x := range d.Class2.Low {
			if lowL == "" && math.Abs(x.C-lo) < 1e-6 {
				lowL = x.Letter
			}
		}
		if lowL == "" {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "no class 2 letter for a lower category temperature of %s °C", fmtSig(lo, 6))
		}
		for _, x := range d.Class2.High {
			if highD == "" && math.Abs(x.C-hi) < 1e-6 {
				highD = x.Digit
			}
		}
		if highD == "" {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "no class 2 digit for an upper category temperature of %s °C", fmtSig(hi, 6))
		}
		if strings.TrimSpace(req.Tolerance) == "" {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "class 2 needs the capacitance change in tolerance, for example 15%% or +22/-82")
		}
		plus, minus := 0.0, 0.0
		if p, mi, ok := codeParseAsym(req.Tolerance); ok {
			plus, minus = p, mi
		} else if p, ok := codeParsePercent(req.Tolerance); ok {
			plus, minus = p, p
		} else {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "tolerance: cannot read %q as a percentage or as an asymmetric change such as +22/-82", req.Tolerance)
		}
		for _, x := range d.Class2.Change {
			if changeL == "" && codeCloseTo(x.Plus, plus) && codeCloseTo(x.Minus, minus) {
				changeL = x.Letter
			}
		}
		if changeL == "" {
			return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeUnsupported, "no class 2 letter for a capacitance change of %s", fmt.Sprintf("+%s %% / −%s %%", fmtSig(plus, 6), fmtSig(minus, 6)))
		}
		code = lowL + highD + changeL
	default:
		return CodeResult{}, codeErr(CodeInvalidValue, "class must be 1 or 2")
	}
	return d.decode(u, code)
}
```

### Task K2: The JavaScript mirror and the parity script

**Goal:** `window.ECalcCore.codes = {decode(item, code, units), encode(item, req, units)}` gives, for the code items of the catalog JSON, the same results as Go (code, bands, value, dimension, fields, English warnings) and throws an `Error` with `code` `invalid_code`, `invalid_value` or `unsupported`; `npm run test:ecalc` runs the core script and the new codes script.

**Files:**

- Create: `scripts/test-ecalc-codes.mjs`, `ui/js/desktop/apps/ecalc/ecalc-codes.js`
- Modify: `package.json`

**Behaviour fixed by this task:**

- The script runs `ecalc-expr.js`, `ecalc-units.js`, `ecalc-eseries.js` and `ecalc-codes.js` in a Node vm without a document, takes the code items from `internal/ecalc/testdata/catalog.en.json`, freezes them deeply (a codec that changes its data fails), and runs every vector of `codes.json`: results are compared field by field (numbers at a relative error of 1e-12), errors by code and message fragment (the message carries no `code:` prefix), every vector needs a `ref`, and every kind needs at least 8 decode, 8 encode and 8 error vectors. It also checks that a result is plain JSON (no NaN, no undefined), that missing request fields default, and a round trip over the E12 values.
- `ecalc-codes.js` is a classic script that adds `codes` to `window.ECalcCore`; it reads `ECalcCore.units` (for `format`, `parse`, `fmtSig`, `roundSig`) and `ECalcCore.eseries` (`nearest`, `TABLES`) when a function is called, so it can load anywhere after `ecalc-eseries.js`.
