### Task B1: Search, resolve and describe tables and codes

**Goal:** the query API sees all three kinds of items. `SearchAll`/`Search` rank calculators, tables and codes together (equal ranks keep the catalog order: calculators, tables, codes); a hit says its `kind`. `Overview` counts the items of every kind and leaves out categories without items. `ResolveItem` finds an item of any kind by id; the id of an item of another kind gets an error that names the right operation instead of "unknown calculator"; `DescribeTable` describes a table.

**GitNexus (before editing):** `SearchAll` LOW (4 impacted: `Search`, the `lookup` of query.go, `Describe`; one caller outside the package, `ecalcSearch` of `internal/tools/ecalc.go`), `searchFieldsOf` LOW (3), `Overview` and `Describe` UNKNOWN in the index (several symbols of that name) and confirmed by `grep -rn "\.Overview(\|\.Describe(\|\.SearchAll(" internal cmd`: only `internal/tools/ecalc.go` calls them; `lookup` (method) is called by `Describe` and `resolve` only.

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/ecalc/query_items_test.go`, `internal/ecalc/query_items.go`
- Modify: `internal/ecalc/query_test.go`, `internal/ecalc/query.go`

**Behaviour fixed by this task** (all covered by the tests below):

- `SearchAll("")` lists every item in catalog order; a table or a code is ranked by id, name (16 locales), tags and category exactly like a calculator; `SearchHit.Kind` is `calculator`, `table` or `code`; the summary is the first sentence of the doc, or for an item without doc `Table with N rows; columns: …` / `Component code of kind …`.
- `Overview` counts all items per category and omits categories with no item; `ItemCount` is the total.
- `ResolveItem(id)` returns the kind and the canonical (lower-case) id; an unknown id suggests up to three hits of any kind; `Describe`, `Calculate` and `Check` on a table or code id answer `not_a_calculator` (`awg is a table, not a calculator; describe lists its columns and table reads its rows`).
- `DescribeTable` returns id, kind, category, group, name, doc, notes, source, `guide`/`mains` with a `caution`, key, `row_count`, `columns` (`id name dim unit units key`) and the `finder`.

```go
// suggestedIDs reads the ids out of "...; did you mean a, b, c?" (none when the message has no suggestions).
func suggestedIDs(message string) []string {
	_, list, ok := strings.Cut(message, "did you mean ")
	if !ok {
		return nil
	}
	return strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSpace(list), "?"), ", ")
}

func derefAll(row []*string) []string {
	out := make([]string, len(row))
	for i, p := range row {
		out[i] = "<null>"
		if p != nil {
			out[i] = *p
		}
	}
	return out

func TestResolveItemAndTheErrorsOfTheWrongKind(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryFixture(t)
	for id, want := range map[string]string{" T_AMP ": "table", "t_code": "code"} {
		kind, canonical, err := cat.ResolveItem(id)
		if err != nil || kind != want || canonical != strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(id)) {
			t.Errorf("ResolveItem(%q) = %q %q %v", id, kind, canonical, err)
		}
	}
	real := queryCatalog(t)
	if kind, id, err := real.ResolveItem("Voltage_Divider"); err != nil || kind != "calculator" || id != "voltage_divider" {
		t.Errorf("ResolveItem(Voltage_Divider) = %q %q %v", kind, id, err)
	}
	_, _, err := real.ResolveItem("")
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownID, "id is required", "calculator, table or code")
	_, _, err = real.ResolveItem("awg_wire")
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownID, `unknown id "awg_wire"`, "did you mean", "awg")

	// The id of an item of another kind says what it is and which operation reads it.
	_, err = cat.Describe("t_amp")
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeNotACalculator, "t_amp is a table, not a calculator", "table reads its rows")
	_, err = cat.Calculate("t_code", CalcRequest{})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeNotACalculator, "t_code is a code, not a calculator", "decode and encode")
	_, err = cat.Check("t_amp", CalcRequest{})
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeNotACalculator)
	_, err = real.DescribeTable("voltage_divider")
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeNotATable, "voltage_divider is a calculator, not a table", "describe and calculate")
	// An unknown id suggests items of the wanted kind only. Which other tables are suggested depends on the content of
	// the catalog, so the tests look at the list, not at its wording or order.
	_, err = real.DescribeTable("awg_table")
	qe := wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownID, `unknown table "awg_table"`, "did you mean")
	if got := suggestedIDs(qe.Message); !slices.Contains(got, "awg") || len(got) > 3 {
		t.Errorf("suggestions %v of %q, want at most three and awg among them", got, qe.Message)
	}
	_, err = real.DescribeTable("awg_conv")
	qe = wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownID, `unknown table "awg_conv"`)
	for _, id := range suggestedIDs(qe.Message) {
		if kind, _ := real.Item(id); kind != "table" {
			t.Errorf("only tables are suggested for a table, got the %s %s: %s", kind, id, qe.Message)
		}
	}
	_, err = real.DescribeTable("")
	wantQueryError(t, err, CodeUnknownID, "id is required", "table id")
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: implement**

Create `internal/ecalc/query_items.go` with exactly this content:

```go
package ecalc

import (
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"strings"
)

// The query API of the items that are not calculators, next to the calculator queries of query.go: Search, SearchAll and
// Overview list items of all three kinds (searchItems), ResolveItem finds an item of any kind, and DescribeTable
// describes a table. The rows of a table are in query_table.go, the component codes in query_codes.go. Output texts are
// English; the structs carry JSON tags because the tool sends them as they are.

// The cautions the tables carry: guide marks values transcribed from a standard, mains marks installation data.
const (
	guideCaution = "Guide values from the cited source; the standard itself is authoritative."
	mainsCaution = "Mains installation data: the applicable national rules decide, and installation work is for qualified persons."
)

// ---- items of every kind ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// searchItem is what the search needs to know about an item of any kind. fallback is the summary of an item without a
// doc text.
type searchItem struct {
	id, kind, category string
	name, doc          Text
	tags               []string
	fallback           string
}

func (it searchItem) summary() string {
	if s := firstSentence(it.doc.in("en")); s != "" {
		return s
	}
	return firstSentence(it.fallback)
}

// searchItems lists every item in catalog order: the calculators, then the tables, then the codes.
func (c *Catalog) searchItems() []searchItem {
	items := make([]searchItem, 0, c.ItemCount())
	for _, calc := range c.Calculators {
		items = append(items, searchItem{id: calc.ID, kind: calc.Kind, category: calc.Category, name: calc.Name, doc: calc.Doc, tags: calc.Tags})
	}
	for _, t := range c.Tables {
		names := make([]string, len(t.Columns))
		for i, col := range t.Columns {
			names[i] = col.Name.in("en")
		}
		items = append(items, searchItem{
			id: t.ID, kind: "table", category: t.Category, name: t.Name, doc: t.Doc, tags: t.Tags,
			fallback: fmt.Sprintf("Table with %d rows; columns: %s.", len(t.Rows), strings.Join(names, ", ")),
		})
	}
	for _, k := range c.Codes {
		items = append(items, searchItem{
			id: k.ID, kind: "code", category: k.Category, name: k.Name, doc: k.Doc, tags: k.Tags,
			fallback: fmt.Sprintf("Component code of kind %s.", k.CodeKind),
		})
	}
	return items
}

// ItemCount is the number of items of all kinds.
func (c *Catalog) ItemCount() int { return len(c.Calculators) + len(c.Tables) + len(c.Codes) }

// ---- describe -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// TableColumnInfo describes one column of a table. Unit is the symbol of the unit the cells are shown in; it is empty
// for text, for plain numbers and for a column whose cells carry their own prefix (4.7 kΩ, 250 µm). Units, given by
// DescribeTable, are the units a column may be shown in.
type TableColumnInfo struct {
	ID    string   `json:"id"`
	Name  string   `json:"name"`
	Dim   string   `json:"dim"`
	Unit  string   `json:"unit,omitempty"`
	Units []string `json:"units,omitempty"`
	Key   bool     `json:"key,omitempty"`
}

// TableFinderInfo is the calculator that selects a row of the table: its variable Var, solved with the fixed Choices,
// is looked up in Column.
type TableFinderInfo struct {
	Calculator string       `json:"calculator"`
	Column     string       `json:"column"`
	Var        string       `json:"var"`
	Choices    []NamedValue `json:"choices,omitempty"`
}

// TableDescription is what DescribeTable returns.
type TableDescription struct {
	ID       string            `json:"id"`
	Kind     string            `json:"kind"`
	Category string            `json:"category"`
	Group    string            `json:"group"`
	Name     string            `json:"name"`
	Doc      string            `json:"doc,omitempty"`
	Notes    string            `json:"notes,omitempty"`
	Source   string            `json:"source"`
	Guide    bool              `json:"guide,omitempty"`
	Mains    bool              `json:"mains,omitempty"`
	Caution  string            `json:"caution,omitempty"`
	Key      string            `json:"key"`
	RowCount int               `json:"row_count"`
	Columns  []TableColumnInfo `json:"columns"`
	Finder   *TableFinderInfo  `json:"finder,omitempty"`
}

func (t *Table) caution() string {
	var parts []string
	if t.Guide {
		parts = append(parts, guideCaution)
	}
	if t.Mains {
		parts = append(parts, mainsCaution)
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, " ")
}

// columnInfo lists the columns of a table; withUnits adds the display units each column offers.
func (c *Catalog) columnInfo(t *Table, withUnits bool) []TableColumnInfo {
	out := make([]TableColumnInfo, len(t.Columns))
	for i := range t.Columns {
		col := &t.Columns[i]
		info := TableColumnInfo{ID: col.ID, Name: col.Name.in("en"), Dim: col.Dim, Key: i == t.keyIdx}
		if col.Unit != "" {
			info.Unit = c.unitSymbol(col.Dim, col.Unit)
		}
		if withUnits {
			info.Units = c.unitSymbols(&Var{Dim: col.Dim, Units: col.Units})
		}
		out[i] = info
	}
	return out
}

// lookupTable finds a table by id (case-insensitive). The error of an unknown id suggests the best search hits of the
// tables; the id of a calculator or a code says what it is.
func (c *Catalog) lookupTable(id string) (*Table, error) {
	key := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(id))
	if key == "" {
		return nil, queryErr(CodeUnknownID, "id is required; use search to find a table id")
	}
	if t := c.Table(key); t != nil {
		return t, nil
	}
	return nil, c.notFound(id, key, "table")
}

// DescribeTable returns the structure of a table: columns with units, the key column, the number of rows, the notes,
// the cautions of guide and mains tables and the finder calculator.
func (c *Catalog) DescribeTable(id string) (TableDescription, error) {
	t, err := c.lookupTable(id)
	if err != nil {
		return TableDescription{}, err
	}
```

```go
// notFound is the error of an id that is no item of the wanted kind ("calculator", "table", "code" or "" for any). The
// id of an item of another kind says what it is; an unknown id suggests the best search hits of the wanted kind.
func (c *Catalog) notFound(id, key, want string) *QueryError {
	if kind, ok := c.Item(key); ok {
		hint := map[string]string{
			"calculator": "describe and calculate work on it",
			"table":      "describe lists its columns and table reads its rows",
			"code":       "describe lists its code kind, and decode and encode work on that kind",
		}[kind]
		code := map[string]string{"calculator": CodeNotACalculator, "table": CodeNotATable, "code": CodeNotACode}[want]
		return queryErr(code, "%s is a %s, not a %s; %s", key, kind, want, hint)
	}
	label := want
	if label == "" {
		label = "calculator, table or code"
	}
	msg := fmt.Sprintf("unknown %s %q; use search to find a %s id", want, id, label)
	if want == "" {
		msg = fmt.Sprintf("unknown id %q; use search to find a %s id", id, label)
	}
	var ids []string
	for _, h := range c.SearchAll(strings.NewReplacer("_", " ", "-", " ").Replace(key)) {
		if want == "" || h.Kind == want {
			ids = append(ids, h.ID)
		}
		if len(ids) == 3 {
			break
		}
	}
	if len(ids) > 0 {
		msg += "; did you mean " + strings.Join(ids, ", ") + "?"
	}
	return &QueryError{Code: CodeUnknownID, Message: msg}
}

// ResolveItem finds an item of any kind by id (case-insensitive) and returns its kind ("calculator", "table" or
// "code") and its canonical id. The error of an unknown id suggests the best search hits.
func (c *Catalog) ResolveItem(id string) (kind, canonical string, err error) {
	key := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(id))
	if key == "" {
		return "", "", queryErr(CodeUnknownID, "id is required; use search to find a calculator, table or code id")
	}
	if kind, ok := c.Item(key); ok {
		return kind, key, nil
	}
	return "", "", c.notFound(id, key, "")
}
```

### Task B2: Table rows, filter, paging and lookups (`QueryTable`)

**Goal:** `QueryTable(id, TableRequest{Filter, Offset, Limit, Lookup})` returns a `TableResult`: the rows that match the filter (a substring, ignoring case, of any cell as it is written in the answer, text cells in English or German), one page of them (`Limit` 0 means 20, at most 50), the formatted and SI cells, and the result of one lookup (`exact`, `ge`, `interp`). `TableResult.Keep(n)` shortens the listed rows and keeps `returned`, `truncated` and `next_offset` consistent (the tool uses it to fit the budget).

**GitNexus:** new symbols only (`QueryTable`, `TableRequest`, `TableLookup`, `TableResult`, `LookupResult`); nothing existing is modified.

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/ecalc/query_table_test.go`, `internal/ecalc/query_table.go`

The tests use the fixture table `t_amp` of `query_items_test.go` (a key in mm², a current with an empty cell, a temperature in degC that is not monotonic, a text column with a plain, a localized and an empty string), the table fixture `t_dec` (a falling x column) of part A, and the generated tables of the default catalog: AWG 10 has 2.588 mm and 5.261 mm² (ASTM B258) and 3.277 ohm per km of copper, AWG 12 has 2.053 mm, the interpolation between two rows of IPC-2221 is the mean of the two widths, and 4.7 is a value of E3, E6, E12 and E24.

```go
	// 128 characters are fine, 129 are not (characters, not bytes).
	if _, err := cat.QueryTable("t_amp", TableRequest{Filter: strings.Repeat("ä", MaxFilterLength)}); err != nil {

func lookupOf(t *testing.T, cat *Catalog, id string, lk TableLookup) *LookupResult {
	t.Helper()
	res, err := cat.QueryTable(id, TableRequest{Lookup: &lk})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%+v: %v", lk, err)
	}
	if res.Lookup == nil {
		t.Fatalf("%+v: no lookup result", lk)
	}
	if res.Rows != nil || res.Returned != 0 || !strings.Contains(res.Note, "Only the lookup was answered") || res.Total != len(cat.Table(id).Rows) {
		t.Errorf("%+v: a lookup alone lists no rows: %+v", lk, res)
	}
	return res.Lookup
}

	cat := queryFixture(t)
	// The key column is the default column; a bare number is in the unit of the column, any unit of the dimension works.
	for _, value := range []string{"2.5", "2.5 mm2", "2.5mm2", "0.0000025 m²"} {
		l := lookupOf(t, cat, "t_amp", TableLookup{Value: value, Output: "amps"})
		if !l.Found || l.Mode != "exact" || l.Column != "section" || l.Value != "2.5 mm²" || l.Output != "amps" || l.Result != "19.5 A" || l.SI == nil || *l.SI != 19.5 ||
			strings.Join(derefAll(l.Row), "|") != "2.5 mm²|19.5 A|70 °C|see note" || l.Message != "" {
			t.Errorf("value %q: %+v", value, l)
		}
	}
	// Without an output column the whole row is the answer.
	if l := lookupOf(t, cat, "t_amp", TableLookup{Column: "SECTION", Value: "4", Mode: "EXACT"}); !l.Found || l.Result != "" || l.SI != nil || strings.Join(derefAll(l.Row), "|") != "4 mm²|26 A|90 °C|" {
		t.Errorf("whole row = %+v", l)
	}
	// Another numeric column: 70 is read in degC, the first row with 70 °C wins.
	if l := lookupOf(t, cat, "t_amp", TableLookup{Column: "temp", Value: "70", Output: "section"}); !l.Found || l.Value != "70 °C" || l.Result != "1.5 mm²" {
		t.Errorf("temperature = %+v", l)
	}
	// A text column compares text, case-insensitively, in English and German.
	if l := lookupOf(t, cat, "t_amp", TableLookup{Column: "note", Value: "SIEHE anmerkung", Output: "amps"}); !l.Found || l.Value != "SIEHE anmerkung" || l.Result != "19.5 A" {
		t.Errorf("text = %+v", l)
	}
	if l := lookupOf(t, cat, "t_amp", TableLookup{Column: "note", Value: "ok", Output: "section"}); !l.Found || l.Result != "1.5 mm²" {
		t.Errorf("first of two matches = %+v", l)
	}
	// Nothing found is an answer, not an error.
	l := lookupOf(t, cat, "t_amp", TableLookup{Value: "3", Output: "amps"})
	if l.Found || l.Result != "" || l.Row != nil || l.Message != "no row has section = 3 mm²" {
		t.Errorf("not found = %+v", l)
	}
	if l = lookupOf(t, cat, "t_amp", TableLookup{Column: "note", Value: "nope"}); l.Found || l.Message != `no row has note = "nope"` {
		t.Errorf("text not found = %+v", l)
	}
	// The row is there but the cell is empty.
	if l = lookupOf(t, cat, "t_amp", TableLookup{Value: "6", Output: "amps"}); !l.Found || l.Result != "" || l.SI != nil || l.Message != "the cell of amps is empty in that row" {
		t.Errorf("empty cell = %+v", l)
	}
}

func TestLookupGreaterOrEqual(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryFixture(t)
	// The first row in table order whose column is at least the value (not the nearest, no tolerance).
	for value, want := range map[string]string{"20": "4 mm²", "19.5": "2.5 mm²", "15.5": "1.5 mm²", "0": "1.5 mm²", "46": "10 mm²"} {
		l := lookupOf(t, cat, "t_amp", TableLookup{Mode: "ge", Column: "amps", Value: value, Output: "section"})
		if !l.Found || l.Mode != "ge" || l.Result != want || l.Row == nil {
			t.Errorf("ge %s: %+v, want %s", value, l, want)
		}
	}
	l := lookupOf(t, cat, "t_amp", TableLookup{Mode: "ge", Column: "amps", Value: "47"})
	if l.Found || l.Row != nil || l.Message != "no row has amps of at least 47 A; the largest is 46 A" {
		t.Errorf("ge beyond the table = %+v", l)
	}
	// It agrees with the table function lookup_ge.
	tbl := cat.Table("t_amp")
	l = lookupOf(t, cat, "t_amp", TableLookup{Mode: "ge", Column: "amps", Value: "20", Output: "section"})
	if want := tbl.LookupGE("amps", 20, "section"); l.SI == nil || !near(*l.SI, want, 1e-11) {
		t.Errorf("ge = %v, LookupGE = %v", l.SI, want)
	}
}

func TestLookupInterpolates(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryFixture(t)
	tbl := cat.Table("t_amp")
	// Linear between the rows where both columns are filled (the row of 6 mm2 has no current and is skipped).
	for value, want := range map[string]string{"2 mm2": "17.5 A", "7": "36 A", "1.5": "15.5 A", "10": "46 A"} {
		l := lookupOf(t, cat, "t_amp", TableLookup{Mode: "interp", Column: "section", Value: value, Output: "amps"})
		if !l.Found || l.Result != want || l.SI == nil || l.Row != nil {
			t.Errorf("interp %s: %+v, want %s", value, l, want)
		}
	}
	l := lookupOf(t, cat, "t_amp", TableLookup{Mode: "interp", Column: "section", Value: "7", Output: "amps"})
	if want := tbl.Interp("section", "amps", 7e-6); l.SI == nil || !near(*l.SI, want, 1e-11) {
		t.Errorf("interp = %v, Interp = %v", l.SI, want)
	}
	l = lookupOf(t, cat, "t_amp", TableLookup{Mode: "interp", Column: "section", Value: "12 mm2", Output: "amps"})
	if l.Found || l.Message != "12 mm² is outside the range of section, 1.5 mm² to 10 mm²" {
		t.Errorf("interp outside = %+v", l)
	}
	// A decreasing x column works too (the range is given low to high).
	fix := loadFixture(t)
	l = lookupOf(t, fix, "t_dec", TableLookup{Mode: "interp", Column: "x", Value: "20", Output: "y"})
	if l.Found || !strings.Contains(l.Message, "outside the range of x, 2.5 to 10") {
		t.Errorf("decreasing outside = %+v", l)
	}
	if l = lookupOf(t, fix, "t_dec", TableLookup{Mode: "interp", Column: "x", Value: "7.5", Output: "y"}); !l.Found || l.Result != "1.5" {
		t.Errorf("decreasing = %+v", l)
	}
}

func TestLookupRefusesWhatCannotWork(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryFixture(t)
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name string
		lk   TableLookup
		code string
		msg  string
	}{
		{"unknown column", TableLookup{Column: "nope", Value: "1"}, CodeUnknownColumn, `table t_amp has no column "nope" (lookup column); columns: section, amps, temp, note`},
		{"unknown output", TableLookup{Value: "1.5", Output: "nope"}, CodeUnknownColumn, `(lookup output)`},
		{"unknown mode", TableLookup{Mode: "nearest", Column: "amps", Value: "1"}, CodeInvalidLookup, `mode must be exact, ge or interp, got "nearest"`},
		{"no value", TableLookup{Column: "amps", Value: "  "}, CodeInvalidLookup, "needs a value"},
		{"ge without column", TableLookup{Mode: "ge", Value: "1"}, CodeInvalidLookup, "mode ge needs a column"},
		{"ge on text", TableLookup{Mode: "ge", Column: "note", Value: "a"}, CodeInvalidLookup, "holds text, so only the mode exact can search it; numeric columns: section, amps, temp"},
		{"interp without output", TableLookup{Mode: "interp", Column: "section", Value: "2"}, CodeInvalidLookup, "needs an output column"},
		{"interp of text", TableLookup{Mode: "interp", Column: "section", Value: "2", Output: "note"}, CodeInvalidLookup, "holds text and cannot be interpolated"},
		{"interp over a column that is not monotonic", TableLookup{Mode: "interp", Column: "temp", Value: "80", Output: "amps"}, CodeInvalidLookup, "not strictly monotonic"},
		{"value of the wrong shape", TableLookup{Column: "amps", Value: "abc"}, CodeParse, `cannot read "abc" for column amps as a current`},
		{"value in the wrong dimension", TableLookup{Column: "amps", Value: "3 V"}, CodeParse, `column amps`},
		{"value that is too long", TableLookup{Column: "amps", Value: strings.Repeat("1", MaxValueLength+1)}, CodeParse, `column amps`},
	} {
		_, err := cat.QueryTable("t_amp", TableRequest{Lookup: &c.lk})
		if qe := AsQueryError(err); qe == nil || qe.Code != c.code || !strings.Contains(qe.Message, c.msg) {
			t.Errorf("%s: %v, want code %s containing %q", c.name, err, c.code, c.msg)
		}
	}
}

func TestLookupAndRowsTogether(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryFixture(t)
	lk := TableLookup{Column: "amps", Mode: "ge", Value: "20", Output: "section"}
	// A filter, an offset or a limit asks for rows too.
	for name, req := range map[string]TableRequest{"filter": {Filter: "ok"}, "limit": {Limit: 2}, "offset": {Offset: 1}} {
		req.Lookup = &lk
		res, err := cat.QueryTable("t_amp", req)
		if err != nil || res.Lookup == nil || !res.Lookup.Found || len(res.Rows) == 0 || res.Note != "" {
			t.Errorf("%s: %+v (%v)", name, res, err)
		}
	}
}

func TestLookupInTheGeneratedTables(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	// AWG 12 and AWG 10 by their number; ASTM B258 gives 2.053 mm for AWG 12 and 2.588 mm / 5.261 mm2 for AWG 10, and the
	// copper resistance of AWG 10 is 3.277 ohm per km.
	for _, c := range []struct {
		lk   TableLookup
		want string
	}{
		{TableLookup{Column: "awg", Value: "12", Output: "diameter"}, "2.053 mm"},
		{TableLookup{Column: "awg", Value: "10", Output: "diameter"}, "2.588 mm"},
		{TableLookup{Column: "awg", Value: "10", Output: "area"}, "5.261 mm²"},
		{TableLookup{Column: "awg", Value: "10", Output: "r_km"}, "3.277 Ω"},
		{TableLookup{Column: "size", Value: "4/0", Output: "diameter"}, "11.68 mm"},
		{TableLookup{Value: "1/0", Output: "awg"}, "0"},
		{TableLookup{Column: "awg", Value: "-3", Output: "size"}, "4/0"},
	} {
		if l := lookupOf(t, cat, "awg", c.lk); !l.Found || l.Result != c.want {
			t.Errorf("awg %+v = %+v, want %s", c.lk, l, c.want)
		}
	}
	// ge answers with the first row in table order, like lookup_ge: the AWG table falls from 4/0 to 40, so the first
	// row is the answer whenever its area is large enough.
	if l := lookupOf(t, cat, "awg", TableLookup{Mode: "ge", Column: "area", Value: "3", Output: "size"}); !l.Found || l.Result != "4/0" {
		t.Errorf("ge on a falling column = %+v", l)
	}
	// Between two rows of the IPC-2221 grid.
	ipc := cat.Table("ipc2221")
	lo, hi := ipc.Rows[3][1].Num, ipc.Rows[4][1].Num // 1 A and 1.5 A, external 1 oz at 10 degC
	l := lookupOf(t, cat, "ipc2221", TableLookup{Mode: "interp", Column: "current", Value: "1.25", Output: "ext_1oz_10"})
	if !l.Found || l.SI == nil || !near(*l.SI, (lo+hi)/2, 1e-11) {
		t.Errorf("ipc2221 interp = %+v, want %v", l, (lo+hi)/2)
	}
	// 4.7 is a value of E3, E6, E12 and E24.
	l = lookupOf(t, cat, "eseries_e24", TableLookup{Value: "4.7"})
	if !l.Found || strings.Join(derefAll(l.Row), "|") != "4.7|●|●|●|●" {
		t.Errorf("e24 4.7 = %+v", l)
	}
	if l = lookupOf(t, cat, "eseries_e24", TableLookup{Value: "4.8"}); l.Found {
		t.Errorf("4.8 is no E24 value: %+v", l)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: implement**

Create `internal/ecalc/query_table.go` with exactly this content:

```go
package ecalc

import (
	"fmt"
	"math"
	"strings"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// The rows of a table for the agent tool: QueryTable lists the rows that match a filter, one page of them, and the result
// of one lookup. Output texts are English; the structs carry JSON tags because the tool sends them as they are.

const (
	// DefaultTableLimit and MaxTableLimit bound the number of rows of one QueryTable answer.
	DefaultTableLimit = 20
	MaxTableLimit     = 50
	// MaxFilterLength is the longest table filter in characters (a filter is a word or a number; every row is compared
	// with it).
	MaxFilterLength = 128
)

// TableLookup is the lookup of a QueryTable request: Mode "exact" (the default) finds the row whose Column equals Value,
// "ge" the first row (table order) whose Column is at least Value, "interp" interpolates the column Output linearly
// over Column at Value. Value is written the way a person types it and read with the dimension and unit of Column (a
// bare number is in the column's unit; a text column compares text). Output names the column to return: without it
// exact and ge answer with the whole row; interp needs it. An empty Column means the key column (exact only).
type TableLookup struct {
	Column string
	Value  string
	Mode   string
	Output string
}

// TableRequest is the input of QueryTable. Filter keeps the rows with a cell that contains the text (case-insensitive,
// numbers as written in the answer); Offset and Limit page through the kept rows (Limit 0 = DefaultTableLimit, at most
// MaxTableLimit). A request with a Lookup and no filter, offset or limit lists no rows.
type TableRequest struct {
	Filter string
	Offset int
	Limit  int
	Lookup *TableLookup
}

// LookupResult is the answer to a TableLookup. Value is the lookup value as it was understood (with its unit); Row is
// the matching row (exact and ge), Result and SI the output cell.
type LookupResult struct {
	Mode    string    `json:"mode"`
	Column  string    `json:"column"`
	Value   string    `json:"value"`
	Found   bool      `json:"found"`
	Output  string    `json:"output,omitempty"`
	Result  string    `json:"result,omitempty"`
	SI      *float64  `json:"si,omitempty"`
	Row     []*string `json:"row,omitempty"`
	Message string    `json:"message,omitempty"`
}

// TableResult is what QueryTable returns. Rows hold the cells as written in the answer (a number with its unit, text,
// null for an empty cell) and SI the same cells as SI numbers (null for text and empty cells). Total counts the rows
// that match the filter; Truncated means that more of them exist than are listed, NextOffset is where to continue.
type TableResult struct {
	ID         string            `json:"id"`
	Name       string            `json:"name"`
	Columns    []TableColumnInfo `json:"columns"`
	Total      int               `json:"total"`
	Offset     int               `json:"offset"`
	Returned   int               `json:"returned"`
	Truncated  bool              `json:"truncated,omitempty"`
	NextOffset int               `json:"next_offset,omitempty"`
	Rows       [][]*string       `json:"rows,omitempty"`
	SI         [][]*float64      `json:"si,omitempty"`
	Lookup     *LookupResult     `json:"lookup,omitempty"`
	Guide      bool              `json:"guide,omitempty"`
	Mains      bool              `json:"mains,omitempty"`
	Caution    string            `json:"caution,omitempty"`
	Notes      string            `json:"notes,omitempty"`
	Source     string            `json:"source"`
	Note       string            `json:"note,omitempty"`
}

// Keep shortens the listed rows to the first n (the tool does that to fit its output budget) and keeps Returned,
// Truncated and NextOffset consistent.
func (r *TableResult) Keep(n int) {
	if n < 0 || n >= len(r.Rows) {
		return
	}
	r.Rows = r.Rows[:n]
	if len(r.SI) > n {
		r.SI = r.SI[:n]
	}
	r.Returned = n
	r.Truncated = true
	r.NextOffset = r.Offset + n
}

// cellOut writes one cell for an answer: its text (a number with the symbol of its column's unit, nil when empty) and,
// for a number, the SI value.
func (c *Catalog) cellOut(t *Table, r, col int) (*string, *float64) {
	cell := t.Rows[r][col]
	if cell.Null {
		return nil, nil
	}
	spec := &t.Columns[col]
	if !spec.Numeric() {
		s := cell.Text.in("en")
		return &s, nil
	}
	s := c.formatValue(cell.Num, spec.Dim, spec.Unit)
	return &s, siOut(cell.Num)
}

// siOut is an SI number of an answer, rounded to 12 significant digits so that the arithmetic of the unit conversion
// (2.5 mm2 is 2.4999999999999998e-6 m2) does not show; nil when x is not finite.
func siOut(x float64) *float64 {
	if math.IsNaN(x) || math.IsInf(x, 0) {
		return nil
	}
	x = roundSig(x, 12)
	return &x
}

// rowMatches reports whether a cell of row r contains needle (lower case); text cells are compared in English and German,
// numbers as they are written in the answer.
func (c *Catalog) rowMatches(t *Table, shown []*string, r int, needle string) bool {
	for col, s := range shown {
		if s == nil {
			continue
		}
		if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(*s), needle) {
			return true
		}
		if !t.Columns[col].Numeric() {
			if de := t.Rows[r][col].Text.in("de"); strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(de), needle) {
				return true
			}
		}
	}
	return false
}

// QueryTable reads the rows of a table: the rows that match the filter, one page of them, and the result of the lookup.
func (c *Catalog) QueryTable(id string, req TableRequest) (TableResult, error) {
	t, err := c.lookupTable(id)
	if err != nil {
		return TableResult{}, err
	}
	filter := strings.TrimSpace(req.Filter)
	if utf8.RuneCountInString(filter) > MaxFilterLength {
		return TableResult{}, queryErr(CodeInvalidFilter, "filter must be at most %d characters; give a word or a number that occurs in a cell", MaxFilterLength)
	}
	res := TableResult{
		ID: t.ID, Name: t.Name.in("en"), Columns: c.columnInfo(t, false), Guide: t.Guide, Mains: t.Mains, Caution: t.caution(),
		Notes: t.Notes.in("en"), Source: t.Source, Offset: max(req.Offset, 0),
	}
	if req.Lookup != nil {
		lr, err := c.lookupInTable(t, *req.Lookup)
		if err != nil {
			return TableResult{}, err
		}
		res.Lookup = lr
	}

	shown := make([][]*string, len(t.Rows))
	si := make([][]*float64, len(t.Rows))
	for r := range t.Rows {
		shown[r], si[r] = make([]*string, len(t.Columns)), make([]*float64, len(t.Columns))
		for col := range t.Columns {
			shown[r][col], si[r][col] = c.cellOut(t, r, col)
		}
	}
	var matches []int
	needle := strings.ToLower(filter)
	for r := range t.Rows {
		if needle == "" || c.rowMatches(t, shown[r], r, needle) {
			matches = append(matches, r)
		}
	}
	res.Total = len(matches)
	if req.Lookup != nil && filter == "" && req.Offset == 0 && req.Limit == 0 {
		res.Note = "Only the lookup was answered; give filter, offset or limit to list rows."
		return res, nil
	}
	limit := req.Limit
	if limit < 1 {
		limit = DefaultTableLimit
	}
	limit = min(limit, MaxTableLimit)
	page := matches[min(res.Offset, len(matches)):]
	if len(page) > limit {
		page = page[:limit]
	}
	for _, r := range page {
		res.Rows = append(res.Rows, shown[r])
		res.SI = append(res.SI, si[r])
	}
	res.Returned = len(page)
	if end := min(res.Offset, len(matches)) + len(page); end < len(matches) {
		res.Truncated, res.NextOffset = true, end
	}
	if res.Total == 0 {
		res.Note = "No row matches the filter."
		if filter == "" {
			res.Note = "The table has no rows."
		}
	}
	return res, nil
}

// ---- lookup ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

func columnList(t *Table) string {
	return idsOf(t.Columns, func(c Column) string { return c.ID })
}

// findColumn resolves a column id (case-insensitive) of the table.
func findColumn(t *Table, name, role string) (int, *QueryError) {
	if i := t.ColumnIndex(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(name))); i >= 0 {
		return i, nil
	}
	return -1, queryErr(CodeUnknownColumn, "table %s has no column %q (%s); columns: %s", t.ID, name, role, columnList(t))
}

func (c *Catalog) lookupInTable(t *Table, lk TableLookup) (*LookupResult, error) {
	mode := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(lk.Mode))
	if mode == "" {
		mode = "exact"
	}
	if mode != "exact" && mode != "ge" && mode != "interp" {
		return nil, queryErr(CodeInvalidLookup, "lookup mode must be exact, ge or interp, got %q", lk.Mode)
	}
	value := strings.TrimSpace(lk.Value)
	if value == "" {
		return nil, queryErr(CodeInvalidLookup, "lookup needs a value")
	}
	colName := strings.TrimSpace(lk.Column)
	var col int
	if colName == "" && mode == "exact" {
		col = t.keyIdx
	} else if colName == "" {
		return nil, queryErr(CodeInvalidLookup, "lookup mode %s needs a column; columns: %s", mode, columnList(t))
	} else {
		var qe *QueryError
		if col, qe = findColumn(t, colName, "lookup column"); qe != nil {
			return nil, qe
		}
	}
	spec := &t.Columns[col]
	out := -1
	if name := strings.TrimSpace(lk.Output); name != "" {
		var qe *QueryError
		if out, qe = findColumn(t, name, "lookup output"); qe != nil {
			return nil, qe
		}
	}
	res := &LookupResult{Mode: mode, Column: spec.ID}
	if out >= 0 {
		res.Output = t.Columns[out].ID
	}

	// A text column compares text (exact only).
	if !spec.Numeric() {
		if mode != "exact" {
			return nil, queryErr(CodeInvalidLookup, "column %s holds text, so only the mode exact can search it; numeric columns: %s", spec.ID, numericColumns(t))
		}
		res.Value = value
		row := -1
		for r := range t.Rows {
			cell := t.Rows[r][col]
			if !cell.Null && (strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(cell.Text.in("en")), value) || strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(cell.Text.in("de")), value)) {
				row = r
				break
			}
		}
		c.fillLookup(res, t, row, out)
		if row < 0 {
			res.Message = fmt.Sprintf("no row has %s = %q", spec.ID, value)
		}
		return res, nil
	}

	x, err := c.Units.Parse(value, spec.Dim, spec.Unit)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, queryErr(CodeParse, "cannot read %q for column %s as a %s: %v", value, spec.ID, spec.Dim, err)
	}
	res.Value = c.formatValue(x, spec.Dim, spec.Unit)
	switch mode {
	case "exact":
		row := t.FindRow(col, x)
		c.fillLookup(res, t, row, out)
		if row < 0 {
			res.Message = fmt.Sprintf("no row has %s = %s", spec.ID, res.Value)
		}
	case "ge":
		row := -1
		largest := math.NaN()
		for r := range t.Rows {
			cell := t.Rows[r][col]
			if cell.Null {
				continue
			}
			if row < 0 && cell.Num >= x {
				row = r
			}
			if math.IsNaN(largest) || cell.Num > largest {
				largest = cell.Num
			}
		}
		c.fillLookup(res, t, row, out)
		if row < 0 {
			res.Message = fmt.Sprintf("no row has %s of at least %s", spec.ID, res.Value)
			if !math.IsNaN(largest) {
				res.Message += "; the largest is " + c.formatValue(largest, spec.Dim, spec.Unit)
			}
		}
	case "interp":
		if out < 0 {
			return nil, queryErr(CodeInvalidLookup, "lookup mode interp needs an output column; columns: %s", numericColumns(t))
		}
		if !t.Columns[out].Numeric() {
			return nil, queryErr(CodeInvalidLookup, "output column %s holds text and cannot be interpolated; numeric columns: %s", t.Columns[out].ID, numericColumns(t))
		}
		if err := t.checkInterp(col, out); err != nil {
			return nil, queryErr(CodeInvalidLookup, "%v", err)
		}
		y := t.Interp(spec.ID, t.Columns[out].ID, x)
		if math.IsNaN(y) {
			xs, _ := t.points(col, out)
			lo, hi := xs[0], xs[len(xs)-1]
			if lo > hi {
				lo, hi = hi, lo
			}
			res.Message = fmt.Sprintf("%s is outside the range of %s, %s to %s", res.Value, spec.ID, c.formatValue(lo, spec.Dim, spec.Unit), c.formatValue(hi, spec.Dim, spec.Unit))
			break
		}
		res.Found = true
		oc := &t.Columns[out]
		res.Result, res.SI = c.formatValue(y, oc.Dim, oc.Unit), siOut(y)
	}
	return res, nil
}

func numericColumns(t *Table) string {
	var ids []string
	for _, col := range t.Columns {
		if col.Numeric() {
			ids = append(ids, col.ID)
		}
	}
	return strings.Join(ids, ", ")
}

// fillLookup sets the result of an exact or ge lookup for row (-1: none): the row and, when an output column is named,
// its cell.
func (c *Catalog) fillLookup(res *LookupResult, t *Table, row, out int) {
	if row < 0 {
		return
	}
	res.Found = true
	res.Row = make([]*string, len(t.Columns))
	for col := range t.Columns {
		res.Row[col], _ = c.cellOut(t, row, col)
	}
	if out < 0 {
		return
	}
	text, si := c.cellOut(t, row, out)
	if text == nil {
		res.Message = fmt.Sprintf("the cell of %s is empty in that row", t.Columns[out].ID)
		return
	}
	res.Result, res.SI = *text, si
}
```

### Task B3: Describe, decode and encode component codes

**Runs after Part K.** It wraps `Catalog.Decode` and `Catalog.Encode`.

**Goal:** `DescribeCode` describes a code item (its `code_kind`, the forms that `decode` reads, the fields that `encode` takes, and the ids of the result fields); `QueryDecode`/`QueryEncode` resolve the kind (a code kind or the id of a code item), call the code engine and answer a `CodeAnswer`: the code, the bands, the SI value with its formatted text (4 significant digits, a temperature coefficient in `ppm/K`), the fields and the warnings, without the parts that are empty. The error of a code kind keeps its code (`invalid_code`, `invalid_value`, `unsupported`) and loses its `code: ` prefix; an unknown kind answers `unknown_code_kind` with the list of kinds.

**GitNexus:** new symbols only.

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/ecalc/query_codes_test.go`, `internal/ecalc/query_codes.go`

The expected values come from the IEC 60062 vectors of part K (`testdata/vectors/codes.json`): `violet green yellow gold` is 750 kΩ ±5 %, `blue grey red` 6.8 kΩ ±20 %, `silver blue gold grey silver` 6.8 µH (MIL layout), `01C` 10 kΩ, `104K 1H` 100 nF ±10 % 50 V, `U2J` −750 ppm/K, `X7R` has no value; an encode of 249k at 1 % is `red yellow white orange brown`, of 10k at 1 % the SMD marking `1002`, of 100n with tolerance K and 50V `104K 1H`. A last test sends every error vector of K through the wrappers and checks the code.

```go
func TestQueryDecodeReadsTheCodes(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	for _, c := range []struct {
		kind, code, canonical, formatted, fields string
		bands                                    int
	}{
		{"resistor_bands", "violet green yellow gold", "violet green yellow gold", "750 kΩ", "tolerance", 4},
		{"resistor_bands", " Blue-Grey, RED ", "blue grey red", "6.8 kΩ", "tolerance", 3},
		{"resistor_color_code", "blue grey red", "blue grey red", "6.8 kΩ", "tolerance", 3},
		{"inductor_bands", "silver blue gold grey silver", "silver blue gold grey silver", "6.8 µH", "layout,tolerance", 5},
		{"smd_resistor", "01C", "01C", "10 kΩ", "family", 0},
		{"smd_resistor", "472", "472", "4.7 kΩ", "family", 0},
		{"capacitor", "104", "104", "100 nF", "family", 0},
		{"ceramic_temp", "U2J", "U2J", "-750 ppm/K", "class,tc,tolerance,industry_code", 0},
	} {
		got, err := cat.QueryDecode(c.kind, c.code)
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s %q: %v", c.kind, c.code, err)
			continue
		}
		var ids []string
		for _, f := range got.Fields {
			ids = append(ids, f.ID)
		}
		kind, _ := cat.resolveCodeKind(c.kind)
		if got.Code != c.canonical || got.Formatted != c.formatted || strings.Join(ids, ",") != c.fields || len(got.Bands) != c.bands || got.Value == nil || got.Kind != kind {
			t.Errorf("%s %q = %+v", c.kind, c.code, got)
		}
	}
	// The tolerance of a resistor is a field with a number and a text.
	got, _ := cat.QueryDecode("resistor_bands", "violet green yellow gold")
	if f := got.Fields[0]; f.Text != "±5 %" || f.Value == nil || *f.Value != 0.05 || f.Dim != "ratio" || got.Dim != "resistance" || *got.Value != 750000 || len(got.Warnings) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("answer = %+v", got)
	}
	// A capacitor marking with tolerance and voltage, and a class 2 code without a value.
	got, err := cat.QueryDecode("capacitor", "104K 1H")
	if err != nil || got.Formatted != "100 nF" || len(got.Fields) < 3 || len(got.Warnings) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("104K 1H = %+v (%v)", got, err)
	}
	got, err = cat.QueryDecode("ceramic_temp", "X7R")
	if err != nil || got.Value != nil || got.Formatted != "" || got.Dim != "" || len(got.Fields) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("X7R = %+v (%v)", got, err)
	}
	if data, err := json.Marshal(got); err != nil || strings.Contains(string(data), "null") {
		t.Errorf("X7R JSON = %s (%v)", data, err)
	}
}

func TestQueryEncodeWritesTheCodes(t *testing.T) {
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	for _, c := range []struct {
		kind      string
		req       EncodeRequest
		code      string
		formatted string
	}{
		{"resistor_bands", EncodeRequest{Value: "249k", Tolerance: "1%"}, "red yellow white orange brown", "249 kΩ"},
		{"resistor_color_code", EncodeRequest{Value: " 6.8k ", Tolerance: "20%"}, "blue grey red", "6.8 kΩ"},
		{"inductor_bands", EncodeRequest{Value: "6.8u", Tolerance: "10%", Bands: 5}, "silver blue gold grey silver", "6.8 µH"},
		{"smd_resistor", EncodeRequest{Value: "10k", Tolerance: "1%"}, "1002", "10 kΩ"},
		{"capacitor", EncodeRequest{Value: "100n", Tolerance: "K", Voltage: "50V"}, "104K 1H", "100 nF"},
	} {
		got, err := cat.QueryEncode(c.kind, c.req)
		if err != nil || got.Code != c.code || got.Formatted != c.formatted || got.Value == nil || got.Fields == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s %+v = %+v (%v)", c.kind, c.req, got, err)
		}
	}
	// Class 2 of the ceramic codes has no value; the capacitor warns about the voltage convention.
	got, err := cat.QueryEncode("ceramic_temp", EncodeRequest{Class: "2", Value: "-55..125", Tolerance: "15%"})
	if err != nil || got.Code != "X7R" || got.Value != nil {
		t.Errorf("X7R = %+v (%v)", got, err)
	}
	got, _ = cat.QueryEncode("capacitor", EncodeRequest{Value: "100n", Tolerance: "K", Voltage: "50V"})
	if len(got.Warnings) != 1 || !strings.Contains(got.Warnings[0], "maker convention") {
		t.Errorf("warnings = %v", got.Warnings)
	}
	// A value that is not a standard value of the series is replaced and the warning says so.
	got, err = cat.QueryEncode("resistor_bands", EncodeRequest{Value: "4.8k", Tolerance: "5%"})
	if err != nil || got.Code != "yellow violet red gold" || len(got.Warnings) != 1 || !strings.Contains(got.Warnings[0], "not a standard value") {
		t.Errorf("4.8k = %+v (%v)", got, err)
	}
}

// Every error vector of the code kinds comes back as a QueryError with the same code.
func TestQueryCodesKeepTheErrorsOfTheVectors(t *testing.T) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile("testdata/vectors/codes.json")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var file struct {
		Errors []struct {
			Op       string        `json:"op"`
			Kind     string        `json:"kind"`
			Code     string        `json:"code"`
			Req      EncodeRequest `json:"req"`
			Error    string        `json:"error"`
			Contains string        `json:"contains"`
		} `json:"errors"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &file); err != nil || len(file.Errors) < 20 {
		t.Fatalf("codes.json: %v (%d error vectors)", err, len(file.Errors))
	}
	cat := queryCatalog(t)
	checked := 0
	for _, v := range file.Errors {
		if _, ok := codeKindOf(v.Kind); !ok {
			continue // an unknown kind is refused before the code kind sees it
		}
		var err error
		if v.Op == "decode" {
			_, err = cat.QueryDecode(v.Kind, v.Code)
		} else {
			_, err = cat.QueryEncode(v.Kind, v.Req)
		}
		qe := AsQueryError(err)
		if qe == nil || qe.Code != v.Error || !strings.Contains(qe.Message, v.Contains) {
			t.Errorf("%s %s %q %+v: %v, want %s containing %q", v.Op, v.Kind, v.Code, v.Req, err, v.Error, v.Contains)
		}
		checked++
	}
	if checked < 20 {
		t.Errorf("only %d error vectors were checked", checked)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: implement**

Create `internal/ecalc/query_codes.go` with exactly this content:

```go
package ecalc

import (
	"strings"
)

// The query API of the component codes: DescribeCode describes a code item, QueryDecode and QueryEncode wrap Decode and
// Encode (codes.go) for the agent tool. They resolve the code kind, turn the errors of the codes into QueryErrors, and
// write a result without the empty parts (a NaN value, empty lists) and with the value formatted. The lengths of the
// texts are limited by Decode and Encode (64 characters each). Output texts are English.

// CodeDescription is what DescribeCode returns. CodeKind is the kind that decode and encode take as their kind; Decode
// lists the forms a code may be written in, Encode the fields of an encode request and Fields what a result carries
// besides the code and the value.
type CodeDescription struct {
	ID       string   `json:"id"`
	Kind     string   `json:"kind"`
	Category string   `json:"category"`
	Name     string   `json:"name"`
	Doc      string   `json:"doc,omitempty"`
	Source   string   `json:"source"`
	CodeKind string   `json:"code_kind"`
	Decode   []string `json:"decode"`
	Encode   []string `json:"encode"`
	Fields   []string `json:"fields"`
}

// codeForms is what is known about the input and output of a code kind without loading its data.
type codeForms struct {
	decode, encode, fields []string
}

// codeFormsByKind describes the five code kinds of codes.go; the keys are the kind ids.
var codeFormsByKind = map[string]codeForms{
	"resistor_bands": {
		decode: []string{"1 to 6 band colours as English names, for example blue grey red (3 bands), brown black red gold (4), red yellow white orange brown (5)"},
		encode: []string{"value (required, for example 4k7)", "tolerance (for example 5%; it fixes the series)", "tempco (6 bands, for example 50ppm)", "bands (3, 4, 5 or 6)"},
		fields: []string{"tolerance", "tcr (temperature coefficient)"},
	},
	"inductor_bands": {
		decode: []string{"4 band colours (EIA) or 5 (MIL, silver first), for example silver blue gold grey silver"},
		encode: []string{"value (required, for example 6.8u)", "tolerance (5% or 10%)", "bands (4 for EIA, 5 for MIL)"},
		fields: []string{"layout", "tolerance"},
	},
	"smd_resistor": {
		decode: []string{"a marking as printed: 472, 4R7, 01C (EIA-96), 1L5, 4K7, 000"},
		encode: []string{"value (required, for example 10k)", "tolerance (for example 1%; it chooses the 3-digit, 4-digit or EIA-96 marking)"},
		fields: []string{"family", "code_3digit, code_4digit, code_eia96 (encode, those that exist)", "tolerance (encode)"},
	},
	"capacitor": {
		decode: []string{"up to three parts as printed: a value (104, 4p7), a tolerance letter (K) and a voltage code (1H), for example 104K 1H"},
		encode: []string{"value (for example 100n)", "tolerance (a letter such as K, or a percentage)", "voltage (for example 50V)"},
		fields: []string{"family", "tolerance (with tolerance_minus and tolerance_plus)", "voltage", "value_code and rkm (encode)"},
	},
	"ceramic_temp": {
		decode: []string{"a ceramic temperature code as printed: X7R, C0G, NP0, U2J"},
		encode: []string{"class (1 or 2, required)", "class 1: tempco (for example -750ppm) and tolerance (for example 120ppm)", "class 2: value as a temperature range (-55..125) and tolerance (for example 15%)"},
		fields: []string{"class 1: class, tc, tolerance, industry_code", "class 2: class, temp_low, temp_high, change"},
	},
}

// genericCodeForms describes a code kind that has no entry of its own.
var genericCodeForms = codeForms{
	decode: []string{"the code as printed or as a list of English colour names"},
	encode: []string{"value (required)"},
	fields: []string{"further decoded fields as listed in the result"},
}

// codeFormsOf returns the forms of a code kind.
func codeFormsOf(kind string) codeForms {
	if f, ok := codeFormsByKind[kind]; ok {
		return f
	}
	return genericCodeForms
}

// lookupCodeItem finds a code item by id (case-insensitive), like lookupTable.
func (c *Catalog) lookupCodeItem(id string) (*Code, error) {
	key := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(id))
	if key == "" {
		return nil, queryErr(CodeUnknownID, "id is required; use search to find a code id")
	}
	if k := c.Code(key); k != nil {
		return k, nil
	}
	return nil, c.notFound(id, key, "code")
}

// DescribeCode returns what a code item is for: its kind and the forms in which decode takes a code and encode takes a
// value.
func (c *Catalog) DescribeCode(id string) (CodeDescription, error) {
	k, err := c.lookupCodeItem(id)
	if err != nil {
		return CodeDescription{}, err
	}
	f := codeFormsOf(k.CodeKind)
	return CodeDescription{
		ID: k.ID, Kind: "code", Category: k.Category, Name: k.Name.in("en"), Doc: k.Doc.in("en"), Source: k.Source,
		CodeKind: k.CodeKind, Decode: f.decode, Encode: f.encode, Fields: f.fields,
	}, nil
}

// CodeAnswerField is one further field of a decoded or encoded code. Value is absent for a field without a number.
type CodeAnswerField struct {
	ID    string   `json:"id"`
	Name  string   `json:"name"`
	Text  string   `json:"text"`
	Value *float64 `json:"value,omitempty"`
	Dim   string   `json:"dim,omitempty"`
}

// CodeAnswer is the answer of QueryDecode and QueryEncode: the CodeResult of the code kind without its empty parts and
// with the value formatted. Kind is the code kind, Code the canonical code text, Bands the colours of a band code. Value
// (SI, in the dimension Dim) and Formatted are absent for a code without a value.
type CodeAnswer struct {
	Kind      string            `json:"kind"`
	Code      string            `json:"code"`
	Bands     []string          `json:"bands,omitempty"`
	Value     *float64          `json:"value,omitempty"`
	Dim       string            `json:"dim,omitempty"`
	Formatted string            `json:"formatted,omitempty"`
	Fields    []CodeAnswerField `json:"fields"`
	Warnings  []string          `json:"warnings,omitempty"`
}

// resolveCodeKind returns the registered code kind a request means: the kind itself or the id of a code item (whose kind
// it is). The error of anything else lists the kinds.
func (c *Catalog) resolveCodeKind(kind string) (string, error) {
	key := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(kind))
	if _, ok := codeKindOf(key); ok && key != "" {
		return key, nil
	}
	if k := c.Code(key); k != nil {
		return k.CodeKind, nil
	}
	return "", queryErr(CodeUnknownCodeKind, "unknown code kind %q; kinds: %s", kind, strings.Join(CodeKindIDs(), ", "))
}

// codeQueryError turns an error of Decode or Encode into a QueryError that keeps its code (invalid_code, invalid_value
// or unsupported); any other error becomes invalid_code with its text.
func codeQueryError(err error) *QueryError {
	if ce := AsCodeError(err); ce != nil {
		return &QueryError{Code: ce.Code, Message: ce.Message}
	}
	return &QueryError{Code: CodeInvalidCode, Message: err.Error()}
}

func (c *Catalog) codeAnswer(res CodeResult) CodeAnswer {
	out := CodeAnswer{Kind: res.Kind, Code: res.Code, Bands: res.Bands, Dim: res.Dim, Fields: make([]CodeAnswerField, 0, len(res.Fields)), Warnings: res.Warnings}
	if out.Value = finitePtr(res.Value); out.Value != nil && res.Dim != "" {
		unit := ""
		if res.Dim == "tempco" {
			unit = "ppmK" // -750 ppm/K, not -0.00075 1/K
		}
		out.Formatted = c.formatValue(res.Value, res.Dim, unit)
	}
	if out.Value == nil {
		out.Dim = ""
	}
	for _, f := range res.Fields {
		field := CodeAnswerField{ID: f.ID, Name: f.Name, Text: f.Text, Value: finitePtr(f.Value)}
		if field.Value != nil {
			field.Dim = f.Dim
		}
		out.Fields = append(out.Fields, field)
	}
	return out
}

// QueryDecode reads a component code: band colours as English colour names, a marking as printed (103, 4R7, 104K 1H,
// X7R). The kind is a code kind or the id of a code item.
func (c *Catalog) QueryDecode(kind, code string) (CodeAnswer, error) {
	k, err := c.resolveCodeKind(kind)
	if err != nil {
		return CodeAnswer{}, err
	}
	res, err := c.Decode(k, strings.TrimSpace(code))
	if err != nil {
		return CodeAnswer{}, codeQueryError(err)
	}
	return c.codeAnswer(res), nil
}

// QueryEncode writes the code of a value: the nearest standard value of the series that the tolerance implies, as band
// colours or as a marking. The kind is a code kind or the id of a code item. What each kind reads from the request is in
// codeFormsByKind; Encode checks the texts.
func (c *Catalog) QueryEncode(kind string, req EncodeRequest) (CodeAnswer, error) {
	k, err := c.resolveCodeKind(kind)
	if err != nil {
		return CodeAnswer{}, err
	}
	req.Value, req.Tolerance, req.TempCo = strings.TrimSpace(req.Value), strings.TrimSpace(req.Tolerance), strings.TrimSpace(req.TempCo)
	req.Voltage, req.Class = strings.TrimSpace(req.Voltage), strings.TrimSpace(req.Class)
	res, err := c.Encode(k, req)
	if err != nil {
		return CodeAnswer{}, codeQueryError(err)
	}
	return c.codeAnswer(res), nil
}
```

### Task B4: The tool operations `table`, `decode` and `encode`; `describe` and `open` for every item

**Goal:** `ExecuteECalc` handles the three new operations and the other items. `table` answers `ecalc.TableResult` and fits it to the budget (first the `si` matrix goes and the `note` says so, then the notes and the source are clipped, then rows are dropped one by one down to one row, with `truncated` and `next_offset` kept right; the lookup result stays). `decode`/`encode` answer the `CodeAnswer`. `describe` routes by the kind of the id (a table answers its columns, a code its forms; both are fitted or small). `open` takes any id: a table or a code opens its page with empty values and choices, values and choices on such an id are `not_a_calculator`; the desktop gates are the same as for a calculator. `search` counts all items.

**GitNexus (before editing):** `ExecuteECalc` LOW (3 impacted: `dispatchECalc` → `dispatchPlatform` → `dispatchInfra`), `ecalcSearch`, `ecalcDescribe`, `ecalcOpen` LOW (3 each, all through `ExecuteECalc`). The request struct only grows.

```go
func TestECalcTableListsAPageOfRows(t *testing.T) {
	exec := ExecuteECalc(nil, ECalcRequest{Operation: "table", ID: "awg"})
	if exec.Event != nil {
		t.Fatal("table must not emit a desktop event")
	}
	out := ecalcDecode(t, exec)
	rows, _ := out["rows"].([]any)
	si, _ := out["si"].([]any)
	columns, _ := out["columns"].([]any)
	if out["status"] != "ok" || out["operation"] != "table" || out["id"] != "awg" || out["total"] != float64(44) || out["offset"] != float64(0) || len(columns) != 5 ||
		out["returned"] != float64(len(rows)) || len(si) != len(rows) || out["source"] == nil || out["notes"] == nil || out["guide"] != nil || out["lookup"] != nil {
		t.Fatalf("output = %s", exec.Output)
	}
	// The default page is 20 rows (the 6,000 bytes of the default budget may allow fewer), and the answer says where
	// to continue.
	if n := len(rows); n < 5 || n > 20 || out["truncated"] != true || out["next_offset"] != float64(len(rows)) {
		t.Errorf("%d rows, truncated %v, next_offset %v", len(rows), out["truncated"], out["next_offset"])
	}
	first := rows[0].([]any)
	if first[0] != "4/0" || first[1] != "-3" || first[2] != "11.68 mm" || first[3] != "107.2 mm²" {
		t.Errorf("first row = %v", first)
	}
	// The next page starts where the first stopped.
	next := ecalcDecode(t, ExecuteECalc(nil, ECalcRequest{Operation: "table", ID: "awg", Offset: len(rows), Limit: 3}))

		t.Errorf("second page = %v", next)
	}
}

func TestECalcTableShortensToTheBudget(t *testing.T) {
	cat, err := ecalc.Default()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	req := ECalcRequest{Operation: "table", ID: "awg", Limit: 50, Filter: " ", Lookup: &ecalc.TableLookup{Column: "awg", Value: "10", Output: "area"}}
	req.Limit = 50
	full := ecalcTable(cat, req, 100000)
	fullOut := ecalcDecode(t, full)
	if fullOut["returned"] != float64(44) || fullOut["si"] == nil || fullOut["note"] != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a full answer lists every row with its si values: %s", full.Output)
	}
	// The si matrix goes first, the rows stay.
	noSI := ecalcTable(cat, req, len(full.Output)-1)
	out := ecalcDecode(t, noSI)
	if out["si"] != nil || out["returned"] != float64(44) || !strings.Contains(out["note"].(string), "si values left out") || len(noSI.Output) >= len(full.Output) {
		t.Fatalf("si must go first: %s", noSI.Output)
	}
	// Then fewer rows, and the answer says where to continue; the lookup stays.
	short := ecalcTable(cat, req, 2400)
	out = ecalcDecode(t, short)
	rows, _ := out["rows"].([]any)
	if len(short.Output) > 2400 || len(rows) < 1 || len(rows) >= 44 || out["returned"] != float64(len(rows)) || out["truncated"] != true || out["next_offset"] != float64(len(rows)) ||
		out["lookup"].(map[string]any)["result"] != "5.261 mm²" || out["total"] != float64(44) {
		t.Fatalf("%d bytes: %s", len(short.Output), short.Output)
	}
	// Whatever the budget, one row is kept.
	tiny := ecalcDecode(t, ecalcTable(cat, req, 100))
	if rows, _ = tiny["rows"].([]any); len(rows) != 1 || tiny["returned"] != float64(1) {
		t.Errorf("tiny = %v", tiny)
	}
}

func TestECalcOpenWorksForTablesAndCodes(t *testing.T) {

	if payload, _ := json.Marshal(code.Event.Payload); string(payload) != `{"app_id":"ecalc","ecalc":{"choices":{},"page":"resistor_color_code","values":{}}}` || !strings.Contains(code.Output, "Use decode and encode") {
		t.Fatalf("code page = %s", code.Output)

	exec := ExecuteECalc(ecalcDesktopConfig(), ECalcRequest{Operation: "open", ID: "AWG"})
	if exec.Event == nil || exec.Event.Type != "open_app" || exec.Event.ID == "" {
		t.Fatalf("event = %+v, output = %s", exec.Event, exec.Output)
	}
	payload, _ := json.Marshal(exec.Event.Payload)
	if string(payload) != `{"app_id":"ecalc","ecalc":{"choices":{},"page":"awg","values":{}}}` {
		t.Fatalf("payload = %s", payload)
	}
	out := ecalcDecode(t, exec)
	if out["status"] != "ok" || out["page"] != "awg" || !strings.Contains(out["message"].(string), "ECalc at the AWG wire gauges table. Use table to read its rows yourself") {
		t.Fatalf("output = %s", exec.Output)
	}
	// Values and choices belong to calculators.
	exec = ExecuteECalc(ecalcDesktopConfig(), ECalcRequest{Operation: "open", ID: "awg", Inputs: ecalcPairs("awg", "10")})
	if got := ecalcDecode(t, exec); exec.Event != nil || got["status"] != "error" || got["code"] != "not_a_calculator" || !strings.Contains(got["message"].(string), "awg is a table") {
		t.Fatalf("output = %s", exec.Output)
	}
	// The gates are the same as for a calculator.
	denied := ExecuteECalc(nil, ECalcRequest{Operation: "open", ID: "awg"})
	if denied.Event != nil || ecalcDecode(t, denied)["status"] != "policy_denied" {
		t.Fatalf("no config must be denied: %s", denied.Output)
	}
}

func TestECalcDecodeAndEncodeRefuseWhatTheyCannotRead(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range []struct {
		req  ECalcRequest
		code string
	}{
		{ECalcRequest{Operation: "decode", Kind: "nope", Code: "103"}, "unknown_code_kind"},
		{ECalcRequest{Operation: "decode", Kind: "capacitor"}, "invalid_code"},
		{ECalcRequest{Operation: "decode", Kind: "capacitor", Code: strings.Repeat("1", 65)}, "invalid_code"},
		{ECalcRequest{Operation: "decode", Kind: "resistor_bands", Code: "gold red yellow"}, "invalid_code"},
		{ECalcRequest{Operation: "decode", Kind: "smd_resistor", Code: "01S"}, "unsupported"},
		{ECalcRequest{Operation: "encode", Kind: "nope", Value: "4k7"}, "unknown_code_kind"},
		{ECalcRequest{Operation: "encode", Kind: "resistor_bands", Value: "abc"}, "invalid_value"},
		{ECalcRequest{Operation: "encode", Kind: "resistor_bands", Value: "4k7", Bands: 7}, "invalid_value"},
		{ECalcRequest{Operation: "encode", Kind: "capacitor"}, "invalid_value"},
		{ECalcRequest{Operation: "encode", Kind: "inductor_bands", Value: "6.8u", Tolerance: "2%"}, "unsupported"},
	} {
		exec := ExecuteECalc(nil, c.req)
		if got := ecalcDecode(t, exec); exec.Event != nil || got["status"] != "error" || got["code"] != c.code || got["message"] == "" {
			t.Errorf("%+v: output = %v, want code %s", c.req, got, c.code)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
type ecalcDescribeTableOut struct {
	Status    string `json:"status"`
	Operation string `json:"operation"`
	ecalc.TableDescription
	Truncated bool `json:"truncated,omitempty"`
}

func ecalcDescribeTable(cat *ecalc.Catalog, id string, budget int) VirtualDesktopExecution {
	d, err := cat.DescribeTable(id)
	if err != nil {
		return ecalcQueryFailure(err)
	}
	out := ecalcDescribeTableOut{Status: "ok", Operation: "describe", TableDescription: d}
	return ecalcFit(budget, func() any { return out },
		func() { out.Doc, out.Notes, out.Truncated = ecalcClip(out.Doc, 240), ecalcClip(out.Notes, 240), true },
		func() {
			cols := make([]ecalc.TableColumnInfo, len(out.Columns))
			copy(cols, out.Columns)
			for i := range cols {
				cols[i].Units = nil
			}
			out.Columns = cols
		},
		func() { out.Source = ecalcClip(out.Source, 120) },
	)
}

type ecalcTableOut struct {
	Status    string `json:"status"`
	Operation string `json:"operation"`
	ecalc.TableResult
}

// ecalcTable answers the rows and the lookup of a table. When the answer is over the budget it first leaves out the SI
// matrix (the rows hold every value with its unit), then shortens the notes and the source, then lists fewer rows (the
// answer says where to continue).
func ecalcTable(cat *ecalc.Catalog, req ECalcRequest, budget int) VirtualDesktopExecution {
	res, err := cat.QueryTable(req.ID, ecalc.TableRequest{Filter: req.Filter, Offset: req.Offset, Limit: req.Limit, Lookup: req.Lookup})
	if err != nil {
		return ecalcQueryFailure(err)
	}
	out := ecalcTableOut{Status: "ok", Operation: "table", TableResult: res}
	note, shortened := res.Note, []string{}
	build := func() any {
		out.Note = note
		if len(shortened) > 0 {
			out.Note = strings.TrimSpace(note + " Shortened to fit the output limit: " + strings.Join(shortened, ", ") + ".")
		}
		return out
	}
	steps := []func(){
		func() { out.SI, shortened = nil, append(shortened, "si values left out") },
		func() {
			out.Notes, out.Source, shortened = ecalcClip(out.Notes, 160), ecalcClip(out.Source, 120), append(shortened, "notes and source clipped")
		},
	}
	for range len(out.Rows) {
		steps = append(steps, func() {
			if n := len(out.Rows); n > 1 {
				out.Keep(n - 1)
			}
		})
	}
	return ecalcFit(budget, build, steps...)
}

	})
	if err != nil {

	}
	return ecalcResult(ecalcCodeOut{Status: "ok", Operation: "encode", CodeAnswer: res}, nil)
}
```

```go
// ecalcOpenItem opens the page of a table or a code. Only calculators take values and choices; the page of anything else
// opens as it is.
func ecalcOpenItem(kind, id string, req ECalcRequest, cat *ecalc.Catalog) VirtualDesktopExecution {
	if len(req.Inputs) > 0 || len(req.Choices) > 0 {
		return ecalcFailure("error", ecalc.CodeNotACalculator, fmt.Sprintf("inputs and choices are only for calculators; %s is a %s, so open it with its id alone.", id, kind))
	}
	name, advice := "", ""
	switch kind {
	case "table":
		name, advice = cat.Table(id).Name["en"], " Use table to read its rows yourself."
	case "code":
		name, advice = cat.Code(id).Name["en"], " Use decode and encode to work with the code yourself."
	}
	launch := map[string]interface{}{"page": id, "values": ecalcOrdered(nil), "choices": ecalcOrdered(nil)}
	event := virtualDesktopEvent("open_app", map[string]interface{}{"app_id": "ecalc", "ecalc": launch})
	return ecalcResult(ecalcOpenOut{
		Status: "ok", Operation: "open", Page: id, Message: "Asked the desktop to open ECalc at the " + name + " " + kind + "." + advice,
	}, event)
}
```

---

### Task B5: Register the operations for the agent (schema, arguments, policy, discovery, manual)

**Goal:** the agent sees and can call the new operations. The schema adds `table`, `decode`, `encode` to the `operation` enum and the parameters `offset`, `filter`, `lookup` (strict object), `kind` (enum of the code kinds), `code`, `value`, `bands`, `tolerance`, `tempco`, `voltage` and `class`; the argument decoder reads them (numbers and numbers as text are accepted for `value`, `tolerance`, `tempco`, `voltage` and `bands`; the `lookup` may also arrive as JSON text; a `lookup` without a usable shape becomes an empty lookup so that the tool answers that it needs a value); `a2aDesktopWrite` leaves A2A peers `search`, `describe`, `calculate`, `table`, `decode` and `encode` (the discovery trims the `operation` enum of a peer to them); the discovery terms and the category text mention tables and codes; the manual explains tables, codes, values, errors and carries one runnable example for each of the seven operations.

**GitNexus (before editing):** `ecalcSchema` LOW (5 impacted through `appendContentToolSchemas` → `builtinToolSchemas`), `decodeECalcArgs` LOW (3: `dispatchECalc` and up), `a2aDesktopWrite` LOW (7: `a2aRestriction` → `roleToolRestriction` → `checkDispatchActionPolicy`). `DescribeAction` already treats only `open` as mutating, so `table`, `decode` and `encode` need no change there (a comment is updated); the test pins it. `ecalcPairs` exists in `internal/agent` and in `internal/tools` (different packages), neither is modified.

- Create: `internal/agent/ecalc_items_test.go`
- Modify: `internal/agent/ecalc_tool_test.go`, `internal/agent/ecalc_policy_test.go`, `internal/agent/native_tools_ecalc.go`, `internal/agent/tool_args_ecalc.go`, `internal/agent/tool_role_policy.go`, `internal/agent/action_policy.go`, `internal/agent/tool_categories.go`, `internal/agent/tool_search_terms/infrastructure_b.yaml`, `prompts/tools_manuals/ecalc.md`

The tests flip what phase 2 pinned deliberately: the operation enum (seven operations), the A2A list (`table`, `decode`, `encode` are allowed for peers; `table` was denied), the manual test (one example per operation, and every example must run with status ok), and the schema cap (800 tokens, measured 750). New tests cover the argument decoding (native, text-mode through `ParseToolCall`, lenient numbers, the three shapes of the lookup), the dispatcher (a table call needs no desktop and fits the inline budget) and the discovery terms.

```go
package agent

import (
	"context"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"aurago/internal/config"

// The tables and codes of the ecalc tool as the agent sees them: how the arguments of table, decode and encode are read
// and that the dispatcher runs them without the desktop.

func TestECalcNativeCallDecodesTableArguments(t *testing.T) {
	tc := ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"table","id":"awg","filter":"1/0","offset":4,"limit":7,"lookup":{"column":"awg","value":"10","mode":"GE","output":"area"}}`)
	req := decodeECalcArgs(tc)
	if req.Operation != "table" || req.ID != "awg" || req.Filter != "1/0" || req.Offset != 4 || req.Limit != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("request = %+v", req)
	}
	if l := req.Lookup; l == nil || l.Column != "awg" || l.Value != "10" || l.Mode != "ge" || l.Output != "area" {
		t.Fatalf("lookup = %+v", req.Lookup)
	}
	// The shapes models send for the lookup instead of the object.
	for name, arguments := range map[string]string{
		"number value": `{"operation":"table","id":"awg","lookup":{"column":"awg","value":10,"output":"area"}}`,
		"JSON text":    `{"operation":"table","id":"awg","lookup":"{\"column\":\"awg\",\"value\":\"10\",\"output\":\"area\"}"}`,
	} {
		got := decodeECalcArgs(ecalcNativeCall(t, arguments)).Lookup
		if got == nil || got.Column != "awg" || got.Value != "10" || got.Output != "area" || got.Mode != "" {
			t.Errorf("%s: lookup = %+v", name, got)
		}
	}
	// A lookup without a usable shape is an empty lookup, not no lookup: the tool then asks for the value.
	for name, arguments := range map[string]string{
		"text":  `{"operation":"table","id":"awg","lookup":"ten"}`,
		"array": `{"operation":"table","id":"awg","lookup":[1,2]}`,
		"empty": `{"operation":"table","id":"awg","lookup":{}}`,
	} {
		if got := decodeECalcArgs(ecalcNativeCall(t, arguments)).Lookup; got == nil || got.Value != "" || got.Column != "" {
			t.Errorf("%s: lookup = %+v, want an empty lookup", name, got)
		}
	}
	if got := decodeECalcArgs(ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"table","id":"awg"}`)); got.Lookup != nil || got.Filter != "" || got.Offset != 0 {
		t.Errorf("a plain table call = %+v", got)
	}
	// Text-mode calls carry the generic fields.
	req = decodeECalcArgs(ToolCall{Action: "ecalc", Operation: "Table", ID: "awg", Offset: 3, Limit: 2})
	if req.Operation != "table" || req.Offset != 3 || req.Limit != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("text-mode request = %+v", req)
	}
}

func TestECalcNativeCallDecodesCodeArguments(t *testing.T) {
	req := decodeECalcArgs(ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"decode","kind":"Resistor_Bands","code":"brown black red gold"}`))
	if req.Operation != "decode" || req.Kind != "resistor_bands" || req.Code != "brown black red gold" {
		t.Fatalf("decode request = %+v", req)
	}
	req = decodeECalcArgs(ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"encode","kind":"capacitor","value":"100 nF","bands":5,"tolerance":"1%","tempco":"50 ppm/K","voltage":"63 V","class":"X7R"}`))
	if req.Operation != "encode" || req.Kind != "capacitor" || req.Value != "100 nF" || req.Bands != 5 || req.Tolerance != "1%" || req.TempCo != "50 ppm/K" || req.Voltage != "63 V" || req.Class != "X7R" {
		t.Fatalf("encode request = %+v", req)
	}
	// Numbers and numbers as text are read as typed.
	req = decodeECalcArgs(ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"encode","kind":"resistor_bands","value":"4k7","bands":"6","tolerance":5,"tempco":50,"voltage":16}`))
	if req.Bands != 6 || req.Tolerance != "5" || req.TempCo != "50" || req.Voltage != "16" {
		t.Fatalf("lenient encode request = %+v", req)
	}
	// Text-mode calls carry code and value in the generic fields.
	req = decodeECalcArgs(ToolCall{Action: "ecalc", Operation: "decode", Code: "103", Value: "x"})
	if req.Code != "103" || req.Value != "x" {
		t.Fatalf("text-mode request = %+v", req)
	}
}

// A text-mode call (a JSON object in the reply instead of a native tool call) reaches the same request.
func TestECalcTextModeCallsDecodeLikeNativeOnes(t *testing.T) {
	tc := ParseToolCall(`{"action":"ecalc","operation":"table","id":"awg","filter":"1/0","offset":2,"limit":5,"lookup":{"column":"awg","value":"10","output":"area"}}`)
	req := decodeECalcArgs(tc)
	if tc.Action != "ecalc" || req.Operation != "table" || req.ID != "awg" || req.Filter != "1/0" || req.Offset != 2 || req.Limit != 5 || req.Lookup == nil || req.Lookup.Column != "awg" || req.Lookup.Output != "area" {
		t.Fatalf("table request = %+v (lookup %+v)", req, req.Lookup)
	}
	tc = ParseToolCall(`{"action":"ecalc","operation":"encode","kind":"resistor_bands","value":"4k7","bands":5,"tolerance":"1%"}`)
	req = decodeECalcArgs(tc)
	if req.Operation != "encode" || req.Kind != "resistor_bands" || req.Value != "4k7" || req.Bands != 5 || req.Tolerance != "1%" {
		t.Fatalf("encode request = %+v", req)
	}
	tc = ParseToolCall(`{"action":"ecalc","operation":"decode","kind":"smd_resistor","code":"103"}`)
	if req = decodeECalcArgs(tc); req.Code != "103" || req.Kind != "smd_resistor" {
		t.Fatalf("decode request = %+v", req)
	}
}

func TestECalcDispatchRunsTableCallsWithoutTheDesktop(t *testing.T) {
	broker := &ecalcJSONBroker{}
	dc := &DispatchContext{Cfg: &config.Config{}, Logger: testLogger, Broker: broker}
	call := ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"table","id":"awg","lookup":{"column":"awg","value":"10","output":"area"}}`)
	out, ok := dispatchPlatform(context.Background(), call, dc)
	if !ok || !strings.HasPrefix(out, "Tool Output: ") || !strings.Contains(out, `"status":"ok"`) || !strings.Contains(out, `"result":"5.261 mm²"`) {
		t.Fatalf("dispatch = %v %s", ok, out)
	}
	if len(broker.json) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("table must not broadcast: %v", broker.json)
	}
	// The answer is sized to the inline budget of the caller.
	call = ecalcNativeCall(t, `{"operation":"table","id":"eseries_e192","limit":50}`)
	out, _ = dispatchPlatform(context.Background(), call, dc)
	if !strings.Contains(out, `"status":"ok"`) || !strings.Contains(out, `"truncated":true`) || len(out) > toolResultInlineBudget(dc) {
		t.Fatalf("%d bytes (budget %d): %.200s", len(out), toolResultInlineBudget(dc), out)
	}
}

func TestECalcSearchTermsFindTablesAndCodes(t *testing.T) {
	catalog := BuildToolCatalog(BuildNativeToolSchemas("", nil, ToolFeatureFlags{}, nil), nil, "")
	for _, query := range []string{"AWG wire gauge table", "cable cross-section table", "resistor color code", "Widerstand Farbcode", "SMD resistor marking", "Kabelquerschnitt Tabelle"} {
		matches := catalog.Search(query)
		found := false
		for _, entry := range matches[:min(5, len(matches))] {
			found = found || entry.Name == "ecalc"
		}
		if !found {
			t.Errorf("%q did not find ecalc in the top five", query)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
		Value:     firstNonEmptyToolString(ecalcParamText(tc.Params, "value"), tc.Value),
		Bands:     ecalcParamInt(tc.Params, "bands"),
		Tolerance: ecalcParamText(tc.Params, "tolerance"),
		TempCo:    ecalcParamText(tc.Params, "tempco", "temp_co"),
		Voltage:   ecalcParamText(tc.Params, "voltage"),
		Class:     ecalcParamText(tc.Params, "class"),
	}
}

// ecalcParamText is the text of the first of the keys that holds a string or a number.
func ecalcParamText(params map[string]interface{}, keys ...string) string {
	for _, key := range keys {
		if text, ok := ecalcScalarText(params[key]); ok && text != "" {
			return text
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// ecalcParamInt reads a whole number that may arrive as a number or as text ("5"); anything else is 0.
func ecalcParamInt(params map[string]interface{}, key string) int {
	if n := toolArgInt(params, 0, key); n != 0 {
		return n
	}
	if text, ok := ecalcScalarText(params[key]); ok {
		if n, err := strconv.Atoi(text); err == nil {
			return n
		}
	}
	return 0
}

// ecalcLookup reads the lookup object of a table call: an object, or the JSON text of one. A lookup that is present but
// has no usable shape becomes an empty lookup, so that the tool answers that it needs a value instead of ignoring it.
func ecalcLookup(raw interface{}) *ecalc.TableLookup {
	if raw == nil {
		return nil
	}
	if text, ok := raw.(string); ok {
		var decoded interface{}
		if json.Unmarshal([]byte(text), &decoded) == nil {
			raw = decoded
		}
	}
	m, _ := raw.(map[string]interface{})
	value, _ := ecalcScalarText(m["value"])
	return &ecalc.TableLookup{
		Column: strings.TrimSpace(toolArgString(m, "column")),
		Value:  value,
		Mode:   strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(toolArgString(m, "mode"))),
		Output: strings.TrimSpace(toolArgString(m, "output")),
	}
}
```
