Replace the entire content of `prompts/tools_manuals/ecalc.md` with:

````markdown
# ECalc (electronics calculators, reference tables and component codes)

Use `ecalc` for electronics formulas: Ohm's law, voltage dividers, filters, timers, op-amp stages, power supplies, RF, standard resistor values and more. It computes with the same catalog and formulas as the ECalc desktop app, exactly and with units; use it instead of calculating by hand. The catalog also holds reference **tables** (AWG wire sizes, PCB trace width after IPC-2221, E-series values and more) that you read with `table`, and **component codes** (resistor and inductor colour bands, SMD markings, capacitor and ceramic codes) that you read with `decode` and write with `encode`. It reads nothing from the network or from files.

## Workflow

1. `search` with a few words (English or German, at most 256 characters): a topic, a part or a formula. A hit has a `kind`: `calculator`, `table` or `code`. An empty `query` lists the categories.
2. `describe` the item you picked. A calculator: its variables with units and defaults, the choices, how many values are needed (`dof`), which input combinations work (`sets`), the computed outputs (`derived`), the checks and the formula. A table: its columns, key, row count, notes and source. A code: its `code_kind` and the forms it reads and writes.
3. `calculate` with the values you know (any complete input set works, so you can solve for whichever quantity is missing), `table` to read rows or one value of a table, `decode` to read a code, `encode` to write one.
4. `open` only when the user wants to see or play with the item; it opens the ECalc app on the desktop (pre-filled for a calculator).

```json
{"action":"ecalc","operation":"search","query":"voltage divider"}
```

```json
{"action":"ecalc","operation":"describe","id":"voltage_divider"}
```

```json
{"action":"ecalc","operation":"calculate","id":"voltage_divider","inputs":[{"name":"vout","value":"3.3 V"},{"name":"vin","value":"12 V"},{"name":"r1","value":"10k"}],"eseries":"E96"}
```

```json
{"action":"ecalc","operation":"calculate","id":"eseries_combiner","inputs":[{"name":"target","value":"5k"}],"eseries":"E24"}
```

```json
{"action":"ecalc","operation":"table","id":"awg","filter":"1/0"}
```

```json
{"action":"ecalc","operation":"table","id":"awg","lookup":{"column":"awg","value":"12","output":"diameter"}}
```

```json
{"action":"ecalc","operation":"table","id":"ipc2221","lookup":{"mode":"interp","column":"current","value":"1.25 A","output":"ext_1oz_10"}}
```

```json
{"action":"ecalc","operation":"decode","kind":"resistor_bands","code":"brown black red gold"}
```

```json
{"action":"ecalc","operation":"encode","kind":"capacitor","value":"100n","tolerance":"K","voltage":"50V"}
```

```json
{"action":"ecalc","operation":"open","id":"rms_waveform","inputs":[{"name":"vrms","value":"230 V"}],"choices":[{"name":"wave","option":"triangle"}]}
```

## Operations

- `search`: `query`, optional `limit` (1-25, default 10). Results hold `id`, `kind`, `name`, `category` and a one-sentence `summary`, best match first; `total` is the number of matches and `truncated: true` means more exist than were returned.
- `describe`: `id` of a calculator, table or code. Calculator vars have `id`, `label`, `name`, `dim`, `unit` (the unit a bare number is read in; empty means the SI unit), `units` (units a value may carry), `input`, `eseries` and the `default`. A table has `columns` (`id`, `name`, `dim`, `unit`, `units`, `key`), `key`, `row_count`, `notes`, `source`, `guide`/`mains` with a `caution`, and a `finder` when a calculator selects its rows. A code has `code_kind` (the `kind` for decode and encode), `decode` (the forms it reads), `encode` (the request fields) and `fields`.
- `calculate`: `id`, `inputs`, optional `choices` and `eseries` (E3, E6, E12, E24, E48, E96 or E192; default E24).
- `table`: `id` and optionally `filter`, `offset`, `limit` and `lookup` (see Tables).
- `decode`: `kind` and `code` (see Codes).
- `encode`: `kind`, `value` and optionally `bands`, `tolerance`, `tempco`, `voltage` and `class` (which of them a kind reads: see Codes).
- `open`: `id` of any item (optional), optional `inputs` and `choices` (calculators only). Without `id` it only opens the app. The values are not checked against each other; the app shows them as typed.

## Values

- Write values the way a person types them: `4700`, `4.7k`, `4k7`, `4R7` (resistance), `2u2`, `10mA`, `12 V`, `25 °C`, `-10 dBm`. A decimal comma works too.
- A bare number is in the variable's default unit from `describe` (`unit`; the SI unit when it is empty). `2` for a capacity shown in Ah is 2 Ah; write `2000 mAh` to be explicit.
- A list variable takes `"4k7, 10k, 2k2"`: separate the items with a comma and no space between a number and its unit.
- `name` is a variable id from `describe`; case does not matter and the label (`V_in`) works too. Choices (a waveform, a material) are `{name, option}` with ids from `describe`; a choice you leave out uses its default.
- A number system (`dim: integer`, units `dec`, `hex`, `bin`, `oct`) is read in the unit of its variable: a `hex` variable takes hex digits with or without `0x`, a `bin` variable binary digits with or without `0b`; the result is shown the same way (`0xFF`). Whole numbers up to 2^53 - 1 only.
- Give at least `dof` values forming one of the `sets`. With more values the first solvable combination is used and the others are checked against the result.

## Reading the result of calculate

- `quantities` lists every variable and computed output with `si` (SI base units), `formatted` (4 significant digits in the variable's display unit) and `computed` (false for what you gave). Report `formatted` to the user.
- `eseries` on a computed resistor is the nearest standard value of the chosen series with its deviation in percent; offer that value when the user wants to buy or build the circuit.
- A choice option may ignore variables (`ignore` in `describe`, `ignored: true` in the result): you need not give them, and when the values you give do not make a solvable set their defaults complete it (`defaulted: true`).
- `combos` (the standard-value combiner `eseries_combiner`, finder `combine`) lists the nearest single standard value and the best series and parallel pairs of the chosen series for the target resistance: `kind` single, series or parallel, `r1`, `r2`, the combined `value` and `dev_pct`, the deviation from the target in percent.
- `warnings` are the calculator's own checks (for example a divider output above its input); mention them.
- `contradictions` lists a redundant value that differs from the computed one by more than 1 %; tell the user their numbers do not agree and which one you computed from (`basis`).
- A quantity with `error` (`range`, `nonfinite`) could not be computed from these values, for example a division by zero; the answer has `status: error` and `code: calculation_failed` then.

## Tables

- `table` lists rows: `columns` names the columns (`id`, `name`, `dim`, `unit`, `key`) and every row in `rows` is an array of cells in that order. A cell is text with its unit (`"2.5 mm²"`, `"19.5 A"`) or `null` for an empty cell; a column whose `unit` is empty shows each number with its own prefix. `si` repeats the numbers in SI base units (m, m², Ω, A, K) for further calculation; it is `null` for text and empty cells.
- `total` counts the rows that match the `filter`, `returned` the rows listed from `offset`. `truncated: true` with `next_offset` means more rows follow: call again with `offset` set to it. `limit` is 1-50, default 20.
- `filter` keeps the rows with a cell that contains the text, ignoring case: numbers as they are written in the rows, text cells in English or German (`"PVC"`, `"1/0"`).
- `lookup` is `{column, value, mode, output}`. `value` is typed like an input (`"12"`, `"2.5 mm2"`, `"70 °C"`); a bare number is in the unit of the column. `mode` is `exact` (default: the row where `column` equals `value`; without `column` the key column; a text column compares text), `ge` (the first row in table order whose `column` is at least `value`) or `interp` (linear between the neighbouring rows; `column` must rise or fall steadily and `output` is required). `output` names the column to return; without it exact and ge answer with the whole row.
- The `lookup` answer has `found`, `value` (as it was understood, with its unit), `row` (formatted, in the order of `columns`), `result` and `si` of the `output` column, and a `message` when nothing was found (a lookup that finds nothing is an answer, not an error). `ge` takes the first row in table order: a table that runs from large to small (AWG from 4/0 to 40) answers with its first row whenever that qualifies, so read the rows when you need the smallest fit.
- With a `lookup` and no `filter`, `offset` or `limit` only the lookup is answered and no rows are listed.
- `guide: true` marks values transcribed from a standard as a guide: the standard itself is authoritative. `mains: true` marks installation data: the national rules and a qualified person decide. Pass the `caution` on to the user and name the `source` when they rely on a value. `notes` explain conditions and assumptions of the table.
- Answers are shortened to fit the output limit: first `si` is left out (the `note` says so), then fewer rows are listed (`truncated`). Use `filter` or `lookup` instead of asking for more rows.

## Codes

- `decode` reads a code, `encode` writes one. `kind` is the `code_kind` from `describe` of a code item (the id of the code item works too).
- Send `code` and `value` as JSON strings even when they look like numbers (`"code":"103"`, `"value":"100n"`): a bare number there makes the whole call malformed. `offset`, `limit` and `bands` are numbers.
- Write band colours as English colour names separated by blanks, commas or dashes (`brown black red gold`; case does not matter) and markings as printed: `103`, `4R7`, `01C`, `104K 1H`, `4p7`, `X7R`, `C0G`.
- `encode` takes the value the way a person types it (`4k7`, `100n`, `6.8u`) and chooses the nearest standard value of the series that the tolerance implies (20 % E6, 10 % E12, 5 % E24, 2 % E48, 1 % E96, 0.5 % and tighter E192); a changed value is named in `warnings`. Without a tolerance 5 % is assumed (a warning says so). `tolerance`, `tempco` (`"50ppm"`), `voltage` (`"50V"`) and `class` (`"1"` or `"2"`) are written as text; a number is read as typed.
- The kinds, what `decode` reads, what `encode` takes and the ids of the `fields`:

| `kind` | `decode` | `encode` | `fields` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resistor_bands` | 1 to 6 colours (`blue grey red` = 6.8 kΩ ±20 %) | `value`, `tolerance`, `tempco` (6 bands), `bands` 3 to 6 | `tolerance`, `tcr` |
| `inductor_bands` | 4 colours (EIA) or 5 (MIL, silver first) | `value`, `tolerance` 5 or 10 %, `bands` 4 or 5 | `layout`, `tolerance` |
| `smd_resistor` | `472`, `4R7`, `01C` (EIA-96), `1L5`, `000` | `value`, `tolerance` (picks the 3-digit, 4-digit or EIA-96 marking) | `family`; encode adds `code_3digit`, `code_4digit`, `code_eia96` |
| `capacitor` | up to three parts: `104`, `4p7`, `K`, `1H` (`104K 1H` = 100 nF ±10 %, 50 V) | `value`, `tolerance` (letter or %), `voltage` | `family`, `tolerance`, `voltage`; encode adds `value_code`, `rkm` |
| `ceramic_temp` | `X7R`, `C0G`, `NP0`, `U2J` | `class` (required); class 1: `tempco`, `tolerance`; class 2: `value` as a range (`-55..125`), `tolerance` (`15%`) | class 1: `class`, `tc`, `tolerance`, `industry_code`; class 2: `class`, `temp_low`, `temp_high`, `change` |

- The answer has `kind`, `code` (the canonical text), `bands` (colour ids), `value` (SI) with `formatted`, `dim`, `fields` (`id`, `name`, `text` and `value` where it is a number) and `warnings`. A code without a value (a class 2 ceramic code) has none of `value`, `dim` and `formatted`. Pass the `warnings` on: they say that an older tolerance reading exists, that voltage codes are a maker convention (check the datasheet), or that a symbol is ambiguous between makers.

## Errors

- `unknown_id`: the message suggests close matches; search first. `not_a_calculator`, `not_a_table` and `not_a_code`: the id names an item of another kind; the message says which operation reads it.
- `unknown_variable`, `not_an_input` (a computed output cannot be given), `unknown_choice`, `unknown_option`, `unknown_eseries`, `duplicate_name`, `too_many_values`: the message lists the valid names; fix the call.
- `parse_error`: the text of one value could not be read with the unit of its variable or column; the message names the variable or column and its dimension.
- `underdetermined`: too few values, or no combination of them is a solvable set; `sets` lists the input sets closest first and the message says what to add.
- `unknown_column`, `invalid_lookup` (bad mode, no value, missing output, a text column in ge or interp, a column that is not steady for interp), `invalid_filter` (more than 128 characters): the message lists the columns or the valid forms.
- `unknown_code_kind`: the message lists the kinds. `invalid_code`: the code to decode could not be read (the message says why: an unknown colour, a wrong number of bands, more than 64 characters). `invalid_value`: a field of an encode request could not be read or contradicts another (a value that is no number, `bands` out of range, nothing to encode). `unsupported`: well formed, but not decodable or not codable, for example a symbol that makers disagree on or a tolerance without a band colour.
- `invalid_operation`: use `search`, `describe`, `calculate`, `table`, `decode`, `encode` or `open`.
- `policy_denied` with `desktop_unavailable` or `desktop_agent_control_disabled` (open only): the desktop is off or the user has not allowed the agent to control it. Give the numbers from `calculate` or `table` instead and say that the user can open ECalc themselves.
- Answers are shortened to fit the output limit; `truncated: true` marks it. Search again with more specific words or fewer results rather than asking for more.
````

```go
		for _, want := range []string{"always on", "virtual_desktop.allow_agent_control", "tools.virtual_desktop.enabled", "A2A", "calculate, table, decode and encode only"} {
			if !strings.Contains(entry.ConfigGate, want) {
				t.Fatalf("ecalc gate %q lacks %q", entry.ConfigGate, want)
			}
```

The values are written as an ordered JSON object (`ecalcOrdered`): the app reads their order as the order of typing. Keep the ids inside the desktop bridge's patterns (`TestCatalogIDsFitTheDesktopBridge`). Verify `TestECalc*`.

## Part C1 — Conductor tables and the two finders (tasks C1.1, C1.2)


**Goal of this part:** fill the table group "conductors" of the catalog with the reference data that the research collected and cross-checked (`P3\research\conductors\`): the current-carrying capacity of cables (IEC 60364-5-52 / DIN VDE 0298-4: copper and aluminium, PVC and XLPE/EPR) with the ambient temperature, grouping and multi-core factors, flexible cords (DIN VDE 0298-4), the NEC ampacities by AWG, the IEC 60228 standard cross-sections, the PCB conductor spacing of IPC-2221B and IPC-2221C and the PCB copper weight; and add the two finder calculators that search these tables, `cable_cross_section_finder` and `trace_spacing_finder` (category Wiring & PCB), which the tables point to through their `finder` field.

**Architecture:** unchanged from part A. This part adds data only: `catalog/tables/conductors.yaml` (13 table items), `catalog/calculators/finders.yaml` (2 calculators), `testdata/vectors/tables/<id>.json` for every table, `testdata/vectors/calculators/<id>.json` for the finders and the regenerated snapshot. No Go or JavaScript file changes. Every table value is transcribed from the research files (cells that no second source confirmed are empty), every table has spot-checked cells that name their sources, and every finder has hand-checked calculator vectors that the Go and the Node suites both run.

**Tech Stack:** YAML (`gopkg.in/yaml.v3` loader of part A), JSON vectors, Go tests, the Node parity script.

**Spec and contract:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-01-ecalc-design.md` ("Tables", "Content correctness"); the phase 3 contract sections 1.1, 1.3, 2, 3 and 8; part A (`part-a.md`: "Contract deviations" and "What the other parts get from this part"). Part A is applied in the worktree this part was built in (`wc1`).

**How this part was made and verified:** the two files and the 15 vector files below were built in the scratch worktree `wc1` on top of part A, vectors first. The table vectors were typed in from the research files by eye (not produced by the program that wrote the YAML); the finder vectors were computed by an independent model of the finders (exact decimal arithmetic on the research CSV values, the verified-cell rules restated) and never by running the engine. The red and the green runs of both tasks were done once each; the results are in the verification section at the end. The edit blocks of task C1.2 were applied mechanically to the task C1.1 file and reproduce the final file byte for byte.

### Contract deviations (where this list and the contract or the controller's notes disagree, this list wins)

1. **The aluminium tables keep all 14 value columns, empty where no cell is confirmed.** The controller's rule is to drop a column without a verified cell. The finder needs the columns to exist: a choice option names a column through an alias (`refs`), and the loader resolves every call for *every* combination of the options of the choices it uses, failing on a missing column (contract section 2 and part A's `resolveTableCall`). With the choices `cable` (4 tables) and `method` (7 methods, two columns each) a dropped aluminium column would be a load error. So `cable_ampacity_al_pvc` has 9 and `cable_ampacity_al_xlpe` 10 columns without a single cell (listed under "What is left out"); the notes (en+de) say which methods are covered and why. The finder reports such a combination as "not covered by the verified data" (check 0). If the controller wants the empty columns gone from the *screen*, part UT can hide columns whose every cell is empty; nothing else changes. The tables keep one layout for all four materials, which also keeps the finder's aliases simple.
2. **`cable_grouping_factors` is transposed.** The research lists the arrangements as rows (text key) and 14 circuit counts as columns. `lookup` needs a numeric key column (part A, deviation 6), and the finder looks the factor up by the number of circuits. So the key is `circuits` (1, 2, 3 ... 10, 12, 14, 16, 20) and each arrangement is a column (`bunched`, `wall_touching`, `ceiling_touching`, `perforated_tray`, `ladder`, `wall_spaced`, `ceiling_spaced`); the research columns `arrangement` and `methods` are folded into the column names (en+de, with the methods in brackets) and the notes. The numbers are the research numbers.
3. **Column ids.** The four ampacity tables use `section` for the cross-section (the contract's example and `lookup_ge(t, c, 20, section)`), not the research id `size_mm2`; `cable_ambient_temp_factors` keeps `ambient_c`, the flexible cords and IEC 60228 keep `size_mm2`. `pcb_copper_weight` has no unit suffixes in its column ids (`t_physical`, `t_ipc4562`, `t_designation`, `t_137mil`).
4. **13 tables, not 8 to 10.** Every research table has verified data, so none is left out as a whole; with the generated `awg` and `ipc2221` the group "conductors" has 15 tables. The controller can drop `cable_multicore_factors` (5 rows, one column) or `pcb_copper_weight` if the list is too long.
5. **Whole columns and rows that are left out.** `cable_multicore_factors`: the column `k_ground` (not one verified cell) and the rows 19, 40 and 61 (their only value was unverified). `flex_cord_ampacity`: the columns `d_rubber_3` and `d_single_rubber_1` (all values from one source) and the 500 mm² row (only an unverified `a_single_1`). The two 0.5 mm² values that Lapp lists as an "extended range" (12 A single-core, 9 A multi-core) are not in DIN VDE 0298-4 table 11 and are left empty; the table notes give the values. `iec60228_cross_sections` keeps the rows 1400 to 2500 mm² (the size list is confirmed by two sources) with the class 2 resistances empty.
6. **Units.** There is no unit for resistance per length, area weight or ounces per square foot. The resistances are columns of dimension `resistance` in ohm for 1 km of conductor (numerically ohm per km), like the `r_km` column of the generated `awg` table, and say "per km" in the name. The area weight (g/m²) and the copper weight (oz/ft²) are columns of dimension `number` with the unit in the name. Thicknesses in µm are written in metres (`34.15e-6`) in a length column with automatic prefixes (shown as 34.15 µm), the 1.37 mil rule in the explicit unit `mil`. The research columns that only repeat a value in a second unit (`t_ipc4562_mil`, `t_137mil_um`) are dropped; the column unit toggle shows both units.
7. **IPC-2221 spacing.** Revision B and C are two tables (the columns differ: B has A5, C has B5 and A8, and A6 and A7 changed meaning). The last row (voltage above 500 V) keeps its values in the same columns (millimetres per volt) with a marker column `per_volt` (1 for that row) and the key `v_min` 500; the notes say so. The IPC-2221C table notes that the wording of B4 and A6 to A8 comes from one source (pcb-toolkit) and is not checked against section 6.3. The disputed B2 cell for 251 to 300 V is 1.25 mm (research choice, explained in the notes).
8. **`cable_cross_section_finder` (details the contract leaves open).** Inputs: design current `ib`, ambient air temperature `ta`, circuits in the group `nc` (all three inputs, `dof` 3, no rules). Choices: `cable` (cu_pvc, cu_xlpe, al_pvc, al_xlpe: aliases `tbl` = ampacity table, `kcol` = factor column `k_70` or `k_90`), `method` (a1 ... f: aliases `c2` and `c3` = the two ampacity columns, `grp` = grouping column: bunched for A1 to B2, wall_touching for C, perforated_tray for E and F) and `loaded` (constant `three`, 0 or 1; an alias cannot combine two choices, so the expressions pick `c2` or `c3` with `if(three, ...)`). The ambient factor is `interp` (linear between the listed temperatures; outside the rows of the column there is no factor and check 1 says so). The grouping factor uses `lookup_ge` on the circuit count, that is the next larger listed count; where that row's cell is empty (bunched, 14 circuits: one source only) the next row is used (`ng` shows the count taken). The section is `lookup_ge` of the required table value `ib / (kt * kg)` over the chosen column; empty cells are skipped (so copper XLPE 2.5 mm² in A1 and B1 are skipped and method F starts at 25 mm²). `itab` is the table value of that section, `iz = itab * kt * kg`. The table value is not corrected for DIN's 15.5 A (1.5 mm², A1 and A2): the IEC values are used. The finder does not check the protective device.
9. **Checks of the cable finder contain the table calls themselves.** The solver evaluates a check only when every name it uses is known and finite, so a check on `a_min` could never fire when `a_min` is empty. The four checks (0 not covered, 1 ambient outside the factor rows, 2 more than 20 circuits, 3 the current is above the largest cross-section) are therefore written with `lookup_ge` and `interp` calls over inputs that are finite.
10. **`trace_spacing_finder`.** One input `v`, choices `revision` (b, c: constant `revc`), `wave` (peak, rms: constant `vf` 1 or the square root of 2) and `cond` (the board condition by IPC designation: b1 b2 b3 b4 b5 a6 a7 a8; aliases `cb` = the column in IPC-2221B and `cc` = the column in IPC-2221C, constant `inb` = 1 where revision B has the column). The designation B5 means A5 in revision B. A8 does not exist in revision B: `cb` is a placeholder (`b1`), `inb` is 0 and the spacing is empty (`0/0`), check 0 says so. The two tables are named in the expressions directly because the column aliases of the two revisions differ. `vpk` is `abs(v) * vf`, `band_min` the lower limit of the voltage band (500 above 500 V, so the per-volt row is highlighted), `s` the spacing in mm or mil: for `vpk <= 500` the `lookup_ge` of the band upper limit (a voltage between two bands takes the next band up), above 500 V the 301 to 500 V value plus `(vpk - 500)` times the per-volt row (`lookup(t, col, 500)`, key `v_min` 500).
11. **Translations.** The names of tables and finder choices (and the option names of the finder choices) in the 14 locales besides English and German were written by the drafter with natural technical terms, but no native speaker has reviewed them.
12. **Task order.** The tables point to the finders (`finder` field) and the finders use the tables, so task C1.1 creates the tables without the `finder` field and task C1.2 adds the finders and then six one-line additions to the tables. Each task leaves the whole suite green.

### Environment and edit conventions

- Windows box. Set `GOTMPDIR` to a short backslash path and create it once (`$env:GOTMPDIR = 'C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p3-c1'`). Run every command from the repository root.
- `internal/ecalc/**` YAML and JSON files are LF in a Windows working copy. Use the micro sign U+00B5 and the degree sign in text exactly as written below; these files contain no backslash.
- Every "Replace ... with ..." block is the exact text of an edit: the replaced text occurs exactly once in the file at that point of the task and is replaced line for line.
- Commit messages end with the trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Run `detect-changes` before each commit (CLAUDE.md); it must not be `partial` or `truncated`. This part adds data files only and changes no existing function, so there is no symbol to run `impact` on.

### Task C1.1: The conductor tables

**Goal:** `catalog/tables/conductors.yaml` holds the 13 tables of the group "conductors" (without the `finder` field, which task C1.2 adds); every table has a vector file with at least three spot-checked cells that name their sources.

**Files:**

- Create: `internal/ecalc/catalog/tables/conductors.yaml`
- Create: `internal/ecalc/testdata/vectors/tables/<table id>.json` for the 13 ids below
- Modify (regenerated): `internal/ecalc/testdata/catalog.en.json`

- [ ] **Step 1: write the vector files first**

Each file is `{"table", "cells", "lookups"}` in the format of part A: a cell names the row by the key in the unit of the key column (a number, or the text of a text key), the column, the wanted value in the unit of that column (a number, a text, or `null` for an empty cell) and a `ref`; a lookup is an expression in SI units with its wanted SI value (or `"nan"`). The expected values come from the research files, never from the engine. An empty cell is checked with `null` where the reason matters (a cell found in one source only).

```yaml
# Conductor and wiring reference tables of the group "conductors" (cable current ratings, correction factors, standard sizes,
# NEC ampacities, PCB conductor spacing, copper weight). The AWG and IPC-2221 trace width tables are generated (generated.yaml).
# Cells that two independent sources did not confirm are empty (null); the notes of each table say which.
# Names are written in all 16 desktop locales; docs, notes and column names in English and German.

- id: cable_ampacity_cu_pvc
  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: conductors
  name: {cs: "Proudová zatížitelnost kabelů, měď, PVC (70 °C)", da: "Kablers strømbelastning, kobber, PVC (70 °C)", de: "Strombelastbarkeit von Kabeln, Kupfer, PVC (70 °C)", el: "Επιτρεπόμενο ρεύμα καλωδίων, χαλκός, PVC (70 °C)", en: "Cable current ratings, copper, PVC (70 °C)", es: "Intensidad admisible de cables, cobre, PVC (70 °C)", fr: "Courant admissible des câbles, cuivre, PVC (70 °C)", hi: "केबल की धारा वहन क्षमता, तांबा, PVC (70 °C)", it: "Portata dei cavi, rame, PVC (70 °C)", ja: "ケーブルの許容電流、銅、PVC (70 °C)", nl: "Stroombelastbaarheid van kabels, koper, PVC (70 °C)", no: "Strømbelastbarhet for kabler, kobber, PVC (70 °C)", pl: "Obciążalność prądowa kabli, miedź, PVC (70 °C)", pt: "Corrente admissível de cabos, cobre, PVC (70 °C)", sv: "Strömbelastbarhet för kablar, koppar, PVC (70 °C)", zh: "电缆载流量，铜，PVC (70 °C)"}
  doc: {en: "Current-carrying capacity of copper conductors with PVC insulation (70 °C) for the installation methods A1 to F, with two or three loaded conductors, at 30 °C ambient air and one circuit (IEC 60364-5-52, DIN VDE 0298-4).", de: "Strombelastbarkeit von Kupferleitern mit PVC-Isolierung (70 °C) für die Verlegearten A1 bis F, mit 2 oder 3 belasteten Adern, bei 30 °C Umgebungsluft und einem Stromkreis (IEC 60364-5-52, DIN VDE 0298-4)."}
  notes: {en: "Reference conditions: one circuit, 30 °C ambient air, continuous operation, AC 50/60 Hz or DC. Installation methods (IEC 60364-5-52): A1 insulated conductors or single-core cables in conduit in a thermally insulated wall; A2 multi-core cable in conduit in a thermally insulated wall; B1 insulated conductors or single-core cables in conduit on or in a wall; B2 multi-core cable in conduit on or in a wall; C cable fixed directly on or in a wall or on an unperforated tray; E multi-core cable in free air or on a perforated tray, at least 0.3 d from the wall; F single-core cables touching in free air (2 loaded: flat, 3 loaded: trefoil). Multiply by the ambient temperature factor and the grouping factor (see the tables Ambient temperature factors and Grouping factors for cables). Method F has no values below 25 mm². IEC and DIN differ in two cells: DIN VDE 0298-4 (2013) gives 15.5 A for 1.5 mm² in A1 and A2 with two loaded conductors; this table carries the IEC values 14.5 A and 14 A. BS 7671 gives 20 A for 2.5 mm² in method A with two cables, IEC and DIN give 19.5 A (the table follows IEC and DIN).", de: "Bezugsbedingungen: ein Stromkreis, 30 °C Umgebungsluft, Dauerbetrieb, Wechselstrom 50/60 Hz oder Gleichstrom. Verlegearten (IEC 60364-5-52): A1 Aderleitungen oder einadrige Kabel im Elektroinstallationsrohr in wärmegedämmter Wand; A2 mehradriges Kabel oder Mantelleitung im Rohr in wärmegedämmter Wand; B1 Aderleitungen oder einadrige Kabel im Rohr auf oder in der Wand; B2 mehradriges Kabel oder Mantelleitung im Rohr auf oder in der Wand; C Kabel direkt auf oder in der Wand oder auf ungelochter Kabelrinne; E mehradriges Kabel frei in Luft oder auf gelochter Kabelrinne, Wandabstand mindestens 0,3 d; F einadrige Kabel mit Berührung frei in Luft (2 belastet: flach, 3 belastet: Dreieck). Mit dem Umrechnungsfaktor für die Umgebungstemperatur und dem Häufungsfaktor multiplizieren (Tabellen Umrechnungsfaktoren Umgebungstemperatur und Häufungsfaktoren für Kabel). Für die Verlegeart F gibt es keine Werte unter 25 mm². IEC und DIN unterscheiden sich in zwei Zellen: Nach DIN VDE 0298-4 (2013) gelten 15,5 A für 1,5 mm² in A1 und A2 mit 2 belasteten Adern; diese Tabelle enthält die IEC-Werte 14,5 A und 14 A. BS 7671 nennt 20 A für 2,5 mm² in Verlegeart A mit zwei Kabeln, IEC und DIN 19,5 A (die Tabelle folgt IEC und DIN)."}

  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: conductors
  name: {cs: "Proudová zatížitelnost kabelů, měď, XLPE/EPR (90 °C)", da: "Kablers strømbelastning, kobber, XLPE/EPR (90 °C)", de: "Strombelastbarkeit von Kabeln, Kupfer, VPE/EPR (90 °C)", el: "Επιτρεπόμενο ρεύμα καλωδίων, χαλκός, XLPE/EPR (90 °C)", en: "Cable current ratings, copper, XLPE/EPR (90 °C)", es: "Intensidad admisible de cables, cobre, XLPE/EPR (90 °C)", fr: "Courant admissible des câbles, cuivre, XLPE/EPR (90 °C)", hi: "केबल की धारा वहन क्षमता, तांबा, XLPE/EPR (90 °C)", it: "Portata dei cavi, rame, XLPE/EPR (90 °C)", ja: "ケーブルの許容電流、銅、XLPE/EPR (90 °C)", nl: "Stroombelastbaarheid van kabels, koper, XLPE/EPR (90 °C)", no: "Strømbelastbarhet for kabler, kobber, XLPE/EPR (90 °C)", pl: "Obciążalność prądowa kabli, miedź, XLPE/EPR (90 °C)", pt: "Corrente admissível de cabos, cobre, XLPE/EPR (90 °C)", sv: "Strömbelastbarhet för kablar, koppar, XLPE/EPR (90 °C)", zh: "电缆载流量，铜，XLPE/EPR (90 °C)"}
  doc: {en: "Current-carrying capacity of copper conductors with XLPE/EPR insulation (90 °C) for the installation methods A1 to F, with two or three loaded conductors, at 30 °C ambient air and one circuit (IEC 60364-5-52, DIN VDE 0298-4).", de: "Strombelastbarkeit von Kupferleitern mit VPE/EPR-Isolierung (90 °C) für die Verlegearten A1 bis F, mit 2 oder 3 belasteten Adern, bei 30 °C Umgebungsluft und einem Stromkreis (IEC 60364-5-52, DIN VDE 0298-4)."}
  notes: {en: "Reference conditions: one circuit, 30 °C ambient air, continuous operation, AC 50/60 Hz or DC. Installation methods (IEC 60364-5-52): A1 insulated conductors or single-core cables in conduit in a thermally insulated wall; A2 multi-core cable in conduit in a thermally insulated wall; B1 insulated conductors or single-core cables in conduit on or in a wall; B2 multi-core cable in conduit on or in a wall; C cable fixed directly on or in a wall or on an unperforated tray; E multi-core cable in free air or on a perforated tray, at least 0.3 d from the wall; F single-core cables touching in free air (2 loaded: flat, 3 loaded: trefoil). Multiply by the ambient temperature factor and the grouping factor (see the tables Ambient temperature factors and Grouping factors for cables). Method F has no values below 25 mm². The four cells for 2.5 mm² in A1 and B1 are empty: they were found in the ABB handbook only. 90 °C values may only be used if terminals, devices and accessories are rated for 90 °C; in building installations DIN VDE 0298-4 usually limits the conductor temperature to 70 °C, so use the PVC table there.", de: "Bezugsbedingungen: ein Stromkreis, 30 °C Umgebungsluft, Dauerbetrieb, Wechselstrom 50/60 Hz oder Gleichstrom. Verlegearten (IEC 60364-5-52): A1 Aderleitungen oder einadrige Kabel im Elektroinstallationsrohr in wärmegedämmter Wand; A2 mehradriges Kabel oder Mantelleitung im Rohr in wärmegedämmter Wand; B1 Aderleitungen oder einadrige Kabel im Rohr auf oder in der Wand; B2 mehradriges Kabel oder Mantelleitung im Rohr auf oder in der Wand; C Kabel direkt auf oder in der Wand oder auf ungelochter Kabelrinne; E mehradriges Kabel frei in Luft oder auf gelochter Kabelrinne, Wandabstand mindestens 0,3 d; F einadrige Kabel mit Berührung frei in Luft (2 belastet: flach, 3 belastet: Dreieck). Mit dem Umrechnungsfaktor für die Umgebungstemperatur und dem Häufungsfaktor multiplizieren (Tabellen Umrechnungsfaktoren Umgebungstemperatur und Häufungsfaktoren für Kabel). Für die Verlegeart F gibt es keine Werte unter 25 mm². Die vier Zellen für 2,5 mm² in A1 und B1 sind leer: Sie wurden nur im ABB-Handbuch gefunden. 90-°C-Werte nur verwenden, wenn Klemmen, Geräte und Zubehör für 90 °C geeignet sind; in der Gebäudeinstallation begrenzt DIN VDE 0298-4 die Leitertemperatur meist auf 70 °C, dort also die PVC-Tabelle verwenden."}

- id: cable_ampacity_al_pvc
  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: conductors
  name: {cs: "Proudová zatížitelnost kabelů, hliník, PVC (70 °C)", da: "Kablers strømbelastning, aluminium, PVC (70 °C)", de: "Strombelastbarkeit von Kabeln, Aluminium, PVC (70 °C)", el: "Επιτρεπόμενο ρεύμα καλωδίων, αλουμίνιο, PVC (70 °C)", en: "Cable current ratings, aluminium, PVC (70 °C)", es: "Intensidad admisible de cables, aluminio, PVC (70 °C)", fr: "Courant admissible des câbles, aluminium, PVC (70 °C)", hi: "केबल की धारा वहन क्षमता, एल्युमिनियम, PVC (70 °C)", it: "Portata dei cavi, alluminio, PVC (70 °C)", ja: "ケーブルの許容電流、アルミニウム、PVC (70 °C)", nl: "Stroombelastbaarheid van kabels, aluminium, PVC (70 °C)", no: "Strømbelastbarhet for kabler, aluminium, PVC (70 °C)", pl: "Obciążalność prądowa kabli, aluminium, PVC (70 °C)", pt: "Corrente admissível de cabos, alumínio, PVC (70 °C)", sv: "Strömbelastbarhet för kablar, aluminium, PVC (70 °C)", zh: "电缆载流量，铝，PVC (70 °C)"}
  doc: {en: "Current-carrying capacity of aluminium conductors with PVC insulation (70 °C) for the installation methods A1 to F, with two or three loaded conductors, at 30 °C ambient air and one circuit (IEC 60364-5-52, DIN VDE 0298-4).", de: "Strombelastbarkeit von Aluminiumleitern mit PVC-Isolierung (70 °C) für die Verlegearten A1 bis F, mit 2 oder 3 belasteten Adern, bei 30 °C Umgebungsluft und einem Stromkreis (IEC 60364-5-52, DIN VDE 0298-4)."}
  notes: {en: "Reference conditions: one circuit, 30 °C ambient air, continuous operation, AC 50/60 Hz or DC. Installation methods (IEC 60364-5-52): A1 insulated conductors or single-core cables in conduit in a thermally insulated wall; A2 multi-core cable in conduit in a thermally insulated wall; B1 insulated conductors or single-core cables in conduit on or in a wall; B2 multi-core cable in conduit on or in a wall; C cable fixed directly on or in a wall or on an unperforated tray; E multi-core cable in free air or on a perforated tray, at least 0.3 d from the wall; F single-core cables touching in free air (2 loaded: flat, 3 loaded: trefoil). Multiply by the ambient temperature factor and the grouping factor (see the tables Ambient temperature factors and Grouping factors for cables). Method F has no values below 25 mm². Aluminium conductors from 16 mm² (IEC also lists 2.5 to 10 mm²). Only the columns with three loaded conductors in A1, A2, B1, B2 and C are confirmed by a second source; the columns with two loaded conductors and the methods E and F are empty (ABB handbook only). All columns are kept so that the four ampacity tables have the same layout. Aluminium conductors need terminals approved for aluminium.", de: "Bezugsbedingungen: ein Stromkreis, 30 °C Umgebungsluft, Dauerbetrieb, Wechselstrom 50/60 Hz oder Gleichstrom. Verlegearten (IEC 60364-5-52): A1 Aderleitungen oder einadrige Kabel im Elektroinstallationsrohr in wärmegedämmter Wand; A2 mehradriges Kabel oder Mantelleitung im Rohr in wärmegedämmter Wand; B1 Aderleitungen oder einadrige Kabel im Rohr auf oder in der Wand; B2 mehradriges Kabel oder Mantelleitung im Rohr auf oder in der Wand; C Kabel direkt auf oder in der Wand oder auf ungelochter Kabelrinne; E mehradriges Kabel frei in Luft oder auf gelochter Kabelrinne, Wandabstand mindestens 0,3 d; F einadrige Kabel mit Berührung frei in Luft (2 belastet: flach, 3 belastet: Dreieck). Mit dem Umrechnungsfaktor für die Umgebungstemperatur und dem Häufungsfaktor multiplizieren (Tabellen Umrechnungsfaktoren Umgebungstemperatur und Häufungsfaktoren für Kabel). Für die Verlegeart F gibt es keine Werte unter 25 mm². Aluminiumleiter ab 16 mm² (IEC nennt auch 2,5 bis 10 mm²). Nur die Spalten mit 3 belasteten Adern in A1, A2, B1, B2 und C sind durch eine zweite Quelle bestätigt; die Spalten mit 2 belasteten Adern und die Verlegearten E und F sind leer (nur das ABB-Handbuch). Alle Spalten bleiben erhalten, damit die vier Belastbarkeitstabellen denselben Aufbau haben. Aluminiumleiter nur an dafür zugelassenen Klemmen anschließen."}
  tags: [ampacity, current rating, current carrying capacity, cable, wire, aluminium, pvc, iec 60364-5-52, strombelastbarkeit, belastbarkeit, kabel, leitung, aluminium, din vde 0298-4, verlegeart]

  doc: {en: "Current-carrying capacity of aluminium conductors with XLPE/EPR insulation (90 °C) for the installation methods A1 to F, with two or three loaded conductors, at 30 °C ambient air and one circuit (IEC 60364-5-52, DIN VDE 0298-4).", de: "Strombelastbarkeit von Aluminiumleitern mit VPE/EPR-Isolierung (90 °C) für die Verlegearten A1 bis F, mit 2 oder 3 belasteten Adern, bei 30 °C Umgebungsluft und einem Stromkreis (IEC 60364-5-52, DIN VDE 0298-4)."}
  notes: {en: "Reference conditions: one circuit, 30 °C ambient air, continuous operation, AC 50/60 Hz or DC. Installation methods (IEC 60364-5-52): A1 insulated conductors or single-core cables in conduit in a thermally insulated wall; A2 multi-core cable in conduit in a thermally insulated wall; B1 insulated conductors or single-core cables in conduit on or in a wall; B2 multi-core cable in conduit on or in a wall; C cable fixed directly on or in a wall or on an unperforated tray; E multi-core cable in free air or on a perforated tray, at least 0.3 d from the wall; F single-core cables touching in free air (2 loaded: flat, 3 loaded: trefoil). Multiply by the ambient temperature factor and the grouping factor (see the tables Ambient temperature factors and Grouping factors for cables). Method F has no values below 25 mm². Aluminium conductors from 16 mm². Only method F (25 to 240 mm²) and 14 cells of method B1 are confirmed by a second source (Prysmian datasheets for AL XZ1 cables); every other cell is empty (ABB handbook only, or a second source that agrees only within 1 A). All columns are kept so that the four ampacity tables have the same layout. 90 °C values may only be used if terminals, devices and accessories are rated for 90 °C. Aluminium conductors need terminals approved for aluminium.", de: "Bezugsbedingungen: ein Stromkreis, 30 °C Umgebungsluft, Dauerbetrieb, Wechselstrom 50/60 Hz oder Gleichstrom. Verlegearten (IEC 60364-5-52): A1 Aderleitungen oder einadrige Kabel im Elektroinstallationsrohr in wärmegedämmter Wand; A2 mehradriges Kabel oder Mantelleitung im Rohr in wärmegedämmter Wand; B1 Aderleitungen oder einadrige Kabel im Rohr auf oder in der Wand; B2 mehradriges Kabel oder Mantelleitung im Rohr auf oder in der Wand; C Kabel direkt auf oder in der Wand oder auf ungelochter Kabelrinne; E mehradriges Kabel frei in Luft oder auf gelochter Kabelrinne, Wandabstand mindestens 0,3 d; F einadrige Kabel mit Berührung frei in Luft (2 belastet: flach, 3 belastet: Dreieck). Mit dem Umrechnungsfaktor für die Umgebungstemperatur und dem Häufungsfaktor multiplizieren (Tabellen Umrechnungsfaktoren Umgebungstemperatur und Häufungsfaktoren für Kabel). Für die Verlegeart F gibt es keine Werte unter 25 mm². Aluminiumleiter ab 16 mm². Nur die Verlegeart F (25 bis 240 mm²) und 14 Zellen der Verlegeart B1 sind durch eine zweite Quelle bestätigt (Prysmian-Datenblätter für AL-XZ1-Kabel); alle anderen Zellen sind leer (nur das ABB-Handbuch, oder eine zweite Quelle, die nur auf 1 A genau übereinstimmt). Alle Spalten bleiben erhalten, damit die vier Belastbarkeitstabellen denselben Aufbau haben. 90-°C-Werte nur verwenden, wenn Klemmen, Geräte und Zubehör für 90 °C geeignet sind. Aluminiumleiter nur an dafür zugelassenen Klemmen anschließen."}
  tags: [ampacity, current rating, current carrying capacity, cable, wire, aluminium, xlpe epr, iec 60364-5-52, strombelastbarkeit, belastbarkeit, kabel, leitung, aluminium, din vde 0298-4, verlegeart]

  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: conductors
  name: {cs: "Součinitele okolní teploty pro kabely ve vzduchu", da: "Korrektionsfaktorer for omgivelsestemperatur (kabler i luft)", de: "Umrechnungsfaktoren Umgebungstemperatur (Kabel in Luft)", el: "Συντελεστές διόρθωσης θερμοκρασίας περιβάλλοντος (καλώδια στον αέρα)", en: "Ambient temperature factors for cables in air", es: "Factores de corrección por temperatura ambiente (cables en aire)", fr: "Facteurs de correction de la température ambiante (câbles dans l'air)", hi: "परिवेश तापमान सुधार गुणांक (हवा में केबल)", it: "Fattori di correzione per la temperatura ambiente (cavi in aria)", ja: "周囲温度の補正係数（気中ケーブル）", nl: "Correctiefactoren voor omgevingstemperatuur (kabels in lucht)", no: "Korreksjonsfaktorer for omgivelsestemperatur (kabler i luft)", pl: "Współczynniki korekcyjne temperatury otoczenia (kable w powietrzu)", pt: "Fatores de correção da temperatura ambiente (cabos no ar)", sv: "Korrektionsfaktorer för omgivningstemperatur (kablar i luft)", zh: "环境温度校正系数（空气中的电缆）"}
  doc: {en: "Correction factors for the current-carrying capacity of cables in air at an ambient temperature other than 30 °C, for conductors rated 60 °C (rubber cords), 70 °C (PVC) and 90 °C (XLPE, EPR) (IEC 60364-5-52 table B.52.14, DIN VDE 0298-4 table 17).", de: "Umrechnungsfaktoren für die Strombelastbarkeit von Kabeln in Luft bei einer anderen Umgebungstemperatur als 30 °C, für Leitertemperaturen von 60 °C (Gummileitungen), 70 °C (PVC) und 90 °C (VPE, EPR) (IEC 60364-5-52 Tabelle B.52.14, DIN VDE 0298-4 Tabelle 17)."}
  notes: {en: "Multiply the current-carrying capacity for 30 °C by k. An empty cell means that the insulation is not permitted at that ambient temperature. The 65 °C value of the 70 °C column (0.35) comes from DIN VDE 0298-4; IEC stops at 60 °C. The 60 °C column (DIN VDE 0298-4 only, for rubber cords) is empty from 10 to 25 °C and the 90 °C value at 85 °C is omitted, because they were found in one source only. For cables in the ground other factors apply (reference 20 °C, IEC table B.52.15). In Germany 25 °C is common practice; the factor for 70 °C is then 1.06.", de: "Mit k multiplizieren. Eine leere Zelle bedeutet, dass die Isolierung bei dieser Umgebungstemperatur nicht zulässig ist. Der Wert bei 65 °C in der 70-°C-Spalte (0,35) stammt aus DIN VDE 0298-4; IEC endet bei 60 °C. Die 60-°C-Spalte (nur DIN VDE 0298-4, für Gummileitungen) ist von 10 bis 25 °C leer und der 90-°C-Wert bei 85 °C fehlt, weil sie nur in einer Quelle gefunden wurden. Für Kabel in Erde gelten andere Faktoren (Bezug 20 °C, IEC Tabelle B.52.15). In Deutschland ist 25 °C üblich; der Faktor für 70 °C ist dann 1,06."}
  tags: [ambient temperature, correction factor, temperature factor, derating, cable, ampacity, iec 60364-5-52, umgebungstemperatur, umrechnungsfaktor, temperaturfaktor, kabel, belastbarkeit, din vde 0298-4]

- id: cable_grouping_factors
  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: conductors
  name: {cs: "Součinitele seskupení kabelů", da: "Reduktionsfaktorer for kabelgrupper", de: "Häufungsfaktoren für Kabel", el: "Συντελεστές ομαδοποίησης καλωδίων", en: "Grouping factors for cables", es: "Factores de agrupamiento de cables", fr: "Facteurs de groupement des câbles", hi: "केबल समूहन गुणांक", it: "Fattori di raggruppamento dei cavi", ja: "ケーブル集合の低減係数", nl: "Groepeerfactoren voor kabels", no: "Reduksjonsfaktorer for kabelgrupper", pl: "Współczynniki grupowania kabli", pt: "Fatores de agrupamento de cabos", sv: "Reduktionsfaktorer för kabelgrupper", zh: "电缆成束敷设降容系数"}
  doc: {en: "Reduction factors for the current-carrying capacity of cables in groups of several circuits (one multi-core cable, or one group of 2 or 3 single-core cables, counts as one circuit), by the arrangement of the cables (IEC 60364-5-52 table B.52.17, DIN VDE 0298-4 table 21).", de: "Reduktionsfaktoren für die Strombelastbarkeit von Kabeln in Gruppen mehrerer Stromkreise (ein mehradriges Kabel oder eine Gruppe aus 2 oder 3 einadrigen Kabeln zählt als ein Stromkreis), nach der Anordnung der Kabel (IEC 60364-5-52 Tabelle B.52.17, DIN VDE 0298-4 Tabelle 21)."}
  notes: {en: "The standard lists the arrangements as rows and the numbers of circuits as columns; here they are swapped so that the number of circuits is the key. The factors apply to cables of similar size that are equally loaded and touch each other, unless stated otherwise; the sizes may differ by at most three adjacent standard sizes (IEC) or one size step (DIN). No factor is needed when the horizontal clearance exceeds twice the cable diameter or when a cable carries less than 30 % of its grouped rating. For single-layer arrangements there is no further reduction above nine circuits (IEC), so the factors for 10 to 20 circuits repeat the value for nine. The two spaced arrangements come from DIN VDE 0298-4 only. Empty cells are not listed in the standard or were found in one source only (the bunched factor for 14 circuits and the spaced factors for 5, 8, 12 and 14 circuits). If the number of circuits is not listed, use the next larger listed number.", de: "Die Norm führt die Anordnungen als Zeilen und die Stromkreiszahlen als Spalten; hier sind sie vertauscht, damit die Zahl der Stromkreise der Schlüssel ist. Die Faktoren gelten für gleichartige, gleich belastete Kabel, die sich berühren, soweit nichts anderes steht; die Querschnitte dürfen sich um höchstens drei benachbarte Normgrößen (IEC) bzw. eine Größenstufe (DIN) unterscheiden. Kein Faktor ist nötig, wenn der lichte Abstand größer als der doppelte Kabeldurchmesser ist oder ein Kabel weniger als 30 % seiner Belastbarkeit in der Gruppe führt. Bei einlagigen Anordnungen gibt es oberhalb von neun Stromkreisen keine weitere Verminderung (IEC); die Faktoren für 10 bis 20 Stromkreise wiederholen daher den Wert für neun. Die beiden Anordnungen mit Abstand stammen nur aus DIN VDE 0298-4. Leere Zellen sind in der Norm nicht aufgeführt oder wurden nur in einer Quelle gefunden (der Faktor gebündelt für 14 Stromkreise und die Faktoren mit Abstand für 5, 8, 12 und 14 Stromkreise). Ist die Stromkreiszahl nicht aufgeführt, gilt die nächstgrößere aufgeführte Zahl."}
  tags: [grouping, grouping factor, bunched, derating, cable, ampacity, iec 60364-5-52, häufung, häufungsfaktor, gebündelt, kabel, belastbarkeit, din vde 0298-4]
  source: "IEC 60364-5-52:2009 table B.52.17 and DIN VDE 0298-4:2013-06 table 21, as reproduced in the Schneider Electrical Installation Guide (figure G16), the ABB SACE Electrical Installation Handbook vol. 2 (4th ed., table 5), ABB Stotz-Kontakt 2CDC400027D0104 (table 7) and Lapp T12 (table 12-6)"

- id: cable_multicore_factors
  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: conductors
  name: {cs: "Součinitele pro vícežilové kabely a šňůry", da: "Faktorer for flerlederkabler og -ledninger", de: "Umrechnungsfaktoren für vieladrige Leitungen", el: "Συντελεστές για πολυπολικά καλώδια και εύκαμπτα καλώδια", en: "Factors for multi-core cables and cords", es: "Factores para cables y cordones multiconductores", fr: "Facteurs pour câbles et cordons multiconducteurs", hi: "बहु-कोर केबल और कॉर्ड के गुणांक", it: "Fattori per cavi e cordoni multipolari", ja: "多心ケーブル・コードの補正係数", nl: "Factoren voor meeraderige kabels en snoeren", no: "Faktorer for flerlederkabler og ledninger", pl: "Współczynniki dla kabli i przewodów wielożyłowych", pt: "Fatores para cabos e cordões multicondutores", sv: "Faktorer för flerledarkablar och sladdar", zh: "多芯电缆和软线的校正系数"}
  doc: {en: "Factors for multi-core cables and cords with conductor cross-sections up to 10 mm² and more than three loaded cores, for installation in air (DIN VDE 0298-4 table 26).", de: "Faktoren für vieladrige Kabel und Leitungen mit Leiternennquerschnitten bis 10 mm² und mehr als drei belasteten Adern, für Verlegung in Luft (DIN VDE 0298-4 Tabelle 26)."}
  notes: {en: "Apply the factor to the current-carrying capacity for three loaded conductors. Count only the cores that carry load current (not PE; a neutral only if it carries current, for example harmonics), and use the next listed number of loaded cores. The factors for installation in the ground and the rows for 19, 40 and 61 cores were found in one source only and are omitted.", de: "Den Faktor auf die Strombelastbarkeit für 3 belastete Adern anwenden. Nur Adern zählen, die Laststrom führen (nicht PE; ein Neutralleiter nur, wenn er Strom führt, z. B. durch Oberschwingungen), und die nächste aufgeführte Aderzahl verwenden. Die Faktoren für Verlegung in Erde und die Zeilen für 19, 40 und 61 Adern wurden nur in einer Quelle gefunden und fehlen."}

- id: flex_cord_ampacity
  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: conductors
  name: {cs: "Proudová zatížitelnost ohebných šňůr (DIN VDE 0298-4)", da: "Strømbelastning af fleksible ledninger (DIN VDE 0298-4)", de: "Strombelastbarkeit flexibler Leitungen (DIN VDE 0298-4)", el: "Επιτρεπόμενο ρεύμα εύκαμπτων καλωδίων (DIN VDE 0298-4)", en: "Flexible cord current ratings (DIN VDE 0298-4)", es: "Intensidad admisible de cables flexibles (DIN VDE 0298-4)", fr: "Courant admissible des câbles souples (DIN VDE 0298-4)", hi: "लचीली केबल की धारा क्षमता (DIN VDE 0298-4)", it: "Portata dei cavi flessibili (DIN VDE 0298-4)", ja: "可とう性コードの許容電流 (DIN VDE 0298-4)", nl: "Stroombelastbaarheid van flexibele snoeren (DIN VDE 0298-4)", no: "Strømbelastbarhet for fleksible ledninger (DIN VDE 0298-4)", pl: "Obciążalność prądowa przewodów giętkich (DIN VDE 0298-4)", pt: "Corrente admissível de cabos flexíveis (DIN VDE 0298-4)", sv: "Strömbelastbarhet för flexibla ledningar (DIN VDE 0298-4)", zh: "软线载流量 (DIN VDE 0298-4)"}
  doc: {en: "Current-carrying capacity of flexible copper cords and cables at 30 °C ambient air by cord type group, for fixed use and continuous operation (DIN VDE 0298-4 table 11).", de: "Strombelastbarkeit flexibler Kupferleitungen bei 30 °C Umgebungsluft nach Leitungsgruppe, für feste Verlegung und Dauerbetrieb (DIN VDE 0298-4 Tabelle 11)."}
  notes: {en: "The permissible conductor temperature depends on the cord type (for example 60 °C rubber, 70 °C PVC); which cord types belong to which column is listed in DIN VDE 0298-4 (tables 1 and 11). Correct for the ambient temperature, grouping and multi-core cords with the factor tables. For cords on reels the factor is 0.80 for one layer (DIN VDE 0298-4 table 27). Not included: the columns for heavy rubber cables (0.6/1 kV) and single-core special rubber cables, the 500 mm² row, the cells for 6 and 10 mm² household appliance cords with two loaded conductors (one source only), and for 0.5 mm² the single-core and multi-core values of Lapp's extended range (12 A and 9 A), which are not part of table 11.", de: "Die zulässige Leitertemperatur hängt von der Leitungsbauart ab (z. B. 60 °C Gummi, 70 °C PVC); welche Bauarten zu welcher Spalte gehören, steht in DIN VDE 0298-4 (Tabellen 1 und 11). Umgebungstemperatur, Häufung und vieladrige Leitungen mit den Faktortabellen berücksichtigen. Für aufgewickelte Leitungen gilt der Faktor 0,80 bei einer Lage (DIN VDE 0298-4 Tabelle 27). Nicht enthalten: die Spalten für schwere Gummischlauchleitungen (0,6/1 kV) und einadrige Sondergummiaderleitungen, die Zeile 500 mm², die Zellen für Haus- und Handgeräteleitungen mit 6 und 10 mm² und 2 belasteten Adern (nur eine Quelle) sowie für 0,5 mm² die Werte des erweiterten Bereichs von Lapp für einadrige und mehradrige Leitungen (12 A und 9 A), die nicht Teil der Tabelle 11 sind."}

- id: nec_ampacity_awg
  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: conductors
  name: {cs: "Proudová zatížitelnost podle NEC a AWG (tabulka 310.16)", da: "NEC-strømbelastning efter AWG (tabel 310.16)", de: "NEC-Strombelastbarkeit nach AWG (Tabelle 310.16)", el: "Επιτρεπόμενα ρεύματα NEC ανά AWG (πίνακας 310.16)", en: "NEC ampacities by AWG (table 310.16)", es: "Intensidades admisibles NEC por AWG (tabla 310.16)", fr: "Courants admissibles NEC par AWG (tableau 310.16)", hi: "AWG के अनुसार NEC की धारा क्षमता (तालिका 310.16)", it: "Portate NEC per AWG (tabella 310.16)", ja: "AWG別のNEC許容電流（表310.16）", nl: "NEC-stroombelastbaarheid per AWG (tabel 310.16)", no: "NEC-strømbelastbarhet etter AWG (tabell 310.16)", pl: "Obciążalność NEC według AWG (tabela 310.16)", pt: "Correntes admissíveis NEC por AWG (tabela 310.16)", sv: "NEC-strömbelastbarhet per AWG (tabell 310.16)", zh: "按 AWG 的 NEC 载流量（表 310.16）"}
  doc: {en: "Allowable ampacities of insulated copper and aluminium conductors rated 0 to 2000 V, with not more than three current-carrying conductors in a raceway, cable or the earth, at 30 °C ambient, by AWG or kcmil size (NEC table 310.16).", de: "Zulässige Strombelastbarkeit isolierter Kupfer- und Aluminiumleiter für 0 bis 2000 V, mit höchstens drei stromführenden Leitern im Rohr, Kabel oder Erdreich, bei 30 °C Umgebung, nach AWG- bzw. kcmil-Größe (NEC Tabelle 310.16)."}
  notes: {en: "US view; for IEC and DIN installations use the cable current-rating tables. The columns are the temperature rating of the insulation (60, 75 and 90 °C); the temperature rating of the terminals (usually 60 °C or 75 °C) limits which column may be used. Aluminium means aluminium or copper-clad aluminium. The overcurrent device for 14, 12 and 10 AWG copper is limited to 15, 20 and 30 A (NEC 240.4(D)) whatever the table says; the last column marks these rows. Correct for the ambient temperature (NEC 310.15(B)) and for more than three current-carrying conductors (NEC 310.15(C)(1)). NEC 2023 values; the first draft of the 2026 NEC adds values that are not included.", de: "US-Sicht (NEC); für IEC- und DIN-Anlagen die Kabel-Belastbarkeitstabellen verwenden. Die Spalten sind die Temperaturfestigkeit der Isolierung (60, 75 und 90 °C); die Temperaturfestigkeit der Klemmen (meist 60 °C oder 75 °C) bestimmt, welche Spalte nutzbar ist. Aluminium steht für Aluminium oder kupferkaschiertes Aluminium. Die Absicherung für 14, 12 und 10 AWG Kupfer ist auf 15, 20 und 30 A begrenzt (NEC 240.4(D)), unabhängig vom Tabellenwert; die letzte Spalte kennzeichnet diese Zeilen. Umgebungstemperatur (NEC 310.15(B)) und mehr als drei stromführende Leiter (NEC 310.15(C)(1)) sind zusätzlich zu berücksichtigen. Werte des NEC 2023; der erste Entwurf des NEC 2026 ergänzt Werte, die nicht enthalten sind."}
  tags: [nec, ampacity, awg, kcmil, current rating, wire, cable, 310.16, us, strombelastbarkeit, belastbarkeit, leitung, kabel, usa]
  source: "NFPA 70 National Electrical Code 2023 table 310.16 (the same values as NEC 2017 table 310.15(B)(16)), checked against the NFPA CMP-6 first draft report of the 2026 cycle, the Omni Cable NEC ampacity data and the Cerrowire ampacity charts"

  doc: {en: "Nominal conductor cross-sections of IEC 60228 with the maximum DC resistance of 1 km at 20 °C for stranded copper and aluminium conductors (class 2) and flexible copper conductors (class 5).", de: "Nennquerschnitte nach IEC 60228 mit dem höchstzulässigen Gleichstromwiderstand von 1 km bei 20 °C für mehrdrähtige Kupfer- und Aluminiumleiter (Klasse 2) und feindrähtige Kupferleiter (Klasse 5)."}
  notes: {en: "Class 1 is solid, class 2 stranded (fixed installation), class 5 flexible and class 6 very flexible. The resistances are maxima per kilometre at 20 °C, shown as the resistance of 1 km. Class 1 copper differs from class 2 from 185 mm² upwards (185 mm²: 0.101 against 0.0991 Ω/km); class 6 has the class 5 values up to 300 mm². The class 2 resistances of 1400 to 2500 mm² were found in one source only and are empty. The sizes 1400 and 1800 mm² are not preferred.", de: "Klasse 1 ist eindrähtig, Klasse 2 mehrdrähtig (feste Verlegung), Klasse 5 feindrähtig und Klasse 6 feinstdrähtig. Die Widerstände sind Höchstwerte je Kilometer bei 20 °C, angegeben als Widerstand von 1 km. Klasse-1-Kupfer weicht ab 185 mm² von Klasse 2 ab (185 mm²: 0,101 gegen 0,0991 Ω/km); Klasse 6 hat bis 300 mm² die Werte von Klasse 5. Die Klasse-2-Widerstände von 1400 bis 2500 mm² wurden nur in einer Quelle gefunden und sind leer. Die Größen 1400 und 1800 mm² sind nicht bevorzugt."}

- id: ipc2221b_conductor_spacing
  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: conductors
  name: {cs: "Vzdálenosti vodičů na DPS podle napětí (IPC-2221B)", da: "Lederafstand på print efter spænding (IPC-2221B)", de: "Leiterabstände auf Leiterplatten nach Spannung (IPC-2221B)", el: "Αποστάσεις αγωγών PCB ανά τάση (IPC-2221B)", en: "PCB conductor spacing by voltage (IPC-2221B)", es: "Separación de conductores en PCB según la tensión (IPC-2221B)", fr: "Distances entre conducteurs d'un circuit imprimé selon la tension (IPC-2221B)", hi: "वोल्टेज के अनुसार पीसीबी चालक दूरी (IPC-2221B)", it: "Distanza tra i conduttori del PCB in base alla tensione (IPC-2221B)", ja: "電圧別のプリント基板導体間隔 (IPC-2221B)", nl: "Geleiderafstand op pcb per spanning (IPC-2221B)", no: "Lederavstand på kretskort etter spenning (IPC-2221B)", pl: "Odstępy między ścieżkami PCB według napięcia (IPC-2221B)", pt: "Distância entre condutores em PCB por tensão (IPC-2221B)", sv: "Ledaravstånd på kretskort efter spänning (IPC-2221B)", zh: "按电压的 PCB 导体间距 (IPC-2221B)"}
  doc: {en: "Minimum spacing between conductors on a printed board by the voltage between them (DC or AC peak), for internal and external conductors and component leads (IPC-2221B table 6-1, the same table as in IPC-2221A).", de: "Mindestabstand zwischen Leitern auf einer Leiterplatte nach der Spannung zwischen ihnen (DC oder AC-Scheitelwert), für Innen- und Außenlagen und Bauteilanschlüsse (IPC-2221B Tabelle 6-1, dieselbe Tabelle wie in IPC-2221A)."}
  notes: {en: "IPC-2221 spacing is functional spacing for printed boards; for mains or safety isolation use the creepage and clearance of IEC 60664-1 and IEC 62368-1. The bands use whole volts, so a voltage between two bands (15.5 V) belongs to the next band up. In the last row (per-volt row, marked 1) the values are millimetres (or mil) per volt: for a voltage above 500 V add them for every volt above 500 V to the value of the 301 to 500 V row. Solder resist does not count as a coating for B2 and B3. One reproduction of the table printed 2.5 mm instead of 1.25 mm for B2 at 251 to 300 V; 1.25 mm agrees with the remark that IPC gives 1.25 mm at 300 V and 2.5 mm at 301 V and with IPC-2221C. IPC-2221C (2023) revised the table, see its own table.", de: "IPC-2221 gibt Funktionsabstände für Leiterplatten an; für Netz- bzw. Schutztrennung gelten die Kriech- und Luftstrecken nach IEC 60664-1 und IEC 62368-1. Die Bänder verwenden ganze Volt; eine Spannung zwischen zwei Bändern (15,5 V) gehört zum nächsthöheren Band. In der letzten Zeile (Zeile je Volt, mit 1 markiert) stehen Millimeter (oder mil) je Volt: Für eine Spannung über 500 V werden sie für jedes Volt über 500 V zum Wert der Zeile 301 bis 500 V addiert. Lötstopplack gilt für B2 und B3 nicht als Beschichtung. Eine Wiedergabe der Tabelle nannte für B2 bei 251 bis 300 V 2,5 mm statt 1,25 mm; 1,25 mm passt zur Angabe, dass IPC bei 300 V 1,25 mm und bei 301 V 2,5 mm nennt, und zu IPC-2221C. IPC-2221C (2023) hat die Tabelle überarbeitet, siehe die eigene Tabelle."}
  tags: [ipc-2221, pcb, spacing, clearance, creepage, conductor spacing, voltage, isolation, leiterplatte, abstand, leiterabstand, spannung, kriechstrecke, luftstrecke, ipc-2221b]
  source: "IPC-2221B table 6-1 (electrical conductor spacing), read from the Altium Resources and P. McGaw reproductions and checked against smps.us and the Siemens EDA article by S. V. Chavez (2025)"
  guide: true

    - {id: b4, name: {en: "B4: external, permanent polymer coating", de: "B4: außen, dauerhafte Polymerbeschichtung"}, dim: length, unit: mm, units: [mm, mil], label: "s"}

  doc: {en: "Copper weight of printed-circuit copper layers in ounces per square foot with the area weight and the thickness by several conventions (physical density, IPC-4562A, commercial designation, 1.37 mil rule).", de: "Kupferauflage von Leiterplatten-Kupferlagen in Unzen je Quadratfuß mit dem Flächengewicht und der Dicke nach mehreren Konventionen (physikalische Dichte, IPC-4562A, handelsübliche Bezeichnung, Regel 1,37 mil)."}
  notes: {en: "A copper weight of 1 oz is an area weight (1 ounce of copper spread over 1 square foot), not an exact thickness: 34.2 µm (density of pure copper), 34.3 µm (IPC-4562A nominal), 34.8 µm (1.37 mil rule) and 35 µm (designation) are all in use. ECalc's unit oz uses 35 µm. The area weight follows from the unit definitions (1 oz/ft² = 305.1517 g/m²); the physical thickness assumes 8.935 g/cm³. Finished copper after processing is thinner (about 30 µm for 1 oz). The designations of 1/4 and 3/8 oz are names and not exact fractions of 1 oz. The rows for 1/4, 3/8 and 4 oz of the 1.37 mil rule are arithmetic extensions. Typical values; empty cells have no published value.", de: "Eine Kupferauflage von 1 oz ist ein Flächengewicht (1 Unze Kupfer auf 1 Quadratfuß verteilt), keine genaue Dicke: 34,2 µm (Dichte von reinem Kupfer), 34,3 µm (IPC-4562A), 34,8 µm (Regel 1,37 mil) und 35 µm (Handelsbezeichnung) sind gebräuchlich. ECalc rechnet mit 35 µm für die Einheit oz. Das Flächengewicht folgt aus den Einheitendefinitionen (1 oz/ft² = 305,1517 g/m²); die physikalische Dicke nimmt 8,935 g/cm³ an. Nach der Fertigung ist das Kupfer dünner (bei 1 oz etwa 30 µm). Die Bezeichnungen 1/4 und 3/8 oz sind Namen und keine genauen Bruchteile von 1 oz. Die Zeilen 1/4, 3/8 und 4 oz der Regel 1,37 mil sind rechnerische Fortsetzungen. Typische Werte; leere Zellen haben keinen veröffentlichten Wert."}
```

- [ ] **Step 1: write the calculator vectors first**

A `set` is a consistent solution (a value for every variable and every derived quantity, `"nan"` where the quantity is empty) for one option of each choice; every option of every choice has at least two sets, and each set is replayed through every rule alternative and through `Solve`. A `solve` entry is one `Solve` call with its expected values and the exact warning indexes. The `ref` of each entry shows the hand calculation (exact decimals, the table cells named). The cable finder's warnings are: 0 not covered, 1 ambient temperature outside the factor rows, 2 more than 20 circuits, 3 current above the largest cross-section; the spacing finder's: 0 column A8 in IPC-2221B, 1 voltage above 500 V.

**Create `internal/ecalc/testdata/vectors/calculators/cable_cross_section_finder.json`** with exactly this content:

- [ ] **Step 3: create the finders**

**Create `internal/ecalc/catalog/calculators/finders.yaml`** with exactly this content:

```yaml
# Finders: calculators that search a table. Each is named by the finder field of its tables, which fixes some of the choices
# and highlights the row of the result. Every name is written in all 16 desktop locales; docs, variable names and warnings in
# English and German (other languages fall back to English).
#
# Table and column names that depend on a choice are aliases (refs) of the choice options. All four cable ampacity tables have
# the same columns, so every combination of the choices resolves; a column without a verified cell is empty, and the finder
# then reports that the combination is not covered.

- id: cable_cross_section_finder
  kind: calculator
  category: wiring
  name: {cs: "Hledání průřezu kabelu", da: "Find kabeltværsnit", de: "Kabelquerschnitt bestimmen", el: "Εύρεση διατομής καλωδίου", en: "Cable cross-section finder", es: "Búsqueda de la sección del cable", fr: "Recherche de la section d'un câble", hi: "केबल अनुप्रस्थ काट खोजक", it: "Ricerca della sezione del cavo", ja: "ケーブル断面積の選定", nl: "Kabeldoorsnede bepalen", no: "Finn kabeltverrsnitt", pl: "Dobór przekroju kabla", pt: "Seleção da secção do cabo", sv: "Välj kabelarea", zh: "电缆截面积选择"}
  doc:
    en: "Finds the smallest standard cross-section of a cable for a design current Ib from the current-carrying capacity tables of IEC 60364-5-52 and DIN VDE 0298-4 (guide values; the standard is authoritative). Choose the conductor and insulation (copper or aluminium, PVC 70 °C or XLPE/EPR 90 °C), the installation method (A1 to F) and the number of loaded conductors (2 for single-phase or DC, 3 for three-phase). The table value, valid for 30 °C ambient air and one circuit, is multiplied by the ambient temperature factor kt (linear interpolation between the listed temperatures) and by the grouping factor kg of the number of circuits (bunched for A1 to B2, one layer on a wall for C, one layer on a perforated tray for E and F; a count between two listed counts takes the next larger listed one). The result is the first cross-section whose corrected capacity Iz = table value × kt × kg is at least Ib, so the table value must reach Ib / (kt × kg). Empty cells of the tables (method F below 25 mm², the 2.5 mm² cells of copper XLPE in A1 and B1, most aluminium cells and the bunched factor for 14 circuits have no value that two sources confirmed) are skipped by the search, and a combination without any cell is reported as not covered. The protective device (Ib ≤ In ≤ Iz), voltage drop and short-circuit limits are not checked. The row of the result is highlighted in the table. The defaults (20 A, 30 °C, one circuit, copper PVC, method B2, two loaded conductors) give 2.5 mm² with Iz = 23 A. Where IEC and DIN differ (1.5 mm² in A1 and A2, two loaded conductors) the IEC table value is used."
    de: "Bestimmt den kleinsten Normquerschnitt eines Kabels für einen Betriebsstrom Ib aus den Strombelastbarkeitstabellen von IEC 60364-5-52 und DIN VDE 0298-4 (Richtwerte; maßgebend ist die Norm). Gewählt werden Leiter und Isolierung (Kupfer oder Aluminium, PVC 70 °C oder VPE/EPR 90 °C), die Verlegeart (A1 bis F) und die Zahl der belasteten Adern (2 bei Einphasen- und Gleichstrom, 3 bei Drehstrom). Der Tabellenwert für 30 °C Umgebungsluft und einen Stromkreis wird mit dem Umrechnungsfaktor für die Umgebungstemperatur kt (lineare Interpolation zwischen den aufgeführten Temperaturen) und dem Häufungsfaktor kg für die Zahl der Stromkreise multipliziert (gebündelt für A1 bis B2, einlagig auf der Wand für C, einlagig auf gelochter Rinne für E und F; eine Zahl zwischen zwei aufgeführten Zahlen nimmt die nächstgrößere aufgeführte). Das Ergebnis ist der erste Querschnitt, dessen korrigierte Belastbarkeit Iz = Tabellenwert × kt × kg mindestens Ib erreicht; der Tabellenwert muss also Ib / (kt × kg) erreichen. Leere Zellen der Tabellen (Verlegeart F unter 25 mm², die Zellen für 2,5 mm² bei VPE-Kupfer in A1 und B1, die meisten Aluminiumzellen und der Faktor gebündelt für 14 Stromkreise haben keinen von zwei Quellen bestätigten Wert) überspringt die Suche, und eine Kombination ohne Zelle wird als nicht abgedeckt gemeldet. Schutzorgan (Ib ≤ In ≤ Iz), Spannungsfall und Kurzschlussgrenzen werden nicht geprüft. Die Zeile des Ergebnisses ist in der Tabelle hervorgehoben. Die Vorgaben (20 A, 30 °C, ein Stromkreis, Kupfer PVC, Verlegeart B2, 2 belastete Adern) ergeben 2,5 mm² mit Iz = 23 A. Wo IEC und DIN abweichen (1,5 mm² in A1 und A2, 2 belastete Adern), gilt der IEC-Tabellenwert."
  tags: [cable, cross-section, wire size, ampacity, current rating, derating, grouping, ambient temperature, installation method, iec 60364-5-52, din vde 0298-4, kabelquerschnitt, leitungsquerschnitt, strombelastbarkeit, verlegeart, häufung, umgebungstemperatur, belastbarkeit]
  source: "IEC 60364-5-52:2009 annex B (current-carrying capacity tables B.52.2 to B.52.5 and B.52.10 to B.52.13, ambient temperature factors B.52.14, grouping factors B.52.17) and DIN VDE 0298-4:2013-06; selection rule Iz = table value × kt × kg ≥ Ib"
  vars:
```
