          name: {cs: "B2 – vícežilový v trubce na stěně", da: "B2 – flerleder i rør på væg", de: "B2 – mehradrig im Rohr auf der Wand", el: "B2 – πολυπολικό σε σωλήνα σε τοίχο", en: "B2 – multi-core in conduit on a wall", es: "B2 – multipolar en tubo sobre pared", fr: "B2 – multiconducteur sous conduit sur une paroi", hi: "B2 – दीवार पर कंड्यूट में मल्टी-कोर", it: "B2 – multipolare in tubo su parete", ja: "B2 – 壁面の電線管に多心", nl: "B2 – meeraderig in buis op een wand", no: "B2 – flerleder i rør på vegg", pl: "B2 – wielożyłowy w rurze na ścianie", pt: "B2 – multipolar em conduta sobre parede", sv: "B2 – flerledare i rör på vägg", zh: "B2 – 墙面导管中的多芯电缆"}
          refs: {c2: b2_2, c3: b2_3, grp: bunched}
        c:
          name: {cs: "C – přímo na stěně nebo na plném žlabu", da: "C – direkte på væg eller på ikke-perforeret bakke", de: "C – direkt auf der Wand oder ungelochter Rinne", el: "C – απευθείας σε τοίχο ή σε μη διάτρητη σχάρα", en: "C – fixed on a wall or on an unperforated tray", es: "C – directo sobre pared o bandeja no perforada", fr: "C – directement sur une paroi ou un chemin de câbles non perforé", hi: "C – दीवार पर सीधे या बिना छिद्र वाली ट्रे पर", it: "C – direttamente su parete o su passerella non forata", ja: "C – 壁面または非有孔トレイに直接", nl: "C – direct op een wand of niet-geperforeerde goot", no: "C – direkte på vegg eller på ikke-perforert renne", pl: "C – bezpośrednio na ścianie lub na korytku nieperforowanym", pt: "C – diretamente sobre parede ou calha não perfurada", sv: "C – direkt på vägg eller på icke perforerad kabelränna", zh: "C – 直接固定在墙上或无孔托盘上"}
          refs: {c2: c_2, c3: c_3, grp: wall_touching}
        e:
          name: {cs: "E – vícežilový na vzduchu nebo na perforovaném žlabu", da: "E – flerleder i fri luft eller på perforeret bakke", de: "E – mehradrig frei in Luft oder auf gelochter Rinne", el: "E – πολυπολικό στον ελεύθερο αέρα ή σε διάτρητη σχάρα", en: "E – multi-core in free air or on a perforated tray", es: "E – multipolar al aire o en bandeja perforada", fr: "E – multiconducteur à l'air libre ou sur chemin de câbles perforé", hi: "E – खुली हवा में या छिद्रित ट्रे पर मल्टी-कोर", it: "E – multipolare in aria libera o su passerella forata", ja: "E – 気中または有孔トレイ上の多心", nl: "E – meeraderig in vrije lucht of op geperforeerde goot", no: "E – flerleder i fri luft eller på perforert renne", pl: "E – wielożyłowy w powietrzu lub na korytku perforowanym", pt: "E – multipolar ao ar livre ou em calha perfurada", sv: "E – flerledare i fri luft eller på perforerad kabelränna", zh: "E – 自由空气中或有孔托盘上的多芯电缆"}
          refs: {c2: e_2, c3: e_3, grp: perforated_tray}
        f:
          name: {cs: "F – jednožilové kabely vedle sebe na vzduchu", da: "F – enlederkabler i berøring i fri luft", de: "F – einadrige Kabel mit Berührung frei in Luft", el: "F – μονοπολικά καλώδια σε επαφή στον ελεύθερο αέρα", en: "F – single-core cables touching in free air", es: "F – cables unipolares en contacto al aire", fr: "F – câbles unipolaires jointifs à l'air libre", hi: "F – खुली हवा में संपर्क में सिंगल-कोर केबल", it: "F – cavi unipolari a contatto in aria libera", ja: "F – 気中で接触する単心ケーブル", nl: "F – enkeladerige kabels tegen elkaar in vrije lucht", no: "F – enlederkabler i kontakt i fri luft", pl: "F – kable jednożyłowe stykające się w powietrzu", pt: "F – cabos unipolares em contacto ao ar livre", sv: "F – enledarkablar i kontakt i fri luft", zh: "F – 自由空气中相互接触的单芯电缆"}
          refs: {c2: f_2, c3: f_3, grp: perforated_tray}
    loaded:
      name: {cs: "Zatížené vodiče", da: "Belastede ledere", de: "Belastete Adern", el: "Φορτισμένοι αγωγοί", en: "Loaded conductors", es: "Conductores cargados", fr: "Conducteurs chargés", hi: "लोडेड चालक", it: "Conduttori attivi", ja: "通電導体", nl: "Belaste geleiders", no: "Belastede ledere", pl: "Żyły obciążone", pt: "Condutores carregados", sv: "Belastade ledare", zh: "载流导体数"}
      default: two
      options:
        two:
          name: {cs: "2 (jednofázově nebo stejnosměrně)", da: "2 (enfaset eller jævnstrøm)", de: "2 (einphasig oder Gleichstrom)", el: "2 (μονοφασικό ή συνεχές)", en: "2 (single-phase or DC)", es: "2 (monofásico o CC)", fr: "2 (monophasé ou continu)", hi: "2 (एकल-फेज़ या DC)", it: "2 (monofase o continua)", ja: "2（単相または直流）", nl: "2 (eenfasig of gelijkstroom)", no: "2 (enfase eller likestrøm)", pl: "2 (jednofazowo lub prąd stały)", pt: "2 (monofásico ou CC)", sv: "2 (enfas eller likström)", zh: "2（单相或直流）"}
          consts: {three: 0}
        three:
          name: {cs: "3 (třífázově)", da: "3 (trefaset)", de: "3 (dreiphasig)", el: "3 (τριφασικό)", en: "3 (three-phase)", es: "3 (trifásico)", fr: "3 (triphasé)", hi: "3 (तीन-फेज़)", it: "3 (trifase)", ja: "3（三相）", nl: "3 (driefasig)", no: "3 (trefase)", pl: "3 (trójfazowo)", pt: "3 (trifásico)", sv: "3 (trefas)", zh: "3（三相）"}
          consts: {three: 1}
  dof: 3
  derived:
    kt: {dim: number, label: k_t, name: {en: "Ambient temperature factor", de: "Umrechnungsfaktor Umgebungstemperatur"}, expr: "interp(cable_ambient_temp_factors, ambient_c, kcol, ta)"}
    ng: {dim: number, label: n_g, name: {en: "Circuit count taken from the table", de: "Aus der Tabelle verwendete Stromkreiszahl"}, expr: "if(lookup(cable_grouping_factors, grp, lookup_ge(cable_grouping_factors, circuits, nc, circuits)), lookup_ge(cable_grouping_factors, circuits, nc, circuits), lookup_ge(cable_grouping_factors, circuits, lookup_ge(cable_grouping_factors, circuits, nc, circuits) + 1, circuits))"}
    kg: {dim: number, label: k_g, name: {en: "Grouping factor", de: "Häufungsfaktor"}, expr: "lookup(cable_grouping_factors, grp, ng)"}
    ireq: {dim: current, label: I_req, name: {en: "Required table value (30 °C, one circuit)", de: "Erforderlicher Tabellenwert (30 °C, ein Stromkreis)"}, expr: "ib/(kt*kg)"}
    a_min: {dim: area, label: A, name: {en: "Smallest cross-section", de: "Kleinster Querschnitt"}, expr: "if(three, lookup_ge(tbl, c3, ireq, section), lookup_ge(tbl, c2, ireq, section))", unit: mm2, units: [mm2, kcmil, AWG]}
    itab: {dim: current, label: I_tab, name: {en: "Table value of that cross-section", de: "Tabellenwert dieses Querschnitts"}, expr: "if(three, lookup(tbl, c3, a_min), lookup(tbl, c2, a_min))"}
    iz: {dim: current, label: I_z, name: {en: "Corrected current-carrying capacity", de: "Korrigierte Strombelastbarkeit"}, expr: "itab*kt*kg"}
  checks:
    - {when: "if(three, if(lookup_ge(tbl, c3, 0, section), 0, 1), if(lookup_ge(tbl, c2, 0, section), 0, 1))", warn: {en: "Not covered by the verified data: no value for this conductor and installation method was confirmed by a second source (most aluminium cells are empty), so no cross-section can be found. Choose another combination.", de: "Durch die geprüften Daten nicht abgedeckt: Für diesen Leiter und diese Verlegeart wurde kein Wert durch eine zweite Quelle bestätigt (die meisten Aluminiumzellen sind leer); ein Querschnitt kann nicht bestimmt werden. Eine andere Kombination wählen."}}
    - {when: "if(interp(cable_ambient_temp_factors, ambient_c, kcol, ta), 0, 1)", warn: {en: "The ambient temperature is outside the factor table for this insulation (PVC: 10 to 65 °C, XLPE/EPR: 10 to 80 °C), so there is no factor.", de: "Die Umgebungstemperatur liegt außerhalb der Faktortabelle für diese Isolierung (PVC: 10 bis 65 °C, VPE/EPR: 10 bis 80 °C); es gibt keinen Faktor."}}
    - {when: "if(lookup_ge(cable_grouping_factors, circuits, nc, circuits), 0, 1)", warn: {en: "The number of circuits is above the largest count of the grouping table (20), so there is no factor.", de: "Die Zahl der Stromkreise liegt über der größten Zahl der Häufungstabelle (20); es gibt keinen Faktor."}}
    - {when: "if(three, if(lookup_ge(tbl, c3, ireq, section), 0, if(lookup_ge(tbl, c3, 0, section), 1, 0)), if(lookup_ge(tbl, c2, ireq, section), 0, if(lookup_ge(tbl, c2, 0, section), 1, 0)))", warn: {en: "The required table value is above the largest cross-section of the table (240 mm²) for this combination. Split the load over parallel cables or size it from another source.", de: "Der erforderliche Tabellenwert liegt über dem größten Querschnitt der Tabelle (240 mm²) für diese Kombination. Die Last auf parallele Kabel aufteilen oder anderweitig bemessen."}}
  formula: ["ireq = ib / (kt * kg)", "itab >= ireq", "iz = itab * kt * kg"]

- id: trace_spacing_finder
  kind: calculator
  category: wiring
  name: {cs: "Hledání vzdálenosti vodičů na DPS (IPC-2221)", da: "Find lederafstand på print (IPC-2221)", de: "Leiterabstand auf der Leiterplatte bestimmen (IPC-2221)", el: "Εύρεση απόστασης αγωγών PCB (IPC-2221)", en: "PCB conductor spacing finder (IPC-2221)", es: "Búsqueda de la separación de conductores en PCB (IPC-2221)", fr: "Recherche de la distance entre conducteurs d'un circuit imprimé (IPC-2221)", hi: "पीसीबी चालक दूरी खोजक (IPC-2221)", it: "Ricerca della distanza tra i conduttori del PCB (IPC-2221)", ja: "プリント基板の導体間隔の選定 (IPC-2221)", nl: "Geleiderafstand op pcb bepalen (IPC-2221)", no: "Finn lederavstand på kretskort (IPC-2221)", pl: "Dobór odstępu między ścieżkami PCB (IPC-2221)", pt: "Seleção da distância entre condutores em PCB (IPC-2221)", sv: "Välj ledaravstånd på kretskort (IPC-2221)", zh: "PCB 导体间距选择 (IPC-2221)"}
  doc:
    en: "Finds the minimum spacing between two conductors on a printed board for the voltage between them, from table 6-1 of IPC-2221B or IPC-2221C. Enter the DC voltage or the AC peak value, or choose AC RMS of a sine wave (the peak is then the RMS value times √2). Choose the revision and the column of the table for the board condition: B1 internal conductors, B2 external uncoated up to 3050 m, B3 external uncoated above 3050 m, B4 external with a polymer coating, B5 (A5 in revision B) external with a conformal coating, A6 to A8 component leads; A6 and A7 mean different things in the two revisions (revision B: A6 uncoated, A7 coated; revision C: A6 coated, A7 uncoated up to 3050 m, A8 uncoated above 3050 m). The voltage bands use whole volts, so a voltage between two bands (15.5 V) takes the next band up. Above 500 V the spacing is the value of the 301 to 500 V band plus the per-volt increment of the table for every volt above 500 V. IPC-2221 gives functional spacing for the board, not safety isolation: for mains or SELV separation the creepage and clearance of IEC 60664-1 and IEC 62368-1 apply. The row of the result is highlighted in the table. The defaults (400 V, revision C, column B2) give 2.5 mm."
    de: "Bestimmt den Mindestabstand zweier Leiter auf einer Leiterplatte für die Spannung zwischen ihnen aus Tabelle 6-1 von IPC-2221B oder IPC-2221C. Einzugeben ist die Gleichspannung oder der Scheitelwert der Wechselspannung, oder der Effektivwert einer Sinusspannung (der Scheitelwert ist dann der Effektivwert mal √2). Revision und Spalte der Tabelle wählen die Leiterplattenbedingung: B1 Innenlagen, B2 außen unbeschichtet bis 3050 m, B3 außen unbeschichtet über 3050 m, B4 außen mit Polymerbeschichtung, B5 (in Revision B A5) außen mit Schutzlack, A6 bis A8 Bauteilanschlüsse; A6 und A7 bedeuten in den beiden Revisionen Verschiedenes (Revision B: A6 unbeschichtet, A7 beschichtet; Revision C: A6 beschichtet, A7 unbeschichtet bis 3050 m, A8 unbeschichtet über 3050 m). Die Spannungsbänder verwenden ganze Volt; eine Spannung zwischen zwei Bändern (15,5 V) nimmt das nächsthöhere Band. Über 500 V ist der Abstand der Wert des Bandes 301 bis 500 V plus der Zuschlag je Volt der Tabelle für jedes Volt über 500 V. IPC-2221 gibt Funktionsabstände für die Leiterplatte an, keine Schutztrennung: Für Netz- oder SELV-Trennung gelten Kriech- und Luftstrecken nach IEC 60664-1 und IEC 62368-1. Die Zeile des Ergebnisses ist in der Tabelle hervorgehoben. Die Vorgaben (400 V, Revision C, Spalte B2) ergeben 2,5 mm."
  tags: [pcb, trace spacing, conductor spacing, clearance, creepage, voltage, high voltage, ipc-2221, ipc-2221b, ipc-2221c, leiterabstand, leiterbahnabstand, leiterplatte, spannung, abstand, kriechstrecke, luftstrecke]
  source: "IPC-2221B and IPC-2221C table 6-1 (electrical conductor spacing); above 500 V the 301 to 500 V value plus the per-volt increment of the table (IPC-2221 section 6.3); AC RMS to peak for a sine wave: peak = RMS × √2"
  vars:
    v: {dim: voltage, label: U, name: {en: "Voltage between the conductors", de: "Spannung zwischen den Leitern"}, default: "400 V"}
  choices:
    revision:
      name: {cs: "Revize IPC-2221", da: "IPC-2221-revision", de: "IPC-2221-Revision", el: "Αναθεώρηση IPC-2221", en: "IPC-2221 revision", es: "Revisión de IPC-2221", fr: "Révision d'IPC-2221", hi: "IPC-2221 संशोधन", it: "Revisione IPC-2221", ja: "IPC-2221 の改訂版", nl: "IPC-2221-revisie", no: "IPC-2221-revisjon", pl: "Wersja IPC-2221", pt: "Revisão da IPC-2221", sv: "IPC-2221-revision", zh: "IPC-2221 版本"}
      default: c
      options:
        b:
          name: {cs: "IPC-2221B", da: "IPC-2221B", de: "IPC-2221B", el: "IPC-2221B", en: "IPC-2221B", es: "IPC-2221B", fr: "IPC-2221B", hi: "IPC-2221B", it: "IPC-2221B", ja: "IPC-2221B", nl: "IPC-2221B", no: "IPC-2221B", pl: "IPC-2221B", pt: "IPC-2221B", sv: "IPC-2221B", zh: "IPC-2221B"}
          consts: {revc: 0}
        c:
          name: {cs: "IPC-2221C (2023)", da: "IPC-2221C (2023)", de: "IPC-2221C (2023)", el: "IPC-2221C (2023)", en: "IPC-2221C (2023)", es: "IPC-2221C (2023)", fr: "IPC-2221C (2023)", hi: "IPC-2221C (2023)", it: "IPC-2221C (2023)", ja: "IPC-2221C (2023)", nl: "IPC-2221C (2023)", no: "IPC-2221C (2023)", pl: "IPC-2221C (2023)", pt: "IPC-2221C (2023)", sv: "IPC-2221C (2023)", zh: "IPC-2221C (2023)"}
          consts: {revc: 1}
    wave:
      name: {cs: "Zadané napětí je", da: "Spændingen er", de: "Spannung ist", el: "Η τάση είναι", en: "Voltage is", es: "La tensión es", fr: "La tension est", hi: "वोल्टेज है", it: "La tensione è", ja: "電圧の種類", nl: "Spanning is", no: "Spenningen er", pl: "Podane napięcie to", pt: "A tensão é", sv: "Spänningen är", zh: "电压类型"}
      default: peak
      options:
        peak:
          name: {cs: "stejnosměrné nebo špičkové střídavé", da: "DC eller AC-spidsværdi", de: "DC oder AC-Scheitelwert", el: "DC ή κορυφή AC", en: "DC or AC peak", es: "CC o valor de pico CA", fr: "continue ou crête alternative", hi: "DC या AC शिखर", it: "continua o picco alternata", ja: "直流または交流の波高値", nl: "gelijkspanning of AC-piekwaarde", no: "DC eller AC-toppverdi", pl: "stałe lub szczytowe przemienne", pt: "CC ou pico CA", sv: "DC eller AC-toppvärde", zh: "直流或交流峰值"}
          consts: {vf: 1}
        rms:
          name: {cs: "střídavé efektivní (sinus)", da: "AC-effektivværdi (sinus)", de: "AC-Effektivwert (Sinus)", el: "AC ενεργός τιμή (ημιτονική)", en: "AC RMS (sine)", es: "valor eficaz CA (senoidal)", fr: "efficace alternative (sinusoïdale)", hi: "AC RMS (ज्यावक्रीय)", it: "efficace alternata (sinusoidale)", ja: "交流の実効値（正弦波）", nl: "AC-effectieve waarde (sinus)", no: "AC-effektivverdi (sinus)", pl: "skuteczne przemienne (sinus)", pt: "valor eficaz CA (sinusoidal)", sv: "AC-effektivvärde (sinus)", zh: "交流有效值（正弦）"}
          consts: {vf: 1.4142135623730951}
    cond:
      name: {cs: "Podmínky desky (sloupec IPC)", da: "Printforhold (IPC-kolonne)", de: "Leiterplattenbedingung (IPC-Spalte)", el: "Συνθήκη πλακέτας (στήλη IPC)", en: "Board condition (IPC column)", es: "Condición de la placa (columna IPC)", fr: "Condition de la carte (colonne IPC)", hi: "बोर्ड की स्थिति (IPC कॉलम)", it: "Condizione della scheda (colonna IPC)", ja: "基板条件（IPC の列）", nl: "Printcondities (IPC-kolom)", no: "Kortforhold (IPC-kolonne)", pl: "Warunki płytki (kolumna IPC)", pt: "Condição da placa (coluna IPC)", sv: "Kortvillkor (IPC-kolumn)", zh: "板件条件（IPC 列）"}
      default: b2
      options:
        # cb names the column in IPC-2221B and cc the column in IPC-2221C; inb is 0 where revision B has no such column (cb is then a placeholder).
        b1:
          name: {cs: "B1 – vnitřní vodiče", da: "B1 – indre ledere", de: "B1 – Innenlagen", el: "B1 – εσωτερικοί αγωγοί", en: "B1 – internal conductors", es: "B1 – conductores internos", fr: "B1 – conducteurs internes", hi: "B1 – आंतरिक चालक", it: "B1 – conduttori interni", ja: "B1 – 内層導体", nl: "B1 – binnengeleiders", no: "B1 – indre ledere", pl: "B1 – przewody wewnętrzne", pt: "B1 – condutores internos", sv: "B1 – inre ledare", zh: "B1 – 内层导体"}
          refs: {cb: b1, cc: b1}
          consts: {inb: 1}
        b2:
          name: {cs: "B2 – vnější, bez povlaku, do 3050 m", da: "B2 – ydre, ubelagte, op til 3050 m", de: "B2 – außen, unbeschichtet, bis 3050 m", el: "B2 – εξωτερικοί, χωρίς επίστρωση, έως 3050 m", en: "B2 – external, uncoated, up to 3050 m", es: "B2 – externos, sin recubrimiento, hasta 3050 m", fr: "B2 – externes, sans revêtement, jusqu'à 3050 m", hi: "B2 – बाहरी, बिना कोटिंग, 3050 m तक", it: "B2 – esterni, senza rivestimento, fino a 3050 m", ja: "B2 – 外層、被覆なし、3050 m まで", nl: "B2 – buiten, onbedekt, tot 3050 m", no: "B2 – ytre, ubelagt, opptil 3050 m", pl: "B2 – zewnętrzne, bez powłoki, do 3050 m", pt: "B2 – externos, sem revestimento, até 3050 m", sv: "B2 – yttre, obelagda, upp till 3050 m", zh: "B2 – 外层、无涂层、3050 m 以下"}
          refs: {cb: b2, cc: b2}
          consts: {inb: 1}
        b3:
          name: {cs: "B3 – vnější, bez povlaku, nad 3050 m", da: "B3 – ydre, ubelagte, over 3050 m", de: "B3 – außen, unbeschichtet, über 3050 m", el: "B3 – εξωτερικοί, χωρίς επίστρωση, πάνω από 3050 m", en: "B3 – external, uncoated, above 3050 m", es: "B3 – externos, sin recubrimiento, por encima de 3050 m", fr: "B3 – externes, sans revêtement, au-dessus de 3050 m", hi: "B3 – बाहरी, बिना कोटिंग, 3050 m से ऊपर", it: "B3 – esterni, senza rivestimento, oltre 3050 m", ja: "B3 – 外層、被覆なし、3050 m 超", nl: "B3 – buiten, onbedekt, boven 3050 m", no: "B3 – ytre, ubelagt, over 3050 m", pl: "B3 – zewnętrzne, bez powłoki, powyżej 3050 m", pt: "B3 – externos, sem revestimento, acima de 3050 m", sv: "B3 – yttre, obelagda, över 3050 m", zh: "B3 – 外层、无涂层、3050 m 以上"}
          refs: {cb: b3, cc: b3}
          consts: {inb: 1}
        b4:
          name: {cs: "B4 – vnější, polymerní povlak", da: "B4 – ydre, polymerbelægning", de: "B4 – außen, Polymerbeschichtung", el: "B4 – εξωτερικοί, πολυμερής επίστρωση", en: "B4 – external, polymer coating", es: "B4 – externos, recubrimiento polimérico", fr: "B4 – externes, revêtement polymère", hi: "B4 – बाहरी, पॉलिमर कोटिंग", it: "B4 – esterni, rivestimento polimerico", ja: "B4 – 外層、ポリマー被覆", nl: "B4 – buiten, polymeercoating", no: "B4 – ytre, polymerbelegg", pl: "B4 – zewnętrzne, powłoka polimerowa", pt: "B4 – externos, revestimento polimérico", sv: "B4 – yttre, polymerbeläggning", zh: "B4 – 外层、聚合物涂层"}
          refs: {cb: b4, cc: b4}
          consts: {inb: 1}

Six tables have a `finder`: the four ampacity tables `{calc: cable_cross_section_finder, column: section, var: a_min, choices: {cable: <cu_pvc|cu_xlpe|al_pvc|al_xlpe>}}` and the two spacing tables `{calc: trace_spacing_finder, column: v_min, var: band_min, choices: {revision: <b|c>}}`; the header therefore shows the choices `method` and `loaded` (cable finder) or `wave` and `cond` (spacing finder). `a_min` is empty (NaN) when nothing qualifies, then no row is highlighted. `cable_ampacity_al_pvc` and `cable_ampacity_al_xlpe` have columns whose every cell is empty (deviation 1): the page may hide them. Text cells `{en, de}` occur in `iec60228_cross_sections.preferred` only.

## Part C2 — Component tables (task C2.1)


**Goal of this part:** the eight reference tables of the group `components` that the phase 3 research delivered, as the catalog file `internal/ecalc/catalog/tables/components.yaml`: SMD chip sizes, ceramic capacitor dielectrics (C0G, X7R …), fuse time-current characteristics, the IEC 60127-2 pre-arcing times of 5×20 mm fuses, miniature fuse formats, battery chemistries, battery sizes and DC barrel plug sizes. Together they have 82 rows, 89 spot-checked cells and 5 `lookup_ge` vectors, one vector file per table. The two E-series tables of the same group (`eseries_e24`, `eseries_e192`) are generated by Part A and are not repeated here.

**How this part was made and verified:** every file below was built and tested in the scratch worktree `wc2` (base `4b3b14ec0`, Part A applied, nothing committed); the code blocks are the exact text of those files. The eight vector files were written first from the research files and the tests were run red before the YAML existed. The YAML rows were generated from the CSV blocks of the research files by a script (so that no cell is retyped), and then checked a second time by an independent script that reads the regenerated snapshot (the engine's own SI output) and compares all 751 cells with the research CSV using its own unit factors. The expected values of the vector files were written by hand from the research files (maker numbers and standard sheets), never taken from the engine.

**Environment.** Windows box. Run Go commands with a short backslash `GOTMPDIR` (create the folder once):

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p3-c2 | Out-Null
$env:GOTMPDIR = 'C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p3-c2'
```

(Git Bash equivalent: `export GOTMPDIR='C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p3-c2'`.) Commit messages end with the trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Write the characters `×`, `Ø`, `°`, `≈`, `√`, `±` and `–` into the files as the characters themselves, never as escapes (the Write and Edit tools decode backslash-u sequences). The files are LF.

**Dependencies.** Part A must be applied first: the table items (`catalog/tables/*.yaml`, loader and JSON), the vector test `TestTableVectors` with `TestTableVectorFilesNameATable`, the table functions `lookup_ge` used by five vectors, the unit `mm`, and the Node twin of the vector test in `scripts/test-ecalc-core.mjs`. GitNexus: this task adds data files only and changes no function, so there is no `impact` run to record; run `detect-changes` before the commit as always.

### Contract deviations (where this list and the contract disagree, this list wins)

1. **`fuse_prearc_iec60127_2` has an added key column `case` (first column, `key: case`).** The research table has no unique column (sheet, characteristic, current range and multiple only identify a row together), but a table needs a unique key. `case` is a language-neutral text such as `F, 0.125–6.3 A, 10 × In` built from the characteristic, the rated-current range (in A, as in the research CSV) and the test multiple. Everything else in the table is the research CSV.
2. **One column id differs from the research:** `example_10x_max_ms` of `fuse_speed_classes` is `example_10x_max`. `ms` is a prefix of `s`, not an explicit unit of the dimension `time` (a column unit must be `""` or an explicit unit), so the column is stored in seconds: 20 ms is 0.02 and 300 ms is 0.3. The page shows them as 20 ms and 300 ms through the automatic prefix. All other ids, including the unit suffixes (`l_mm`, `v_nom` …), are the research ids; the unit of the column is the one in the id (`pin_pitch_mm` is millimetres), the page can display another unit.
3. **Specific energy in Wh/kg has no dimension in `units.yaml`.** `wh_kg_example` is a `number` column and the unit stands in the column name ("Specific energy of the example cell (Wh/kg)"); `wh_kg_typ` is a text column because the source gives ranges ("150–220"). The `units.yaml` file is not touched.
4. **Dimensions used for the other columns:** `length` in `mm` (display `mm`, `in`; `mil` too for the SMD sizes), `power`, `voltage` and `current` in the base unit (display `""`, so 0.0625 W reads 62.5 mW and 0.8 V reads 800 mV), `time` in seconds, `temperature` in `degC` (display °C, °F), `tempco` in `ppmK`, `ratio` in `pct` for the capacitance change of the dielectrics, `ratio` with unit `""` for the test-current multiple of the fuse table (display `""` or `pct`, so 1.5 reads 150 %, as Littelfuse prints it), and `number` for the IEC sheet and the speed rank. Cells are not checked against the `positive` flag of a dimension, so −55 °C, −15 % and 0 V are fine.
5. **UNVERIFIED cells are `null`, the notes say so.** Empty: the discharge cut-off of the CR cell and the IEC letter of LiFePO4 (`battery_chemistries`); the ANSI designations of AAA, C, D, 9V and CR2032 and the diameter, height and voltage of the 14500 (`battery_formats`); the inner diameter of EIAJ-05 (`dc_barrel_connectors`). **Left out:** the column `iec_code` of `mlcc_dielectrics` (every value comes from Wikipedia only, so no cell is verified) and the row `2.5 × 0.7` of `dc_barrel_connectors` (single source, every value of it unverified). The row remarks that carried the word "UNVERIFIED" in the research (the 14500, the CR cell, EIAJ-05, TR5) are reworded to say what is empty and why. TR5's body height had no column in the research and stays out.
6. **Editorial texts stay and are named in the notes.** The `use` texts of X8R, X7S, X7T and X6S (`mlcc_dielectrics`) and the `meaning` texts of `fuse_speed_classes` are editorial wording that the research says is not quoted from a source; the `notes` of the two tables say so. FF, M and TT have no sourced 10 × In example, so that cell is empty.
7. **Where makers differ, the research choice is carried and the notes say so:** `smd_chip_sizes` (0402 power 1/16 W against 0.1 W, 2010 and 2512 voltage 200 V against 400/500 V, 2512 body size, mixed-up inch/metric codes), `mlcc_dielectrics` (Y5V is "Class III" for KEMET but a class 2 dielectric in IEC terms), `dc_barrel_connectors` (EIAJ-04 inner diameter 3.3 mm against 3.4 mm), `battery_chemistries` (LiFePO4 charge limit 3.6 against 3.65 V and cut-off 2.0 to 2.7 V in the sources; the example specific energy uses the nominal voltage, so it is an upper bound for alkaline cells).
8. **`guide: true` only on the two transcribed-standard tables** (`fuse_prearc_iec60127_2` and `dc_barrel_connectors`); the other six are definitional or typical-value tables and carry no standard banner (the battery notes say "typical values", the SMD notes call the rating columns typical). No table here is a mains or installation table, so no `mains: true`. The standards themselves (IEC 60127, JEITA RC-5320A, EIA-198, IEC 60086) were not read; the `source` fields name the makers and catalogue entries that were.
9. **No `finder`.** Finders belong to part C1 (wiring only), so none of these tables has one. All eight tables have a **text key**, so `lookup(T, C, key)` cannot be used on them (contract deviation 6 of Part A); `lookup_ge` works on every numeric column and has five vectors (`smd_chip_sizes`, `mlcc_dielectrics`, `fuse_speed_classes`, `fuse_prearc_iec60127_2`, `dc_barrel_connectors`). `lookup_ge` returns the first row in table order, so it only means "the smallest …" in tables whose column is ascending (the SMD power column is).
10. **The `ref` texts of the vectors are ASCII** (`degC`, `x`, `+-`); keys and wanted texts that must equal a table cell keep their characters (`5×20 mm`, `F, 0.125–6.3 A, 10 × In`, `5.5 × 2.1`, `150–220`).

### What the tables contain

| Table id | Kind (research) | Rows × columns | Key | Empty cells | Banner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `smd_chip_sizes` | typical maker data | 10 × 13 | `imperial` | 8 (no part of that maker in the size, or its datasheet was not read) | – |
| `mlcc_dielectrics` | definitional (EIA RS-198) + maker data | 8 × 10 | `code` | 23 (class I/II/III fields do not apply, no alias) | – |
| `fuse_speed_classes` | definitional | 5 × 5 | `code` | 3 (FF, M, TT example) | – |
| `fuse_prearc_iec60127_2` | transcribed standard (two makers agree on every cell) | 30 × 9 | `case` | 15 (no limit in that direction) | guide |
| `fuse_formats` | typical maker data | 3 × 8 | `format` | 3 | – |
| `battery_chemistries` | typical | 8 × 10 | `chem` | 13 | – |
| `battery_formats` | typical | 10 × 10 | `format` | 30 (mostly ANSI, thickness, 14500) | – |
| `dc_barrel_connectors` | transcribed standard + typical | 8 × 9 | `name` | 13 | guide |

Text cells are plain strings (the same in every language) or `{en, de}`; the names of the tables are in all 16 locales, column names, `doc`, `notes` and the text cells in English and German. Group `components`, category `tables`.

### What other parts must know

- **Part B (tool):** table ids and key columns are in the table above; every key is text, so a `lookup` with mode `exact` has no numeric key to match on these tables, while `ge` works on numeric columns (`table` action with `lookup.mode: ge`, for example `p_typ_w` ≥ 0.2 W in `smd_chip_sizes` gives the 1206 row). Example filters that return rows: `filter: 0805` (SMD), `filter: X7R`, `filter: 18650`, `filter: 5.5` (barrel plugs).
- **Part UT (table page):** `fuse_prearc_iec60127_2` and `dc_barrel_connectors` carry `guide: true`. Text cells with `{en, de}` appear in the remark, use, meaning, mounting and name columns; `units` lists use `""` (automatic prefix), `mm`, `in`, `mil`, `degC`, `degF`, `ppmK`, `pct` and `min`/`h`.
- **Z (controller):** the snapshot is regenerated by the controller after merging all content parts. `c2-manual-lines.md` has the manual lines (en, de) of the eight tables and of the two generated E-series tables.

  doc: {en: "EIA temperature-characteristic codes of ceramic capacitors (C0G, X7R, X5R, Y5V …): temperature range, temperature coefficient or maximum capacitance change, and typical use.", de: "EIA-Temperaturkennlinien-Codes von Keramikkondensatoren (C0G, X7R, X5R, Y5V …): Temperaturbereich, Temperaturkoeffizient bzw. maximale Kapazitätsänderung und typische Anwendung."}
  notes: {en: "Code reading (class II/III): 1st letter = lower temperature (X −55 °C, Y −30 °C, Z +10 °C), digit = upper temperature (5 +85, 6 +105, 7 +125, 8 +150 °C), last letter = max. capacitance change (R ±15 %, S ±22 %, T +22/−33 %, V +22/−82 %). Class II/III capacitors also lose capacitance with applied DC voltage and with age (ageing); the temperature code says nothing about DC bias. Some makers (e.g. KEMET) call Y5V \"Class III\"; in IEC terms it is a class 2 dielectric. The IEC 60384-8/-9 equivalents are not listed because only one source gives them. The use texts of X8R, X7S, X7T and X6S are editorial wording derived from the code meaning, not taken from a source.", de: "Code-Lesart (Klasse II/III): 1. Buchstabe = untere Temperatur (X −55 °C, Y −30 °C, Z +10 °C), Ziffer = obere Temperatur (5 +85, 6 +105, 7 +125, 8 +150 °C), letzter Buchstabe = max. Kapazitätsänderung (R ±15 %, S ±22 %, T +22/−33 %, V +22/−82 %). Klasse-II/III-Kondensatoren verlieren zusätzlich Kapazität mit angelegter Gleichspannung und mit der Zeit (Alterung); der Temperaturcode sagt nichts über den DC-Bias. Manche Hersteller (z. B. KEMET) nennen Y5V „Klasse III“; nach IEC ist es ein Klasse-2-Dielektrikum. Die IEC-60384-8/-9-Entsprechungen sind nicht aufgeführt, weil nur eine Quelle sie nennt. Die Anwendungstexte von X8R, X7S, X7T und X6S sind redaktionelle Formulierungen aus der Bedeutung des Codes, keine Quellenangabe."}

  source: "EIA RS-198 temperature codes as printed in the KEMET datasheets C1003 (C0G), C1002 (X7R), C1006 (X5R) and C1005 (Y5V) and the TDK MLCC Product Guide; code reading after Wikipedia \"Ceramic capacitor\""

  rows:

    - ["X8R", null, "II", -55, 150, null, null, -15, 15, {en: "Decoupling/bypass at high temperature (e.g. automotive)", de: "Abblocken/Entkoppeln bei hoher Temperatur (z. B. Automobil)"}]
    - ["X7R", null, "II", -55, 125, null, null, -15, 15, {en: "General-purpose bypass, decoupling and filtering where Q and stability are not critical", de: "Allgemeines Abblocken, Entkoppeln und Filtern, wo Güte und Stabilität unkritisch sind"}]
    - ["X7S", null, "II", -55, 125, null, null, -22, 22, {en: "Decoupling with higher capacitance per size than X7R, wider tolerance", de: "Entkoppeln mit mehr Kapazität je Baugröße als X7R, weitere Toleranz"}]

    - ["X5R", null, "II", -55, 85, null, null, -15, 15, {en: "High-capacitance decoupling and bypass up to 85 °C", de: "Entkoppeln und Abblocken mit hoher Kapazität bis 85 °C"}]
    - ["Y5V", null, "III (KEMET)", -30, 85, null, null, -82, 22, {en: "Low-cost bypass/decoupling where stability does not matter; avoid where temperature varies", de: "Billiges Abblocken/Entkoppeln, wo Stabilität egal ist; bei schwankender Temperatur meiden"}]

  doc: {en: "The characteristic letters of miniature fuses (FF, F, M, T, TT) with their names and speed order, and the maximum pre-arcing time at 10 times the rated current for two of the classes.", de: "Die Kennbuchstaben von Geräteschutzsicherungen (FF, F, M, T, TT) mit Bezeichnung und Reihenfolge der Trägheit sowie die maximale Schmelzzeit beim 10-fachen Nennstrom für zwei der Klassen."}
  notes: {en: "The letter is printed on the end cap of the fuse together with rated current, rated voltage and breaking capacity (e.g. L = low, H = high, as used by Schurter). The exact pre-arcing limits depend on the standard sheet (size, breaking capacity), see the table of IEC 60127-2 pre-arcing times. Never replace a fuse with a slower class or a higher rating. The meaning texts are short editorial wording, not quotations from a standard, and the inrush examples are general engineering guidance. The 10 × In example exists only for F and T, the two classes with a sourced value; FF, M and TT are left empty.", de: "Der Buchstabe steht mit Nennstrom, Nennspannung und Schaltvermögen (z. B. Eine Sicherung nie durch eine trägere Klasse oder einen höheren Nennstrom ersetzen. Die Bedeutungstexte sind kurze redaktionelle Formulierungen, keine Zitate aus einer Norm, und die Einschaltstrom-Beispiele sind allgemeine Ingenieurspraxis. Das Beispiel bei 10 × In gibt es nur für F und T, die beiden Klassen mit belegtem Wert; FF, M und TT bleiben leer."}

  source: "IEC 60127 characteristic letters (names from DIN EN 60127-4 and DIN 41571-2); 10 × In values from the Schurter FSF/FST 5x20 and Littelfuse 217/218 datasheets"
  columns:
    - {id: code, name: {en: "Marking", de: "Kennbuchstabe"}, dim: text}
    - {id: name, name: {en: "Name", de: "Bezeichnung"}, dim: text}
    - {id: speed_rank, name: {en: "Speed rank (1 = fastest)", de: "Rang (1 = am schnellsten)"}, dim: number}
    - {id: meaning, name: {en: "Meaning", de: "Bedeutung"}, dim: text}
    - {id: example_10x_max, name: {en: "Example: max. pre-arcing time at 10 × In (5×20 mm, 0.125–6.3 A)", de: "Beispiel: max. Schmelzzeit bei 10 × In (5×20 mm, 0,125–6,3 A)"}, dim: time}
  rows:
    - ["FF", {en: "very quick-acting", de: "superflink"}, 1, {en: "Interrupts overcurrents fastest; for protecting sensitive semiconductors", de: "Schaltet Überströme am schnellsten ab; zum Schutz empfindlicher Halbleiter"}, null]
    - ["F", {en: "quick-acting", de: "flink"}, 2, {en: "Fast response to overload and short circuit; general protection of electronics without inrush", de: "Schnelle Reaktion auf Überlast und Kurzschluss; allgemeiner Elektronikschutz ohne Einschaltstrom"}, 0.02]
    - ["M", {en: "medium time-lag", de: "mittelträge"}, 3, {en: "Between quick-acting and time-lag; tolerates small inrush peaks", de: "Zwischen flink und träge; verträgt kleine Einschaltspitzen"}, null]
    - ["T", {en: "time-lag", de: "träge"}, 4, {en: "Tolerates inrush currents (transformers, motors, capacitor charging) but still clears sustained overload", de: "Verträgt Einschaltströme (Trafos, Motoren, Kondensatorladen), löst bei Dauerüberlast aber aus"}, 0.3]
    - ["TT", {en: "long time-lag", de: "superträge"}, 5, {en: "Slowest class; for very high or long inrush currents", de: "Langsamste Klasse; für sehr hohe oder lange Einschaltströme"}, null]

- id: fuse_prearc_iec60127_2
  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: components
  guide: true
  key: case
  name: {cs: "Doby tavení pojistek (IEC 60127-2, 5×20 mm)", da: "Sikringers smeltetider (IEC 60127-2, 5×20 mm)", de: "Schmelzzeiten von Sicherungen (IEC 60127-2, 5×20 mm)", el: "Χρόνοι τήξης ασφαλειών (IEC 60127-2, 5×20 mm)", en: "Fuse pre-arcing times (IEC 60127-2, 5×20 mm)", es: "Tiempos de prearco de fusibles (IEC 60127-2, 5×20 mm)", fr: "Temps de préarc des fusibles (IEC 60127-2, 5×20 mm)", hi: "फ्यूज़ का प्री-आर्किंग समय (IEC 60127-2, 5×20 mm)", it: "Tempi di prearco dei fusibili (IEC 60127-2, 5×20 mm)", ja: "ヒューズの溶断時間(IEC 60127-2、5×20 mm)", nl: "Voorboogtijden van zekeringen (IEC 60127-2, 5×20 mm)", no: "Smeltetider for sikringer (IEC 60127-2, 5×20 mm)", pl: "Czasy przedłukowe bezpieczników (IEC 60127-2, 5×20 mm)", pt: "Tempos de pré-arco de fusíveis (IEC 60127-2, 5×20 mm)", sv: "Smälttider för säkringar (IEC 60127-2, 5×20 mm)", zh: "熔断器弧前时间(IEC 60127-2,5×20 mm)"}
  doc: {en: "Minimum and maximum pre-arcing (melting) times of 5×20 mm glass fuses with low breaking capacity, quick-acting (IEC 60127-2 sheet 2) and time-lag (sheet 3), at test currents of 1.5 to 10 times the rated current.", de: "Minimale und maximale Schmelzzeiten von 5×20-mm-Glasrohrsicherungen mit niedrigem Schaltvermögen, flink (IEC 60127-2 Normblatt 2) und träge (Normblatt 3), bei Prüfströmen vom 1,5- bis 10-fachen Nennstrom."}
  notes: {en: "Limits are pre-arcing (melting) times at room temperature for 5×20 mm glass fuses with low breaking capacity. A fuse that meets the standard opens between t_min and t_max at the given multiple; an empty time means no limit in that direction. Each row is one test current of one rated-current range, the first column names it. Ratings of 8 A and above extend beyond the classic standard-sheet range; check the actual datasheet. The standard itself was not read: the values are those that Schurter and Littelfuse print for their fuses, and the two makers agree on every cell. Sheets 1 and 5 (high breaking capacity) and the sheets for 6.3×32 mm fuses are not covered.", de: "Grenzen sind Schmelzzeiten bei Raumtemperatur für 5×20-mm-Glasrohrsicherungen mit niedrigem Schaltvermögen. Eine normgerechte Sicherung löst beim angegebenen Vielfachen zwischen t_min und t_max aus; eine leere Zeit bedeutet keine Grenze in dieser Richtung. Jede Zeile ist ein Prüfstrom eines Nennstrombereichs, die erste Spalte benennt ihn. Nennströme ab 8 A gehen über den klassischen Normblattbereich hinaus; das konkrete Datenblatt prüfen. Die Norm selbst wurde nicht gelesen: die Werte sind die, die Schurter und Littelfuse für ihre Sicherungen drucken, und beide Hersteller stimmen in jeder Zelle überein. Die Normblätter 1 und 5 (hohes Schaltvermögen) und die Blätter für 6,3×32-mm-Sicherungen sind nicht enthalten."}
  tags: ["fuse", "pre-arcing", "melting time", "time-current", "iec 60127-2", "5x20", "glass fuse", "quick-acting", "time-lag", "sicherung", "schmelzzeit", "feinsicherung", "kennlinie", "prüfstrom"]
  source: "IEC 60127-2 sheets 2 (F) and 3 (T) as printed in the Schurter FSF/FST 5x20 and Littelfuse 217/218 datasheets (the standard itself was not read)"

  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: components
  key: chem
  name: {cs: "Chemie baterií (napětí a hustota energie)", da: "Batterikemier (spændinger og energitæthed)", de: "Batteriechemien (Spannungen und Energiedichte)", el: "Χημείες μπαταριών (τάσεις και πυκνότητα ενέργειας)", en: "Battery chemistries (voltages and energy density)", es: "Químicas de baterías (tensiones y densidad de energía)", fr: "Chimies de batteries (tensions et densité d'énergie)", hi: "बैटरी रसायन (वोल्टेज और ऊर्जा घनत्व)", it: "Chimiche delle batterie (tensioni e densità di energia)", ja: "電池の種類(電圧とエネルギー密度)", nl: "Batterijchemieën (spanningen en energiedichtheid)", no: "Batterikjemier (spenninger og energitetthet)", pl: "Rodzaje ogniw (napięcia i gęstość energii)", pt: "Químicas de baterias (tensões e densidade de energia)", sv: "Batterikemier (spänningar och energitäthet)", zh: "电池类型(电压与能量密度)"}
  doc: {en: "Cell voltages (nominal, end of charge, discharge cut-off) and specific energy of the common primary and rechargeable battery chemistries.", de: "Zellspannungen (nominal, Ladeschluss, Entladeschluss) und spezifische Energie der gängigen Primär- und Sekundärzellen-Chemien."}
  notes: {en: "Typical values; always use the datasheet of the actual cell. Specific energy depends on cell size and design (high-power cells have less). The example column is the nominal voltage times the capacity divided by the mass of the cell named in the next column, rounded to whole numbers. Li-ion charging needs a CC/CV charger with the exact end voltage; never charge primary cells (alkaline, CR). LiPo and Li-ion differ in construction, not in cell voltage. Two cells are empty because no source confirms them: the discharge cut-off of lithium primary cells (CR) and the IEC letter of LiFePO4. Lead-acid has no IEC 60086, 61951 or 61960 letter.", de: "Typische Werte; immer das Datenblatt der konkreten Zelle verwenden. Die spezifische Energie hängt von Zellgröße und Bauart ab (Hochstromzellen haben weniger). Die Beispielspalte ist die Nennspannung mal Kapazität geteilt durch die Masse der in der nächsten Spalte genannten Zelle, auf ganze Zahlen gerundet. Li-Ionen-Zellen nur mit CC/CV-Lader und exakter Ladeschlussspannung laden; Primärzellen (Alkali, CR) nie laden. LiPo und Li-Ion unterscheiden sich in der Bauweise, nicht in der Zellspannung. Zwei Zellen sind leer, weil keine Quelle sie bestätigt: der Entladeschluss der Lithium-Primärzellen (CR) und der IEC-Buchstabe von LiFePO4. Blei-Säure hat keinen IEC-Buchstaben nach IEC 60086, 61951 oder 61960."}

## Part C3 — Materials tables (task C31)


**Goal of this part:** the table group `materials` of the ECalc catalog: `resistivity_conductors` (22 rows × 11 columns), `dielectric_constants` (14 × 12), `thermocouple_types` (8 × 26) and `solder_alloys` (7 × 11), all in one file `catalog/tables/materials.yaml`, with 80 spot-checked cells in four table vector files (16 of them check a cell that is empty on purpose). The research data is `P3\research\materials\` (SUMMARY.md and one file per table); every number in the YAML was compared with it by script (see the verification section).

**Architecture:** unchanged from part A: a table item of `tables/*.yaml` with typed columns, SI rows, a text key, and vectors in `testdata/vectors/tables/<id>.json`. Nothing outside the table file, its vectors and the generated snapshot changes; no Go or JavaScript code and no `units.yaml`.

**Tech Stack:** YAML and JSON data; Go 1.27 for `TestTableVectors`, Node for `scripts/test-ecalc-core.mjs`.

**Spec and contract:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-01-ecalc-design.md` ("Tables", "Content correctness"); the phase 3 contract sections 1.1, 1.3, 3 and 8; part A (`P3\part-a.md`, section "What the other parts get from this part") for the schema as built.

**How this part was made and verified:** the files below were built in the scratch worktree `P3\wc3` (part A applied on the base commit `4b3b14ec0`) vector-first (the table vector test red, then the YAML, then green), and the plan text was generated from those files by a script, so the code blocks are the exact file contents. Besides the Go and Node suites, two scripts compared the built tables with the CSV rows of the research files (English and German text, every number converted to SI); they found no difference except the deliberate ones listed below.

### Contract deviations (where this list and the contract disagree, this list wins)

1. **Units that the catalog lacks.** A thermoelectric voltage is written in volts: `voltage` has the prefixes but no explicit `mV` unit, and a column `unit` must be `""` or an explicit unit. The columns use `units: [""]`, so the page shows `5.269 mV` for `0.005269`. The sensitivities (µV/K) and the densities (g/cm³) have no dimension in `units.yaml` (Part A's file, not edited); those columns have the dimension `number`, the cells are the numbers of the research file, and the unit is part of the column name ("Density (g/cm³)"). Resistivities are written in `ohmmm2m`, temperatures in `degC`, tolerances in `tempdiff`/`degC`, and α in `""` (1/K) with `units: ["", pctK, ppmK]`.
2. **Empty cells (`null`) beyond the contract's UNVERIFIED rule.** UNVERIFIED in the research: α of gold, nickel, iron, unalloyed low-carbon steel, stainless steel 1.4301 and nichrome 80/20 (controller decision: empty, the row note names the spread or the single source), the SAC405 liquidus, the ISO 9453 number 703 of Sn96.5Ag3.5. Not found: the ISO 9453 number and designation of SAC405. Controller decisions: the IEC colours of thermocouple type B (weakly sourced), and, because a search excerpt is not a source that was read, the α of phosphor bronze CuSn6 (0.00065 /K) and the upper ends of the ranges of alumina 96 % (εr 9.4, tan δ 0.0004, Kyocera A476); the table notes say these values were not confirmed from a primary document, and the CoorsTek values of the alumina row stay. Mine: the loss tangent of air (the research wrote 0 with the remark "no value in the sources"; a table must not show an unsourced zero, the row note says air is practically lossless). Each of these cells has a vector with `want: null`.
3. **Copper is exactly 1/58.** The row `Copper, annealed (standard)` has ρ20 = 0.017241379310344827 Ω·mm²/m (not the research's rounded 0.017241), the value of the wire calculators (`wiring.yaml`: `1.7241379310344827e-8` Ω·m); the aluminium row has 0.028264 and both rows α 0.00393 and 0.00403 /K as the calculators.
4. **Research columns that are not shipped:** `id` (the first column, a display name, is the key), `flags` (implementer-only) and `freq_hz` (one representative frequency would mislead for a range such as "60 Hz – 2 GHz"; the text column `freq` stays). The `_min`/`_max` range columns are shipped.
5. **Text keys, no finders.** The key columns (`material`, `alloy`, `type`) are text, so `lookup` cannot use them; no calculator of phase 3 looks these tables up, so none has a `finder` and the vectors have `cells` only (the key of a cell vector is the English text of the key cell). The research rows that would share a key carry the grade or the frequency in the key text ("FR-4 high-Tg (example), 1 GHz", "Hydrocarbon/ceramic laminate RO4003C").
6. **`guide: true` only on `thermocouple_types`.** The research says no guide note for all four tables; the thermocouple table is transcribed standard content (tolerance classes and colours read from maker tables, not from the IEC text), where the banner "the standard is authoritative" is right. The other three say "typical values" in their notes.
7. **Notes extended from the research's own flags**, nothing invented: the tin row (two reliable digits), the PTFE row (tan δ is an upper limit), the PVC row (0.05 is a representative pick inside the source range 0.04 to 0.1), the air row, the K, T, E, R, S and B rows of the thermocouple table (reference range of K, ranges ending at 400 and 1000 °C, class 1 above 1100 °C for R and S, type B) and the rows whose cell is empty. The table notes (en, de) state every omission and why.

### Environment and edit conventions

- Windows box. Set `GOTMPDIR` to a short backslash path and create it once (`$env:GOTMPDIR = 'C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p3-c3'`). Run every command from the repository root.
- YAML and JSON under `internal/ecalc/` are LF in a Windows working copy. Use the micro sign U+00B5 for µ and the Greek capital omega U+03A9 for Ω in unit texts (not the Greek small mu U+03BC or the ohm sign U+2126; the Greek table names contain U+03BC only as an ordinary letter); tools that decode backslash-u escapes (Write/Edit) must be given the characters themselves.
- The snapshot `internal/ecalc/testdata/catalog.en.json` is generated: regenerate it with `go test ./internal/ecalc -run TestCatalogSnapshot -update`, never merge it by hand. If another table part is merged first, regenerate again.
- Commit messages end with the trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Run `detect-changes` before the commit (CLAUDE.md); it must not be `partial` or `truncated`. This task changes data files only (no function), so no `impact` run is needed.

- [ ] **Step 3: create the table file**

Create `internal/ecalc/catalog/tables/materials.yaml` with exactly this content:

```yaml
# Materials tables: resistivity of conductor and resistance materials, permittivity and loss of dielectrics, thermocouple
# types and soft solder alloys. They are typical values from handbooks and maker data sheets (the thermocouple table is
# transcribed from IEC 60584 as the makers print it), so the notes say so. A cell that the sources could not settle is
# empty (null) and the row note or the table note says why; the vectors in testdata/vectors/tables/ pin those empty cells.
# Cells are written in the unit of their column: Ω·mm²/m (ohmmm2m), 1/K, °C (degC), K for tolerances (tempdiff degC) and V
# for the thermoelectric voltages (the research lists mV; the unit "" shows 5.269 mV again).
- id: resistivity_conductors
  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: materials
  name: {cs: "Měrný odpor vodičových a odporových materiálů", da: "Resistivitet for leder- og modstandsmaterialer", de: "Spezifischer Widerstand von Leiter- und Widerstandswerkstoffen", el: "Ειδική αντίσταση υλικών αγωγών και αντιστάσεων", en: "Resistivity of conductor and resistance materials", es: "Resistividad de materiales conductores y resistivos", fr: "Résistivité des matériaux conducteurs et résistifs", hi: "चालक और प्रतिरोधक पदार्थों की प्रतिरोधकता", it: "Resistività di materiali conduttori e resistivi", ja: "導体・抵抗材料の抵抗率", nl: "Soortelijke weerstand van geleider- en weerstandsmaterialen", no: "Resistivitet for leder- og motstandsmaterialer", pl: "Rezystywność materiałów przewodzących i rezystancyjnych", pt: "Resistividade de materiais condutores e resistivos", sv: "Resistivitet för ledar- och motståndsmaterial", zh: "导体与电阻材料的电阻率"}
  doc: {en: "Resistivity at 20 °C and temperature coefficient of common conductor, contact, resistance and solder materials, for estimates of wire resistance and voltage drop.", de: "Spezifischer Widerstand bei 20 °C und Temperaturkoeffizient gebräuchlicher Leiter-, Kontakt-, Widerstands- und Lotwerkstoffe für Abschätzungen von Leitungswiderstand und Spannungsfall."}
  notes: {en: "Typical values at 20 °C. Real conductors differ with purity, alloy content and temper (cold work raises the resistivity). The linear model ρ(T) = ρ20 · (1 + α · (T − 20 °C)) holds only in a moderate range around 20 °C; for iron, nickel and tungsten the error grows quickly with temperature. Annealed copper (IEC 60028) and hard-drawn aluminium wire (IEC 60889) are the standard values of the wire calculators; the other rows come from handbooks and maker data sheets, and the columns for the lowest and highest resistivity show how far the sources spread. For constantan and manganin the makers specify a band for α instead of a single value (columns α lower and upper limit); inside that band the resistance is practically constant. α is left empty where the sources disagree or only one source was found: gold, nickel, iron, unalloyed steel, stainless steel and nichrome (the row note names the spread). The only α found for phosphor bronze was not confirmed from a primary document and is left empty too, and the resistivity of tin is only reliable to two digits. The sources give no α for the solders. 1 Ω·mm²/m = 1 µΩ·m = 100 µΩ·cm; % IACS = 1.7241 µΩ·cm / ρ × 100.", de: "Typische Werte bei 20 °C. Reale Leiter weichen je nach Reinheit, Legierungsgehalt und Zustand ab (Kaltverformung erhöht den spezifischen Widerstand). Das lineare Modell ρ(T) = ρ20 · (1 + α · (T − 20 °C)) gilt nur in einem mäßigen Bereich um 20 °C; bei Eisen, Nickel und Wolfram wächst der Fehler mit der Temperatur schnell. Weichgeglühtes Kupfer (IEC 60028) und hartgezogener Aluminiumdraht (IEC 60889) sind die Normwerte der Leitungsrechner; die übrigen Zeilen stammen aus Handbüchern und Herstellerdatenblättern, und die Spalten für den niedrigsten und höchsten Wert zeigen, wie weit die Quellen streuen. Für Konstantan und Manganin geben die Hersteller statt eines Einzelwerts ein Band für α an (Spalten α untere und obere Grenze); innerhalb dieses Bands ist der Widerstand praktisch konstant. α bleibt leer, wo sich die Quellen widersprechen oder nur eine Quelle gefunden wurde: Gold, Nickel, Eisen, unlegierter Stahl, Edelstahl und Nichrome (die Zeilenanmerkung nennt die Streuung). Das einzige gefundene α von Phosphorbronze wurde nicht aus einem Primärdokument bestätigt und bleibt ebenfalls leer, und der spezifische Widerstand von Zinn ist nur auf zwei Stellen verlässlich. Für die Lote nennen die Quellen kein α. 1 Ω·mm²/m = 1 µΩ·m = 100 µΩ·cm; % IACS = 1,7241 µΩ·cm / ρ × 100."}
  tags: [resistivity, conductivity, temperature coefficient, tcr, alpha, copper, aluminium, silver, gold, constantan, manganin, nichrome, iacs, material, spezifischer widerstand, leitfähigkeit, temperaturkoeffizient, kupfer, widerstandslegierung, werkstoff]
  source: "IEC 60028 (annealed copper) and IEC 60889 (hard-drawn aluminium wire); CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 84th ed., section 12 (pure metals); Wikipedia, HyperPhysics and Engineering ToolBox (textbook values after Giancoli and Serway); Isabellenhütte and Kanthal data sheets (manganin, constantan, nichrome); Deutsches Kupferinstitut, Aurubis and Bikar data sheets (brass, phosphor bronze); Elgin and Lamineries Matthey data sheets (steels); NIST solder database, Kester and Indium Corporation (solders)"

  name: {cs: "Permitivita a ztrátový činitel dielektrik", da: "Permittivitet og tabsfaktor for dielektrika", de: "Permittivitätszahl und Verlustfaktor von Dielektrika", el: "Σχετική διηλεκτρική σταθερά και εφαπτομένη απωλειών διηλεκτρικών", en: "Relative permittivity and loss tangent of dielectrics", es: "Permitividad relativa y tangente de pérdidas de dieléctricos", fr: "Permittivité relative et tangente de pertes des diélectriques", hi: "परावैद्युतों की सापेक्ष विद्युतशीलता और हानि स्पर्शज्या", it: "Permittività relativa e tangente di perdita dei dielettrici", ja: "誘電体の比誘電率と誘電正接", nl: "Relatieve permittiviteit en verliesfactor van diëlektrica", no: "Relativ permittivitet og tapsfaktor for dielektrika", pl: "Względna przenikalność elektryczna i tangens kąta strat dielektryków", pt: "Permitividade relativa e tangente de perdas de dielétricos", sv: "Relativ permittivitet och förlustfaktor för dielektrika", zh: "电介质的相对介电常数与损耗角正切"}
  doc: {en: "Relative permittivity εr and loss tangent tan δ of circuit board laminates, cable insulation, glass and ceramic substrates, with the frequency of the measurement.", de: "Permittivitätszahl εr und Verlustfaktor tan δ von Leiterplatten-Basismaterialien, Kabelisolierstoffen, Glas und Keramiksubstraten, mit der Messfrequenz."}
  notes: {en: "Typical values. εr and tan δ depend on frequency, temperature, humidity and, for laminates, on resin content and glass weave; always state the frequency with the value. For impedance design use the board maker's stack-up data (Rogers: the design Dk). The lowest and highest columns show the range between sources or grades. For Rogers laminates εr is the process value at 10 GHz and the design Dk is the value to use for line impedances. Several loss tangents come from a single data sheet (polyethylene, PVC, borosilicate glass, Kapton, alumina 99.5 %), and the generic FR-4 row is a collection of values from application notes, not one maker. The upper ends of the ranges for alumina 96 % (Kyocera values) were not confirmed from a primary document and are left empty. tan δ is the ratio of the loss to the stored energy per cycle; the dielectric attenuation of a line grows with √εr · tan δ · f.", de: "Typische Werte. εr und tan δ hängen von Frequenz, Temperatur, Feuchte und, bei Laminaten, von Harzanteil und Glasgewebe ab; den Wert immer mit der Frequenz angeben. Für den Impedanzentwurf die Lagenaufbau-Daten des Leiterplattenherstellers verwenden (Rogers: den Design-Dk). Die Spalten für den niedrigsten und höchsten Wert zeigen den Bereich zwischen Quellen oder Sorten. Bei Rogers-Laminaten ist εr der Prozesswert bei 10 GHz, und für Leitungsimpedanzen gilt der Design-Dk. Mehrere Verlustfaktoren stammen aus einem einzigen Datenblatt (Polyethylen, PVC, Borosilikatglas, Kapton, Aluminiumoxid 99,5 %), und die Zeile für allgemeines FR-4 sammelt Werte aus Applikationsschriften, nicht von einem Hersteller. Die oberen Bereichsgrenzen von Aluminiumoxid 96 % (Kyocera-Werte) wurden nicht aus einem Primärdokument bestätigt und bleiben leer. tan δ ist das Verhältnis von Verlust- zu gespeicherter Energie je Periode; die dielektrische Dämpfung einer Leitung wächst mit √εr · tan δ · f."}
  tags: [permittivity, dielectric constant, dk, loss tangent, tan delta, df, fr-4, rogers, ptfe, laminate, pcb, insulation, epsilon, permittivität, dielektrizitätszahl, verlustfaktor, leiterplatte, isolierstoff]

- id: thermocouple_types
  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: materials
  guide: true
  name: {cs: "Typy termočlánků (IEC 60584)", da: "Termoelementtyper (IEC 60584)", de: "Thermoelement-Typen (IEC 60584)", el: "Τύποι θερμοζευγών (IEC 60584)", en: "Thermocouple types (IEC 60584)", es: "Tipos de termopares (IEC 60584)", fr: "Types de thermocouples (IEC 60584)", hi: "थर्मोकपल के प्रकार (IEC 60584)", it: "Tipi di termocoppie (IEC 60584)", ja: "熱電対の種類 (IEC 60584)", nl: "Thermokoppeltypen (IEC 60584)", no: "Termoelementtyper (IEC 60584)", pl: "Typy termopar (IEC 60584)", pt: "Tipos de termopares (IEC 60584)", sv: "Termoelementtyper (IEC 60584)", zh: "热电偶类型 (IEC 60584)"}
  doc: {en: "The standard thermocouple types B, E, J, K, N, R, S and T: conductor materials, temperature range of the reference function, tolerance classes 1 and 2, thermoelectric voltage and sensitivity, and the colours of thermocouple cables.", de: "Die genormten Thermoelement-Typen B, E, J, K, N, R, S und T: Schenkelwerkstoffe, Temperaturbereich der Referenzfunktion, Toleranzklassen 1 und 2, Thermospannung und Empfindlichkeit sowie die Farben der Thermoelementleitungen."}
  notes: {en: "The thermoelectric voltage is defined with the reference (cold) junction at 0 °C; at another reference temperature subtract the voltage of the same type at that temperature. The sensitivity changes with temperature, so use the reference function or table, not a constant, for accurate work. Voltages and sensitivities are taken from the NIST ITS-90 tables, whose reference functions equal those of IEC 60584-1. Tolerance: the larger of the fixed value (°C) and the proportional value (factor × |t|) applies; for types R and S the class 1 limit above 1100 °C is ±[1 + 0.003·(t − 1100)] °C, and class 1 is not defined for type B (class 3 exists but is not listed). The tolerance classes are transcribed from three agreeing maker tables, not from the IEC table itself. IEC 60584-1:2013 limits the type K reference function to 1300 °C (the NIST tables go to 1372 °C). Colours follow IEC 60584-3:2007 (the positive core in the type colour, the negative core white, intrinsically safe circuits with a blue sheath); the 2021 edition, which also adds types C and A, was not checked. The IEC name of the type E colour is violet, makers write purple. The IEC colours of type B are weakly sourced and left empty. ANSI MC96.1: the negative core is always red; the thermocouple-grade jacket is not established for types R, S and B. For type B the mean sensitivity between 0 and 100 °C is not meaningful (the output is almost zero below about 50 °C). Older national colour codes (DIN 43714, BS 1843, JIS, NF) differ: check the colours of an existing installation before connecting.", de: "Die Thermospannung ist für eine Vergleichsstelle bei 0 °C festgelegt; bei anderer Vergleichsstellentemperatur die Spannung desselben Typs bei dieser Temperatur abziehen. Die Empfindlichkeit ändert sich mit der Temperatur – für genaue Messungen die Referenzfunktion oder Tabelle verwenden, nicht einen konstanten Wert. Spannungen und Empfindlichkeiten stammen aus den NIST-ITS-90-Tabellen, deren Referenzfunktionen mit denen der IEC 60584-1 übereinstimmen. Grenzabweichung: Es gilt der größere Wert aus festem Wert (°C) und proportionalem Wert (Faktor × |t|); bei den Typen R und S gilt für Klasse 1 oberhalb 1100 °C ±[1 + 0,003·(t − 1100)] °C, und für Typ B ist Klasse 1 nicht festgelegt (Klasse 3 gibt es, sie ist hier nicht aufgeführt). Die Toleranzklassen sind aus drei übereinstimmenden Herstellertabellen übernommen, nicht aus der IEC-Tabelle selbst. Die IEC 60584-1:2013 begrenzt die Referenzfunktion von Typ K auf 1300 °C (die NIST-Tabellen reichen bis 1372 °C). Die Farben folgen IEC 60584-3:2007 (Plus-Ader in der Typfarbe, Minus-Ader weiß, eigensichere Kreise mit blauem Mantel); die Ausgabe 2021, die auch die Typen C und A ergänzt, wurde nicht geprüft. Die IEC-Bezeichnung der Farbe von Typ E ist violett, Hersteller schreiben purple. Die IEC-Farben von Typ B sind nur schwach belegt und bleiben leer. ANSI MC96.1: Die Minus-Ader ist immer rot; der Mantel der Thermoleitung ist für die Typen R, S und B nicht festgelegt. Für Typ B ist die mittlere Empfindlichkeit zwischen 0 und 100 °C nicht aussagekräftig (die Thermospannung ist unterhalb von etwa 50 °C fast null). Ältere nationale Farbcodes (DIN 43714, BS 1843, JIS, NF) weichen ab: vor dem Anschließen die Farben einer bestehenden Installation prüfen."}
  tags: [thermocouple, thermoelement, type k, type j, type t, type e, type n, type r, type s, type b, iec 60584, tolerance class, colour code, color code, farbcode, thermospannung, seebeck, temperature sensor, temperaturfühler]
  source: "IEC 60584-1:2013 (conductors and reference-function ranges); tolerance classes after SAB Bröckskes, Thermosense and TC Direct (IEC 60584-1 classes); thermoelectric voltages after the NIST ITS-90 Thermocouple Database; colours after IEC 60584-3:2007 (TC Direct, Tempco, EPIC Sensors) and ANSI MC96.1 (Thermometrics, Omega)"

- id: solder_alloys
  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: materials
  name: {cs: "Pájecí slitiny", da: "Loddelegeringer", de: "Lotlegierungen", el: "Κράματα συγκόλλησης", en: "Solder alloys", es: "Aleaciones de soldadura", fr: "Alliages de brasure", hi: "सोल्डर मिश्रधातुएँ", it: "Leghe per saldatura", ja: "はんだ合金", nl: "Soldeerlegeringen", no: "Loddelegeringer", pl: "Stopy lutownicze", pt: "Ligas de solda", sv: "Lödlegeringar", zh: "焊料合金"}
  doc: {en: "Common soft solder alloys for electronics: composition, ISO 9453 designation, melting range, density and typical use.", de: "Gebräuchliche Weichlotlegierungen für die Elektronik: Zusammensetzung, Kurzzeichen nach ISO 9453, Schmelzbereich, Dichte und typische Verwendung."}
  notes: {en: "Typical values from maker data sheets. Non-eutectic alloys are pasty between solidus and liquidus; eutectic alloys melt at one temperature. Use the maker's data sheet for the soldering profile. Lead-containing solders (Sn63Pb37, Sn60Pb40) are restricted by RoHS in the EU; use them only where an exemption applies (for example repairs of old equipment). The liquidus of SAC405 is left empty because the sources give 217, 219 and 225 °C, and no ISO 9453 number of SAC405 was found. The number 703 for Sn96.5Ag3.5 rests on a single weak source and is left empty. The ISO 9453 numbers 401 (Sn99.3Cu0.7) and 301 (Sn42Bi58) come from one maker catalogue. The densities are typical values and differ by up to about 2 % between makers.", de: "Typische Werte aus Herstellerdatenblättern. Nicht-eutektische Legierungen sind zwischen Solidus und Liquidus teigig; eutektische Legierungen schmelzen bei einer Temperatur. Für das Lötprofil das Herstellerdatenblatt verwenden. Bleihaltige Lote (Sn63Pb37, Sn60Pb40) sind in der EU durch RoHS beschränkt; nur verwenden, wo eine Ausnahme gilt (zum Beispiel Reparatur alter Geräte). Der Liquidus von SAC405 bleibt leer, weil die Quellen 217, 219 und 225 °C nennen, und für SAC405 wurde keine ISO-9453-Nummer gefunden. Die Nummer 703 für Sn96,5Ag3,5 beruht auf einer einzigen schwachen Quelle und bleibt leer. Die ISO-9453-Nummern 401 (Sn99,3Cu0,7) und 301 (Sn42Bi58) stammen aus einem Herstellerkatalog. Die Dichten sind typische Werte und weichen zwischen Herstellern um bis zu etwa 2 % ab."}
  tags: [solder, lötzinn, lot, alloy, legierung, sac305, sac405, sn63pb37, lead-free, bleifrei, eutectic, eutektisch, melting point, schmelzpunkt, liquidus, solidus, iso 9453, rohs]
  source: "ISO 9453:2006 (alloy numbers and designations, after the Stannol catalogue and the iTeh preview); Kester alloy temperature chart and technical data on soft solders; Indium Corporation solder alloy directory and Indalloy 256 data sheet; DKL Metals E-Qual data sheet; NIST database for solder properties"
  key: alloy
  columns:
    - {id: alloy, name: {en: Alloy, de: Legierung}, dim: text}
    - {id: common_name, name: {en: "Common name", de: "Handelsname"}, dim: text}

### Tables and cells left out, and uncertain values

**No table is left out and no column is dropped for lack of data.** Every column of the research files appears in the tables except `id`, `flags` and `freq_hz` (deviation 4).

**Empty on purpose** (each pinned by a `want: null` vector and explained in the table notes): α of gold, nickel, iron, unalloyed steel, stainless steel 1.4301, nichrome 80/20 and phosphor bronze; the upper ends of εr and tan δ of alumina 96 %; tan δ of air; the IEC colours of type B; the SAC405 liquidus; the ISO 9453 numbers and designations of SAC405 and Sn96.5Ag3.5 (number 703 unverified); `c1_tol_frac` of R and S (class 1 above 1100 °C is a formula, stated in the note); `emf_1000` of type T and `seebeck_1000` of types T and E (outside or at the end of the range); the ANSI thermocouple-grade jacket of R, S and B (not established).

**Kept, but weakly sourced** (the controller accepts single maker or handbook sources for typical values; listed so the review can overrule):

- tin ρ = 0.11 Ω·mm²/m: the sources range from 0.109 to 0.115, the row note says so;
- copper (pure) α = 0.0040 and aluminium (pure) α = 0.0043: the textbook values of HyperPhysics (0.00386) and Engineering ToolBox (0.0038) are 3 to 12 % lower; brass α = 0.0017 against 0.0015 (Engineering ToolBox);
- PVC tan δ 0.05 is a representative pick inside the single source's range 0.04 to 0.1 (row note);
- the tolerance classes of the thermocouples are from three agreeing maker tables, the IEC table itself was not read; the colours follow IEC 60584-3:2007 and were not checked against the 2021 edition (both said in the table note); the type K reference range is the IEC 1300 °C (NIST: 1372 °C);
- the ISO 9453 numbers 401 (Sn99.3Cu0.7) and 301 (Sn42Bi58) come from one maker catalogue (Stannol); the SAC405 density and the use "BGA solder spheres" rest on a single maker and on search excerpts;
- the standard rows copper (IEC 60028) and aluminium (IEC 60889) were not re-read in the standards (the web previews were not reachable); their values are those already used by the ECalc wire calculators, and the aluminium pair was verified by the controller through HD 532 S1 and GB/T 17048-2017.

## Part C4 — General tables (task C4.1)


**Goal of this part:** add the catalog file `internal/ecalc/catalog/tables/general.yaml` with 15 general reference tables (478 rows) and their 15 vector files: SI prefixes, SI units, physical constants (CODATA 2022), the Greek alphabet, IP codes (IEC 60529), protection classes (IEC 61140), mains voltage, frequency and plugs of 48 countries, ISM and EU SRD bands, LoRaWAN regional plans, Wi-Fi channels, the German amateur radio bands (AFuV Annex 1), logic levels, RS-232/RS-485/LVDS levels, the ASCII table and wire colours (IEC/DE and US NEC). No Go or JavaScript code changes: part A's loader, the table page of part UT and the tool of part B read the tables as they are.

**How this part was made and verified:** every file below is the exact text of a file in the scratch worktree `P3\wc4` (Part A applied, nothing committed). The YAML and the vector files were produced by one generator script (kept outside the repository) that parses the CSV blocks of `P3\research\general\*.md` instead of retyping them, applies the decisions below and writes the files with LF line endings; the vector expectations are separate literals taken from the research text and the sources it cites, never read back from the engine. The red and green runs below were really executed in that worktree.

**Environment.** Windows box. Run Go commands from the repository root with a short backslash `GOTMPDIR`:

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p3-c4 | Out-Null
$env:GOTMPDIR = 'C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p3-c4'
```

(Git Bash equivalent: `export GOTMPDIR='C:\tmp\go-build-ecalc-p3-c4'`.) Commit messages end with the trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Write the micro sign (U+00B5) and the Greek capital omega (U+03A9) as characters; the file also holds the Greek letters of the alphabet table (including the small mu U+03BC, which belongs there) and the superscript digits of the units; tools that decode backslash-u sequences must be given the characters themselves, and a backslash in a YAML text is written `\\` inside the double quotes (the ASCII table has two).

**Dependencies.** Part A (the `Table` loader, the dimension `text`, the dimensions `number`, `integer`, `frequency`, `power`, `voltage` and `ratio` with the unit `pct`, display `units` lists and the table vector test `TestTableVectors`). The files of this part are independent of the parts C1 to C3 (no shared ids: the ids of the group are listed in the Files section and none of them occurs in the other groups' files of the drafting worktrees).

### Contract deviations (where this list and the contract disagree, this list wins)

1. **15 tables instead of the 10 to 12 of the contract's size guide.** The research delivered 15 topics (ip_codes and protection_classes, the four radio tables and the two level tables were each one topic of the brief), and every one of them is shipped.
2. **No `finder` on any general table.** The finder calculators are part C1's (wiring); nothing in this group is selected by a calculator.
3. **Columns that are not shipped:** the provenance column `check` of six research files (`mains_by_country`, `ism_bands`, `lora_regional_plans`, `logic_levels`, `line_interface_levels`, `wire_colours`) and the `id` columns of `physical_constants`, `ism_bands` and `logic_levels` (internal handles); the CODATA 2018 value and uncertainty columns of `physical_constants` (2022 only, see the decisions); the `test_hint` column of `ip_codes`; the research column `position` of `ip_codes` (the position is part of the key text, see 5). The source marks `(WP)`/`(WS)` in the notes of `mains_by_country` are spelled out as Wikipedia and WorldStandards.
4. **A column has one dimension, so rows with mixed units use text or the dimension `number`.** `physical_constants` holds value and uncertainty as text with every printed digit (`6.62607015×10⁻³⁴`, German with a decimal comma) and the unit as text: the cells of one column are metres per second, joules, coulombs and so on, and the page rounds a numeric cell to the significant-digits setting (3 to 6), which would show c as 299800000. `line_interface_levels` has the dimension `number` for min, typ and max and a text column `unit` (V, mV, kΩ, V/µs, UL, mA, Ω). `logic_levels` keeps the output limits as text (`4.4 / 3.84 V`, `VCC − 0.1 / 3.8 V`: two values for two load currents, one of them a formula) next to the numeric input limits. `lora_regional_plans` keeps the frequency as text (a list such as `868.1; 868.3; 868.5 MHz` or a formula such as `902.3 + 0.2·n MHz`) next to numeric step and bandwidth.
5. **Keys.** Numeric keys (so that `lookup` works): `si_prefixes` by `exponent`, `wifi_channels` by `channel`, `amateur_bands_de` by `nr`, `ascii` by `dec`. Every other table has a text key that is unique in English: the first column, or `key:` where another column is the key (`si_units` by `quantity`, `line_interface_levels` by `parameter`, `wire_colours` by `conductor`, `physical_constants` by `name`, `greek_alphabet` by `upper`). Where no column is unique the key text is composed: `ip_codes` (`1st numeral: 5`, `2nd numeral: 9K`, German `1. Kennziffer: 5`), `lora_regional_plans` (`EU868 default uplink channels`), `ism_bands` (`ISM 13.56 MHz`, `SRD 868.7–869.2 MHz`: named after the centre frequency or the edges), `line_interface_levels` (`RS-485: receiver differential threshold`: the interface and the parameter).
6. **Frequencies are stored in hertz and powers in watts** (the dimensions `frequency` and `power` have no explicit MHz or mW unit, the cell `unit` stays `""`): 13.56 MHz is `13560000`, 1 W is `1`. The page shows them with the automatic prefix and the significant-digits setting; `ism_bands` and `amateur_bands_de` say in their notes that digits beyond the setting are rounded. The duty cycle of `ism_bands` is a `ratio` with the unit `pct` (10 % is written `10`).
7. **`ascii.dec` is an `integer` column with `units: ["dec", "hex", "bin", "oct"]`** (the number-system units cannot be the cell unit, so `unit` stays `""`; because the list has no `""` entry the page opens in `dec`). The research's `hex` column is a text column of two-digit strings (`"0A"`, quoted, because a text cell must be a string).
8. **Single-source cells are left empty (`null`) or out**, as decided by the controller, with the exceptions below; every omission is named in the `notes` of its table. Details are in the next section.
9. **German texts that the research wrote itself** are carried over as they are (list at the end of this part). Texts that this part wrote (German notes, column names, labels such as `Standard-Uplink-Kanäle`, `1. Kennziffer: 5`, `exakt (abgeleitet)`) and all 14 names in the locales other than English and German are also machine-written and have not been reviewed by a native speaker.
10. **Item `name` is written in all 16 locales; `doc` and `notes` in English and German; column names in English and German; text cells are plain strings where both languages agree and `{en, de}` where they differ.** Decimal points in text cells are written with a comma in the German variant.

### Decisions applied to the research data

| Decision | Applied as |
| --- | --- |
| `physical_constants`: CODATA 2022 only | 30 rows, the 2022 value and standard uncertainty; the exact constants have no uncertainty (empty cell); the note says which constants are exact and which are exact because derived |
| `ip_codes`: drop the `test_hint` column (Wikipedia only) | 20 rows (8 entries for the first numeral: 0 to 6 and X; 12 for the second: 0 to 9, X and 9K) with `short` and `definition`; the note says that test conditions and the letters A to D, H, M, S, W are not listed |
| UNVERIFIED and single-source cells become `null` | `protection_classes`: the IEC 60417 number of class I (5019) and the whole remark of class II (functional-earth variant, symbol 6092: en.wikipedia only); `greek_alphabet`: the uses α "common-base current gain" and θ/ϑ "angle; temperature" (not backed by a source read) and the placeholder texts of ι, ξ, ο, υ; `ism_bands`: the notes of three SRD rows that quoted further limits (rows 44a, 56a and 57c of the decision) are cut to the plain use; `wire_colours`: the row PEN (marking `green-yellow with blue markings at the ends`, one source), the "may be bare" of the US grounding conductor and the historical colour notes; `mains_by_country`: Brazil's voltage (127 V or 220 V by region) and Japan's frequency (50 Hz east, 60 Hz west) have no single value |
| The binding legal text counts as one authoritative source (controller decision after review) | `ism_bands`: power, power reference and duty cycle of the SRD rows `433.05–434.79 MHz` (10 mW e.r.p., 10 %), `2400–2483.5 MHz` (10 mW e.i.r.p.) and `5725–5875 MHz` (25 mW e.i.r.p.) come from Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/180 and are shipped; the vectors pin them, and the notes say "SRD limits per Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/180; check EUR-Lex for later amendments." |
| Electrical levels of a single maker document stay, with the document named ("typical per ...") | `line_interface_levels`: RS-232 load 3–7 kΩ, receiver input impedance 3–7 kΩ and slew rate 30 V/µs (TI SLLA037A), RS-485 unit load ≈ 12 kΩ (TI SLLA272D), LVDS output voltage 247/454 mV and offset voltage 1.125/1.375 V (TI SN65LVDS31 data sheet): each named in the Condition column and in the notes; `logic_levels`: 74LS VOH 2.5 V and VOL 0.4/0.5 V (TI SN74LS00 data sheet), named in the row's remark |
| `mains_by_country`: 48 countries, plug types as text, `guide` and `mains` | `voltage` (dimension `voltage`) and `frequency` (dimension `frequency`) numeric, `plugs` text such as `C, F`; the notes name the retired IEC World Plugs page, the three-way comparison and the five voltage decisions (CN, KR and AR 220 V, CY 230 V, RU 230 V, MX 127 V) |
| Text-heavy tables (ascii, greek_alphabet, si_units) | text columns; the numeric key `dec` for ASCII; `quantity` as the key of `si_units`; `upper` for the Greek letters |
| German texts written by the research | carried over, listed below for a German review pass |

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the vector files first**

Every file has the format of part A (task A3): `cells` name a row by its key (a number in the unit of the key column, or the English text of a text key), a column and the expected cell (a number in the unit of that column, the English text of a text cell, or `null` for an empty cell); `lookups` evaluate a table function and want an SI number. Every entry carries a `ref` naming the source of the expected value. Cells that must stay empty are pinned as `null` (for example Japan's frequency, or the duty cycle of the 2.4 GHz SRD row, for which the decision gives no limit).
