### 1. Item kinds in the catalog (A)

- The loader reads `calculators/*.yaml`, `tables/*.yaml` and `codes/*.yaml` (sorted, in that order). Every file is a YAML
  list of items; every item has `kind` (`calculator` only in `calculators/`, `table` only in `tables/`, `code` only in
  `codes/`). Ids are unique across all kinds and match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` (max 63). `Catalog` gets `Tables []*Table`,
  `Codes []*Code` and `Item(id) (kind string, ok bool)`; `Calculator(id)` stays. Categories: tables → `tables`, codes →
  `codes`, calculators → any calculator category (not `tables`/`codes`/`pinouts`).
- Common fields of every kind: `id kind category name(16 locales) doc(en,de; optional for tables/codes) tags source`.

#### 1.1 Table items

```yaml
- id: cable_ampacity_cu_pvc
  kind: table
  category: tables
  group: conductors            # conductors | components | materials | general (list sections)
  name: {16 locales}
  doc: {en: "…", de: "…"}      # optional
  notes: {en: "…", de: "…"}    # optional, shown under the table
  tags: [ampacity, belastbarkeit]
  source: "…"
  guide: true                  # optional: the "guide values — the standard is authoritative" banner
  mains: true                  # optional: the mains safety note
  key: section                 # optional key column for lookup(); default: the first column
  columns:
    - {id: section, name: {en: Cross-section, de: Querschnitt}, dim: area, unit: mm2, units: ["mm2", "AWG"], label: "A"}
    - {id: a1_2, name: {en: "A1, 2 loaded", de: "A1, 2 belastet"}, dim: current, unit: ""}
    - {id: note, name: {en: Note, de: Hinweis}, dim: text}
  rows:
    - [1.5, 15.5, "—"]
    - [2.5, 19.5, {en: "see note 2", de: "siehe Anmerkung 2"}]
  finder: {calc: cable_cross_section_finder, column: section, var: section, choices: {material: cu_pvc}}   # optional
```

- Column `dim` is a dimension of `units.yaml` or `text`. Numeric cells are finite YAML numbers written in the column's
  `unit` — `""` (the base symbol, no prefix) or an explicit unit id of that dimension (`mm2`, `kcmil`, `degC`, `ppm/K` …)
  — or `null` (empty cell). The loader converts them to SI (factor or the unit's `to` expression); table cells are not
  checked against a dimension's `positive` flag. Text cells are a plain string (language-neutral) or `{en, de}` (other
  locales fall back to en). `units` = display units offered for the column (same semantics as var `units` of phase 2);
  `label` = optional typeset label. Column ids unique per table, `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`.
- Every row has exactly as many cells as there are columns. The key column must be numeric with unique non-null values
  or text with unique values.
- `generate: awg | ipc2221 | eseries_e24 | eseries_e192` instead of `rows`: the rows (and the columns listed in §5) come
  from the engine (formula-derived tables); the YAML then carries every other field.
- `finder`: a calculator id; `column` = a table column; `var` = a variable or derived id of that calculator whose solved
  value selects the highlighted row (row whose `column` value equals it within 1e-9 relative); `choices` = choice options
  that the header fixes and hides. The calculator's table functions must reference this table under those choices.

#### 1.2 Code items

```yaml
- id: resistor_color_code
  kind: code
  category: codes
  code: resistor_bands          # a registered code kind (K registers 5)
  name: {16 locales}
  doc: {en, de}
  tags: [...]
  source: "…"
  data: {…}                     # kind-specific, validated by the code kind (K)
```

- A implements the plumbing: `type Code struct { ID, Category, CodeKind string; Name, Doc Text; Tags []string; Source
  string; Data any }` plus a registry `RegisterCodeKind(id string, k CodeKind)` with
  `type CodeKind struct { Load func(raw *yaml.Node, fail func(string, ...any)) any; JSON func(data any, lang string) any }`.
  `Load` validates and returns the typed data stored in `Code.Data`; `JSON` renders it for a language. A unknown `code`
  value fails loading. A's tests register a test-only kind. K registers the five real kinds in `codes.go` (`init`).

#### 1.3 Catalog JSON (`LocalizedJSON`)

`items` stays one array in catalog order (calculators, then tables, then codes). Per kind:
- calculator: unchanged.
- table: `kind id category group name name_en doc notes tags source guide mains key columns rows finder` — `columns[]` =
  `{id, name, dim, unit, units, label}` (always all fields; `units` `[]` when unset; `label` `""`); `rows` = arrays of
  SI numbers, `null`, or localized strings; `finder` = `null` or `{calc, column, var, choices}`.
- code: `kind id category code name name_en doc tags source data` (data via the kind's `JSON`).
Every field always present, never omitted.

### 2. Table functions in the expression language (A, Go + JS + vectors)

- `lookup(T, C, key)` → value of column `C` in the row whose key column equals `key` (numeric: within 1e-9 relative;
  NaN when no row matches or the cell is null).
- `lookup_ge(T, C, x, OUT)` → value of column `OUT` in the FIRST row (table order) whose column `C` is not null and ≥ `x`;
  NaN when none.
- `interp(T, X, Y, x)` → linear interpolation of column `Y` over column `X` (rows where both are non-null; `X` strictly
  monotonic over them, checked at load); NaN outside [min X, max X]; exact at the nodes.
- `T`, `C`, `X`, `Y`, `OUT` are identifiers that name a table / a column of that table, or an **alias** defined by a choice
  option: options may carry `refs: {alias: table_or_column_id}` next to `consts`. Every option of a choice defines the
  same alias set. Table/column arguments are not variables: they are excluded from `Deps`, cannot be inputs, and
  `lookup`/`lookup_ge`/`interp`/aliases are reserved names. All numeric columns used must be numeric; values are SI.
- The loader resolves every table-function call for every combination of the options of the choices whose aliases it
  uses, and fails on an unknown table/column, a text column, or a non-monotonic `interp` X column.
- Go: the calculator holds the resolved references; `Solve` keeps its signature. JS: `window.ECalcCore.tables =
  { register(items), get(id) }` in the new `ecalc-tables.js` (register is called by the shell after the catalog loads and
  by the node script with the snapshot); `ECalcCore.solve.solve(calc, inputs, choices, units)` keeps its signature and reads
  tables through `ECalcCore.tables`. Choice option JSON gains `refs` (always present, `{}` when unset).
- Vectors: `core.json` gains `table_functions` cases (with a small fixture table defined inside the vector file).

### 3. Table vectors (A defines, C fills)

`testdata/vectors/tables/<table id>.json`:
`{"table": id, "cells": [{"key": <key value in the key column's unit, or a string>, "column": id, "want": <number in
the column's unit, or a string (en text), or null>, "ref": "…"}], "lookups": [{"expr": "lookup_ge(t, c, 20, section)",
"env": {}, "want": <SI number>, "ref": "…"}]}`. Every non-generated table: ≥ 3 spot-checked cells with `ref` naming the
source, and the file name equals `<table>.json`; every generated table: ≥ 5 cells checked against published values
(ASTM B258 for AWG, the IPC-2221 chart/equation for the grid, IEC 60063 for E-series). The Go test (and the node script
for lookups) checks them; a vector file without a table fails.

### 4. UI (UT, UK)

- Shell: page by kind — `calculator` → `ECalcCalcPage.create`, `table` → `ECalcTablePage.create`, `code` →
  `ECalcCodePage.create` (if missing: an empty-state message). All three take the same options object (with `item` for
  table/code) and return `{dispose()}`. The rail shows Tables and Codes once they have items; the Tables list is sectioned
  by `group` (keys `desktop.ecalc_group_<group>`).
- Table page (UT): title, guide banner (`desktop.ecalc_guide_values`), mains note (`desktop.ecalc_mains_note`), optional
  finder header (the finder calculator rendered by `ECalcCalcPage` in a compact header mode, with the fixed choices hidden;
  after each solve the matching row is highlighted and scrolled into view), filter box (matches any cell text,
  case-insensitive), sortable columns (click: asc → desc → table order), per-column unit dropdown from `units`, numbers via
  `ECalcCore.units.format` with the significant-digits setting, null as "—", sticky header, horizontal scroll inside the
  page, notes and source under the table, "Copy table" (TSV of the visible rows in the shown units). Keyboard: filter box
  focus with `/`.
- Code pages (UK): per `code` kind — resistor (4/5/6-band selector, SVG resistor with clickable bands opening a colour
  menu, value field showing the bands of the nearest standard value, tolerance and tempco), inductor (same, µH), SMD
  resistor (SVG chip printing the code; code ↔ value, 3-digit/4-digit/EIA-96/R notation), capacitor (code ↔ value,
  tolerance letter, voltage code), ceramic temperature (code ↔ low/high temperature and change, class 1 and 2). All logic
  through `ECalcCore.codes` (K). The colours of the drawing come from the code item's data (`hex`), never from the theme.
- i18n: every new string a `desktop.ecalc_*` key in all 16 locales.

### 5. Generated tables (A)

- `awg`: rows AWG 4/0 … 40 (47 rows). Columns: `size` (text: "4/0", "3/0", "2/0", "1/0", "1" … "40"; the key column,
  `key: size`), `awg` (dim `number`: 4/0 = -3, 3/0 = -2, 2/0 = -1, 1/0 = 0, then 1 … 40 — used by lookups),
  `diameter` (dim `length`, unit `""` with display `units: ["", "in", "mil"]`), `area` (dim `area`, unit `mm2`,
  `units: ["mm2", "kcmil"]`), `r_km` (dim `resistance`: the DC resistance of 1 km of annealed copper at 20 °C, column name
  says "per km"). Formulas: ASTM B258 diameter 0.127 mm × 92^((36 − n)/39); ρ20 = 1/58 Ω·mm²/m (IEC 60028).
- `ipc2221`: rows = currents 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10 A; columns: external and internal width for
  1 oz at ΔT 10 °C and 20 °C (and 2 oz at 10 °C), from I = k·ΔT^0.44·A^0.725 (k 0.048 / 0.024, A in mil²), widths in mm
  (units mm, mil), copper 1 oz = 35 µm (the phase 2 `oz` unit).
- `eseries_e24`: 24 rows (E24 values 1.0 … 9.1) with text columns marking membership in E3/E6/E12/E24 ("●" or "");
  `eseries_e192`: 192 rows (E192 values) with membership columns E48/E96/E192. Values from the engine's IEC 60063 tables.
- Generated table items live in `catalog/tables/generated.yaml` (A owns that file; name/doc/notes/source written by A).

### 6. Codes (K) — engine API

Go (`codes.go`):
```go
type CodeResult struct {
    Kind   string      `json:"kind"`             // the code kind
    Code   string      `json:"code"`             // canonical code text (e.g. "brown black red gold", "103", "1H", "X7R")
    Bands  []string    `json:"bands"`            // colour ids for band kinds, else []
    Value  float64     `json:"value"`            // SI value (Ω, H, F, V) or NaN when the kind has none
    Dim    string      `json:"dim"`              // dimension of Value or ""
    Fields []CodeField `json:"fields"`           // further decoded fields (tolerance, tempco, voltage, temperatures …)
    Warnings []string  `json:"warnings"`         // English
}
type CodeField struct{ ID, Name, Text string; Value float64; Dim string } // json tags id,name,text,value,dim (Value NaN→null)
func (c *Catalog) Decode(kind, code string) (CodeResult, error)
func (c *Catalog) Encode(kind string, req EncodeRequest) (CodeResult, error)
type EncodeRequest struct{ Value string; Bands int; Tolerance string; TempCo string; Voltage string; Class string }
```
JS (`ecalc-codes.js`): `window.ECalcCore.codes = { decode(item, code, units), encode(item, req, units) }` returning the
same shape (Value NaN → null). Errors: Go returns an error with a stable code prefix (`invalid_code:`, `unsupported:`);
JS throws `{code, message}`. Shared vectors `testdata/vectors/codes.json` check both (decode and encode cases, errors).
Input syntax: band colours as English colour ids separated by blanks/commas/dashes (case-insensitive); SMD/capacitor
codes as printed (`103`, `4R7`, `01C`, `104K`, `4p7`, `1H`); ceramic codes as printed (`X7R`, `C0G`, `NP0`).
Encode picks the nearest standard value of the series implied by the tolerance (20 %→E6, 10 %→E12, 5 %→E24, 2 %→E48,
1 %→E96, ≤0.5 %→E192) and says so in a warning when the value changed; a 4-band code holds 2 significant digits, 5/6
bands hold 3. Data (colours, letters, voltage codes, class tables) comes from the code items' `data` (from K's research in
`P3\research\codes\`).

### 7. Tool actions (B)

- `table`: `id`, optional `filter` (substring over every cell text, case-insensitive), optional `offset`/`limit` (paging,
  limit 1–50, default 20), optional `lookup` = `{column, value, mode, output}` (mode `exact|ge|interp`, value a string with
  unit, output a column id; strict schema object). Output: columns (id, name, unit), rows formatted in the column units
  plus SI, `total`, `offset`, `returned`, `truncated`, `guide`, `mains`, notes, source, lookup result; fitted to the inline
  budget.
- `decode`: `kind` (enum of the 5 code kinds), `code`. `encode`: `kind`, `value`, optional `bands` (4|5|6), `tolerance`,
  `tempco`, `voltage`, `class`. Output = `CodeResult` (+ formatted value).
- `search`/`describe` cover tables and codes (describe: table → columns, row count, key, notes, guide; code → kind,
  fields, accepted input forms). `open` works for any item id (values only for calculators).
- Policy: `table`/`decode`/`encode` are read operations (non-mutating) and allowed for A2A peers. Update the tests that
  pin the enum, the A2A list and "table returns invalid_operation". Parameter names must not clash with `ToolCall` fields
  of another type (`values` is the Sheets matrix; `code`, `key`, `value`, `text`, `direction` are strings; `offset` int).
- Manual examples for every operation (the manual test requires one per op).

### 8. Content (C1–C4)

- Source data: `P3\research\<group>\*.md` (written by research agents; read their SUMMARY.md first). Transcribe exactly;
  cells marked UNVERIFIED stay out (or the table stays out) — list them in the report. Every table: `source` naming the
  sources actually used, `guide: true` for transcribed standard tables, `mains: true` for mains/installation tables,
  notes en+de, names in 16 locales, ≥ 3 vector cells. Keep the research ids where sensible.
- C1 also writes the finders in `catalog/calculators/finders.yaml` (category `wiring`): `cable_cross_section_finder`
  (current, ambient temperature, grouping, installation method, material/insulation → smallest standard cross-section
  whose corrected ampacity ≥ the current; uses `interp`/`lookup` for the factors and `lookup_ge` for the section; refs
  select table and columns) and `trace_spacing_finder` (voltage + IPC-2221 class → minimum spacing). Hand-checked
  calculator vectors per phase 1/2 rules; each table's `finder` field points to its finder.
- Group sizes are roughly: conductors 8–10 tables, components 6–7, materials 4, general 10–12.

### 9. Testing per part

- A: `go test ./internal/ecalc -count=1`, `npm run test:ecalc`, snapshot regenerated; a fixture table + a fixture finder
  in tests (not in the shipped catalog except the generated tables).
- UT: `go test ./ui -run ECalc -count=1`, bundle check, browser test extended with a table page (generated tables and a
  fixture finder injected into the served catalog), copy, sort, filter, unit toggle, highlight.
- K: Go + node vectors (`npm run test:ecalc` runs both scripts).
- UK: its own browser test with the 5 code items.
- B: query/tool/agent/audit tests + manual examples.
- C: `go test ./internal/ecalc -count=1`, `npm run test:ecalc`, the table vector tests.

### 10. Plan part format

`P3\part-<x>.md` in the phase 2 style: "Contract deviations" first, tasks `<X>1 …` with Files, TDD steps and COMPLETE
code/data generated from the verified worktree files, a verification section with the exact commands and results. Report
≤ 300 words.
